reviews.title: Nice electric shaver
reviews.text: I purchased this shaver strictly based on reviews from other owners. Product arrived quickly and was ready to use right out of the box. Great shave on most areas of my face. Slightly less effective on tougher areas like under the chin and where the neckline starts but, ease of use and long battery life (3 uses before I decided to charge) make it a winner. I gave 4 stars due to it not including an adapter for charging.

reviews.title: A good effort....
reviews.text: Let me first say that I know that no electric can come close to a razor blade shave. But this one seemed to not be even trying. I received the razor 5 days ago and tried it out immediately on my 2 day scruff. It seemed to cut right through it no problem but never seemed to get everything or get close to the skin. So I shaved again the next day and it seemed to be better but again, never close to the skin and still missing some spots even though I went over them multiple times. So I thought, maybe I have to use this wet. This morning I used it in the shower and it was better but never could get my neck well and it tore up a good portion of the neck. I spent 15 minutes trying to get everything but couldn't so I went back to my bladed razor and finished. I purchased this to save time and it's actually worse/slower than just using a regular razor. I've returned it this morning. My 15yo dull Norelco does a better job than this one. I'm not exaggerating. You get what you pay for. Side note...when it comes time to replace either the foil or the blades...as stated in the English-is-definitely-not-a first-language instruction manual, there is no place to get them. Not sure if one size foil/blades fits all but...be aware of this.

reviews.title: Very nice quality.
reviews.text:
I was pleasantly surprised to find that this eyeglass case was very good quality and feels durable. The bottom is made with dark brown leather, while the inside has a very nice baby pink, soft, fuzzy lining like most eye glass cases while the whole case itself feels very study and like it would last a long time. The top part is fuzzy with the ears sticking up, just like pictured.

Opening and closing the case is a little on the stiffer side; definitely not the worst I’ve ever had but it’s probably because the hinges are new, over time they may loosen up a bit. In the meantime, simply use a bit of caution with where you place your fingers when closing the case.

Overall I am very happy with this purchase and it was well worth the wait of shipping from Japan. This is an adorable eyeglass case that is well made with good quality materials.

reviews.title: Helps with comfort and may save a pair of shoes you had thought of throwing away
reviews.text: I started off by putting all four pieces in a pair of black pumps and these made it hard for me to fit my feet in the shoes comfortably (the shoes were kind of tight to begin with). Truthfully, I don't really feel like I need the heel pieces. However, I really love the part that goes under the front of my foot. It adds a cushion and it has a ridge to prevent my feet from sliding to the tip of the shoe (and, thereby, help prevent my toes from getting crowded in the very tip of my pumps). I had another pair of shoes that are heels and open-toed sandals that had given me blisters on my pinky toes because my feet kept sliding forward and rubbing on the sandal band (that crosses over the toes). I put the pieces of the kit that go under the front part of my feet and it did feel like it helped keep my feet from sliding forward so much---so now I don't feel like I have to throw these shoes away after all (although I'll still have to try wearing them for an entire day and see how they fare, but I have hope). The other good thing about this kit is that the backs of the pieces are sticky so the pieces stay in place, but it's not too sticky, so I can remove the pieces and put them in other shoes. I did receive this kit at a discount in return for my honest review, which I have provided.

reviews.text:
Love these! There are two pieces for each shoe- toe & heel. I first put them both in my "everyday heels" but it made the shoe hard to get into (though leaving just the heel part I was easily able to get into them) so I then put them into a pair or heels I had to have because they were so cute but they didn't have my size so I got 1/2 size up. Typically when I wear these heels I get the blister on my heel and my foot slides around but the pads made them just snug enough that I barely slide in them and the heel is covered and no more blister! There is a puffed out part on the top of the heel piece so they don't have to stuck out of the top to get the coverage you need and where the heel part also goes under your foot too it doesn't move and shift around. My super cute some times heels just turned into my all the time "everyday heels"! The toe piece feels nice too but for me was more of a space filler, I don't tend to have problems on the bottoms, was comfy to walk on though.

I will definitely be buying these again when these ones get worn out or if I find another pair that don't fit quite right! The shoe store just got much more exciting! I did get a discount on these to provide my honest feedback and that is what I have done here.

reviews.title: Happier Feet After a Day in Heals
reviews.text:
I am not an everyday heel wearer but I do love wearing heels when the opportunity arrives. The problem is that my feet usually hurt after wearing them for a long time or I get blisters because I do not wear them all the time. I have used other products in the past but they always end up moving or not lasting so I have been looking for a long lasting solution. This is a heal kit that includes a toe cushion and a blister protector.

Pros:
-Thick pads
-Toe pads have a ridge for fitting
-Blister pad is thick and cover the whole shoe edge
-Very sticky backs
-Don't move once in place

Cons:
-A bit difficult to get into place
-Blister pad pushes foot slightly forward

These pads are thicker and have a more satin finish than others I have tried and that makes them more comfortable to wear. They have very sticky backs which is good for staying power but does make it a little bit difficult to get into place. The toe cushion with the ridge makes wearing the highest of heals comfortable. The blister cushion which is comfortable to wear and does work to prevent blisters after a long day of wearing your shoes, however the cushion pad does push your foot a bit forward so if your shoes are already tight these may not work. My feet are happier after wearing my heels with the pads in them.

I received this heal kit at a discount for my honest and unbiased review and opinion. Opinions expressed are mine and mine alone and may differ form yours.

Comes in a great neutral color and baggie that both my husband and I like. If I were to critique anything - I did have a previous sleep mask also with deep eye pockets like this, however the material was more plush than this mask, with longer fibers, and I do miss that super soft plush feel on my face. reviews.title: Excellent four piece gua sha set. Good quality aventurine/jade. Great value/bargain.
reviews.text:
This is a very impressive collection of four different shaped gua sha. They are crafted from quality aventurine/jade, not resin. One has to be careful, because there are resin sets that look very similar to jade, but has a plastic feel. So, if you want real aventurine/jade gua sha massage tools, this is the set to consider.
The four aventurine/jade pieces are color matched, creating a cohesive collection. They have a general green background, with splotches of lighter and darker greens interspersed within. Attached are photos to show real world images, with a ruler for size reference. You can see the consistent coloration of the set.
The jade is not overly polished, retaining some of that natural, raw feel. It is polished enough that the surfaces are adequately smooth. Inspection of each gua sha found no defects or flaws, no scratches or nicks.
If you collect gua sha massage tools, you'll be happy to include these in your collection. Also, the comely presentation makes this a very worthwhile gifting option.
At the current cost of $14.68, this is an excellent value/bargain. That would be $3.67 for each of the gua sha. That's an amazing bargain. Especially considering that it's aventurine/jade, and not resin or some other synthetic substitute.
Considering the quality of the gua sha massage tools and the incredible value, this product set deserves a 4.75 - 5 star rating, with a very high level recommendation.

reviews.title: No support for head/misleading shipping & return info
reviews.text:
I was so excited to receive this Cooling Pillow after reading about it. However, it only took a few minutes to realize that there is literally NO SUPPORT for your neck and head with this pillow. Your head will sink right to the bed level. If you're a side sleeper, the same thing will happen and the end of the pillow will fluff up covering your face. I fought much of the night to use this item before I gave up with a raging neck and headache from lack of support. This company really needs to indicate the level of firmness of the pillows they're selling. The cooling concept is good but the rest of the story is not so good.
OK - it's then obvious I need to return this item so I start the process only to find out they charge $20.00 more on Amazon versus their website sales for the same exact pillow but offer Free Shipping on Amazon. That might be OK if you're happy with the item and want to keep it. But now it's time to return it. I have to pay return shipping when I feel they didn't adequately describe the pillow i.e. no reference to firmness and support, so return shipping should be on their shoulders. So I pay the return shipping and when I receive the refund, they've deducted $13.58 for their cost to ship it to me in the first place. BUT IT WAS FREE SHIPPING!!!! No where in the item description did it say if I returned it they'd deduct the free shipping! That's like saying "I'm giving you an imaginary $20 bill but if you decide to return it I want a REAL $20 bill!"
I'm just totally not happy with the company policies on this item. (Or perhaps I'm just being like my user name - a seahag.) It's such a simple fix, too. Add a level of firmness to the description. Be honest and up front in the return policy on the Amazon website description that shipping will be deducted if returned. Yup, you write it in the paper that accompanies the merchandise but not on Amazon where it can be seen BEFORE we push the Purchase button. It's too late once we receive the merchandise and then read the paper enclosed. Very MISLEADING!
Buyer Beware.

I suffer from overheating at night where I come in contact with my pillow, which results in waking with a headache on the surface in contact with my pillow. This results in having to toss and turn all night. The idea of the pillow was to keep my head cool.

The pillow is cool when you first lay down (good). Over a period of half an hour it warms up quickly as it draws the heat from your head. Then it releases the heat back to you and I wake up at the same intervals as before having to turn the pillow over to get a cool surface again. (bad.)

Would I recommend this pillow to others? It is a comfortable pillow which holds its shape nicely, but if you suffer as I do, this pillow does not help and I do not recommend it for relief of overheating headaches.

Thumbs up for comfort. Thumbs down for cooling.

reviews.text: This product will do a gentle cleaning of silver coins with a short dip. Used by many coin collectors, although most will not admit it.

reviews.title: Be careful, once contaminated will ruin other coins
reviews.text:
I'm not sure which coin I cleaned that contaminated by jar (probably a really dirty penny - actual dirt rather than tone) but after that the silver coins I cleaned started getting brown spots after several days. Its also important to thoroughly rinse the coin in running water after dipping (don't just dip it in water) then dip it in deionized water and let it dry. I want to find some kind of holder I can snap a coin into then dip so that when drying neither side is actually touching anything. Paper towels are rough and can scratch proof coins' mirrored fields. If you have a lot of coins to clean or even just a few very valuable coins I suggest getting the gallon sized container so that you can use new cleaner for each coin and aren't risking contamination. Use gloves and be sure to tightly close the jar. When left in my hot car it leaked even though the jar remained upright and crystals formed all around the lid (maybe that's what ruined my jar rather than contamination?).

When in doubt, don't clean your coin, let the pros at PCGS/ANACS/NGC/IGC do the conservation work.

Update June 2021: I realized that my first review was given after not completely following instructions. Instructions say to first clean the coin with a mild soap solution. When doing this I got really excellent results. It will remove more than surface dirt, although best used on a coin that is in F or better condition. Changed to a 5 star rating and highly recommend it! (comment about packaging still applies)

This pretty much does what it is advertised to do. It removes some dirt and tarnish from coins without really doing the type of deep cleaning that would lessen their value. Be aware that this means it will not remove much more than surface dirt and blemishes and this somewhat weakly. Don't expect it to change a dark coin to have luster. It is also pretty pricey. So if you are an experienced coin collector it is a good thing to have. If you just want to really deep clean coins and don't care too much about their subsequent valuation by a numismatist, baking soda cleans much better for a lot less money.
Beware! This is a liquid that for some reason was packaged in a jar rather than a bottle. When I opened it I got spills all over the table it was on.

The jar will last forever. You just dip your toothbrush in, you only need a little.
Makes your teeth feel clean.
Supposedly the clay freshens breath too, I'm not sure. I'll ask my husband sometime.

Cons:
You look terrifying while using it. It scares children (I've tested this with my son). Maybe this could be considered a pro, I'll let you decide.
You'll be rinsing charcoal bits from your mouth for awhile after using it.
It's a little messy, make sure you get super close to the sink before spitting and rinse it right away.

Will I buy it again? Yep.

reviews.title: Must have for an emergency, especially with kids!
reviews.text:
I camp a lot and there are times when the bathroom facilities are quite a ways away. Instead of walking (or riding a bike) in the middle of the night just so I am totally awake by the time I get back to camp, I set this up in the corner. Easy, secure, it snaps onto any 5 gallon bucket. The lid is a really nice touch.
This is especially useful if you have little ones that just can't quite make it to the bathroom. It is low enough for them to comfortably sit. I also purchased the sanitation bags. Clean up couldn't be easier. Twist, tie, toss.
The seat stores well since it's pretty flat. It slides in nicely behind the truck (or car)seat. I would definitely recommend this product for anyone going camping that does not have a self-contained trailer or motor home.

reviews.title: I bought this Toilet Seat to be the lid for ...
reviews.text: I bought this Toilet Seat to be the lid for my emergency kit which I am keeping in a 5 gallon bucket. The toilet seat does fit securely onto the bucket, however, the lid does not stay securely closed. If the bucket were tipped over, which is likely considering the hecticness associated with natural disasters, the lid would definitely come open and the contents of the emergency kit would spill out. I resulted to using a normal lid for my 5 gallon bucket/emergency kit to keep it closed, and put this toilet seat in my closet in case I go camping or tailgating. To be fair, I have not used this product to actually use the bathroom. I gave I 2 stars simply because it wouldn't stay shut.

reviews.title: Don't buy a bucket before this arrives
reviews.text: It is what it is - a toilet seat you put on a bucket to make a camp toilet. They claim it will fit on any 3 to 6 gallon bucket, which is true, more or less. It doesn't fit tightly - or securely - on a "pickle bucket" I got from a fast food place; but it does work. I advise you get this first, then find a bucket at Lowe's Hardware or Home Depot that it will securely snap onto, and buy that. I weigh around 230 to 240 pounds, a friend who also tried it out weighs around 300 pounds; it is comfortable to use and sturdy enough to support either of us. I like having it for those late night or early morning "calls of nature", so I don't have to go out in the dark to find either a bathroom or a safe spot to go. I'm in the process of setting up a "permanent" campsite, and this will be part of the gear I use there, for inclimate weather and such. You can buy those bags that gell the waste, or use small trash bags, or just put a layer of cheap kitty litter in the bottom and add more after each go - any of those options or a mix of them will help control odors and make cleaning it out easier. A mix of sawdust, kitty litter and baking soda works too, absorbing liquids and smells. For the price, it's fine.

reviews.title: like a glove
reviews.text:
fairly well made, the stitching is even, the french turn panels are evenly matched for size/alignment. it
holds the pad very securely by the corners / edges. the covers are a bit larger than the plastic "bracket" holder, so it should provide some protection if dropped. it doesn't have any clips that cover up the corner display info (e.g. battery / clock) like a generic pad holder.

it has dedicated openings for the mic, headphones, camera, speakers power & volume. you'd probably have to remove it from the tray to access the memory card/sim. the four slots for angle viewing work well in my lap, as well as on a table. the open on / close off feature works correctly (hidden magnet). it's fairly attractive, but it certainly isn't leather, it's a polyurethane leatherette cover material. the elastic pen loop is too small for a sharpie, but works fine for a bic size pen, probably would be too large for a stylus, but I don't have one to check. the front pocket would work fine for $$ or some papers - nothing too bulky - although I could slide my phone about half way in, i think the pocket might stretch out if frequently used for that purpose. there is not an inside pocket. it has a couple of edge magnets to help closure, they're strong enough to support the weight of the cover when flipped over, so it probably wouldn't fly open if it was dropped (at least until it hit the ground) - note to self: let someone else verify this feature

overall it's pretty attractive, fits nicely and should hold up for a while. I bought 3 others along with it (thx Amazon return policy), I liked the feel & look of this one over the others.

Purilens is now the only preservative free contact saline on the market. Yes it is part of a cleaning system, but that system works with this saline. You do NOT have to use their cleaning system to use just the saline.
With Simply Saline & Unisol off the market, with NO notification to the public, this is all that's left for the ones of us who are allergic to preservatives.
The down fall is once opened, you MUST use the bottle up in 15 days or throw it away, hence my 4 stars. I wear daily disposable contacts but like to add a drop of saline to buffer my eyes, though I can insert without, I prefer the added comfort.
I have tried Clear Care Rinse & Go , which has very little preservatives in it, but my eyes goop up almost immediately. So Purilens is all that's left for me.

I didn't expect to look like I'm 25 or get carded for a bottle of wine at 37.

I originally didn't plan on writing this review until I was 50. By that time, I reasoned, there could be no ambiguity between my chronological age & my apparent age; some 40 years olds might pass for 25, but no 50 year old could. I still intend to update this review when/if I do reach that age, but I feel compelled to write something here. Some who read this may not be alive by the time I am 50. reviews.title: Something works, I woke up pain-free for the first time in over a year
reviews.text:
Got a free pair of the low intensity rings (not neodymium) over 10 years ago. I was pretty sure he was a scam artist, but just wanted to get my free rings. When they didn't arrive quickly, I fired off an email to him complaining. To my surprise, the rings really did come a little while later after a nice apology from Alex.

I didn't notice much out of the free rings, but I did notice a little something and since he had instructions on how to build your OWN rings right on his website, I decided to do a little test. Still skeptical and not wanting to give a scammer any of my money, I found a website which sold neodymium magnets in the range his website suggested and created 2 rings according to his instructions, with a compass to determine which side should face up. Once I had it all figured out, I wrote a big R on one ring to indicate it should be worn on my Right pinky and an L on the other to indicate it should be worn on the left just to make sure I always wore the rings correctly.

I wore the rings a couple times back then but noticed they gave me really bizarre energy spikes and seemed to almost give me anxiety or something. I was in my late 20s or early 30s and I was just worried they were doing something unhealthy, so I stopped using them and wrote Alex off as a quack.

Fast forward to last night. I am now almost 42 and I have had increasing pains in my legs, joints and especially problems with my feet. It's really weird when you start developing pain for apparently no reason. I have to make an appointment with the doctor soon, but at first I attributed the pains to low magnesium, ill-fitting shoes, and straining my body with starting a new yoga and walking routine too forcefully. However, the more time that has gone by (over a year now), I began to suspect it's some underlying health issue, which is why I need to see the doctor for a complete checkup again.

For the past year, I have had what I believe is plantar fasciitis. The yoga helped for over a year until I sprained my big toe and had to stop. Still, when I would wake up in the morning, my heel and hamstring were tight and sore and required stretching, which is the basic symptom of plantar fasciitis. The bottoms of my feet begin to hurt if I stand too long or walk too much. My ankles and knees also hurt if I exert myself too much running. My lower back often is a bit sore because I have swayback and if I do not do abdominal exercise regularly, it starts to LOOK like swayback and also gets sore. Again, the yoga greatly fixed this problem: I had a straighter stance without belly tipping forward and butt sticking out (makes you look 20 pounds lighter and about 2 inches taller) and this also meant I had no pain in my lower back, not even if I slept too long on a bad mattress. Yoga was the answer to most of my prayers until I had to stop doing it. I am very much looking forward to the day my toe heals up so I can begin again!

ANYWAY, with all these pains increasing and not being able to do yoga or run, I bought night splints to stretch out my feet while I sleep so that hopefully my plantar fasciitis will be healed eventually. And I bought several supplements which I have been taking for over 6 months now trying to address any deficiencies which may be the cause of this apparent degeneration. Nothing has really helped much as far as I can tell.

LAST NIGHT, on a whim, I got up from the couch and found my homemade "Alex Chiu" neodymium rings and put them on before I went to sleep. I did not put on my night splint for plantar fasciitis. I woke up today with no pain in my feet or back and feeling well-rested after just 5 hours of sleep. I went back to bed for another 3 hours, which borders on too much sleep for me (especially after doing nothing but lay on the couch the previous evening) and still woke up with no lower back pain.

I have no idea what the rings did, but it is obvious they did something. My guess is they improved circulation which may have in turn moved something carried in the blood that may settle in the extremities of legs and feet, but that doesn't explain why my lower back doesn't hurt.

I can honestly say that I wish I had worn these rings when I first made them now. I will definitely be wearing them every night for the foreseeable future and if anything interesting happens, I will update this review.

These are homemade rings, but if I feel they really start to improve my health, I might just buy the very expensive (and most powerful) foot bar magnets as a way to say thank you to Alex. He certainly has received a lot of negative attention for his website and I was one of the people who made fun of the site back then, too. I got a free pair of rings from him, learned how to make my own, and never gave him a penny or even thanked him. Instead, I continued to joke about the website with people online until I forgot about it. Now I feel like a complete jerk because there is no way my pain-free body is a result of anything but these rings. I have woken up daily with these pains for over a year now, there is simply not a day that I get out of bed and don't stumble immediately to the wall to stretch out my hamstrings due to pain. Today I did not. Last night I wore the rings. End of story.

reviews.title: Wore them for 18 months, no results
reviews.text:
Let's face it, these rings probably don't do anything. Most likely any benefits gained from these rings is a result of a placebo effect. In any case there's no way to prove it one way or the other. I've worn them for a month and haven't noticed anything but I'll give them at least a year until I dismiss them completely.

One big problem with these rings is that they are very uncomfortable to wear, the plastic is very hard and pointy. And there have been several nights where they've fallen off, or where my hands have gotten too close and the rings have stuck to each other. I'm going to make a finger sleeve soon, hopefully that helps with the comfort problem.

EDIT: I purchased these rings in October 2011 and I have stopped wearing them as of March 2013 because it is clear they don't work. I wanted to believe these rings worked as all of us do but from my experience it is as I expected, they don't do anything.

I've been balding for the past 3 years and I am considerably more bald than I was when I started wearing the rings. I've seen no increase in healing, in fact I developed a RSI injury in my wrists 9 months ago and the rings had no effect in preventing/healing it.

I still think these rings can make you feel better about yourself and even improve health through the powerful placebo effect. But any benefits from these rings are most certainly the product of your mind and attitude and not the result of any real physical effect the rings are having on your body. However if these rings help you feel better about yourself because they make you feel you are giving yourself a shot at staying young or healthy then by all means wear them. It's your attitude that can in turn cause real physical improvements. It doesn't matter that the rings themselves don't actually do anything.

I had a few sleep issues, the one bothering me the most was waking up with my ring and small fingers numb on both arms (due to some vertebrae problem). After four nights of wearing these, the numbness issue went away. It is now many months later and the issues have not returned. I still have my other sleep issues, but I'm happy that one went away. Only problem I have with these is that they either may come loose at night and fall off, or less often may tighten and I wake up with a finger numb from lack of blood flow. To be fair, I can't scientifically say that these indeed fixed the issue with the numbness, but the problem had occurred for several months before trying the rings, and has been gone ever since that fourth day of wearing them. Still debating the other set for feet.

reviews.title: It works but somewhat roughly made
reviews.text: Wow, I can't believe Alex is selling the rings on Amazon as well. FYI, I am his high school friend and who helped him design the instruction manual in the early stage of his business. In fact, I was wearing the rings as shown in the demo pictures. I am the person who actually partially influenced him to research on magnetic therapy. Back in 1991, I told Alex that that I received magnetic therapy on my earlobe for helping to improve my vision. He then started reading books on his own and doing all those experiments at home. He did not go to colleage, but like to do try things on his own. I think most people owe Alex an open mind to give it a try, just as Hillary said about Trump. I am not a Trump supporter though. Anyway, I think the rings will make you speed up metabolism, but it is somewhat roughly made. If he gets some big investors involved such as those in the Shark Tank show, they may be able to help him to improve the design and make it more comfortable to wear. Of couse, they may just laugh him off the show, if he even made to that show. I found it make me difficult to fall asleep, so I don't wear them, as I have to work M-F, unlike Alex he who usually gets up at 1 pm and live on his own schedule. To sum up, the rings do work somehow, and a few people may feel no effect, and I believe most do. If it is comfortable to wear, I would give it 5 star rating. Cheers!

reviews.title: Very very nice cable!
reviews.text:
I'm always hooking up something new on my home network it seems, or moving something around, and I don't enjoy making my own cables. I end up buying a lot of patch cables. I stumbled across these and figured I would give it a try, initially for the flatness aspect. I have another flat ethernet cable from who knows where that I got years ago and I liked it, so I thought I'd try these.

Granted, for home use, a Cat8 cable is completely insane overkill. I won't have 40Gb network infrastructure probably ever. So what?

First impressions - it looks great. Stark white cable with blue/turquoise ends. Solidly done strain relief. It comes neatly coiled in a resealable baggie. Once out of the package, it is surprisingly flexible. When I saw photos of all the shielding inside the cable, I thought it would be quite stiff, but it is not. The cable jacket feels almost richly smooth, if that makes any sense. Unexpected but nice.

The cable does ship with plastic protectors covering the ends, which I didn't realize at first as I was installing one in a dimly lit location. I was initially confused why it wouldn't plug into my pfSense box, but then I looked closer with a flashlight and realized my mistake.

I can't say I've noticed a network speed improvement or not, as nothing on my network is faster than gigabit.

If these people ever make a 1-foot version, I'll probably buy a bunch and swap out the old Cat5 cables I have between my patch panel and my network switch, as those have been in my basement for several years and I've had a couple get flaky on me.

reviews.title: Works just fine to replace O.E. 3-cell battery if you have a PCIe SSD instead of usual SSD drive.
reviews.text: I think the seller could have included a slim plastic tongue depressor for separating the bottom cover from the upper body of the Dell laptop. You do not want to use a sharp, metal probe to free the cover from the sides of the upper body because you could cut some of the delicate circuit wiring inside. Also, you can almost double the run time of the O.E. 3-cell battery with a 4-cell as listed; it would also be nice if the seller would include a small set of laptop internal screws such as the M2x5 screw needed to more securely attach the new higher capacity 4-cell battery's upper right corner. Be advised that the dead center bottom cover screw doubles as a grounding screw, so to avoid getting a NO BATTERY message like I did upon non-screwed reassembly of bottom cover and upper body, make sure all screws are snug tight before powering on. Old, O.E. 3-cell was only getting 6 hours of run-time, while this new 4-cell battery looks like it is going to get some 13 hours of run-time. Very pleased, but downgraded product one star for lack of a useful plastic separation tool and a screw that costs 2 cents to put into box. Used Voltaren dosage ruler to separate halves of laptop.

reviews.text:
These headphones are very good. Some of the previous headphones I've used include the Apple In-Ear with 3-button mic (not the ones that come with your iPhone, the $80 dual-armature ones), and Klipsch S4i.

These sound very similar to the Klipsch S4i but have a better in-ear feel as well as amazing materials. The metal and wood casing really seals the deal for me. They are very clear, a tad bass-heavy (yet still punchy, not muddy), and do well with the midrange and highs. The tangle-free cord works and feels like an article of clothing, not a piece of electronics.

The casual listener will be blown away, and the audiophile will not find in-ear headphones in the price category that beat these.

I should say right away that I am an average consumer and cannot got into the details that some other reviewers will so I will say what I think with limited knowledge of sound technology.

Build:
The earbuds feel expensive and solid. Aluminum and wood along with cable covered in cloth create a premium feel. Speaking of cable- no matter how I shove them in my pocket the cable refuses to tangle and it never takes more than 2-3 seconds to fully stretch it. 90 degree audio jack means earbuds when plugged in take less space in your pocket which is great. The remote is good with mic button being ease to locate even though volume control buttons feel little cheap. My only real negative comment can be made to remote placement. It is located at the point where two ear cables meet and in winter when you zip your coat over the earbud cable the remote ends up on the chest level under the coat. Thus when you need to change the song or talk to a person using a mic you need to unzip a coat third way down. I wish the placement was like in Apple's earbud close to one of the buds.

Sound:
As I said I am not a pro but I would say the sound is a big step up from Apple standard buds. You can hear more instruments and more words in the songs and overall it creates more feeling of immersion.

Fit:
I had no problem fitting the earbuds using the smallest tips but I have more or less standard ears in general. Since the buds go in the ear you have to be careful walking on the streets since it passively isolates all the sounds around you.

Verdict:
I got it on sale on Amazon and I think they worth every penny. I am sure that some earbuds for $200-400 bucks may sound better but they usually lack utility (tangle free cable, comfortable mic) of the lower-end headphones. These are perfect for casually enjoying music during commute or watching a movie in flight.

reviews.title: I love this thing
reviews.text:
I love this thing!!!
What a time saver!!! No more DVDs for me...
They could improve the joystick on this thing, but I take a horrible joystick over burning and carrying CD/DVDs any day of the week!!!
You need to put your ISOs inside a folder called _ISO or _iso , and inside that folder, you can create sub-folders to organize your stuff...
It also can emulate external HDs and Thumb drives (writable or read-only)... Which is great for keeping your stuff safe on unknown system (if you write protect it).
And if you like to integrate all windows updates to your installation disk, you can use the virtual thumb drive instead of creating ISOs, that way, you can always change something later on, without having to recreate the whole thing... (I personally use NTLite and WinReducereX, they both do basically the same thing, but sometimes one is better than the other, depending on the version... So if it doesn't work on one, try the other...)
I hope this helps...

Some tips:
# Use a SSD instead of a regular HD (the Samsung 850 evo up to 500GB is perfect (it uses very little power, one of the lowest on the market) (the 1TB uses way more power... Stay with 500GB or less... You can Google "samsung 850 evo power consumption" and look at the anandtech site for the power consumption compassion of many models and sizes)
# Format your drive as NTFS (the only compatible with the VHD_Tool++.exe that you download from their site)
# Use VHD_Tool++.exe to create VHD files with the size you want the virtual HD to be;
# f you want it to be a virtual thumb drive, rename the VHD file to RMD (virtual Thumb Drive);
# You can also add &D and &DW to the name of the files to force a behavior;
VHD and RMD modes based on the name of the file: (I used VHD as the extension, but it works the same way for RMD)

NAME.VHD = CD-MODE (it will mount you virtual HD or thumb drive only)
NAME&D.VHD = DUAL-MODE (it will mount your virtual HD and the real HD, but the real will be read-only)
NAME&DW.VHD = DUAL-MORE (same as above but the real HD is writable)
# Create a folder structure that makes since for you... i.e:
_ISO\ISOs\Windows Install\Win 7
_ISO\ISOs\Windows Install\Win 10
_ISO\ISOs\Tools\Some recovery iso (whatever tools you use...)
_ISO\ISOs\Live Images\Ubuntu.iso
_ISO\VHDs\virtual drive you use to backup you friend's file before you do a clean install.VHD
_ISO\RMDs\virtual thumb drive you keep you windows installation disk updated (using NTLite).RMD

reviews.title: A microcontroller case with multiple device emulation features and state memory, switch and backlit LCD panel, USB 3.0
reviews.text: A nice usb attached file based cd/dvd-rom emulator. It let's you "emulate" a real physical cd/dvd (read-only) optical disk drive. The case has a small electronics section with a multi-line backlit LCD panel that produces pixelated symbols, graphics and text. The "jog switch" on the Left side of the unit allows thumb control up, down, and momentary press into the body of the device. The "jog switch" allows scrolling through a two line text menu which displays wrapped text if items have labels that are too long. Then pressing in on the "jog switch" selects the item. - The device arrives without a hard drive, it will take a spinning drive, or an ssd. The software requires the drive be formatted as a "simple" MBR volume, and not a GPT volume. Once the volume type is chosen, the drive can be divided into partitions and formatted with a file system. The enclosure electronics only support NTFS and FAT file systems. The device can function (both) as a USB hard disk, and as a USB CD/DVD-rom drive "simultaneously" or as one or the other (HDD or CD/DVD) "exclusively". Once the drive is formatted creating a folder called _iso and putting iso files into the folder activates the ability to "mount" the iso files in emulation mode. The first time after the _iso directory is created the device must be unplugged and replugged in, so that the device sees the _iso folder and starts in "dual HDD and CD/DVD-rom emulation mode". Once in dual mode the LCD screen lists the iso files it can see in the _iso folder. Scrolling up and down the list with the "jog switch" then selecting one by pressing into the body of the device with the jog switch.. automatically mounts the selected iso file and exposes the file as virtual CD/DVD physical media to the computer. In dual mode, the computer "lists" a USB hard drive and a virtual USB CD/DVD drive (empty), pressing the jog switch to "mount" an iso file is reflected on the computer as "actively inserting a CD/DVD" physical media piece into the virtual drive, and will activate Autoplay. Pressing again on the jog switch emulates "actively ejecting a CD/DVD" physical media piece from the virtual drive. The Last virtual CD/DVD "mounted" is remembered when the device is unplugged and plugged back into the computer.. this is called "saving".. which means "save the current state of the device to memory".. so that when it starts again.. it immediately mounts and exports the iso file as a "filled CD/DVD virtual device" with bootable media already in its slot. The silver switch on top of the device is called the "Backup" button.. which means.. "backup the current state of the device to the device memory, before unplugging it" in my experience it remembers state without doing this.. but if you do press the Silver top button and hold it down long enough the LCD displays "Data Saving..." as a confirmation. Microsoft VHD and RMD read/write formats are also supported, but I have not tried those. WindowsToGo is supposed to be supported but I have not tried that yet. A virtual CD/DVD-R burn function to allow a computer to burn virtual media would be helpful, but the current software does not emulate read/write media that looks like a piece of CD-R or DVD-R media. It comes with a black neoprene carry case wrapped in black fabric. It also comes a white USB cable that is 3 feet long, has a USB 3.0 micro-B style end (not a type C) [this is the split, dual sided connector that looks sort of like a mini-SATA connector] that plugs into the top of the device and a normal size type A connector on the opposing end to plug into a computer. The internal drive connector is a normal SATA drive style connector with power and signal sides. The case does not have a facility for mounting the drive, the drive is plugged in and shoved into the case and held in place by friction and a landing zone at the bottom made of plastic that works to center the drive in the case. The case display and electronics are bolted into position by "peeling" the flexible top of the rubber strips on eithr side away from the grooves to get access to screw holes in the side of the case. The electronics package with the drive attached is shoved into the case until the copper accented holes of the electronics packages line up with the holes in the case. A minature screw driver 1 inch long and four tiny screws are provided.. however you only need two to secure the drive electronics to the sides of the case.. and by association, with the entering plastic base inside the case for the user supplied SSD or spinning drive.. the drive is also secured. The rubber strips are then "pressed" back into the sides to cover up the screw access holes used to secure the electronics package. Because the ends of the rubber strips are narrower than the main body of the rubber strips they flex underneath the groove edges and smooth out of their own accord. Advanced menus contain a LCD panel brightness, USB volt meter, Drive model and serial number and manual mode control. Some antivirus suites will (hide) the HDD by default, and it must be manually forced (online) from the Windows Computer Management > Disk Management - control panel component, by right clicking the Left drive grey control box and clicking on (Online) to bring it online and automatically assign it a drive letter. Hot swap and possible data corruption depending on the Operating System handling of USB devices is still a problem enforced by the Operating System behavior. The enclosure Advanced menus do provide features to manually Safely disconnect.. but mostly it just seems to work. The GPT volume limitation, and requirement for MBR volumes only.. means 2 TB is the (limit) to the supported drive size in this device, anything larger will be be unreachable outside of the first 2 TB of drive space. This drive model is not encrypted, data is breachable if lost. A different model supports on the fly drive encryption.

reviews.title: Convenient but not necessarily fast
reviews.text:
I used to carry a full key ring of six DTSE9 flash drives plus two Sandisk Extremes, and even then I didn't always have the bootable disc I needed. I was constantly reformatting and Rufus-ing the drives and it sucked. This enclosure has replaced all of my flash drives and is much more convenient. The build quality is solid. The menu is easy to understand. I like that you can save the currently loaded iso so that you don't have to frantically try to find the right one while the computer is booting. The company seems legit. They release firmware updates somewhat regularly and replied to my email within one day.

The only downside to this enclosure is that it will bottleneck a fast SSD. It uses SATAII internally which has a real-world max throughput of about 250MB/s. Mechanical hard drives are too slow to be affected by this limit whatsoever, but a good SSD will have its sequential read/write speeds cut in half running in this enclosure. Is it faster than an optical drive? Much much faster. Is it faster than my trusty DTSE9's? Hell yes. Is it faster than a Sandisk Extreme? Barely. Am I going to deduct a star? Nope. Mea culpa for not reading the fine print on their website. It's a bummer that it has the internal SATAII bottleneck but ultimately I bought it for convenience, not speed. And realistically most I/Os are random anyway which means that for real-world use there is probably not as much of a bottleneck as the benchmarks would suggest. This is also why I would still recommend putting an SSD into the enclosure even with the SATAII connection... SSDs have much faster random performance than mechanical drives so you still see a definite benefit.

Bottom line is that it's a great product, just don't expect it to put up any big bragging numbers on the benchmark.

reviews.title: Absolutely essential for any ststem builder/maintainer.
reviews.text:
Indispensable. Lots of information on potential use cases available on the internet, which if you're looking at this you may have already reviewed. Some caveats:

1. Using the jog dial and entering a menu, much less changing a setting, while the drive is being transferred to/from will drop the transfer speed momentarily.
2. If the jog dial fails, you lose any functionality that differentiates this from a regular USB SATA enclosure. Not a modular or replaceable component, and one that is almost guaranteed to fail sooner or later. No problems yet, however. Gentle use should prolong its life.
3. Any change in settings will force the drive to dismount from the system without confirmation. Another reason to NOT TOUCH THE DRIVE when an operation is in progress.

reviews.title: Hyper-Functional + Simple Styling
reviews.text: I was looking for an easy, un-cumbersome way to protect + reasonably weather shield my micro 4/3rds and this is it. Easy to attach and disconnect to gear through sturdy loop + clip (the ribbon is silkier/more lightweight though), cover and uncover for less than ideal shooting conditions, or just sling over a neck or shoulder (does not include camera strap). The biggest selling point for me was the minimalist styling (I wanted the Pen to be on display, not the case) and light weight. I switched from DSLRs with hefty cases and was done with the neck strain. Easy to use as a protective case for air travel, collapses small enough for a pocket if you want to ditch it mid-shoot, and I could see it easily fitting several configurations. My Olympus + 25MM does just fine, with a little wiggle room if needed for a bigger body/larger lens. Scuba-like material seems reasonably waterproof, but there are minor gaps at the closure. Hefty Velcro has n e v e r accidentally come undone.

reviews.title: Extended to garage 150ft away
reviews.text: Works great. I can use my laptop in the garage and more importantly my wireless outlet controller to turn on my engine block heater for my truck. Some people have issues with the setup. What the fail to understand is you need the units on the same electrical phase. In the USA you have two 110V phases coming into the house, combined it 220V. So the signal needs to be on the same phase. If not then you need a repeater to jump over to the other phase, or simply change out your wiring at the breaker box so both outlets are on the same phase. My remote garage is 150ft away and I have no problems.

reviews.title: Great way to get faster internet across your house
reviews.text:
Due to the layout of our condo, it's really hard to get any wifi signal in the room furthest from the router and there's no way to move the router closer. To address this problem, I had originally purchased a wifi extender before I realized this type of product exists.

I purchased the "wifi" version (TL-WPA7517KIT) and so far I am very happy with it. It only took a couple minutes to install (one unit connects to router, the other goes wherever you want your signal). With the wifi extender, I only got ~5-10 mbps in the "far" room with poor wifi. Now, I'm getting ~80 mbps through both the ethernet connection AND similar speeds on wifi. I synced the connections so this seems to allow some sort of seamless wifi boost throughout our house. I live in a pretty densely packed residential area so even in the room with the router, I typically get ~100 mbps maximum, so the 80 is fantastic.

I may purchase a second "wired add on" for my home office set up, which is in another bedroom and sometimes gets spotty wifi connection due to interference from neighbor wifi signals.

Have used all kinds of routers, repeaters, etc to try to get wireless in a remote room. This adapter set worked perfectly. Unlike many repeaters which use WiFi to obtain an internet connection to amplify, this one uses the second version of Powerline, which is like using an ethernet connection directly to a wireless Access Point. Installation is basically a matter of plugging in two small adapters. It uses mesh-like technology apparently developed by TP-Link.
This thing works, NO slow down in internet speed for your network, can easily integrate with your existing network (and SSID's) automatically to keep you connected to best signal where ever you are in your home..

For me, it functions like an additional mesh point for the far off bedroom over our garage, which I got a strong WiFi signal to using the included Powerline and Wireless adapters. The WiFi adapter operates on both 2.4Ghz and 5 Ghz, which is an important feature. Frankly, I can't believe this works so perfectly!

reviews.title: Take your time, set it up and break it in right...
reviews.text: I have one of these playing in a shallow down-firing sealed box that's too big for it (0.8 cu. ft versus 0.65 recommended), decent amount of polyfill, and I'm running 320W RMS to it on the 5th channel of my Powerbass amp. I tuned the amp with a 60 hz signal tone and a multimeter to make sure I am not sending the sub a clipped signal. The bass is there, but it really comes on strong as I get right at 300W - 320W RMS. The reason I purchased this sub is because it had dual voice coils to go down to 2 ohms and matched the 2 ohm output of the amp's 5th channel perfectly. My previous, less expensive shallow mount sounded just fine, but at 4 ohms it was only getting 250W RMS from the amp - I figured this setup might sound a little bit louder due to more power available, and once I broke it in properly it did just that. This is a great sub for its purpose, if you only want one shallow sub and need to bring the impedance to 2 ohms to get the most from your amp, this is a great buy. Enclosure matters (space = bass), polyfill matters (get a bag from Wal-mart for less than $5, you'll be glad you did), and proper tuning at rated power matters. Very pleased with the amount of bass in my sedan's trunk.

reviews.title: Another Coil Failure
reviews.text:
I know drivers blow on occasion, even when spec'd properly, but there seems to be a trend developing. I built my system based on information off the car forums from others with nearly identical setups. Out of dozens with similar setups it's only those that chose the MB Quart driver that are reporting failures, just weeks after installation. Unfortunately for me these reports didn't start coming in until after I made my purchase. Mine lasted about two weeks. It's a shame, it's a really nice unit; structurally built well, shallow depth, and sounds great- while it works.

I was driving mine with a JL Audio XD300 monoblock, rated at 300W RMS at 2 ohms, which should match up perfectly. I set my input sensitivity with my multimeter following the instructions with the amp. The gain was rarely over about 60%, simply because it overpowered my stereo if it was any louder. I'm not an expert in car stereos, but I'm a mechanical engineer and am quite comfortable around electronics; I don't believe that anything was wrong with my setup.

I replaced it with a Pioneer TS-SW2501. The difference in build quality is startling, the Pioneer is a juggernaut. I really like the MB Quart and maybe I just got a bad apple, but if someone was asking my recommendation for a 10" shallow mount sub I'd say get the Pioneer TS-SW2501. YMMV.

reviews.title: FANTASTIC SOFTBOX.  Saves you money without skimping on quality!
reviews.text:
I paid a small fortune for a name brand softbox this size. I needed a second one for those rare times when I wanted to have that "feral" catchlight that comes from having two of these as the main light source. It isn't often that I want that look so for those few times I didn't feel like spending top dollar for a second strip softbox. I came here to amazon and found this one. I didn't have illusions that this box would be as good as it's more expensive partner but I was wrong. EVERY BIT AS GOOD -- strong material that doesn't seem like it is going to tear any time soon, inner diffusion panel, outer diffusion panel, AND it comes with an egg crate grid to provide direction (my name brand one didn't have the grid).

This came with a speed ring that doesn't fit my hensel monolights but that's okay because I have other speedrings that I can use and they fit the softbox just fine.

Some folks commented that this is difficult to put together.... I have never met a softbox that is easy to put together nor have I ever met one that comes with instructions. Softbox sellers assume you know how to put them together but if you don't, watch a YouTube video. As for the difficulty putting them together, a lot depends on how strong you are. I'm not all that strong, I usually have an assistant to help with putting softboxes together, AND, I use oven mitts which help with strength and traction. My oven mitts have a grippy surface. If yours don't, ignore the oven mitt suggestion. I rarely dismantle the softboxes.... I do so only when I need to travel with them. If you need to dismantle and reassemble often you might be frustrated by ANY softbox.

BOTTOM LINE: GREAT ALTERNATIVE TO NAME BRANDS..... this is a great softbox at a fraction the cost of their well known twins. You might need to purchase a speedring to work with your particular lights if these bowen mounts don't work for you. I would definitely purchase this brand again if I need another softbox.

I have not had a chance to test it out on a subject but will try to update this review once I have. I gave this softbox 4 stars only because of how difficult it is to put together and that it did not have any instructions. Other than that this is an amazing softbox and worth every penny.

So if you have the room to leave this up permanently and if you have the muscle to get this together I say BUY, BUY, BUY!!!

reviews.title: Lovely Appearance, Performs its Job Well, May Need a Ground Loop Isolator
reviews.text:
I picked up this handy little AUX Switch Box to tidy up my work from home / gaming desk setup and allow me to easily switch between my speakers, headphones, personal computer, and company laptop. The unit does exactly what I wanted it to do, but I did want to confirm that thanks to its simple design you will likely need to add a ground loop isolator ($4-8 ea) for each input beyond your first one.

The 3.5mm jacks feel tight, and paired well with the random assortment of 3.5mm cables I've accumulated over the years. The selector knobs have reasonably positive detents, the aluminum knobs feel nice enough, and the overall package performs nicely. It even looks at home next to my inexpensive Bravo Audi headphone amp.

My only real gripes are the lack of ground loop isolation on the inputs, and the layout of input and output jacks. It would have been a lot tidier if there were two inputs and two outputs on the front and back of the device to keep my back-of-desk arrangement nice and tidy, but I understand that it would have taken more work to get the PCB to layout nicely.

Overall, I'm giving the switch box a 5/5 stars because it does its job, I was aware of the potential flaws with the ground loop isolation, and its affordable as all getout. I could have made something myself, but for this price, why bother?

Pros:
- Inexpensive
- Allows easy switching between inputs AND outputs
- Attractive, minimalist package

Cons:
- Some feedback if there are multiple grounded input devices
- Input/Output jacks leave room for improvement

Neutral:
- You gotta install your own rubber feet

Recommended Improvements:
- Integrate a ground loop isolating transformer if space permits
- Have 2 inputs and 2 outputs on the rear of the switch instead of 4 inputs on the rear, and 4 outputs on the front.

reviews.title: Works perfectly

If I run the source through my JDS lab Objective2 amplifier first before the splitter then run the output as the Klipsch speakers it cleans that noise and makes it dead quiet. For those with persistent noise perhaps a ground noise isolator might help. But it's not a fault of the splitter, it's your source or amplifiers that are the problem.

I've used a few of these fiberglass & acrylic devices and this one is the only that I've seen with 4 inputs and 4 outputs. Upon plugging in the 2nd input device, a buzz was occurring and needed the buzz box to resolve that (~$8/ea). Once those arrived, I was able to route audio between two computers ending at either my desk speakers, or over to my headphones with two clicks of the dial.

Quick info:

Design: no idea why the dials are aligned the way they are, as the dials dont line up with each other. Maybe it's on purpose. Drives the OCD a little bit but does the job.

Build quality: its a PCB and acrylic boards with relatively cheap knobs, but assembled pretty well all things considered. The PCB board is of pretty good quality too

Aesthetics: you either like this sort of "open" design or you don't. I have it sitting next to a legato Wave XLR and StreamDeck which are very tidy and nice looking. With all the wires on the front and back, it's hard to have this just out and about and not want a little place for it. Suffice to say I'm working on a 3D printed enclosure for this thing because it's not the prettiest. But does it's job and does it well.

Very happy with this 3.5mm audio switch. I have been looking off and on for something like this for a long long time. *** Ignore the lint. That's from me handling the item. This device arrived arrive clean. Pristine.

The short of it is: you can select one input from among four sources. Then you select one output from among four possible outputs.

I hooked up three desktop computers as the inputs/audio sources. Then I pluged in two outputs, one is a 2.1 speaker system (probably 10 to 15 watts) and the other, headphones. I cranked up a movie and two youtube music videos on each audio source (desktop computers), with volume maxed. Switching between sources and outputs, there is no crackling, no hissing, no humming, no buzzing. Just no distortion that I could detect. Audio is crisp and clear. So in my case, I do not need a ground loop noise isolator nor ferrite choke snap-on noise isolators (as some commentators have mentioned). But be aware in case you should have hissing/buzzing.

I sticky'ed a two magnets (these ones: "FINDMAG Neodymium Magnet" https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07L48XL2R) to the back of this audio switcher and stuck it to my computer. Still not hearing any interferance. But I wouldn't know if that'd be a thing. It does slide down just a bit, so maybe stronger magents or my computer case is crap metal.

You might notice the rubber feet. They are "grip'y" (but not slimy sticky) to reduce sliding and keep the switcher stationary. But as mentioned I stickied on some magnets for my setup.

I should note, the packaging was very well done (pics). The item was not dented, scratched, nor otherwise damaged.

All in all, am very happy with this purchase. So much so, I stopped everything I was doing just to get this review in with pics and description. Here's to hoping it holds up to the 6 month and 1 year mark.

Bye bye now and happy upcoming St. Patrick's Day

reviews.title: MVP award goes to Theater Solutions 8” slim sub for $150
reviews.text:
Long review, but honest and maybe a tone of disappointment. don’t worry too much about it, life goes on.

I have a complex situation. I’m remodeling a 40 foot coach. As I’m ripping the TVs out, because I’m not into TVs, Amazon threw me a teaser with a little tube amp for hundred &1/2. I thought🤔I like a little nice music, so, I just slapped together a little system for about 500 bucks including $150, 8”inch slim sub for my tight design layout constraints.

It sounded alright; very detailed and warm, great sounding actually but it was lacking in the bass department for sure. Two little matchbox fives and a shoebox 8”?!?!

If i was going to step it I was thinking to go for a Klipsch or a Polk in the 3 to 450 range

I went out on a limb and purchased one of these “chest thumping, room pressurization, bad boys“
Nothing but good reviews, right? Well, except maybe one or two…

I saved about 20% getting a used one expecting a couple scuffs, not a concern since I’ll probably end up throwing some black leather wrapped gold 10 inch drawer pulls on the top as guardrails to keep my ashtray from sliding off as I’m driving down the road plunking this thing right between the drivers and passenger seat! (Who says smokers don’t deserve some nice music, and functionality?)

Well to my surprise and to the compliments of my seller, they upgraded to a brand new unit because they didn’t like the condition it was in upon preparing for shipment. Thank you! (heck, I’ll pay for shipping for the ugly one too if you don’t think U can sell it…maybe that’ll solve my problem…hahahahaha 😳)

Elated!!!! Then and then … the let down.

ZERO chest pounding bass!
ZERO presence, completely dull and flat and still disturbingly subdued at that: trying to pretend to complement a 50watt amp running some $120 moukey’s

I was horrified!!!! And internally saddened because I knew I was asking for 12” power and something that takes up the space of an eight

Don’t get me wrong, I’m not sure if it’s capable of distortion. I did everything I can to make that thing more than waffle in the air silently without a single slap or crackle. But…I’m not sure if it’s capable of much of anything. (In my random systemenvironment configuration?🤷🏾)

Absolutely bewildered by the reviews at this point. I’m pretty sure most everyone is complementing as a replacement of a ported sub with this thing.
My son brought over my 15-year-old KLH he inherited and beat to crap. I can’t say it sounded that great after all these years but it was louder than this “$600 sneaker audiosnob reference material”. It is most certainly not. Not with what I’ve experienced thus far. But then again I probably wouldn’t know anyway I’m just a regular guy. Fooled by big booming 80s music I suppose

Still, moving on. I called SVS direct and they quickly offered a solution of a line driver to boost the signal coming from the single Sub port coming from the dayton reciver. (apparently it happens in certain situations and I must be in one of those situations)

Great, bought a 20 dB booster and waited a week for it to arrive. Hooked it up and I had to double check that I hooked it up! Yes it increased it to about the level of putting the SVS app at 0db. Greatish I can achieved a lukewarm level of volume approaching noticeable without overdriveing the internal SVS amp.(that would destroy the sub per SVS) I’m running out of time to return this thing!!!

And I don’t know what it is….. it’s solid. Think of a hefty toad!. It’s rock friggen solid. I just feel like I can’t unleash the beast that it’s supposedly is. Some fleetwood mac hints strongly at it 😀

Took another risk, purchased a headphone tube amplifier “one little bear“. Another hundred bucks with a couple wires and another week or so waiting.

Meanwhile I’m rationalizing, taking as much blame as possible. I mean, I’m tearing out a dishwasher and a fridge, furnace and a water heater at the same time. I got huge holes in my vessel. I’ve got my little couch turned on end and the built-in cabinet speaker placement it’s not ideal. It’s horrible actually.

So I reposition the satellites into a “docked” configuration, up on the dashboard, presenting basic stage and imagery (helps)

Little bear arrives, along with two kinda wrong cables. I cobble it together fire it up and it’s…improved incrementally. But ultimately, in a single word that might say (your not alone fellas)

”“underwhelmed“”

So Then, Out of desperation, I “Y” in in the Theater solutions eight 😱 😳🤯‼️😮

I couldn’t believe it for the first time there was actually some presence of bass in the room. Some pretty damn good sounding bass in the room if I might say!!! The shoebox saved the day!

It’s like I have a giant hole in the frequency range I think i want and I don’t think this thing can produce, frankly, on its own. But boy do these two seem to work together pretty well!!!!

So here’s the deal. It’s still not quite right but neither of my furnishings. And the bottom line is this thing is capable of producing thuds incomprehensibly well for something that’s not much bigger than a crockpot!!! This thing is basically a 13 inch cube!!!! And when it comes to RV life space is extremely premium. I don’t have room for a two drawer filing cabinet to provide some chest pounding bass! So with that, I’m going to keep it AND the 8” soon fed with a 50htz highpass ant cranking the built in lowpass to the140 max. Then probably cross the SVS somewhere under 80. If I send it back there’s nothing else I can buy with my space constraints and id be stuck with the eight alone Like I said, its gorgeously tiny: I think I can actually bury half of it into the dash like Homer backing himself into the shrubs…

Maybe I’ll do an update, maybe I won’t. The bottom line is sealed subs are not what you might think. Super tight super detailed >>>super quiet<<< bass. It has its limits with music that is designed around booming bass. Still glad to have it. This is the cleanest system I’ve ever had

I also have 2 of the PB-1000 pro's in my living room and although those get louder and deeper, they cannot compete with the detail, texture and accuracy of this sealed sub running nearfield in my office. Really this is the first sub I have heard that can replicate the accuracy/speed of bass when using headphones but with the added benefit of shaking my desk! Very happy with my purchase.

reviews.title: Best Subwoofer I Have Ever Owned--Beyond My Expectations
reviews.text:
There is nothing to dislike about this subwoofer. I used the SVS app to assist with the set-up. It quickly detected that my sub was connected to my Denon AVR via the LFE connection and subsequently automatically disabled its own internal bass management. I have no desire or need to change any of the app's suggested default settings. It is positioned 11 inches away from my living room's front wall just behind the home entertainment center.

The sub is paired with my new POLK Legend L-200 front speakers. This is a marriage made in "heaven" so to speak. The Denon base management system appropriately assigns the proper frequencies across the various drivers. No more boominess as I experienced with my previous sub and speakers. This SVS sub delivers the best bass I have ever experienced without in any way compromising the upper frequencies. I have not a single complaint or negative comment. Best investment I have made in quite a while.

I let the receiver calibrate the setup as I usually do. I may play around with some manual settings to see if I can get a little more power from the sub.

I'm really disappointed because I hear so many good things about SVS and my first subwoofer from them is underwhelming. I don't recommend this subwoofer because decent set of quality speakers will easily overwhelm the bass from this subwoofer.

reviews.title: Perfect subwoofer to complete my home theater system with great tech support.
reviews.text:
For my small TV room I had purchased Klipsch R-30C center speaker as well as Klipsch R-51M left-right speakers, but wanted to get the entire 20 to 20,000 Hz sound spectrum. My left-right speakers go down to 62 Hz, so I obviously needed a sub to complete the system. The SVS SB-1000 Pro filled this need completely.

In addition, after I ran the optimizer for my receiver, no signal went to the subwoofer. I called SVS tech support, and the tech patiently ran me through the settings for my receiver. I turned out that the optimizer identified the R-51M speakers as Large, which was the reason no signal went to the sub. He had me change them to Small, and I got my signal back to the sub. This was going the extra mile to help me debug the optimizer settings of a receiver from another company entirely, to get everything working.

Lastly, the SB1000 Pro is engineered so that you can't tell that the low frequencies are coming from the left corner of the room, but rather, from the listening position, it sounds like all of the bass is split between the two left-right speakers.

Just an overall excellent product, with great bass and some of the best tech support I have ever experienced.

reviews.title: Outstanding subwoofer....
reviews.text:
Purchased this sub to replace my Klipsch R-100SW, which is part of my 5.1 system: Klipsch RP-600 M fronts, RP-500 Center, R-51M surrounds, and Denon AVR-X3700H running the show.

After re-running Audyssey, and using REW to find the best crossover frequencies, this sub has changed my entire viewing experience.

This subwoofer gives clear, precise, deep bass, and it's accuracy has improved dialogue clarity substantially.

This is a huge upgrade to the Klipsch sub, whose bass, when compared to the SB-1000 Pro, is a muddled, rumbly mess.

Both music and movies are a joy to listen to. Absolutely worth the price.

reviews.title: sb1000 a nice subwoofer
reviews.text: I do not know much about Subwoofers other then they are big expensive and provide deep articulate bass. This one is little, affordable, and provides very nice articulate bass. Though it is more for music as it does not provide the excessive bass you get with movies. The remote program that comes with it is fun to play with and will take a bit of a learning curve to dial in the best settings but out of the box this little sub is the sub that does deliver nice sounding bass my room is 18x12 but I am 7 ft from speakers in near field listening and they are a great addition, adding meat to the bone to my low frequencies from my monitor speakers. If you want to quibble the amp could us a few more horsepowers as my column control is at 80% of its capacity for me to find the proper volume. I have a two-channel system and I use a speaker connection ( not RCA) and the sub blends in flawlessly. Two competitors that also look good are the speedwoofer 10 s mk 2 ( not available at this writing) and the monolith by monoprice though they are ported and much bigger. Note I was able to buy the sb 1000 at its $499 pricenow it is $100 more, soooo ?

reviews.title: Very Nice Subwoofer
reviews.text: This sub gives nice deep and accurate bass. The phone app to control the sub is very nice and easy to use. I bought one sub and was very happy with the results. I decide to buy a second unit. I have a fairly large room, a finished basement. I was using a 5.0 system with no sub as I have large speakers with good bass. I made it a 5.1 system with the first sub and thought it provided sufficient bass but decided to go for two to better fill the room. I am still undecided if two subs were really worth it. To keep the bass from booming, I had to turn the volume down. I am not a bass head and like a clean sound. With these subs you discover the over exaggerated bass of most commercials and many TV shows. While I think these are excellent subs, I question the need if you have large speakers with sufficient bass. I am certainly glad I did not buy one of their more expensive units.

The SVS SB-1000 Pro delivered everything I wanted!! It has fixed some of the sound inconsistencies and delivers clean and crisp bass that is placed correctly! It took a little tweaking out of the box, but it’s setup perfectly now and it is a big upgrade for me!! Love it!!

reviews.title: Triple 4K @ 60hz on M1 Mac!
reviews.text:
It works, despite some of the dips in the Q&A stating otherwise. Running 3 X Dell 27” 4K displays all at 60hz from my M1 Max MacBook Pro no issues whatsoever. I have a lot of experience with different docks and this one runs a combination of DisplayLink for 2 of the display outputs and DP Alt Mode for the other. This means you MUST have the DisplayLink software on your computer, this is probably why so many people don’t think this dock works. You absolutely have to have the software installed for it to work. Mine worked without a hitch on the very first plug-in.

DisplayLink is a compressed video stream / software solution for being able to minimize the bandwidth to be able to fit all of the data necessary for 3 display across a single Thunderbolt connection. In day to day use for productivity this is a perfectly acceptable solution (this is how I use it). If you’re doing something that’s high frame rate and high resolution intensive on the DisplayLink connected screens it is possible you could see a slight degradation in video quality or a tiny bit of latency. Just something to consider before committing to a dock utilizing a DisplayLink solution.

If you need an easy triple 4K display dock for your Mac without using a bunch of adapters or guessing if it will work be compatible, get this dock. It just flat out works!

I upgraded to this dock from a CalDigit TS3+ which only supports two monitors and I recently added a third, this dock was the one I chose and it was a first time hit.

reviews.title: Really connects to 3 monitors!
reviews.text:
This device stuck out to me originally because it advertises that it can connect to 3 monitors all at once. I always have at least 2 monitors running in my work-from-home space and I want to accommodate all 3 when I need to, this docking station has proven to be reliable and effective every day since. I love that it doesn’t burn out and it doesn't suck a ton of energy out of one system in order to power another, which is unlike other stations of its kind.

This docking station is also clean and sleek which makes it easy to leave out. It is also heavy and sturdy which allows me to place other devices on top of it without fear of bending or breaking. The ports themselves are easy to use and haven’t broken or been out of service yet, which seems to happen with a lot of other docking stations. This docking station also has a few different types of ports which I don’t personally use (I’m a USB/HDMI guy), but I imagine that those would be useful as well for other WFH spaces.

I highly recommend this docking station to anyone with multiple monitors running at once. It is a great way to connect all of them without involving more wires and more clutter on the desk. I can’t wait to keep using this in my space and think it will remain as reliable as ever!

reviews.title: Better option than similarly priced Dell D6000
reviews.text:
If you have an Apple MacBook Pro with M1 silicone, you will need a DisplayLink capable dock if you want more than 1 or 2 external monitors (depending on which MBP you have).

This dock works flawlessly once you install the DisplayLink drivers. I am running three monitors:

- 1920x1200 @ 60Hz
- 2560x1440 @144Hz
- 1920x1200 @ 60Hz

And the dock has no issues with video playback, sleep, flickering, display flickers; it just works. I already had the DisplayLink drivers from when I set up the Dell so it was 100% plug and play.

I have had and used the similarly priced [[ASIN:B099NZ18TX Dell D6000]] for a few months now and here is my take:

- Construction wise, the Dell is beefier for sure. It's smaller but heavier, meaning it likely has more metal components inside for heat dissipation. This may have long term implications. The Plugable unit is much, much lighter and doesn't feel quite as high quality as the Dell. To be fair, this unit doesn't get as warm as the Dell unit does.

- The Dell's cable is fixed so if it gets damaged, you're out of luck; the whole unit needs to be replaced. Given that this cable is going to be plugged and unplugged possibly hundreds of times, this is a serious reason to consider the Plugable unit which has a fully detachable cable.

- Both units have an external power brick.

- The Dell D6000 passes through 65W while the Plugable unit only passes through 60W. Unfortunately for me, the 14" MacBook Pro M1 draws 67W. Both are going to be fine for the Air. Check your wattage requirements before purchasing if this matters to you.

- The Dell D6000 has an additional USB-C connector in the front that the Plugable unit does not.

- However, the Plugable dock has a total of 6 USB ports compared to the Dell's 5. Personally, this works out better for me because the MBP itself still has available USB-C ports.

- The Dell D6000 has issues when the machine is powered on from a cold start; it will not connect until you unplug it and plug it back in. The Plugable unit does not have this issue. When you cold boot the laptop, it only displays one of the three external monitors. But once logged in, all three external monitors connect without issue after a slight delay. This is not the case with the Dell as I need to log in on the built-in screen, unplug the cable, and plug it back in. This is a big win for the Plugable.

- The Dell D6000 has less flexibility with the accepted video cables with 1xHDMI and 2xDisplayPort whereas this Plugable dock provides much more flexibility to use the cables you have. Use either the 3xHDMI or 3xDisplayPort (can mix and match)!

- The Dell D6000 had some banding on the HDMI connection. It was extremely faint and you had to look for it, but definitely noticeable. Do not notice the same issue with this dock, even using identical cables.

To get the sound to work with the unit, you'll need to select the Plugable USB device in the sound output.

Can't speak for the longevity of the unit or support, but if you're considering the Dell D6000 or this Plugable, the Plugable is the clear winner.
