First time here & excited to try the Quzi ($16) which is supposed to come with chicken and beef cubes. Had like a total of 4 morsels of meat in it. Meanwhile while has been waiting for my go order saw huge plates with lots of meat go out. Flavor was good but other places around that serve food the same whether for there or to go.
Amazing food and nice ambiance. Try their hookah and you can't go wrong! Shawarma authentic to the Syrian one I used to have back home.

Stopped there randomly for lunch and had the chicken shawarma wrap. It was delicious. Especially liked the pickled vegetables in the sandwich and that the bread was crispy. The chicken was moist and flavorful. The fries that came with it were seasoned well and crispy. I will be coming back!

As a first generation arab-american I've eaten middle eatern/ mediterranean food and believe when I say this is some of the best food I've ever eaten from the appetizers to the entrees everything I've tried was delicious. Definitely my new favorite restuarant in St. Louis.

Omg the best Middle Eastern food i have had!!! I have lived in 4 different states and there's usually 1 spot my hubby and I will take out on a weekly, biweekly basis and I think we have found the one in STL. My hubby's friend/colleague graciously did take out from this restaurant. I got the chicken shawarma plate. The chicken was tender and perfectly seasoned. There were cabbage, onion, hot peppers, white sauce which were perfect accompaniments for the chicken shawarma. It reminded me of halal guys but the taste was fresher and less greasy( i hope they don't take offense to that). Anyway, 10/10 best chicken shawarma!

The only thing more impressive than the Arch in St Louis is Rozanna's food! Loved the unique menu options, quality made food, and hospitable service. Cheese Fatayer - a must order as an appetizer. Freshly baked, warm and fluffy bread with pockets of cheese inside. Slightly sweet, salty, and simply delicious. Mushroom Sujuk - mushroom, meat and potatoes are so tangy and saucy. This I've never had before at any middle eastern restaurant. The warm bread with black/white sesame folded on top of the clay pot is great. Highly recommend! The Mixed Grill - ok ok, this for sure is a must order to try all the different kinds of kabobs. The Chicken Shish is the winner, as stated on the menu but I loved the beef kabobs too. The white garlic sauce on the side...oh man, I was eating that up on its own it was so good. Baklava was decent, nothing above expectations. More layers of dough and less stickiness than I'm used to.

Very good sandwiches. I had sujuk, my dad had kafta- looking forward to trying the clay pots. Sujuk was pressed with lots of cheese and garlic sauce. Pickles were mild. Fries and cabbage/mint salad were great.

We elected to eat outside out of Covid concerns. The service was excellent and the food was full of flavor. We would much rather support a business like this, as they take pride in their food and service. We will go back for sure.
Very nice lamb shank. They give out free pita bread with three types of dipping sauces. Beautiful interior, very relaxing.

Rozanna is absolutely fantastic! Reviewing after my second time here, and both times we have had wonderful food and wonderful, caring service. This time I got the chicken shawarma plate as well as their eggplant dip which are both so incredibly flavorful. Even the rice tastes marvelous. Highly recommend coming here and giving it a try even if you've never had this type of food before -- you'll end up loving it!!

Got the Suzuk sandwich as takeout, impressive portion, sausage wasn't really spicy but sandwich was very rich and delicious. They gave me an extra side of their garlic mayo. Fries were crispy 20 minutes after. Didn't care for the salad but that's just me. Will definitely try again.

BEST ARABIC FOOD IN THE MIDWEST Rozanna is by far the best Mediterranean restaurant in the Midwest !!! I have tried arabic restaurants all over the country and this is the one !! 10/10 flavor, spices and perfectly marinated grilled meats. They are very friendly and the owners came to greet us and check on us frequently. The food is spiced perfectly. We got the mixed grill and Shawarma which was delicious YOU DID NOT VISIT STL UNLESS YOU ATE AT ROZANNA Also just fyi: we felt very comfortable with spaced out seating and masks worn by the employees

Excellent, stopped in for a late lunch and was very happy that we did. The food and service were excellent. The lamb shank was one of the best I've ever had. Appetizers were excellent and made in house. Shawarma was tasty and fresh. Highly recommend Rozanna if you are looking for excellent Mediterranean/Syrian food.

We tried Rozanna for take out lunch today. We had the chicken Shwarma sandwich and the sish tawouk sandwich. Both were really good! We also had the spinach fatayer. It could have used a sauce for dipping to keep it moist. The interior of the restaurant has been totally remodeled and looks very nice. The person who served my order was very friendly. They took all the precautions for COVID. We will definitely order from here again.

Authentic, delicious, warm. Best shawarmas I've had in St. Louis and I've tried many restaurants. Delicious garlic sauce/toum! Super friendly staff, prompt service. My new favorite shawarma spot in the city!
We loved everything at rozanna, food and service were superb. We'll definitely cone back to explore all the options on the menu.
Great food and great service! Make sure to ask for extra garlic sauce, you'll want it on everything!

Best Mediterranean food ever! Everything about Rozanna is perfect. The staff is friendly, the dining experience is great, the environment is warm and welcoming, and the food is top notch. My daughter in law is Syrian and her and her mother were so impressed with everything here. I've tried just about everything in the menu now and have not found one thing to complain about. I highly recommend eating here.

This is a true GEM! Everything on their menu is delish! We normally order the Mouhamara, Musakaa, Sujuk Sandwich, Chicken Shawarma and the Veggie platter! It's all sooo good! So glad Rozanna's is in Chesterfield/Ballwin!
The food here was excellent, everything from starter to dessert and coffee. Staff was friendly. Restaurant clean and decor cozy and quaint. We are already planning our next visit!!

Stopped by here earlier to pick up Dinner. We ordered the Lentil Soup, Kibbeh, Makanek Sandwich, Rozanna Mixed Grill (kebabs), and the Sujuk Sandwich. All are very good with aromatic spices. The Sujuk was a little over cooked and still good; prefer it rarer. We originally wanted the Mushroom Sujuk, and the Makanek Rozanna, both platters. Unfortunately I was told that these two dishes are very hot and will melt the takeout containers. Will return and have them in the Restaurant. They do have dine-in, and outdoor seating. Very friendly.
Delicious! Had for carry out tonight did not disappoint. They were also extremely nice and attentive answering questions about my allergy. We will definitely be back

#BradyEats lunch al fresco on a sunny 50 degree November day. Their outdoor includes 4 patio-heaters, but it was their food was spot on with unique flavors. Especially the sauces. The appetizer of rich puréed beets, potato & garlic mash, a delicious lamb shank sauce, and the more untie KIBBEH LABNIEH with yogurt sauce entree & Hot Mousakka (which I didn't see in the online menu) with rice killed it as our favorite the day! We'll definitely be back for outdoor seating during COVID-Distancing and carry-out.

This is, hands down, the best Middle Eastern restaurant in the greater St. Louis area. The lamb shank is out of this world. The falafel is amazing. Mixed grill, Shish Tawook, Makanek, it is all great. Lovely service. Reasonably priced. You won't be disappointed.
Amazing food. We've eaten at just about every middle eastern restaurant in five states and this was top two. Very low key and casual. Good service. Fair prices. Easy parking. Just excellent.
Delicious! The hummus, Tabbouleh & the other main dishes we shared were wonderful! First time there and loved it!

I don't know how West County got so lucky to have this new ethnic restaurant. The TABBOULEH was so fresh and flavorful, the home made hummus is the perfect combo of olive oil and lemon, the YALANGY (stuffed grape leaves) were the best I've ever had, the SHISH TAWOOK ROZANNA was unbelievably AMAZING with the flavor like no other...like heaven in your mouth and the Beef SHAWARMA meat was absolutely perfect texture and flavor. Don't forget to save room for desert and try the ZNOUD EL SETT!!! You HAVE to try this restaurant!!!
Best Mediteranian food, fresh home made and healthy. I ordered mixed grill, my wife ordered Rozanna kabob. Everything is delicious, great service, surely will come back to try other meals.

Just as so many have written, what a delightful restaurant! Went here on a whim this past Sat. Night. We were seated right away (6pm or so) and they had a very steady stream of business. The restaurant was clean, our waitress kind and efficient and the food...SO SO good! I had the chicken shawarma, my husband had the mixed grill. The food was hot, the flavors excellent. It is a middle of the road priced restaurant but I had left overs (enough for a lunch) so ai feel like the price point was justified. I don't write a ton of reviews (I have to feel very strongly good or bad) and this was a strong REALLY good. We will be back!
The food was unreal. I've had the opportunity to try authentic schawarma in my world travels and this here competes with some of the best. I was absolutely floored when I took the first bite. Wow!

Went here last month, service and food was excellent. Ordered the same food tonight, and it wasn't so great. It was warm ( not hot) and obviously had been sitting for a while before arriving at our table. Portions were skimpy and one kind of meat from the mixed grill wasn't even there. Fries were old and stale. After our server asked us how everything was, we explained our experience, but she didn't seem to care, just responding with an artificial apology. Dessert and tea were good but took forever to reach us.

My parents and I came here for lunch on Friday. So glad we decided to stop by because I had only done carry out in the past which was always delicious. But now post Covid I felt comfortable going out to the restaurant and I am glad I did because the service and the food was excellent. I loved their pre meal appetizer that was complementary, it was delicious! So fresh! We ordered the mixed grill and the grape leaves with rice, it was excellent!

Had a wonderful dinner last night at Rozanna Mediterranean Restaurant in Manchester! Started with a complimentary starter of 3 different dips with pita bread, followed by the lamb shank for my husband (falling off the bone with flavor) and the wonderful Beef Shawarma for me. Large portions, so part of our dinners went home so we'd have room for their fabulous rice pudding and baklava for dessert. Excellent service - Katie ran the front of the house with detailed precision, ensuring everyone who came in was greeted promptly, seated and had their starter dips in front of them while they were looking over the menu trying to decide between the many great choices on it. Fabulous place to put on your list of local restaurants to return to often whether it's for family dinner, date night, girls' night out or just an "I don't want to cook tonight evening"

Excellent lunch at Rozanna today. My husband had the Beef shwarma sandwich while I had the beef kafta sandwich. Both came with a pickle slaw and fries. We enjoyed the mint tea with our meal. Large portions excellent food and service From large family groups, to couples to groups of friends meeting ip, Rozanna is an excellent place.

Went to Rozanna for Friday night dinner with some co-workers. It was a bit of a drive from the city but definitely worth it. We were able to reserve a table for 4 outdoors and we were seated immediately. It wasn't too busy but we had to ask our waitress to take our order after waiting around for 15-20 minutes. The hummus with 3 complimentary dips is great; options are seasoned olive oil, mashed beets and garlic mashed potatoes. The mashed beets is definitely the best of the 3. I opted for the chicken shawarma plate and it was a huge serving! The chicken was seasoned and cooked well and the cabbage mix offered a nice mix of texture to the dish. My friends also enjoyed their dishes; the Sujuk sandwich is definitely one of the hits!

We live close and were looking for something we hadn't tried/new and saw the awesome reviews. SO glad we went; we will be back for sure! The chicken swarmva was DELISH, as were the cheese rolls and the mean sambusa! The rice and chicken from the swarmva were good on their own and even better together and then we tried the sauce and it was over the top delish! We did get there a bit after they opened and they were still setting up the outside/patio tables yet they were all very kind and thoughtful. Also appreciated that the employees all wore masks and were very gracious with our menu questions.

Delicious, fresh, good service. I had the ouzi and husband had the combo plate. Both were out of this world and we grunted "mmmm, you should've gotten *this*" to each other multiple times. We will be back!

Amazing!! I've been several times and everything is delicious. Rozanna is the best Middle Eastern restaurant in town. I loved the hummus and the grape leaves. My hubby got the mixed grill and said it was outstanding. I'm vegan and there are so many choices. Lucky to have this place nearby.

Spur of the moment choice and we will return!!! We had the hummus app and enjoyed the complimentary dips as well (seasoned olive oil, mashed beets and garlic mashed potatoes). We then shared chicken dish with fries on side, and it was delicious as well. Our waitress was friendly and helpful with our decisions since we had no idea what to order. We sat outside and enjoyed the beautiful day on their well decorated patio.
Delicious food . Very courteous staff .Prompt service .Would strongly recommend this place .
The most wonderful flavors, the subtlety of one layer upon another...it has been years since I've had Mediterranean food like this. Do not miss the chance to try it!

Loved the food I had the shwermaa sandwiches and kubbaa so happy to find such great middle eastern food in Saint Louis definitely going back. Would love to sit outside and have their hookah next time.

The atmosphere is good. Service is super slow and disorganized. People sitting next to us (arrived after us) got their dinner 15 minutes before us. My wife ordered stuffed Cabbage Rolls with Lamb Chops and it was very good. I ordered 2 sandwiches; Makanek & Sujuk. They were the WORST Makanek & Sujuk sandwiches I have ever eaten. DO NOT order them.. really bad.

This is our favorite Mediterranean restaurant in the area! The service is great and the food is authentic Mediterranean. So many amazing options on the menu that you can't go wrong with anything. Also the desserts are to die for! I personally love the lazy cake and the Arabic ice cream.
My daughter and I were wishing for some nice middle eastern food. The food was delicious. Very authentic. Everything made fresh.
This place is really good. The mixed plate was absolutely delicious! The yogurt sauce is the boss. I will be back!

We love this recently opened Mediterranean restaurant! The service is great and the food is terrific. The best hummus I have had in St. Louis! I had the mixed grill which had an assortment of kebabs with rice which was delicious. The small plates are great and my wife loved the vegetarian options. Couldn't be happier that this great placed opened so close to home!

I love this place been there twice in a week lentil soup,tabooli salad ,little cheese bread mix grill all excellent very beautiful presentation and amazing customer service George came by every table to ensure satisfaction two very hard working and caring ladies run the show in the kitchen and trust me they know their stuff not googled or YouTube recipes very authentic

Wow. Dropped in on an early Sunday (around 11:30am) probably right after opening. Someone was mopping the dining room floor when we arrived. Very welcoming, both the room and the people. Our server immediately brought us water/drinks, along with some pita bread and a trio of delicious 'dips', one of which was made with beets and yogurt that I've never had before and it was amazing. We stuck to the sandwich side of things ("sandwich" should be in quotes since they were really wraps made with what I would call Lavash bread). I ordered the beef kafta sandwich and my wife had the chicken. Both sandwiches were delicious and big portions served with fries (batter dipped variety - tasty) and a yummy cabbage salad. Great experience, dinner options are a bit pricey, but from our lunch I'm sure they're worth the price. Food was excellent and service was also very good. Looking forward to going back for dinner sometime.

Just moved to the area and came upon this gem! Portions are sizable and the food is delicious- full of flavor. Nice outdoor patio too. Well worth your time and money to stop by and support this local business
Excellent Chicken Shawarma. One of the best in town. I asked for some customization and I got exactly what I wanted. Must try!!
The nicest staff and owners, very accommodating, and the food is very authentic. My favorite Mediterranean restaurant in St. Louis.

They follow COVID protocols and guidelines which I highly respect and offer a very homey experience. I've ordered quite a few things from here and needless to say everything was spectacular! The lamb meat on the shanks comes right off the bone! The shawerma (both chicken and beef) were extremely flavorful! The tabuleh and yalangy was on point! The kebeh was ok (I'm not a huge fan of kebeh but my boyfriend loved it!) but I'm definitely coming back to try the kebeh labnieh and grape leaves since I heard a lot about them! Oh and not to forget the dessert.. I absolutely love their lazy cake. Definitely coming back!

This place is ABSOLUTELY amazing! We had hummus to start which was beautifully blended. The house appetizer is also served with some very tasty bread and a blend of dips. The beef Schwarma sandwich is great, as well as the desserts! A must go for Mediterranean in St. Louis

Best Mediterranean restaurant we've found in all of St. Louis. Great flavors and high quality ingredients make all of the difference. We had the Quzi and vegetarian platter and both were delicious. We also had the lentil soup which was a standout. Too often they are bland and/or pureed out of existence but the soup here was perfect. We stopped in here on a bit of a whim and unfortunately don't live too close, but we will still definitely be returning many times to support such great food!

Alright I gotta give this place an honest review as a true Syrian! Note: this is simply my personal opinion about the food and service with some constructive criticism. Ordering: it was very easy ordering on the website and informed us when the food will be ready (20 minutes). However, I feel like they don't look at the online orders coming in because they took another 15 minutes to make the food when we got there. Next time we'll just call. Kibbeh: the dough was thin and perfectly crunchy, beef was tender and pretty good. I just wish it had walnuts or pine nuts. I guess I'm used to the nuts texture in kibbeh. Also, it felt like it had sujok seasoning in the beef which it didn't really need because it kind of took away from the actual dough flavor. Overall 8/10 Chicken shawarma: it was way better than other places in St. Louis! Loved the tahini garlic sauce it's literally perfect. I appreciate that they're trying to replicate the authentic Syrian shawarma with pita and thin lavash; but I personally think that it doesn't necessarily need 2 kinds of bread, either pita or lavash, and I say that because lavash bread in the US isn't paper thin like the one in Syria. With that said, it was soft and not too thick at all. The chicken was tossed in some acidic sauce and when you add the pickles it's a little too acidic. The chicken can absolutely do without the acidity and just let the pickles do the work. Not too greasy which I also loved. 9/10 Pistachio ice cream: ughhh the texture. Literally perfect just like the ones you get in Syria. First I got hit by the rose water then got used to it, it's actually super nice. 10/10

We came back with family and friends a total of 10 people. Had the best food, drinks and fun. Friendly service and great atmosphere. I ordered lamb shank my wife ordered mixed grill. The best shank ever. I still have few items to try , sure coming again.

Excellent Middle Eastern food! Friendly service and safe during COVID. We went for dinner and indoor seating was full so we ate outside and had wonderful gas heaters close to our table, very cozy! We ordered a few tasty dishes, including a delicious eggplant dish with tomatoes and onions, stewed, served with pita. Everything tasted freshly made! The owner introduced herself and asked us how we enjoyed our meal. We were pleasantly surprised at the end with complimentary baklava, which was the best I've had in a long time. Highly recommend trying this place for something different and new!
Good food. Tried a few things, mixed grill and hummus. Recommend. Owners very nice.

Santorini Greek Island Grill is the best place to eat on the UCSB campus. The food is fresh, well-prepared, and delicious. The staff is efficient, courteous, and friendly (e.g., they call you "my friend"). The menu is interesting, varied, and contains many healthy options. (I like the chicken pita meal.) The place is well-managed and you can see that everyone there takes pride in what they do. The prices are reasonable. These are some of the reasons I have been a loyal customer for the last two years and why I plan to continue coming to Santorini's for lunch in the future.

Friendly, fast, and delicious. The GYRO is great. A little salty sometimes but very enjoyable. Some may find it a bit oily, but it's delicious and probably the best food to eat in the UCen. The CHICKEN is dry sometimes and doesn't compare in flavor to gyro. The falafel is fabulous. I love their FRIES. Who knew simple french fries could taste so good. Breakfast 7-11am is definitely worth it! Their BREAKFAST WRAP wakes you up and is so convenient for UCSB students and faculty. The prices are so affordable Greek food; ~$6-8 for a meal. The line is super quick and the employees are very friendly!

For this place to have 4 stars, the people of Santa Barbara must be depressingly starved of Greek food. Perhaps I simply went on a bad day, but the gyro plate mostly tasted as though it came out of a cafeteria. The gyro meat was dry, and the fries and salad that came along with it were nothing to write home about. For the most part I'd say it was bog-standard fast-food Greek, what you might expect to get at a a Luna Grill or Daphne's. Not bad, by any means, but not worth 4 stars.

This is my favorite restaurant on-campus and maybe in the general Santa Barbara area. I love to stop by Santorini's to get the hummus and pita as a delicious, fulfilling snack. Before I knew about this plate, I was a big fan of the Sabra hummus and pretzels packs. For less than a dollar more than these packs cost ($5 total), you get twice as much food and the pita is warm and delightful--I'm hooked! For breakfast, I get a side of eggs and pita. The eggs have veggies in them (think onions, bell peppers) which add a nice texture. This meal is a regular for me and it is very good way to start your day. For lunch, I usually get the veggie pita meal. The pita is simple (greek salad laid on a pita that has been smeared with hummus) but it does the trick! I get the fries with this meal EVERY TIME because they are magnificent. Seasoned with yummy seasoning salt and with a crunchy outside/soft inside; these are my favorite french fries pretty much anywhere. I have also had the fried calamari salad here and let me say WOWEE, it is tasty. Although I generally avoid meat, there are always people in line at lunch ordering the chicken and lamb pita which smells very good from over the counter. The workers are always nice, efficient (lines move very quickly here), and helpful. You (and your wallet) are missing out if you haven't tried it already!

This place is the THE place to eat on campus and and probably all of IV. I've had quite a few of their items and my go to is the chicken salad and calamari plate. The calamari is crispy and delicious and the salads are always great, crispy lettuce, tomato, onion, olives and feta cheese. No ranch here, just the taziki sauce and oil. It's great and definitely worth a try.

FINALLY! Awesome food at a price that doesn't break my bank. It's not cheap but their portions are large enough that I can split it into two meals. Every menu item looks great and I've tried the plates, sandwich and salads, but the Santorini Salad is my jam! It has gyros and chicken piled generously over a bed of lettuce, olives, tomatoes and onions. Their dressing does a great job cutting through the heaviness of the meat. I have absolutely no complaints about this place. Even the staff is excellent. They really handle large crowds quite efficiently so even if the line is long, there isn't much of a wait. Can't recommend enough!
Loaded fries are bomb, so is the cali pita, definitely some of the best food you can get on campus
A great option for a meal if youre on campus and in a rush! Pretty fair portions and the beef meat is very tender. The fries here are also seasoned very well. Pita bread for every meal you order.

Probably the best place to eat on campus. I always got the chicken pita meal for lunch while attending UCSB. It was so delicious and all for a reasonable price. I'd highly recommend. Now that I've graduated I miss eating here.

Love Santorini's! I get lunch here every week because it's the best place to eat on campus. I grew up on mediterranean food and this place is legit. The Baklava tastes just like my aunt's! Also, the price is great for the amount of food you get. One thing that really stands out to me is the meat. Meat at other places around IV can be kinda sketchy and have grizzle or taste a bit funny. The chicken and the gyro meat here are always fresh though! Santorini also catered all the food for my club's free CPR/AED certification course in Corwin, and it was a hit! The trainers were thrilled and everyone was all smiles while eating it. Even my vegetarian friends were happy. The service is great, the workers are very friendly and nice, and the helpings are generous. I'm gonna miss this place when I graduate!

darn, I wish i took a picture. I am a UCSB employee and am kicking myself for not trying this place sooner. their calamari salad has to be the BEST calamari i have ever had in my life. i dont know what they did to this to make it so amazing. you should also try their wings both hot and lemon dill. OUT OF THIS WORLD. they need to open another stentorian in SB and not just on UCSB campus. theres not enough Greek places here. it is my favorite kind of food. I cant wait to go back and try what else they have
OMG so good !! Chicken pita meal is delicious !! So fulfilling and it doesn't make you feel bad about eating out haha . Definitely recommend (:

First of all, know that I have tried this place multiple times during my time being student at UCSB. I have always been so confused as why this place had so many good reviews, so I tried different things from the menu to really make up my opinion. Honestly, the food is simply not good, and especially way over priced for what you get. The quinoa from the quinoa salad is way over cooked and it tastes very watery, almost tastes like mush. The chicken that came with it was burnt, very hard and dry. The hummus has a very odd consistency, it looks chunky. At the counter, the person taking care of the cashier is sweating over the food, handing you a cartboard box dirty from the worker's fingers. Also, the service isn't very friendly and you almost feel like you're annoying them. While looking at the menu, I have been greeted with a seemingly agressive " WHAT DO YOU WANT ". When asked for the ingredients of a plate, the woman did not know what they were, she had to ask her boss who rapidly slammed the ingredients in a 2 seconds sentence, barely understandable. Drinks do not have lids, your straw will float out of your drink. $10 plates, 60 cents for a side of hummus.. Ended up tossing the food away two times in a row. This place has potential, it just has to wake up honestly. Won't go again unfortunately.
It was surprisingly sooo good.. the meat on the salad was delicious & the guy working there was really nice too!

I'm so happy this place opened up in UCSB's UCEN. The food is fresh, the service is fast, and the prices are reasonable. I have eaten here twice. First time, I ordered the chicken gyro sandwich and it was spot on. Very flavorful and fresh. The second time, I ordered the chicken gyro salad. Also delicious, especially the dressing. I will definitely be back!
This place was very hard to find!!!! Upon entering the campus, there are no signs directing you to the restaurant. Other than this place being hard to find, the food is good!!

The best spot to eat on campus!! Unsure if it's just beginner's luck but Santorini's is insanely good for it's price. I don't know much about Greek food but I've tried both Aladdin's and Lovin Oven and have to say that this one beats them both in quality and value. The portions are huge, I got the gyro plate and they actually stacked that meat up to the top. I usual eat like a fatass and had a hard time finishing the meal. It's the only place to eat on campus that won't make you feel like you just gibbed for 7 bucks. Try it out now cause I just don't believe any food place on campus can stay this good before it becomes corrupt.
Great food better Service. Alan and his crew are awesome and I love their breakfast!

Super good. I want some right now haha. The money you spend is worth it here. The gyro plate is amazing and you can choose your side and you get a drink. Very satisfied and super yummy. It is also quick.
I go here at least once a week, my favorite is the chicken pita sandwich. And the workers there are always super sweet.

This may actually be the worst falafel pita sandwich I have seen in my life. I have eaten a lot of falafel. To pay upwards of five dollars for this is absolute robbery, and they would never get away with it off campus. IV Deli Mart's falafel isn't even that great, but it shines in comparison to this. Do not go here.
Great Greek food with friendly service from Alan. I had a lamb gyro from a place down south this week that confirmed that Santorini offers the best gyro around and definitely my favorite.

Located in UCSB's university center, this is an excellent place to pick up high quality food on the run. I'm in love with their falafel. Further, today I forgot my credit card and the very generous owner let me pay via IOU and said to come back later to pay. The gesture really made my day. In summary, good food and good people.
Tastes good, service is decent. $8.93 for the gyro plate which is kind of pricey for how much they give you. Would rather go to panda tbh but I enjoyed the food

This is the best restaurant on campus. There's also a few locations in San Diego, which made me sad because I thought we were special to have this place. It's located in the UCen, and it shares floor space with Romaine's. There's plenty of tables and booths inside, but it does get crowded during meal times. There's also tables in the UCen, as well as a patio area. The prices are pretty high, but the portions are great. I got the Santorini platter, which has meat, sausage, two wings, pita bread, and two sides. Everything tastes great and is well-cooked. The meat is juicy and tender. I'm not a big fan of the wings, I find it a little dry. They also have fries, which are pretty tasty. My favorite Greek food item is pita bread. They don't make it as nice as the bread at Daphne's, but it comes close. Service is top-notch. The workers are very quick and pleasant. Even when the line gets long, the service I receive does not change. Great food, great establishment.

Hands down, the best restaurant on the UCSB campus in terms of quality, variety, and value. Santorini is my favorite place to stop for greek food, and actually one of the few good mediterranean options in Santa Barbara. Their vegetarian platter, which includes a generous portion of dolma, falafel, hummus, and spanakopita, is excellent. With a side of their freshly-chopped greek salad, this makes a very satisfying meal. Their gyro sandwiches and salads are worth a try. While their grilled chicken can be a bit dry, it has good flavor as well. The little team that runs Santorini has a positive attitude and are always friendly. I love stopping by because both their food and service impress me. If you're on the UCSB campus and want food that is flavorful and a step above typical college fare, Santorini is the place to go.
This shit is legit. Don't listen to anyone who says it's too salty; it's supposed to be, and its flame. You won't find better french fries in the area, and the gyros sandwiches really turn me on.

More like 3.5 stars... I'm a bit short of calling myself a fan. I think I quite like mediterranean food, so I gave this place a try. Santorini is located conveniently in the UCEN of UCSB and if you're trying to get food and can't wait for the ridiculous Panda line, this is a good alternative. I usually get the gyro plate, which is a pretty good deal since you get the fire roasted gyro and your choice of two sides. In my opinion, the salad isn't very worth it since it's just iceberg lettuce, but it's a decent option for those who don't want two sides that are all carbs. I used to like the rice, because it's like a run-down version of mediterranean yellow rice. The first few times I've had it, the seasoning was spot-on. It was flavorful without being too salty. Same with the fries, which are apparently a favorite amongst Santorini regulars. Nowadays, however, I find that everything just seems a bit too salty. The meat needs to be paired with the naan bread in order to not be overwhelmingly salty, the rice is a bit too mushy and also super salty, and the fries taste heavier than in the beginning. I'm not sure if this is just me getting tired of Santorini, but I've been pretty disappointed the past two times I'm back. I think I'll come back a while later and redetermine how I feel, but for now, it's just a little too salty. If you really like your food flavor packed and heavy in flavor, this shouldn't be a problem. Or, you can choose to skip the rice and just have a lighter meal. Either way, I've experienced pretty good food from Santorini, and hope it's just a coincidence that I didn't find the past two visits particularly impressive.

Attending UCSB Spring Insight on the SB campus this weekend. Stopped in to Santarini's Island Grill. I have to tell you the food was so much better then anticipated and the service was even better. I ordered the chicken pita special which came with a salad, feta fries, and a whole chicken breast grilled to perfection. Truly out of this world. My wife had the gyros very fresh and tender. Delicious ! An extra shout out to Zack, only the best cashier of the UCSB campus. So if you have the pleasure of dropping one of your children off on the UCSB campus for the next four years, make a detour to Santarini's it will make those students loans easier to swallow.
The best choice for a quick and healthy lunch in UCSB. The worker there are really nice.

I'm very happily surprised by Santorini's! This restaurant is in the UCEN of UCSB and unique as there aren't many Mediterranean cuisines in this area. I wasn't going in expecting much since it is a restaurant on campus but it exceeded my expectations! I got the gyro plate and it includes the meat, 2 sides (I chose veggies and salad) there is also rice and fries, and a pita bread cut into 4 pieces. Please look at the images as they have photos of this meal. The meat is VERY tender and well flavored. It tastes as it has been marinated for a long while and care was put into this dish. The side salad was delicious and I'm a huge fan of the grilled veggies that holds a lot of flavor as well. the plate is very filling and all this for $8.07 including tax! As this is located in the UCEN where there is a lot of traffic during the lunch hour, the service is very fast and efficient. Overall I'll definitely be back and I want to try their $1 Wednesday breakfast special from 7-9!
Best food on campus. Loaded fries are the best. 8 bucks for fries sounds expensive, but they put so much chicken and gyro in there it is well worth it.

Today's the first time I tried out this place. Suffice to say I scrutinized the food a bit more than I should have. Nonetheless IT WAS GOOD! Service was fast and friendly, and the food's super fresh and good for low-carb diets (forget about the pita in this review). Anyways for lunch, I ordered the $7.50 ($9 with taxes) Souvlaki Platter 1+ 1 with Chicken and Sausage gyro. It come with 2 sides (I got salad w/ feta and roasted veggies for the low-carb thing, you can also get rice or fries as well), pita bread quarters (I didn't eat these, but I did give these away!), as well as the tzatziki and red vinegar/oil sauces, separate from the main entreé. For the most part, I was satisfied with the meal. The gyros sausages were absolutely tender and delicious. GET THE GYROS if you come here. The chicken was good, where I can bite into the skewers to find clear juices running out. However it does not beat the gyros. There's grease on the sausage gyros (There isn't much on the chicken), but as a high-fat/low carb ketogenic person, this was fantastic, especially since you can dip your food into the red vinegar olive oil that they give you! I didn't get kicked from Keto from the gyros, so that implies that they probably use 100% meat and not some substitute for their gyros! Much of the menu is for high fats/low carb diets and I'd say if you want a low fat place to eat, go somewhere else. S/O to the tzatziki sauce for being SO GOOD. This food will make you thirsty though, dressings have a bit of a bite and saltier for some people, keep in mind that. Also, I know the people there can answer questions because this girl in front of me asked if Apple Pay is accepted here, which is not available now, but could be added later according the the cashier. It's good to see the staff answering questions. The prices for the big plates are on par with what to expect for the portions, so expect me to be back again.
One of the best places to eat at UCSB but still not that good.. don't get the falafel, nobody likes it. I recommend the chicken; most people like the gyros but I'm not a fan. Good prices.
very bad customer service and super disappointed in the way employees spoke to customers

totally disappointed. The water pitcher was dirty, lots of finger prints on the doors at entrance. I expected shrimp and seafood on the buffet but was told it is only at night.Then why does it not say that on their web page? Not a good value, over priced average food. waitress went and sat down to eat as soon as we got our food??? Service avg at best
So many combinations for bowls, good value for a good-sized dinner. I've been coming here forever, and I love it.

Delicious! You choose your ingredients and there are lots of options. Numerous veggies and many different meat choices. You can also choose tofu. On top of that, they offer just about every sauce you can imagine (from sweet to spicy) and have a handy chart with suggested sauce mixtures. There is an option for all you can eat. I got that option the first time and definitely did not need it. The small bowl, stacked high, is probably enough for many adults. The meat is shaved a little too thin for my taste, but still delicious.
The food was pretty good and I liked the thicker sauces. However the mongolian place downtown has more choices and seems fresher. The employees weren't very friendly either.

This place is great if you want a quick meal with lots of food. It's not amazing or anything but the food is tasty and the service is good. They have a large selection of fresh veggies, meat, and sauces. You build your own bowl so you can get a ton of food if you pile it on right.

Of all the offerings of Mongolian BBQ in Boise, this place has always been consistently the best. Run by a familiar crew of folks, food and service are consistent. One of the friendliest waitresses in Boise works her. She's always ready with a smile and remembers my drink order though I don't think I could be called a regular there. Decor takes me back to the nineties, which is a good thing. It's a comfortable and casual place to eat. It's hard to beat one of their hot bowls of noodles made by you to your liking! Try the Mongolian BBQ sauce on your food. Tasty!

They have great quality service that is hard to beat. The food is absolutely amazing. I have only come here twice, but I suggest getting a medium bowl and putting a lot of stuff in it. They have two sides of the serving table so there are two people who cook your food. As I said, this place is amazing.
They can be rude. Flavor is good and according to what you put on your noodles. Prices are average.

The food is usually okay here, but I had the worst experience tonight! I filled my bowl as usual, and then filled an additional bowl of different sauces/oil like I always do for maximum flavor. The chef cooking my noodles continuously sprayed water on my food then entire time it was cooking, and then end result was flavorless pile of disgusting food. The person working check-out told me they do that because their grill gets too hot. They should turn the heat down instead of watering down the customer's food because I couldn't even eat the mess they coked up for me. It's too expensive to be messing up like that...

The decor is what you'd expect from most mongolian independently owned establishments. The food on the other hand was more that you could shake a stick at. They wont bitch at you for piling it high and deep. You can also take it home with you which would probably work out terrific for the great amount of starving college students attending boise st. there.
The best mongolian in town. Very cheap and very good food. Had to wait in line for 20 minutes on a weekday with all the Albertson(Super Valu) folks from their corporate offices.

First Idaho Mongolian experience and it was very tasty. Good variety of very fresh and delicious vegetables. All food was grilled to perfection. Service was timely and pleasant. Don't let the location fool you for one second (next to car wash) this place is worth the stop.
Not a pleasant environment. Food is ok... Just look elsewhere. So many better choices

This was my first Mongolian BBQ experience. I love the concept, and I think this place executes it very well. We were served by an incredibly friendly (and very pretty) young woman who took the time to explain the process and ensure we knew what we were doing. The prices are fair. We got the medium bowl for $10, which could easily be split into three reasonably sized meals. I will only be in Boise for about 5 months, and I will definitely be taking advantage of this awesome little place while I'm here!
This is my favorite of Boise's Mongolian Bbq restaurants. Great food, fair price, friendly long-time staff. Perfect for eating healthy!

Many people insisted that we try this place. We were very disappointed. Both my husband and I felt sick for 2 days. The atmosphere is dark and gloomy, so I wonder what was creeping in the shadows. The food, including meats, sits out by the grill awaiting your selection prior to it being cooked. How hygenic is this? The bill was higher than I imagined it would be as well. We'll stay away from here.

This place is so good!!!!!! The service was amazing! A really nice lady came in and sat us down and asked if we'd been here before and gave us the run down and we made big bowls for each of us. The chefs were fun to watch and the secret is to load up your bowl with meat and noodles and tons of sauce like eight scoops and a few scoops of oil. Definitely recommend!

Flew in to Boise and searched for Mongolian bbq and decided to go to the one most reviewed. Is this place cheap and good value for money? Yes. Seeing crab as one of the options for this price was great. Is this the best Mongolian bbq place I have been to? No. The selection is decent. But the sauces are too watered down. Even after adding one full bowl of sauce in one bowl of my food, there wasn't much flavor and needed the sriracha. 4 stars just because this place is in Boise and what better options do you have? :).

Mongolian BBQ is like the Subway of Mongolian food. I mean you can create whatever, I mean whatever you want. This is where I go when I want great food, and leftovers for the next two meals. The servers and chefs are very friendly. I usually find a piece of someone else's meal in my own. Not a big deal though. Great place to go on a date.

This place is pretty good. Prices are usual, portions are large, selections very good (fresh and well stocked). The food, after being cooked in front of you on the traditional round grill, is served hot in a bowl. We usually get the food served on a plate in other similar restaurants and the result of the bowl presentation is that all the sauces and seasonings sink to the bottom. That makes the food at the top of the bowl somewhat bland, and the food at the bottom very warm and much more flavorful. In the future, I would start eating from the bottom of the bowl for the best result. Our meal was served with a small bowl of rice and excellent service. Recommended!
Showed up 30 mins before closing, having driven 5 hours to eat here. Only to be told they had just ran out of food and couldn't serve us. What a joke.

They are getting more restrictive on how much goes in a bowl, I understand because some people go way over the top. The place is clean but not super clean, the staff is nice but not really nice. Over all the food is great if you make it great and its a better than average place to eat!

My job takes me all over the U.S. and thus I've been able to try few Mongolian BBQ joints and this is the best I've found. I've been stopping in at this restaurant every time I've been in Boise for the last 20 years and its never let me down.

i dont really know what mongolian food is supposed to taste like, but this place rocks. if it werent so oily, id eat here more often. but there is something special about gettting my car washed at mister's next door and eatting mongo on a sunday afternoon. took me about 5-6 goes before i got my secret formula of success down. that being said, my secret formula is inscribed in my will so it can be past down to the next generation.

I served in the Navy for 15 years, traveled to several countries and have eaten Mongolian BBQ in many. I currently travel across the states and to Boise often. Although this is my first time at this location I will be back. I can't set this place apart from the rest. The food was fresh and good you pick the sauces so you can't really complain about the flavor. Two thumbs up in my opinion. Last note. The service was phenomenal. My glass was never empty.
We went here today and it was so good. It is easy to be a vegetarian at places like this. I loved every bite. I wish it were close to my house; I would be there all the time!

I've been a BIG fan of the Mongolian BBQ in St. George, Utah for many years. I've eaten there countless times over the past several years. I knew the same family or friends of the family operated some restaurants in Idaho too, but never had the opportunity to eat there until this last weekend. The formula for great Mongolian BBQ is easy -- LOTS of fresh vegetables and other fresh ingredients, several meat choices, and plenty of sauce! Pick what you want in your bowl and have the cook stir-fry it up. Make sure and tip your cook while you're waiting! This Mongolian BBQ location in Boise doesn't disappoint! It was most definitely fresh and most definitely delicious! Inside the restaurant was older looking but seemed more or less clean and well maintained. Staff was attentive and friendly. We ate here twice over the Memorial Day weekend and the food and service were excellent both times. My only compliant is that there isn't a Mongolian BBQ location in my hometown of Salt Lake City, Utah. Please, please, pretty please open a location in Salt Lake City. I swear I would eat there all the time!

Absolutely love this place! Came for a takeout order and the employees helped teach me how to get my bowl ready. A super fun way of putting together your own order. After living in hawaii for 4 years, this place is such a nice present. The bowls are 100% customizable and easy to assemble. You go through and add everything you would like in your bowl including the sauces and the chefs cook it on a hot plate in front of you! Very fun and exciting The employees saw me struggling to decide on things and had me add MORE food to my bowl and recommended sauces for me to add which was so nice. Definitely coming back to this place.

Went here for the first time with my boyfriend, and we both enjoyed it. Everything was clean and orderly. All of the food items were fresh, and I could not stop scooping up those veggies! The chef gave us tips on what flavor of sauces to add, and our waitress was very pleasant and considerate. My boyfriend finished eating before me, so our waitress came to box up his leftovers. She offered to box mine up since she was there with the idea of continuing to eat out of the box, so we could continue our conversation without being interrupted again by the staff - so simple, but so brilliant! I really can't think of a single complaint other than we felt a little rushed toward the end. I'm pretty sure my fortune said something about going back there to eat again... :)
Good food and swift service. An easy way to go out and still stay within a budget. Nothing fancy, just good food.
Clean, tasty, 10 bucks. That about sums it up! Plenty of room, not too crammed in like some places, booths were comfortable and clean. I would go back again!
First time here, came with colleagues since they recommended it. Place was busy during lunch, which is always a good sign. Food was pretty good, and service was nice as well. Good food option!

I am a huge fan. Used to work across the street and was frequently tempted by this place. It's as good as any mongolian I have had and the downtown location is difficult to beat. Very friendly staff and good beverages. This will remain a downtown favorite of mine.

My family and I went to this Mongolian BBQ last week, it was our first time there. I liked the fact that there are different pricing options. You can have 1 serving of either a small, medium or a large bowl. Then there's all-you-can-eat if you're really hungry. We are from southern California, and most of the Mongolian BBQ around here are all-you-can-eat only, some have 1 serving prices, but I don't remember seeing different prices for different bowl sizes. The veggie selection is good, the sauces selection is huge. The meat selection is good. They have beef, chicken, pork, imitation crab (if you look closely there are shrimps in there.) But I was disappointed to see that they do not have lamb. I always eat lamb at Mongolian BBQs. My family liked the flavor, the food, the selection. They would give it 4 stars, but I did not like the flavor no matter what different combination of sauces I tried. Plus, I'm really disappointed with the lack of lamb. I would give it 2 stars. So to compromise, I'm giving this restaurant 3 stars. If you're in the area, and you enjoy buffets, I think this is a good place to give it a shoot, the prices are very reasonable for a buffet restaurant too.
So delicious. Fast, fresh, simple. You pick your own veggies, meat, and sauce from the bar, hand them the bowl, and watch them stir fry it. Friendly service. Great place!!! :)

Do you like getting a shit-ton of food for a good price? I know I do. Pick out your ingredients, slap them in a bowl, and watch it get cooked for you. It's quite tasty and you shouldn't have to eat for the rest of the day!

This is one of my least favorite Mongolian BBQs. Normally, they're all pretty similar, but this one has really weird tofu (honestly they leave it swimming in water and it has such a strange texture), they tend to be more expensive than other Mongolian's and I really think their sauces are watered down. Best Mongolian in town is in the strip mall on Milwaukee and Fairview!
Awesome noodles great that meat is frozen sliced. All begs are fresh yummy. Staff very helpful an nice. Quick service always w a smile
Typical Mongolian BBQ. It was as I expected. Really friendly service, I did however think there might be a few more items.
Good food overall but the noodles leave something to be desired. Friendly staff and the place is clean and serviceable.

This has to be one of my favorite lunch stops in Boise. In fact it is not uncommon for me to come here up to 2 times in a one week stay while here. The staff are friendly, the food is good (hell if it isn't it's mostly your fault since you are putting it all together yourself), and its quick. For $8-12 (incl tax and tip) you have plenty of food and they even serve you a bowl of rice in addition to what you have prepared in your own bowl. I personally got 2 meals out of my small bowl. It's nothing fancy, but maybe that is why I like it. Plus I have a nice meal and I am not in a rush and still get in and out in an hour.
I'm a food snob and this is one of the best Mongolian BBQs that I've eaten at. Boise and Mongolian BBQ don't seem like they should be in the same sentence, but it's good.
If it's not good it's your own fault! ;-) All the fixins, three sizes of bowel, good selection of sauces and Dr Pepper to wash it down. $10 for lunch--and some serious eats!

So first off I'll tell you that this place is in no way, shape, or form a "fine dining" establishment. The bottom line is this; it's cheap, it's good, and it's filling. If you leave unsatisfied or hungry, it's basically your own fault. You get to choose your own ingredients all the way around, so if you didn't like your food then you chose poorly on ingredients. This place is old, basic, and not impressive by any means. So if you are looking to impress that new girlfriend or first date, this isn't where you take them. It's a hole in the wall place with a bunch of Asian guys running it who speak little or broken "Engrish", who just sit around most of the time playing on their cell phones. They'll refill your drink when you need it, but don't expect to make any idle chat or anything.....they're too busy with their cellphones. All of this is really okay, as long as you don't go into this place expecting more than what it really is. Basically it's a fast food Asian joint, where you can get good, filling, cheap, messy food that leaves you feeling better than if you went and ate at McDonalds. I can say that the other location in Nampa is exactly the same way, now that I've eaten in both places. If this sounds good to you, by all means give it a try. If you're looking for something more high end, fancy, or impressive then I'm afraid you're going to need to keep on looking.
Great place to get delicious Mongolian style food for low cost. The staff is friendly and the place had a great atmosphere.

This is one of our favorites in Boise! You create your own meal so I f you aren't satisfied then it's your own fault. Prices extremely reasonable for what in get in your meal. Friendly staff and it is fun to watch the cooks put your meal together.

Lots of food for a decent amount of money, build your own bowls, decent seating area, but best to take out, freshly prepared and all the ingredients are also fresh. One of the greatest Mongolian barbecue's I've been to!

This is one of my favorite Mongolian BBQ spots. It is pretty clean, the staff is quick and courteous and the food is kept appropriately chilled while waiting to be piled into your bowl. I frequented Mongolian BBQ while pregnant, because it was the only way I could stomach vegetables. :) I love all the options here. Tons of veg (such as cabbage, pepper, onion, snap peas, carrots, broccoli, zucc) protein (pork, chicken, beef, imitation crab, bay shrimp, tofu, nuts) and other toppings (pineapple, water chestnuts, bamboo shoots, herbs). They have the standard sauces. I like to mix Mongolian BBQ, Sweet & Sour, Fire Oil, Garlic Sauce, and Lemon Juice to create a spicy, sweet, smokey yum. The last time I came, I was with a couple of girlfriends. I ordered a glass of $4 Chardonnay, thinking "Eh, whatever. The night is young". They brought me out the BIGGEST glass of chardonnay ever! Filled to the top! :) And it complemented my spicy noodles quite nicely.

Oh man! Everytime I eat Mongolian BBQ I get overstuffed and have to save the rest for a late dinner. I am so in love with these places it's almost pitiful! I went here today with a friend and had the best time ever. We say down and we watched part of the New England Patriots vs Denver Broncos game. It was a great setup for someone who is now handicappable. They made room for me and made me feel welcome. After the food was done, I was easily able to wheel into the bathroom and made it easily to the toilet. Thank you guys and gals for being so helpful!

This is a great place for good Mongolian food. The staff are friendly and super quick. This is a great place for take-out! Its quicker to get take-out at the Mongolian BBQ than at McDonald's. This is a great addition to Boise!
One of my stand by favorites. Always lots of fresh choices and vegetarian options. Great way to get your kids to eat their veggies.
Very tasty! I like that you pick and choose your ingredients. They were very accommodating for gluten free. Four gf sauces to choose from. They wiped down the grill before they cooked my dish.

Hands Down BEST Mongolian BBQ in Boise!! Clean and excellent service. The chefs were great and the food was soooooo good I had to get another order to go just to have some more at home for later!! I will be back. Thanks!!

A chill, laid back kind of dive. Quick process. The longest amount of time was spent on what I wanted in my bowl... and how to mix the sauces. The nice thing is having a chart available with suggested mixes. It's a reasonable price for an all-you-can-eat sorta thing. Or if you're not a competitive eater, they have single bowl prices. Staff is super friendly and was very attentive. Again, it's a bit of a dive, so don't expect more than a diner type of atmosphere.

I like this place. Went here for lunch today and there was a constant flow of people here. Food was delicious. Im not picky so the frozen looking meat didnt bother me. The selection of veggies n sauces was good n fresh. The staff was friendly and attentive.

I thought from the reviews this was going to be out of this world Mongolian, but alas it wasn't :( I think it's because I have been eating Hu Hot Mongolian for the past few years and well this just doesn't compare. It wasn't bad at all, but nothing special. We pribably won't go back.
This is my favorite of Boise's Mongolian Bbq restaurants. Great food, fair price, friendly long-time staff. Perfect for eating healthy!

This place is rock-steady. I was a regular eater at this place in 2005. It was great at that time. I went back in 2008 and it was the same. The only complaints I had was the decor but who in their right mind goes to an asian restaurant for the decor and ambiance anyway!! I went back in 2010 on my way back from Denver to Seattle and this place has improved. Not in the food since IMO the food was perfect but the owners have updated the interiors for the better. I will drive 7 hours to eat here, if fuel was not $3.50 :)
Excellent choices, very clean, nice staff - my only complaint was the food was undercooked. Maybe it was an off day.
Veggies were kind of brown and sauces aren't full of flavor. Service wasn't bad but the person I was with got sick a few hours after.
Great place, endless choices, satisfies every time, 3rd visit, will return again!
This place is way better then the one on Overland. Sorry it just is. Definitely will be back again.

Great for Picky Eaters because you create your own bowl. Fresh Food and Enormous Portions. Very tasty, I recommend putting more ladles of sauces then less to keep the dish moist. Be careful of putting too many jalepenos in your bowl as well. I have never been able to go back for seconds, so I usually get the mighty khan and have enough for another meal plus when I get home. Friendly people, great service. Fun restaurant because everyone gets exactly what they want. Did I mention Good for vegetarians.

Checked out this location for dinner on a Friday evening. I've been to their Nampa location, usually for lunch so I knew I liked their food. This Boise location is a little nicer on the inside, but the same great service and food. I was surprised it wasn't that busy for a Friday, but my husband and I were there around 5:30pm. The restaurant was very clean, nice decor and open feeling. And college football was on a big screen tv, but in the background. Perfect! I love that they allow you to take it to go or take home leftovers. I've been to other places that were not all-you-can-eat and didn't allow you to take leftovers. I've never revisited those places. Mongolian BBQ's leftovers are so good the next day. They do have an AYCE option, but no leftovers from that. Either way it's a great value for the food you get. There was a wide variety of vegetables that looked and tasted very fresh and with the meat (thin sliced pork, beef and chicken) and seafood (shrimp and krab mix) offerings everything was very appetizing. As usual I hardly had enough room for the goodness that is the noodles. Also, they do give you a small bowl of white rice. It was good with all the extra juices from the sauce. *My husband usually goes for lunch and said they don't offer the seafood mix during their lunch hours* The hostess and waitress we had were very welcoming and friendly. This is a bit out of the way for us, but when I'm on that side of town I'll be sure to remember my great experience. My husband is lucky enough to work near here so he'll be a continued customer (bringing me his leftovers!)

This is a great place for a quick bite. Options were plentiful, so you can definitely go healthy. Food was done quickly and efficiently. Service was good also, and they will answer questions if you have any. We did the all you can eat option and did smaller bowls to sample different flavors.

This was by far the worst Mongolian BBQ I've ever tasted. I know Mongolian BBQ places can be hit and miss, but this was a huge MISS. The staff were very friendly, which is the only reason I'm giving two stars. We did our usual routine and added the recommended amount of sauce and oil. When we tasted our food, it was as if we hadn't added any sauce at all. My husband added soy sauce and sriracha to make his more flavorful. Mine tasted like it had been seasoned with the scrapings of a charcoal grill or cigarette butts. The noodles were rubbery and the tofu was like chewing on an eraser. Again, nice enough staff, but the food was inedible. Don't waste your time at this location.
Clean, tasty, 10 bucks. That about sums it up! Plenty of room, not too crammed in like some places, booths were comfortable and clean. I would go back again!

My boyfriend and I have a little tradition of coming here after we fly back into town. It's become something I really look forward to, and it's my first feeling of "home" after being gone for a while. The staff is always friendly, and the restaurant is pretty clean. We usually catch it when it's slow, which is an added bonus. The food - awesome. There are so many options and combinations, and for how much you get, it is cheap! The chefs are great and can offer recommendations on sauces and oils if needed. I always end up going home with leftovers.
The food is phenomenal. Well I suppose that's because I pretty much make it myself. ;) Great service. I would rate this one better than the downtown one for sure. The staff is way more awesome.

Stopped by for lunch the other day. The quality of the food is fine, but as a meat-eater, it was all kind of soupy/saucy and just not very substantial. I would rather go to Haveli, just up the street and get this kind of selection plus some meat items. If you're a vegetarian and you like Indian food, this place is a good bet. Everything tasted good. I might go back again if I'm not too hungry just to see what other items might pop up.

"She may not look like much, but she's got it where it counts." Yeah, I just quoted "Star Wars" to lead off a positive review of an Indian food joint. WHAT? It's true, though. From the outside, Gokul looks like a ramshackle strip mall entity gone to pot. It's in the same tiny strip building as a check-cashing place, and that never raises my hopes for good food. But inside... oh, how I love the sweet, sweet flavors that await. The restaurant is completely vegetarian and smoke-free, so I'm always happy that I don't have to worry about what's going into my body. In addition to its regular vegetarian buffet, Gokul features a monthly vegan buffet. Honestly, if you like Indian food, you meat eaters wouldn't know or care that you weren't actually devouring flesh. No need for fake meat, either -- all the flavor is in the spices, cheese (paneer) and veggies. Gokul's buffet, which is available for lunch or dinner, isn't massive, but it's pretty balanced between roughly 6 hot, creamy dishes, one or two rice/grains, one or two breads, a bevy of fruits and vegetables and at least one dessert. I honestly have never had a bad meal here, and there's always something yummy to squeal over. Last night, I hit my personal jackpot, as vegetable korma AND paneer tikka masala was available. Usually, there's only one or the other -- along with other dishes -- when I go. To make things even better, they had one of my favorite desserts ever -- gulab jamun. Those are the little doughnut-like balls that swim in delicious honey-like syrup. It was like the Gokul folks knew I was coming! Total awesome sauce. The staff at Gokul are very friendly and take dirty plates away promptly. They're also really, really good about refilling your water glass quickly. Even better -- they show fun Bollywood movies on the big wall toward the back of the restaurant. Dinner and a movie takes on a whole new meaning here, and I adore it. Because it's on Page somewhat near Lindbergh, I only stop in when I have other tasks to take care of out in the County. I've been making a bigger point of creating errands out that way, though, just so I can visit Gokul. For about $10, you just can't go wrong.

The food is always great and the staff is always very attentive! I've been to Gokul more times than I can count and I never leave disappointed. Sometimes I leave with more Indian food in my tummy than ever thought possible, but that is a different story... Just writing about it makes me crave Gokul. The buffet is where it's at! (Not to say that carryout a-la carte menu isn't also delicious.) The food is always really good... and always 100% vegetarian. Don't let this scare you meat-eaters away!! There is not a huge selection, but that is understandable considering the size of the restaurant. And possibly the best selection on the buffet: the Gulab. They are round milk pastries soaking in a rose syrup. What a wonderful dessert! They also offer Vegan buffet twice a month, and it's usually quite busy those nights. The dishes that normally have cream contain coconut cream as a substitute... there is a faint but delicious coconut taste to those dishes. They also use tofu as a substitute for paneer. It is really worth a try, even if you are not a vegan. All of the staff are extremely friendly and helpful. Plates are never piling up on tables (even when they are busy), and your water glass almost never drops below half. And more often than not, the owner is there, working along with the rest of the staff. It may be hard to find the first time you go, but it won't be somewhere you forget. I would give this restaurant 6 stars, if I could.

A great place to eat at 8pm on Christmas after arriving at the airport -- partly because it was open, but also because it was delicious, the staff was friendly, and a hilarious Bollywood film was projected on the wall. It was such a good experience that I even forgot that there was no meat in any of the dishes.

Ahh, memories of my first trip to Devon Street in Chicago. Places like this are a dime a dozen (seemingly) up there, but alas St. Louis has only one. The best part is that is is all vegetarian, so us veggie lovers can let our guards down. The bad part is that the location is not convenient for us city dwellers. If it was in my neighborhood, I would be here every week! Like the other reviewers state, this is a casual buffet-only place. The buffet items are usually pretty fresh and always pretty good. I was there recently and the Bollywood movies were on!

This is the best food in St. Louis. Period. I have moved in and out of St Louis over the past 7 years and Gokul is always the thing I miss most! Now with young children it is hard for us to get out to eat, and my husband will drive almost 30 minutes each way to get take out from here! I find the food at the Page location to be tastier (read: spicier) than the Delmar location. Possibly not a good choice if you can't stand any spice. They do have the basic non-spicy choices (Korma, etc) but their Palak Paneer and Tikka Masala are spicier than what you would get at a more Americanized establishment.

Good flavorful food. The naan is good...a little different than other places yet warm and flavorful. I would not say its the largest buffet selection in StL but what they have is very good. Inside is bigger than it looks from outside. Service is attentive but not overbearing. Love the fried papad. Top it off w/ a little sweet vermicelli pudding. Definitely a great place for some Indian/vegan lunch.

My family and I love going to Gokul quite regularly, especially for their vegan buffet (trust me--you won't miss the milk!). The selection is always huge and the food is very fresh, including an entire half of the buffet filled with chutneys and salads. One of my favourite dishes is the Saag Paneer and there is a soup on there most days with black beans and cinnamon that is not to be missed. The vegetable korma made with soymilk on vegan night is quite yummy too. They try to have different veggie items, to keep things interesting. As we're eating, the waitstaff will often bring a basket of fresh naan to the table. They also have had a Valentine's day special where I got a chance to try this drink called a "faluda." Really different and exotic!
Fast and delicious vegetarian Indian food in a casual, smoke free environment. Try the lunch buffet to sample a variety of dishes - everything we've tried has been excellent.

What a rip off!! Very horrible experience. Simply avoid this place as there are much better restaurants in St. Louis. I have been to dozens of indian restaurants but very unhappy with the quality of their food. They need some lessons on how to please their customers so that they can come back again and again. Paid twice the buffet price for a box of carry out food, a total ripoff!!

I love 5 star establishments. This place deserves more than 5 stars. I ate here on Wednesday Evening for the first time while on a business trip. The South Indian buffet was second to none. The quality rivaled the best I have found in California and/or New York. Every dish was fresh, seasoned meticulously and prepared like I was in Mumbai. I was blown away! Even the faluda (rosewater yogurt shake) was amazing. Their gulab jamon for desert rivaled some of the best across India. If you crave South Indian cuisine you must try this place. The service is amazing as well as these are really nice people. I may return soon to St. Louis just to eat here!

You can drive by this place every day on the way to work and not pay any attention to it, but it's a jewel. They do sell authentic Indian sweets, but it is mostly a restaurant. They feature a buffet for lunch which is very inexpensive - ends up as 8 something after tax. The inside is a bit higher class than you might expect from the average indian buffet joint - you get real napkins! It's well decorated and clean. The food served is generally not spicy, but is well seasoned, a lot of the dishes have a sweeter taste to them. I like it a lot, it is different than some other Indian places I have been to. Selection is small. Last lunch trip there were 4 main dishes to choose from, in addition to naan and rice. The yogurt/sauces/vegetable section is quite good though. Big note: The place is vegetarian, BUT that is hard to notice since the flavors are so good, and there is a protein replacement in the dishes - like paneer or beans. I like it a lot. If the selection was bigger, this place would be an easy 5.

Holy schneikes!!! I am a recent convert to Indian food and really hadn't been anywhere other than Taj since discovering how much I like the stuff. I know this is odd but they are local and convenient and somehow I hadn't branched out until the wife suggested we try Gokul. Equally odd is the fact that I am far from being a vegetarian but somehow my favorite Indian dishes are all vegetarian. I really, really enjoyed this place. Everything was freshly prepared and extremely flavorful. The woman running the front of the house was incredibly warm and inviting and took a fair amount of time to explain her restaurant and their offerings to us...something I always appreciate! Prices are very reasonable and not a bad bite on the entire buffet. I will most certainly be back!
vegeterian food , good taste try there weekend buffet

This place is the greatest dining friend for a vegan. Not only is it 100% vegetarian to start with so you know there aren't any issues with animal products being on the premises, but they'll make any of the dishes as vegan as well. Also...they do have vegan nights on Mondays (I think for their buffet), I was there once for their buffet at lunch time. They were kind enough to point out which items were vegan and would have gladly brought me out vegan naan, though I declined the offer. To my surprise, and without asking, they brought out a portion of Mattar Paneer that they made vegan for me substituting coconut milk for yogurt and tofu for the cheese. It was simply amazing.

This place is fantastic, and the food was surprisingly fresh and tasty. The chef, Nase (sp?), brought out round after round of tasty treats. I am a carnivore, but I loved the vegetarian choices. Try Delhi's Chaat. It is like Indian Nachos. The Sev Puri are rocking little crispy things stuffed with all kinds of sweet and savory goodness.

Gokul might be my favorite restaurant ever! Back when I went to school in St. Louis, I had a standard dish: spicy veg korma and maybe some naan. It was just sooooo delicious. Now, I live in Houston, which has plenty of cheap and divey Indian restaurants, but none as flavorful as this place! I miss you, Gokul! I'll try to come back soon!

Since my last review, I've taken at least five new people to Gokul (a few of them multiple times!) and have returned umpteen times alone. The situation is the same - Gokul is the shiznit, yo. I always leave with a full tummy and a satiated sweet tooth (mmmmm... galub jamin *drool*), and my meat-eating friends ALWAYS remark that they don't miss meat at this all-vegetarian restaurant. As a cheese and cream lover, I still tend to avoid vegan nights, but I hear it's pretty rad in its own way. It seems that fewer Bollywood movies are screened, but that's not worth a star demerit in the ratings. Keep up the great work, Gokul!

I hate this place. Previous day stale food, over cooked and unnecessary use of ginger garlic paste in the food. This place is over rated because people actually never eaten good Indian food. Trust me this is worst and unhygienic food. Hated the attitude of cook who is also the manager who runs this place.

Had lunch here with the Husband yesterday. Have been wanting to try this place for awhile, but it's by my office and there's not a snowballs chance in Hell that anyone I work with would agree to eat lunch here. Their loss, for sure! They have a vegetarian lunch buffet for only $7.99! Lots of selection including salad, appetizers, main courses, and desserts. The lady who runs the place is super-nice. When I told her it was my first time there, she proceeded to whip up a couple of their menu item appetizers using the buffet ingredients. OMG were they good, and I never would have thought of putting those things together myself. I always wonder when I am at foreign food buffets if people are giggling at me because I'm not eating the food in the right combinations or something. Probably so, but who cares?! Their naan is also noteworthy. It is soft on the inside with a crispy outside and SOO delicious. I asked the lady why theirs is so good and she said it was because they make it vegetarian. It's ridiculous how much I like meat, so the fact that I am into this vegetarian place should speak volumes about how tasty the food is. Seriously, you have to try this place. And tell the lady that you are new so she will whip up the appetizers for you. She is so nice she probably would anyway, even if she recognizes you as a regular.

Went to Gokul with my fiance for the lunch buffet. I am Indian - originally South Indian but grew up in Maharashtra which is more like central/North India, hence I am familiar with, and enjoy both South and North Indian cuisines. Since I moved to St. Louis from NY, the hunt has been on for awesome and authentic Indian restaurants. We have been frequenting Mayuri for a while, and I like Mayuri quite a lot. This time we decided to try Gokul on Page Ave for a change (well, mostly since we had eaten at Mayuri the previous day :-) ). From outside, the place doesnt give you much hope for great food...but as foodies know, never go by the exteriors. Upon entering, we encountered a neat little space with a buffet awaiting us. Now to the food - it was excellent. I was super excited to see "Pav Bhaji" in the line up, along with Indian snacks such as chaat, bhel puri, pani puri etc. The Pav Bhaji did not disappoint, it was as tasty as it would be back home (in India). They were also thoughtful enough to add chopped onions and lime wedges in the buffet line up, which go very well sprinkled on the bhaji. The sambar ( a very typical South Indian dish that not everyone can do justice to) was delicious. It was flavorful and with lots of vegetables, unlike the sambar I encountered at Mayuri on our last two visits which was too "watery". The chhole or chickpeas curry reminded me of my mother's chhole, I dont think I need to say more. I also tried a couple of other dishes like the navratan korma and I dont have anything bad to say about them.
