I could not taste all the dishes there, because I had to go for second servings of the Pav Bhaji - however, we will sure be going back very soon. People- enjoy this authentic vegetarian Indian food.

Good, inexpensive vegetarian Indian food. We came late... about 30 minutes before close and the items on the buffet still tasted fresh. In fact, they made more naan while were there even though it was clear that we would be the last 2 in for the night. They only had about 4-5 entrees in the buffet, plus a few sides, but it's clear based on the other reviews, that these change each day. All 4 dishes were very good, even though I didn't know their names. I felt a bit rushed as they were going through their closing procedures while we were there, but I should no better than to go into a restaurant 30 minutes before close.

Yum! The vegan naan is awesome... and even my husband who can have dairy loves the vegan buffet. Also, the service here is awesome. We went in around 3 (after lunch and before dinner) and they made us fresh naan and made sure that the buffet was fresh. We will be going back as many Mondays as possible.
Quite good. I highly recommend. The food is a little confusing if you haven't had this before but the staff are helpful in recommending.

We came here after a morning of rock climbing nearby on a Saturday, the buffet certainly hit the spot after a fun few hours of climbing. We really enjoyed the all vegetarian buffet. Every dish we had were superbly flavorful and not too spicy. The mini dosai's were just the right size allowing you to eat other things too. The paneer was firm on the outside and tender on the inside! Great vegetarian place! Will be back again!

It looks sketchy and cheap. It's in a terrible location (for me). And I'm neither a vegan nor a vegetarian. But I will drive 30 minutes to get to this great little hole in the wall, specifically for their buffet. Their staff is friendly, and the last time I was in they had a Bollywood movie projected and playing on one of the walls. They know what they're doing, and happily (for them) it's getting around. Make sure a Googlemap this place first if you've never been. It's pretty easy to miss amid the dozens of stripmall joints on this section of Page. Check this place out... it's a winner!

A friend of mine told me about this place about a year ago, and I hate to admit I was skepitcal. I love indian food and usually frequent closer establishments like House of India, but when I tried this all vegetarian Indian house of yummy-ness-let's just say the ride down Page doesn't turn me off anymore. I don't know the names of any dishes, so you may not find this review any help at all, but hopfeully you can trust that everything I ate was FANTASTIC! And the drinks-YUM, YUM! I had a sugar cane drink with lemon and ginger and it was clean and crisp and super yummy. My friend had the coconut drink, also very tasty. They have a special drink that has noodles in it, it seem very interesting and I would like to try it next time. Our server ( I use the term loosely because the restaurant serves off a buffet every day, but you are always welcome to order off the menu as well) made us indian nachos. UM, they were SO good that If that's all I ate, I would have been totally fine. They had chick peas, kidney beans, some sort of inidan sauces all atop those yuumy little fried crunchy strips, you must try them, spicy and sweet. SOOOO good. And back to the buffet, I've been there during the week and the weekend. IT seems that there is a bigger spread with more variety on the weekend. They also deliver AND to my area, so I WAS even happier!! Though, I have yet to utilize those services.

This place is the joint. It is without a doubt, the best fast food Indian buffet in the St Louis area. The cutlery isn't the finest, but the cuisine makes up for it. I've only been twice, but both times were the charm. The pakora isn't dry like a lot of restaurants and it is FULLY vegetarian. I don't have to pass fake-indian-wannabee-chicken tikki masala to get to the delicious veggie korma or those excellent potatoes. Some of the food on the line isn't super standard or familiar, but that just means they know how to diversify and experiment. And, they actually don't over salt the food like Rasoi (not bashing Rasoi, but y'all know y'all need to keep the salt shaker upright a little more often). The only complaint is that it's far. Not like Taiwan far, but not a Metrolink stop away either. It would be great if they opened up something in the Indian-hating Loop (yes, I said it. Joe Edwards prices out all the Indians. Chipotle anyone?).

Vegetarians and Indian food lovers rejoice! I came here for their lunch buffet, on the recommendation of a friend who really knows his Indian food. I was a bit skeptical (I'm one of those people who always, always orders chicken tikka masala at Indian restaurants and I am not ashamed), but the food completely blew me away. Pro-tip: try the food that you've never heard of before. Sure, their paneer tikka masala is tasty, and their veggie korma is good, but the best stuff at the buffet were the other things. There were three dals available and all of them were fantastic. There were also a few chickpea dishes which were absolutely delicious. Being adventurous at this place will reward you, I promise. At $8, the lunch buffet is also a great deal. They have a huge selection, there were at least 10 main dish options and an entire buffet cart with just sauces and condiments. You won't miss the meat at all.

Wow, I really love this place. I have been back a few more times since my previous review. I am always impressed with how delicious their lunch buffet is. I can't even try to explain the different things I have tried here because they are all good and I can't remember the names for the life of me. But I will say that the cashew dish is my absolute fave. Mmmffff! Also the owner is really nice and he brought my friend and I some "Indian nachos" to try when I inquired about one of the buffet items. When we came for the dinner buffet they were playing the movie "My Name is Khan" and we got to watch that while dining. (It's a really good movie.) I want to come back here a thousand million tiiiimes! I have never loved vegetarian food so much in my whole life! o.o;

I confess....I'm not a vegetarian, not even a closet vegetarian. While I thought the buffet was good, I felt like something was missing.....namely meat (but i can't judge a vegan restaurant on that now can I). Hence, this review is more targeted at the sweets Gokul sells by the box at the table inside the entrance. I can't exactly keep my hands off the Mango Burfi!!! You get about eight chunks of them in a plastic container. (I think they sell by pound and by half pound) It was so rich and delicious! If you like mango flavors and sweets in a solid form, you have got to buy a box and try it out yourself.

MS T, another co-worker and I visited Gokul for lunch. The co-worker has been there several times and I have been there twice now. It is very convenient to our place of work. Prices are reasonable and the restaurant is bright and clean. We all chose to have the lunch buffet. I tend to eat way too much at Indian lunch buffets so I really don't need a huge selection to be well satisfied. The buffet is not extensive, but was certainly more than adequate. We were there somewhat early and all of the dishes were fresh and hot. I enjoyed my usual dal makhani along with vegetable khorma, two to three other dishes and plenty of naan and rice. It seems that dal makhani is different everywhere. This version was thinner than I normally see, but was subtly spiced and good. I loved the channa sag dish. It was creamy, well spiced and the channa just melted in you mouth. This along with some rice would be all I need. They also had a cabbage dish with some potato and onion, again excellent and a nice contrast to the more creamy curry style dishes. The vegetable korma was very rich and good each time. There are a number of things I am not mentioning; salads, desserts, pakoras, and of course naan. The coriander chutney was nicely spicy. I am not vegetarian but always enjoy Indian vegetarian dishes. I found Gokul's food to be tasty and satisfying. I can certainly recommend it for vegetarian lunch. I plan to take Ms. T back for dinner some time and we will order from the menu which is quite extensive.

This place is great! It's a fully vegetarian indian restaurant and they have a fully vegan buffet about once a month - sign up for their emails and they'll email you with dates of the vegan buffets. The food comes quickly, isn't too exepensive, and the staff members are GREAT! The food is very good, I especially love the aloo gobi. Did I also mention they usually have a movie every night (awesome Bollywood movies)??? Yes that's right folks, you get dinner and a movie here! I love Gokul!

I love this place. Usually, I get Chaat there -- indian snack foods that make my heart sing! I love getting the Dahi Puri, Bhel Puri, and the Samosa Chaat. :) They're my favorites. They also have a buffet -- which tends to be good, but sometimes they don't always have enough food. Check first before eating. The service is somewhat slow -- the main reason it didn't get 5 stars but all in all it's a great place for delicious food. : ) Be ware, it's easy to miss when you're driving... so take careful notice.

I love Gokul. I moved to Saint Louis a year ago and Gokul has been my place to go for Indian food cravings. The taste is very authentic Gujarati/North-Indian style, and it is a pure vegetarian place. They have buffet for both lunch and dinner. I love their Samosas and pick them up every now and then. The only downside would be their fairly predictable items for the buffet.

I am Indian food lover and this is the place where I had worst Indian food ever. The food in the buffet was cold. I order chikoo milkshake they described milkshake come with ice-cream but when I order there was no ice cream, after having that milkshake my throat started hurting and I had to get allergy medicine. I had chikoo milkshake before at other places but never had this bad experience before. I did not like any of the dish in buffet. I had to cooked at home after coming back from this place as no one ate anything. I read the review on this restaurants and went there thinking this might be good place for vegetarian but really if you like Indian this is not what you are looking for. There are other Indian restaurants in town and they have good vegetarian compare to this restaurant.
Great food. Chef made Jain spicy chana masala. Which was so good that reminded me chana puri dish from Havemore restaurant in Ahmedabad India.

I love this place! Buffet is amazing! Best Veggi Korma...hands down! The service is great too. They have given my son free mango juice several times! I cannot say enough good about this place. I am not a vegetarian but this restaurant is but it is so damn good that meat would gild the lily.

Tasty vegetarian Indian buffet. Friendly owners and a pleasant restaurant. However, they are closing May 12, 2014 and moving to a new location . The photo has a note from the owner inviting you to his new location at 6101 Delmar (Loop) .

My wife talked me into going. She had a good friend in town who was a vegetarian. Now I consider myself to be a meat eater extraordinaire, so I was not looking forward to going here. But you know what they say "happy wife... happy life". When we arrive it is a small place in a small strip mall type building. I went there not expecting to be impressed. The night we went they had a vegetarian buffet. The food was outstanding, very flavorful. And the nan was great. The biggest compliment I can give is that I would definitely go back.

I went here for the second time today with my sister, for their Saturday lunch buffet, and the selection was a bit different, but everything was equally as amazing! I love a good indian buffet, but sometimes it's hard to tell whether or not things are vegetarian, and the number of vegetarian options is always much less than at Gokul. It's so nice to pick up a dosa (filled crepe) from the buffet and not worry about finding flesh when biting into it! So nice for a vegetarian like myself, and so rare! Also, while some things are spicy at Gokul, everything doesn't burn my mouth out the way that a lot of indian food tends to do. If I have to drink so much water that I'm in the bathroom more than once, we have a problem. The owner was there today, and he personally showed me how to assemble "indian nachos," a mixture of fried pita chip like dough, potatoes, chickpeas, onions, mint chutney, tamarind chutney, and yogurt sauce, with a brown mixture of spices (not spicy but very flavorful) on top. Delicious! He also insisted I let him personally make me some dishes the indian way next time, probably because my sister and I were the only non-indian people there (know what that means? it's authentic!), and he found me aimlessly wandering the left side of the buffet trying to make sense of some of it. They had puri, crisp tortilla pieces (for nachos), puffed rice, pickled red onions, cucumbers, and carrots, tamarind sauce (sweet), mint chutney (a bit spicy), yogurt sauce (a nice cool down), rice pudding, white onions, and a cold potato and chickpea mixture on the left side of the buffet. And on the right side, they had naan, sambar, dal, vegetable korma, matar paneer, saag (creamy spinach), spicy potatoes, an eggplant and potato dish, and 2 kinds of rice (plain basmati rice, and basmati rice with vegetables). The left side seems to be consistently the same, while the right side changes. But there is clearly a huge selection, and everything was sooo tasty! My only gripe is with the atmosphere. It's not the prettiest place I've ever eaten for sure, and the bathroom is sketchy to say the least. And while the food more than makes up for it, I'm really looking forward to their new location in the loop, where Miss Saigon used to be!

In honor of my ROTD yesterday I think I should update my review to add that I tried their vegan buffet last Monday and it was pretty dang good. I really had no idea what to expect from it. Vegan food to me sounds like an oxymoron since I consider animal products to be food, and from a vegan perspective, it's not food. LOL. But that aside, I am open-minded when it comes to trying new cuisine and since I positively adore their vegetarian buffet, I thought I'd give the vegan buffet a shot. Elle P. went with me and so did Sean H. but he pretty much just watched us eat because Indian food alone is pretty gross to him, Indian food + vegetarian alone is extra gross to him, and VEGAN Indian food? Let's not even go there, lol. My favorite dish was still the yellow korma stuff with the cashews in it, and my least favorite dish was the spinach saag. I think they had to use some kind of fake cream stuff to make the saag or maybe it was some soy based thing....I dunno. It was just nasty. I took one bite and nearly barfed. I positively cannot stand the flavor of whatever was in that saag. I should have asked the owner so I know to avoid whatever that ingredient is. It has a distinctive milky flavor but it's not really milk. Ugh. But the korma was SO good. Also I tried about 3-4 other dishes with mostly beans and potatoes as the main ingredient and it was sooooo tasty. For dessert I noticed they had "cream of wheat" according to the sign. I tried some and it was so tasty! More like a cake than cream of wheat. A little dry, but still so good. Cinnamon was the predominant flavor in this dessert. So satisfying and I didn't feel quite as guilty later. I also was not really sick the next day which might have been a coincidence as I pretty much ate nothing apart from the buffet that day, but maybe it was due to the lack of cream. I rarely get ill the next day from their vegetarian buffet alone, though. Haveli's food makes me sick more often (I still love it though) but that would probably be due to the amount of spice they put in compared w/ Gokul. The vegan buffet was noticeably LESS spicier IMHO than the normal buffet.

pure goodness! I love meat, but Gokul was hardly a compromise. Gokul's food is packed with flavor. we got the roasted eggplant and the the veggie korma(the korma spicy and the eggplant extra spicy, and by extra spicy they do mean extra authentic spicy.)

We found ourselves in St. Louis for a family funeral this past weekend, and had Gokul cater the dinner after the wake. Obviously this was a tough time for everyone in the family, but having food that comforted our collective Sri Lankan souls was for that reason so much more important. Everything from the pakoras and vadas to the various curries (matter paneer, channa saag) and rice were flavorful and fragrant, and the service was just right. Everything is vegetarian, by the way. When I was talking to the owner (who was on hand), he asked me how long I'd be in town. I told him just until Sunday, and he said, "Well then you'll have time to come in for a full meal." You gotta like that.

Giokul Is fantastic. The food is always good and prepared fresh. One thing that stands is the food is not overly spicy. Sometimes I want to taste the food and not just a mouth full of heat. If you like tasty Indian food try this place it is one of the best Indian restaurants in the STL area. Also the buffet is very well priced. I wish I could eat there everyday.

Gokul is one of the few all veg restaurants in St. Louis. I went today for the first time in a few months and was presently surprised! They updated their decor, added some table cloths and replaced the styrofoam plates with real ones! There was even a nice man to bring you drinks instead of using the old water cooler they had. Sometimes when a restaurant updates the decor, they lose out on the quality of food and/or increase the prices. This is not so at Gokul. The food as just as fantastic as always and the prices did not go up from what I could tell. You really do not need to be a veg to enjoy this place. It's some of the best Indian I've ever had.

I came back tonight for Gokul's twice-monthly vegan night! The Page location has vegan night every 1st and 3rd Monday of the month. The selections are great. Lots of hearty dishes that will leave you feeling deliciously satisfied. And vegan naan! Score. :) I loved pretty much everything I put on my plate. I have a hard time remembering the names of all of the dishes, however; there were a few potato dishes, a yellow daal, channa masala, and tons more. Service here is pretty friendly as well. Gokul gets my stamp of approval for sure!

again, though gokul presents decent food, the freshness of the ingredients is suspect, and the /quantity/ of the vegetables in the dishes left us wanting much more, particularly considering this is a 100% vegetarian restaurant.

A very solid three stars. It was nice to visit a mom and pop place that has so many local fans. Gokul was packed around 1:15 on a Saturday afternoon. The atmosphere is homey and the buffet features a very wide array of food. The food was fine. Nothing spectacular. In my opinion, there are tastier Indian/South Asian buffets in St Louis. For example, the Daal was watery and not as flavorful as I've had in other restaurants in town. I can see why vegetarians are so excited about Gokul. Where else can you go and have such a wide variety of vegetarian dishes? But the novelty of a meatless buffet doesn't make up for the fact that the food isn't quite as fine or flavorful as some other places (and no, I'm not referring to the flavor of meat, I'm referring to vegetarian dishes I've had at other restaurants). If I lived closer to Gokul or if I found myself in the neighborhood, I'd definitely be back. I doubt, however, that I'd ever make the trip to that part of the County again just for that buffet.

I have visited this restaurant 3-4 times but every time there has been some problem but this last visit made sure that I will never go to this place.The restaurant is open till 9.30pm on Thursday,we reached there at 8.25pm.We were seated at the table and while serving water the server says that we close the buffet at 8.35pm, I mean how do you expect that we would finish our dinner in 5-10mins in a restaurant serving buffet.Then we asked for a la carte at that point the server says "We don't serve now as its 8.30pm ,we only do carry outs" I mean if you say the restaurant is open till 9.30 and close the kitchen at 8.30 then why were we taken to be seated??? What was the point? The manager and the staff no one even apologized when we left the restaurant. Such arrogant server and such service, no wonder have never seen this place fully occupied even though this is the only place serving vegan in our area.
I'm not sure why gokul has such high ratings. It's ok, the people are friendly, and they have a buffet for dinner, which is a plus, but house of India is much better.

Ms T and I met Mr B for lunch recently and I continue to maintain my strong rating for the lunch buffet at Gokul. I won't go into the list of items offered, I know it varies from day to day. There were too many to try and everything I ate was nicely seasoned and very good. I am not a vegetarian, but I really enjoy vegetarian Indian and always eat way more than I should. The bhindi masala was particularly good on this day.

This place is a little hard to pinpoint - thank goodness for my iPhone/GPS/gadgetry. Or maybe it was because I was (ever so slightly) hungover. No, it's hard to find. My friend never would have found it if I hadn't been wearing a magenta shirt and waving frantically to her driving up and down the street. But my hangover definitely helped me eat my money's worth. The food is delicious. Vegetable korma and saag were my faves, along with their rice and assorted potato goodness. Did I mention it's cheap? Next time I'll try the faluda. By the time I seriously considered a beverage, I was well on my way to fulfilling my daily caloric allotment. In case you have trouble finding it, there's a check cashing place adjoining, an Indian grocery on the other side (not adjoining) and kitty-corner from Walgreens (on Warson). Good luck. I'm not hungover anymore.

Gokul is my absolute favorite Indian restaurant, so I feel a little blasphemous for this review. Sadly, I went on a Thursday evening, and it was a little disappointing. There were only two occupied tables, but they were slow refilling things at the buffet. They were also very slow at refilling water. My friend asked for some more water (her glass was completely empty), and it took at least 15 minutes for someone to come back. By then, we were the only table and finished eating. We would've asked again, but everyone disappeared during that time. The food was still good, though... except the potatoes in the korma were still mostly raw. Since the Delmar location has opened, there seems to have been a decline in the quality of the Page location. Again, I feel absolutely blasphemous! I will definitely go back. I am not giving up so easily. But I may try on a night I know they will be busy... like one of the delicious vegan nights. Food was 4 stars. Service was 1 star. Very sad, considering I've had many, many 5 & 5 experiences there.

Daaaaaaaaaaaaaang. "You won't miss the meat" has never been so true. I was hesitant to try this place as I am a self-proclaimed "meatitarian." But wow. Just wow. So tasty! They have so many different things on the menu and I can't even remember what they were called but I just know that I loved most of what I tried! It's about $8 or so for the lunch buffet and it was so worth it. I ate my fill and felt very satisfied but not super ill afterwards. I don't think that just because this place is veg that it is necessarily "healthier" though. I mean, damn, most of what I ate was swimming in heavy cream sauce, lol. BUT it wasn't super spicy like other places and I didn't have severe indigestion later or pain in the bathroom the next day. LOL. TMI. But yeah...the only spicy thing was the mint chutney stuff which disappointed me because I love mint chutney and I really could not eat this stuff! Basically it's true what other reviewers have said--the more adventurous you are willing to be here, the more you will be rewarded! Also the naan here is EFFING AMAZING it's soft and pillowy and hot and tasty and unfff. I ate four pieces and I regret nothing! NOTHING! The lemon rice was a hit for me but I wish they had veggie rice like at Haveli. I still love Haveli though and I would probably go back to both places equally. It's hard for me to say which Indian buffet is my favorite in town because I love Indian food so much that all of them area good in my eyes...!! Also, oh the irony. I just wrote a review for a steakhouse and now Gokul. Proof that I will never break out of my meat-itarian ways! :P

I was craving some Indian food and so headed out to Gokul as soon as I landed in St. Louis for a business meeting. Gokul did not disappoint. Got my fix of good desi chat (snacks). Had some Pav Bhaji and Dahi Puri. Both were excellent. Also, tried their Rose Water faluda which just brought back memories of Juhu beach. This is a stereotypical Desi snack house - loud bollywood music, videos being projected on a wall and the requisite college kids mass consuming the buffet. Expect good food and a noisy fast-food like atmosphere.

LOVE LOVE LOVE! It is hard to find a place that can make indian tea....not here! So yummy. The food was un-matchable by other indian places I have visited. The sampler (not the real name, but what I will call it) was amazing. Way too much food for one person. I would love to go on a day that the buffet was up and running just to try more options.

I came here the other night with Allison B. and it was great! It had been a while since I last visited Gokul, so it was a blast from the past for me. :) I'm doing a vegan challenge this month, so I could only partake in the animal-free products. No worries -- they had plenty for me to choose from! The wonderful woman working there pointed out all of the vegan things for me, which was nice. She then informed me that the naan was NOT vegan (sadface!) but that she would bring out some vegan naan (happyface!) Everything was delicious. And the fact that the waitress brought out some vegan naan to the table made me very happy!

One wouldn't expect to find a 100% vegetarian Indian restaurant flanked by payday loan joints on Page, but yet it stands! You can order off the menu here, but unlike most places they run DINNER buffets, and they are both excellent and inexpensive. Casual, group-friendly, kid-friendly, and a fun ambiance that includes Bollywood movies projected onto one of the walls. While there are constants like vegetable korma at the buffet there's still a notable amount of variety from visit to visit. Also has a chaat bar, a first for me in STL. Go. Experiment. And don't be a wimp if you're a meat-eater - vegetarian or not, this is just great food!

My friend and I just happened to find this place while picking up groceries at the Indian store across the street. I was highly disappointed, initially, when I learned this place was vegetarian (I am a total carnivore!). I then saw that they served Samosa chaat and I was suddenly super excited. The samosa chaat here is amazing and only $6.99! I also tried the aloo and gobi dish which wasn't anything to write home about and was a little expensive for the amount of food you receive. You have to go out and try the Samosa Chaat!!

Don't miss this place for fresh tender coconut water if u are at St. Louis Arch visit. This place ultimate Chaats being served too. Hostess is very friendly and courteous and thus adds charm to ur dining experience.

I've only been there once, but I did enjoy it. The atmosphere is anything but normal though, as an Indian movie was playing loudly on the one wall big enough to act as a screen. For the record, I prefer fountain soda as well, no cans.
I've been here twice. The first time it was delicious! The second time it was only ok and their food made me ill. Haven't been back since.

Best Indian food in town and certainly the most gracious and friendly staff as well. In a nut shell - great staff, best value (quality & quantity), quick and casual without degrading the service or quality of the food. In greater detail - I should confess upfront that my family and I are Gokulophiles (I've probably eaten here 80 - 100 times) and that may have something to do with the the 5 stars (chicken or egg?). Also, our experience is specific to the Page & Warson location. We've been to the Delmar location and found that, while it's good and represents the brand well, we found ourselves missing the staff and comforts of the original location. The staff genuinely care about the presentation of the restaurant, the freshness of the food and helping novices find something they will want to eat again and again. The buffet is a great way to try many things in one visit and the options are consistently good. The Vegetable Korma, Saag Paneer and Naan bread are a few of our favorite items. Ordering from the menu bring even more diversity of choice - the Samosa Chaat or Ragda and Malai Kofta always satisfy. The location and storefront are misleading (looks smallish and is next to a payday loan store), but once inside, you'll be impressed with the detail in the decoration, the cleanliness.

Nothing to see. Move it along. Gokul hasn't changed - and that's a GOOD thing. The same great food is available on that fabulous buffet, and there's a chance that the paneer tikka masala has even improved a bit (as if that were possible). Even though my foot was broken for three months, I still was determined to eat at Gokul. Friends fetched food for me while I hobbled around on crutches and pointed out what I wanted. Meanwhile, the ever-friendly staff recognized me from all my visits and took an interest in my health. Fast forward to this week, when I dined at Gokul crutch-free for the first time in a month with Stephanie S. They had my two favorite dishes - the paneer and the vegetable korma - as well as lemon rice with raisins and nuts and the cabbage/potato dish. Moreover, the staff brought us baskets of hot, fresh naan (even though there was naan on the buffet) and constantly filled our water glasses. And when it came time to pay, the cashier remarked that it was great to see me without crutches again and asked how I was doing. Honestly, it astounds me that they remember me, but it truly warms the heart. Great food and great people - Gokul is exactly what a restaurant should be.

I've been a fan of Gokul since 2003 when the Page location was a mere hole in the wall filled with computer geeks, styrofoam plates, beautiful Indian women, and tasty food. While the food is just as great, the atmosphere is totally different now and is much more inviting. The prices have stayed the same which is awesome. Vegan night is amazing! They are very friendly and you can tell that the staff is dedicated to a great dining experience. The pakoras are the best in town!!!
My favorite restaurant in StL. Period. Inexpensive and incredible tasting vegetarian buffet. Very vegan friendly, open every day, and always happy to see you. If you haven't been, you're missing out.

Lunch here was fantastic. I had a 4 hour layover at the airport and decided to get a cheap $15 rental car and roam around a bit. Got a haircut at Great Clips and went searching for some good Indian food! It was great. All vegetarian, try the chaats, samosas, and pakoras.

A rare vegetarin-only restaurant in St. Louis County, whoo hoo! Thankfully Gokul has recently redecorated and lost the horribly vertigo-inducing movie-projection on the back wall. Much much nicer now. The food is quite good. Mid-week lunch buffet tastes a bit "leftover", but the navratan korma is delicious. Naan could be a bit fresher, rice, while a jasmine, is good but too sticky for proper indian. If you are lucky to arrive on a masala dosa buffet day, count yourself lucky, it's my favorite!

Very unhappy with my recent experience at the Resturant. I ordered Sev Puri and it had very strong Garlic sauce. When complaint about the sauce the managers says "Other People loved it". I could not even have second bite from the Sev Puri. Despite me complaining " The manager charges for the Sev Puri in bill even if I rejected" The manager was rude and will not even accept mistakes. Food in the Buffet is always reheated. I wonder it is cooked fresh or previous day food. Looking at the number of people visiting the restaurant, I doubt whether food is changed on daily-basis. This will be my last visit and never again I would not recommend anyone to this horrible restuarant. The resturant has scope of improvement provide they change their thinking process and learn how to speak to their customers good if they complaint.

OMG. Omg! My new favorite Indian restaurant!!! Yes, I said it. I LOVE THIS PLACE. So my friend and I drove past the other branch on Delmar a few days ago, and planned on trying it sometime soon. However, earlier today I was in the Maryland Heights area for work and was craving some Indian food for lunch. I pulled out my good old Yelp app and was excited to find that a Gokul Snacks & Sweets was only a mile away. I got there in time for the lunch buffet. Here's the scoop: Lunch buffet is from 11:30am - 3pm. $7.99 Dinner buffet is from 3pm-close. $9.99 This place is 100% vegetarian, and serves vegan food on the weekend. Pricing is the same on the weekend (I think it's $9.99, but it could been a bit more-don't quote me on that). They have a wider food selection on the weekend. The only differences between this branch and the one on Delmar is that the Delmar one is Kosher in addition to being vegetarian, and is a bit pricier. Now, on to the food!! It was nothing short of amazing. I mean, seriously. The BEST vegetable korma I ever had. That was my favorite item in the buffet. I was really in the mood for some chicken tikka masala, but the paneer tikka masala really hit the spot well. What I found interesting was that the daal makhni (creamed lentils) was not really that creamy, but still tasted very good. The aloo zucchini was good as well. I love their naan! Tasted very buttery, but it wasn't oily at all. It worked so well with the paneer tikka masala. It was all so good that I managed to gobble down two plates all by myself. For dessert, I had the rice pudding, which was not overly sweet or thick/heavy. The gulab jamun are bite size and are another good option for desert. DEFINITELY give this place a try if you like Indian food, whether you're a vegetarian or not. Meat lovers, you won't be disappointed, I promise. Happy eating!

My husband and I have gone to Gokul on Page for a few years now, but for the past year we've primarily ordered takeout. That's where this establishment shoots itself in the foot -- BIG TIME. Their customer service for takeout orders completely cancels out the deliciousness of their food (hence the two-star rating). It started with three bad experiences related to wait time. Two of those three times I had ordered online, via Gokul's website. And when I or my husband arrived to pick up our order, we either had to wait over 15 minutes for the order or Gokul staff never received it at all, which caused a wait time of 40 minutes and resulted in a frustrated husband who gave up altogether on dinner that night. The third time I chose to call in because their website proved unreliable. But even then when I arrived to pick up my food, it was not ready. I complained to the woman behind the counter about the recurring issue. She was apologetic as well as argumentative, providing excuses for the delays. Lastly and most aggravating, the staff at Gokul on Page outright LIES to you, specifically when you request extra chutney in your takeout order. This has been our experience all the time and it is the very reason I'm writing this critical review. I now open my bag to verify they included extra chutney and have caught them in the lie again and again. My husband goes off their word only to be angry when he gets home. I simply cannot comprehend the reason for such a lie. If they want me to pay extra for my request, they should ask. But lying about 20 cents worth of chutney is reputational suicide! So, in sum, while the food is great, the POOR, UNTRUSTWORTHY CUSTOMER SERVICE makes me lose my appetite.

Horrible service! They offer online orders and ALWAYS seems to misplace the order or overlook it. One time they admitted they didn't check their online orders, the second time they said they waited until I arrived so the chaat wouldn't get soggy, and I've lost track of all the other excuses they gave me. When I arrive the dish is never ready and I still wait a good 20 minutes for my chaat which should be quick to make, considering there were no other customers present! They ask online what spice level you want but don't even care about that because both my chaats were bland when I specifically asked for extra spicy!!! They are also unbelievably stingy with chutney and probably give no more than 5 drops of chutney per dish. It is quite obnoxious that I always have to pay for extra chutney, they should be putting enough to start with. I always give them a chance every few months but they find a new way to disappoint me. I do not think I will be returning, regardless of how badly I am craving chaat. I would rather drive or fly to Chicago for quality service and to get what I paid for.
Was very impressed with the lunch buffet. Smaller selection than most Indian buffets, but the quality is extremely high.

Still seriously heart this place. In fact, my sis and I have a "regular table" now, and the service just gets friendlier and friendlier. The food today was out of this world, as it always is. But I have to downgrade to 4 stars for one reason and one reason only...they started burning some SERIOUS incense just as I had moved to my second plate of food. Um, did they learn nothing from Top Chef restaurant wars when Dale made the HUGE mistake of decorating the restaurant with vanilla scented candles? And this was incense...WAY STRONGER. I'm not a fan of incense ever, but especially not when I'm trying to actually taste my food. I literally couldn't, and had to waste some glorious potatoes, vegetable korma, spiced rice, and dosa. Huge bummer. To the girl working there-next time, please forgo the incense burning so I can enjoy your yummy food. Or at least wait until I'm gone. Thanks.

I stopped here to eat before catching a flight home. The buffet was great - all the food was fresh, and lots of variety. The proprietor insisted that I try "Indian Nachos." He made me a plate and I'm a fan! It was crunchies with raita, garbanzos, kidney beans, cilatro & onion, and several chutneys. My only problem was that I ate so much I got a tummy ache! I really enjoyed it, and I've eaten Indian food all over the country (the US, that is-)

Gokul is fantastic! I've been to most of the Indian restaurants in St. Louis, and I enjoy them all. House of India and Ruchi are great, and we go to both on are a regular basis. But Gokul was exciting because they have a variety of dishes that we haven't seen anywhere else. The staff at Gokul told us that the dishes are "snacks" or "light food". Many of the dishes are combinations that we would not have figured out on our own. One (kind of like Indian nachos) was layers of chick peas, brown beans, onions, fried crisps, smaller fried crunchy things, and 3 different sauces. It was fantastic. Another dish was hot dog buns that you dip into a brown, chopped mix of veggies. Another was small, savory, fried donuts, topped with another veggie mixture (maybe dal?). They were all pretty delicious. The restaurant itself is small, very casual, and has a long buffet along one wall (the buffet is open for lunch every day and dinners on the weekend). They also have a wide variety of dishes on the menu, many of which we have never seen or heard of. One was potato samosas, broken up and topped with a variety of veggies, sauces and crispy things. It looked great. When we were there, they were showing a Bollywood movie on the far wall, with the volume turned down low. It's in Hindi but there are subtitles. The restaurant is smoke free and VERY casual. On our visit, almost everyone in the restaurant was Indian, which is a good sign. The staff couldn't have been nicer, showing us which dishes go together and even making us a plate of one of the chaat combinations (the Indian nachos). We can't wait to go back.

Really liked this place. Unfortunately it is closed. They have another location on the loop if you want to try their food. I haven't been to the other location yet but they say it is the same food on their website.

I think if I were a vegetarian I'd give this place 5 stars. If I was vegan, I'd give it 6 stars--I'd find a way. I think that it is absolutely amazing to find a buffet that is entirely vegetarian, and it's even more impossible to find an entirely vegan buffet, which they do for dinner on the first and third Monday of every month. And I'll definitely keep this place in mind, when I'm going out with my vegetarian friends, but I'm not a vegetarian. Reviewing this place strictly on the food and not the novelty of a vegetarian buffet, I give this place 3 stars. I love daal, but it wasn't great here. My friend loves vegetable korma, and while we both liked theirs, we've had better. We both liked their naan. It was buttery and warm. They also had some desserts and fresh fruit. I've just had better and cheaper Indian buffets (this one was like $11.75).

We will be back for sure. They were a little slow because it was a 2 man show but were SUPER friendly and the food was outstanding. Not to mention it is SO affordable. They have a couple options that are all-you-can-eat, not that we needed it. Two entrees got us both dinner and lunch the next day.

This is just for the buffet which was supposed to be my treat for Raksha Bandhan/India's independence celebration. The paneer chili advertisement really got me rushing there.. unfortunately the paneer chili and gobi manchurian were stale. The falooda was great, but the bhel was horrible. A good price and good looking food, but the taste was quite lacking.

I've been wanting to try Gokul for awhile now, seeing the glowing reviews. Also being that I'm a vegetarian and an all vegetarian place is hard to find. We arrived right when it opened, which had its pros and cons. All fresh food, but nothing was labeled and it wasn't all out yet. We might've come a little later had we known, but I assumed it opened at 11 when really it's 11:30. Anyhow, we got right on the buffet. This is the biggest Indian buffet I've seen in STL, with a huge amount of options. They had palak paneer, which was easy to recognize, and vegetable korma. Lots of other sauces and delicacies. I liked those a lot, and the dal was the perfect consistency and spice. The naan was a little different than others I've experienced: less fluffy, more chewy, and almost tasted liked it was brushed with a flavored oil. It was good and I definitely consumed enough to make this judgment! Our water glasses were kept filled, though my sister had to ask for a refill on her diet coke. The service was fine, but not extremely friendly. I wanted to ask what a couple things were but didn't because of this. I definitely liked it and look forward to going back. I like that they rotate items - I have gotten a little bored of the other Indian/Asian buffet (Everest) that I like going because they never change items.

We went for lunch and decided to skip the buffet and order chaat instead. We got the samosa chaat, pav bhaji and ragda pattis. The samosa chaat was too sweet for my liking but my friends liked the pav bhaji. The ragda pattis was a disappointment, having too much ragda in proportion to the pattis. The masala chai was good. Would probably not be back here for the food anytime soon.

The ayce crabs are their saving grace. The place is nice, open, has touch tunes, and the staff seem friendly... But they seem to ignore new customers and only talk to their regulars. Ive spent a lot of time there with an empty drink.
Love Ott's; great place for lunch and drinks. Julie and Michelle are especially great severs, always a friendly word and quick with refills. Couldn't recommend it more....

The person at the door couldn't tell if my ID was 'fake' or not because it was a NY license. There was an obnoxious bouncer flashing his flashlight at my wife and I while we were eating, for no apparent reason. The place was empty, the lights were on, I did not understand why he did that. Perhaps to inform me of his 'presence?' We get it brother! you're a bouncer. The food was a disappointment. I can usually finish sub-par food, but I couldn't even get through a quarter of the pulled pork sandwich.

Too many overserved, loud and profane clowns sitting at the bar. Maybe the lunch crowd is better. Don't come here in the late evening. Victory and Ollie Gators are nearby, have comparable food and a much better class of customers.

I used to come to this place a lot. Figured it's been a while, so I'll give it a shot since I moved closer again. It seems their attention and good/priority service goes to the regulars. They'd rather watch the new people sit there patiently with an empty glass in front of them. Very unprofessional vibe here.

This place has so much potential but continues to miss the mark. The bartenders overall are pretty nice but they spend TOO MUCH TIME socializing at the cash registers instead of waiting on customers. You can sit at the bar and watch them talking while waiting for them to acknowledge you. It's ridiculous. It's like working is a social event. Also, several of them have been there for too long and it's obvious. They seem sick of their jobs. Being a regular customer doesn't matter either. The food isn't bad as far as bars go but its overpriced for Berlin. Ott's will probably hang in there for a bit longer but with newer more updated options like Dooneys and certainly more to come in the area- especially in Marlton, which is close enough - Ott's should realize they need to step up their game. I was there recently on a Saturday and it was pretty dead. Tells you something. I'd hate to see them go under but, if so, it's their own fault. Get with it Otts management and staff.

Service is just horrible and has gotten worse. We will not return. Went 4/9 beautiful Sunday day. Few tables nothing crazy. Server doesn't know meaning of servicing who sat first. We sat and waited 5 min for service. 2 guys showed up she comes out waits on them. We tell her ready she says after I put order in will be right over, really!!!! We had the $5.00 wing and roast beef special. Being in restaurant bus in know why roast beef was $5.00. Was very bad. If this is what they serve daily. All fat!!! We won't return.

Aaaaaah, Otts!.....miss the old Otts, it had character and it was fun to write on the bathroom walls, it is asthetically pleasing inside now albeit way more loud now with that high ceiling and wish that pool table was not in there. The food prices went up but for bar food it's better than most, their burgers are great and they have good specials daily. Now the fun part, the staff!....Julie and Michelle are fantastic, personable and both work hard, id rather go there during the day to see them since they are the most pleasant to talk to as for two of their other female coworkers who tend bar leave a little to be desired, the first one is very beautiful but she is downright rude and not nice to talk to unless you are a young kid she went to high school with who are always in there acting like total tools then it's ok but she tends to forget about the other paying customers who want service, I'm not there to get a date with her, I'm there to get food and some beers and stagger to my truck and the other one is pretty ignorant as well, I think her name is Jamie? she only tends to her regulars and again thinks everybody wants to date her and loses focus of her other customers who want good service as well, I try to stay away if those 2 are working. Trivia night is cool but hard to hear the guy reading the questions because the acoustics suck in there now and finally, beer pong night needs to go,I'm tired of tools wearing tap out and affliction clothes and acting tough when most of them only watch the sport they support, it's a great bar but there is a real young crowd it seems and I don't prefer that scene much anymore.So if you want good bar food, reasonably priced drinks, nice Tv's and some female eye candy and mostly nice staff like Ray, Julie, and Michelle and Kelly then head in there but the other female staff leaves a little to be desired, the manager, I forget his name but he's tall and stocky is very polite also.

As I add this Ott's location to Yelp, I am struggling with how to categorize it. It's obviously a bar, but what kind of bar? It's not exactly a dive, though I didn't find the establishment (particularly the bathrooms) to be all that clean. I wouldn't consider it a sports bar, though there are TVs everywhere, a pool table and a shuffleboard table. I also wouldn't say it's a pub. The menu isn't comforting or inventive or Irish-inspired. Seems like Ott's Green Top Inn is having an identity crisis. Why is it even called an Inn? There doesn't appear to be any lodging available... Still, I suppose the service was quick enough. The patrons give off the vibe of local regulars (townies?) who go there for a relaxed place to drink and socialize. If that's all you're looking for, then I guess it doesn't matter what you call the place.
Came here for a light bite and drinks on a Sunday at 7:00. Gigantic inside bar and huge outdoor patio. All the bartenders were so down to earth and friendly. Would definitely come back.
Wings suck. Not seasoned. Burgers are dry and not seasoned well. Bread for the burgers suck. Tastes like plastic bags. Service slow.
Typical local bar ... they have liquor and beer and bar stools and tables ... Seems more spacious, though, compared to other places. Fairly clean inside and decent service.

Perhaps an off night? Went to Ott's on a Monday night around 7. Sat for a few minutes until the bartender noticed me. I asked if they had any drink specials, and a menu was literally "tossed" to me. Nothing I was interested in, so I ordered a Jack Daniels on the rocks. My go-to. The bartender fills the highball glass with ice almost resembling a "snow cone". Waiting for a typical pour, the bartender fills the glass an inch full---no kidding, and holds it up to the light to inspect it. Did they install cameras since my last visit? Never at this bar, nor any other for that matter, have I had this drink made with so little alcohol in it. I had to ask for a double to make it a "normal". On top of that, not once did a bartender come back to ask if I would like to see a menu, as I was planning on getting an appetizer. Meanwhile, evertone around me is eating. So I stopped another bartender and asked him if there were any food specials tonight.....NO. As I was finishing my drink, and getting ready to leave, the couple next to me asked another bartender about food specials....turns out it was DOLLAR taco night. Anyway, paid my bill.....$13.25 for one drink.....exact same drink at Redstone if not a bit larger, would've cost me $10.00.......just don't get it? As I signed my tab, the same bartender who was unaware of taco deal said, "You're gonna leave with out getting something to eat?" "Yup".

I just wanted to say that we just did takeout from here today and we loved it. I had grilled chicken wings and they were excellent!! My wife had crab legs and she enjoyed them as well. They even gave us a Thank You package that my wife said was a nice touch. BTW the package was chocolate chip cookies. Anyway I felt compelled to write this review to let everyone know that this is a good place to grab some food from.

Stopped by for a few beers and some light dinner. They had what looked like a nice selection of draft beer, so I asked for a list. There isn't one I was told by a bartender in his mid 40s. Huh? You have to look on the chalkboard, I was told. So I had to get up and walk over to the chalkboard at the chicken scratch to order something other than bud. After ordering some overpriced flatbread pizza, another bartender came over an hour later and gave me a beer list. Now why wasn't I given that in the beginning? Because one of the beers was switched over and the other guy didn't feel like explaining which one. Okay. Then I looked online and noticed that there was all you can eat snow crabs that day, which nobody had mentioned. Geez what lousy service. I received an updated beer list just as I was about to leave. This was once a known dive bar which caught on fire and recently rebuilt. Although nice inside, it still has the dive bar attitude, but not the prices. I don't want to pay $5 to $7 for a draft beer and have to walk over to try to read a mess on the chalkboard.

Great place! Doesn't feel like I've been to Jersey if I haven't stopped in for a bite. Great atmosphere friendly service and fun food. I love the pretzel bites! The Delmonico is my husband's favorite and my new favorite is the Ruben. It's the best I ever had. I've never had anything here that wasn't good.

Great place to stop and get some drinks and the food is outstanding! Place is spacious, great service, what more can you ask for? You should definitely ask for Morgan at the bar great personality and great service with a smile! I will go here again and again! Stay away from the Meatloaf!

We were looking for a laid back place to have lunch outdoors, this place was perfect. We sat on their patio. The server was very attentive and food was delivered (appetizer and entree) was delivered promptly. We had the pretzel bites as an appetizer, for our entree we had caesar salad with salmon on it as well as their shrimp rice bowl. Everything was enjoyable. The pretzel bites came out super hot, delicious. The caesar salad came with a nice size piece of salmon. The shrimp bowls came with nacho type chips, that was a little different but we enjoyed it. I recommend dining here.

"Hey look, mister - we serve hard drinks in here for men who want to get drunk fast, and we don't need any characters around to give the joint "atmosphere". " I think Jessica is missing the point in trying to categorize Ott's Green Top Inn: its just a bar. Although of the four Ott's in South Jersey, this is probably the runt of the litter. And you know what, that's just fine. Because sometimes you just want to sit at a bar and drink; maybe watch TV, listen to regulars and watch shuffleboard. As for the "inn", that denotes hospitality; at Ott's the bartenders are always attentive, the food is served hot, and there are always a few characters that give the place atmosphere.

My husband and I prefer this Ott's to the new Voorhees one. We love going there on Sunday afternoons. They have a huge bar with lots of places to sit and be able to see a tv for sports games. The beer selection is great and we like the seasonal cocktail and food menus. Some of our favorite menu items: Buffalo chicken flatbread Boneless wings Loaded tater tots Cheese steaks
Love going to this place after a hockey game with the boys. Prices are good and food is on point. It has a nice deck to sit outside on the nice nights.
No atmosphere "Ok" service Food. NOT THE IT USED TO BE Not going back Staff indiferant Many other choice in area Otts was a great place at one tine

I loved this place when it was a dive bar. It took them a really long time to fix it after the fire. I have no idea why. I went in tonight for the first time in a very long time and the place was just not the same. I miss the old wooden seats bar etc. we sat in the enclosed area on the porch. It was freezing and not enough heat. I slept with my jacket on and was still cold. The menu is changed and they need to find the chef and food they had before the fire. I went with the idea of having a roast pork sandwich which I always liked there. It was taken off the menu. They have all these wraps now and melts. Salads etc. give me old fashioned bar food. They did not even have a good roast beef sandwich. I ordered French onion soup which was not very good. My friend ordered the gumbo soup special and it came out cold. I mean cold. Not warm. I ended up ordering a French dip was mediocre at best. They gave a half cup of au jus. The sandwich was small and not even full with meat to the end. The fries were not bad. The pickle was the best thing. And of course the Corona. I guess the remodeling was more than they expected or did not get enough insurance money. Not going back soon.
If I can give zero star I would. One older lady she's a bartender that works is very rude. Food is not worth the money.

Worst customer service ever.. I sat down and the bartender was rushing me to order because kitchen were going to close , when they advertised they close at 2 am ..I got there at 11:30 . Bartender never asked how was the food I ordered . Never come back

What a joke of a live music venue! Stopped in and left with brain damage from the loud craziness I saw. One beer was too long a stay. This place used to be a great place to see live music in South Jersey. I can't even review the food because there was no way I would have been able to eat through that spectacle.

Place is a joke ... how could they still be in business as a live music venue. Seriously... every time the music is horrible... too loud, screaming, it's unbelievable. I've given it so many chances because a lot of our friends say "hey let's go to Otts" I cringe every time because every performance I've seen there is terrible. I Ben when I hear it's a good band at Otts it's always a huge let down.

The wings are great, the otts tots are to die for and the flatbread pizzas are amazing too. The service the first time I went for dinner was a little slow on the drink refills but in her defense the server was alone and the bartender seemed more concerned with socializing than filling the drink orders the waitress was giving her. The second time was for lunch and the service was much better and the food was equally as good as the first time. I'm looking forward to taking my daughter for all you can eat crabs to see how th at is.
Great tap selection and the seasonal salads were great. Best experience we have had here in a while. :)

Food was ok came her for lunch and not busy at all. It took a while for a roast beef and salad to come out. A bit pricey for two beers a glass of wine a salad and roast beef. Ok for lunch but nothing to really rave about.

The new otts gets an a for atmosphere but food needs work. I was served cold chicken wings and my friends taco salad was not very good piled with too large lettuce peices and no other ingrdients. Also no more shuffleboard or pool table. I believe that will deter some people from going there that are used to that in the old otts

$5 COVER ON A FRIDAY & SATURDAY NIGHT? What a joke. This is a dive bar in Berlin. The other local bars Ollie Gators, Dublin Square, Lucky Lou's, and Racks all have live bands and do not charge a cover. I went there this past Saturday and there might of been 20 people in the entire place and they still had the audacity to ask for a cover. Worst thing is... the band doesn't start playing till 10pm but they start collecting a cover at 8pm (sometimes earlier). This is poor management. I have taken my wife up on a Friday night to grab a bite to eat and bouncer hassles me about trying to get a cover. We paid $10 bucks and then ate our meal and left around 945pm and the band still didn't even play a song yet. WHAT A JOKE. The old OTT's was 100x's better. No shuffleboard now, pool table is in a terrible spot and whatever genius configured the TV set up should be fired. You can only see tv's if you site on 1 side of the bar. The other side has small 20inch tv's that you need a pair of binoculars to view. This bar is only hanging on by charging covers. It is empty on most nights by midnight. This place used to be rocking till 2 or 3am. I know at least 15 to 20 people that have refused to ever go back there again for a drink randomly on a saturday night because no one wants to pay a cover to hang out at a TOWN BAR. You are not PJs. You want more people, get rid of the cover. Bad Business.

Decided to meet my husband for dinner during the week thinking that you can't go wrong with bar food, right? Well, it was very disappointing. My "famous chicken tenders" were cold as were the French fries that came with them. The so-called buffalo sauce was really just hot sauce...no flavor and it was cold (I got it on the side). And even though I requested ranch they gave me blue cheese dressing. My husband's filet mignon sandwich looked like 2 tiny hockey pucks on a gigantic roll and didn't even come with fries. If it wasn't so overpriced maybe we could have overlooked the petite serving size. And not one of the several bar tenders even checked with us after our meals were served even though they could easily see that my plate was barely touched. They were more interested in talking to regulars or each other. We will not be going back.

I like the other ott's better. . The food from the kids menu is not good at all.. My girls had the pasta with meatballs and couldn't eat it.. The meatballs were hard and the pasta was soggy.. Happy kids makes the time go better so you can guess how it went.

Been going to Otts, well a long time. The new (well not so new now) change is ok in my opinion, got rid of the riff raft so to speak I guess?? Only reason I can think of for the price increases and complete theme change. To the the food, had it all, for the most part real good, not great for the price, that's not a bad thing. One of my favorites is the Delmonico steak w fries. Put it this way, I remember when it was 5.99 now 13-14 ish. Still well worth it, thin piece of rib eye what it is, and 99% of the time cooked perfectly for me. Very red not raw. Everything else burgers, wings ect all good as stated. Place just lost that home town feel. " get em in feed em, get em out" make sense to anyone? But again will be back. Nice place for all types of groups, family, guys after work, u and your lady or partner. Or you and one of your kids. So it covers all. Enjoy

This place is okay, food is decently priced and drink are average. What gets you is the $5.00 cover. There is one every Friday and Saturday night. Most bars in Philly don't even charge that much if anything to get in. You could literally go there on a Friday with some homeless man playing the kazoo and they would still milk the cover from you for the live entertainment. I hop around with a group of about 8 friends, so we've since opted to go elsewhere on weekends in order to save the $40.

Disappointed. I ordered an italian roast pork sandwich. Here's the description "Thinly sliced roast pork served on a toasted garlic Kaiser roll with roasted red peppers, long hots and provolone cheese" Where were my long hots??? The main reason i ordered the sandwich. The pork was not thin and was dry as hell. Throw some au jau on it atleast. I went there tonight for the rib special, but the customer next to me had a plate of ribs that didnt look appetizing. I should have left.

This is our go to spot. The bartenders are friendly the food is good, the bathrooms are clean and there is a beautiful deck to eat al fresco when the weather turns warm. The manager Tim is super accomodating and engaged. We love their happy hour!
The best bar around! Food is always great! Hot n Honey wings like the Ott-Tots behind the bar are amazing! Great draft beer selection... GO!

Really terrible enviornment, over crowded and overrated by far. Insanely bad management the management are terrible people who serve underage people who are their friends and wont even let underage people in with their parents service takes forever to loud to even talk the only good thing was the band playing the place is a dump i wouldnt recommend it to my enemys should be shut down. I only gave them one star because i have to in order to warn future customers

Can't get bar service unless your beer is empty. Bar tenders are chatty AF with each other or regulars.. I've gone several times after work for dinner, I've asked for a menu, got a beer, and didn't have someone come by and ask if I wanted to order food until my beer was empty.

First time in the new spot . Looked clean . Beer selection is very good cause they got involved with the crafts. Please ask what the price is. I got the bill at one was 9.50.. no way is the craft beer world that would be the cost. Unless that sixtel from Kramer was $180. And then you are stretching on a 10%... Do get some better glasses though . Got a burger . Medium well . But tough to cook it that way on a frozen so it was well done .. Descent though . A little skim on the fries . And then a 2 dollar up charge Pricing on the menu a little high for what you get .

This place is exceptionally average. It's a shame too, because I really want to like this place as it is close to my house. The inside is decorated nicely and inviting as everything looks clean. It features a decent sized deck for warmer weather dining. I've been here a few times and each time the word that comes to mind as far as the food is mediocre. I'm left wanting more as far as taste. The most recent time I came I got the chicken fingers platter with fries. I asked for them buffalo style and out came chicken fingers with a side of buffalo sauce. Note to the cooks: this is not "buffalo style". The server took it back and brought it out with the chicken tossed in the Holy Hot flavored sauce. The sauce was nothing special, it just seemed like hot sauce that lacked a little flavor. Not only was that an issue, but I got soup along with it and for some reason, it was brought out along with my entree so I had to eat my soup rather quickly so the rest of my food didn't get cold. I've given this place more than enough chances to wow me and it looks like I'll try to find another place close to me for a last minute bar to go to.

Give it 3 stars for the beer selection. The food is ok, had the salmon dinner recently. Salmon was atlantic which doesn't have much taste anyway. Good mashed potatoes but the vegetables were over cooked. Gotten other things here and its good, but not great. The service is hit or miss. Server we had the other night although attentive (asked how everything was) seemed rushed and there were very few tables to serve. In the past I've had exceptional service and service so bad I almost didn't want to go back. One bartender in particular was very rude. The place itself is nice with lots of TVs for sports watching.

Been going to Otts, well a long time. The new (well not so new now) change is ok in my opinion, got rid of the riff raft so to speak I guess?? Only reason I can think of for the price increases and complete theme change. To the the food, had it all, for the most part real good, not great for the price, that's not a bad thing. One of my favorites is the Delmonico steak w fries. Put it this way, I remember when it was 5.99 now 13-14 ish. Still well worth it, thin piece of rib eye what it is, and 99% of the time cooked perfectly for me. Very red not raw. Everything else burgers, wings ect all good as stated. Place just lost that home town feel. " get em in feed em, get em out" make sense to anyone? But again will be back. Nice place for all types of groups, family, guys after work, u and your lady or partner. Or you and one of your kids. So it covers all. Enjoy Here for lunch on Sunday. Service great, got the roast beef, no fat all meet. Onions Yuk but did not hinder flavor, 3 bloody Mary's out of this word good!! Service great, people great? All good we're these other folks come up up w these complaints, my nerves. I'd be pissy if things went on spot, but they were, so another 4-5 stars. Enjoy

This restaurant is exactly what you think it's going to be. It's a local bar restaurant. All of the customers that go here look and act like they've been coming here for a long time. There a big bar in the middle of the place and tables all around it. The waiters and waitresses have an IDGAF attitude with a side of sass and nice-ness. The food is also exactly as you'd expect as well. It's sort of like they do the bare minimum but it's OK food. If you're coming after work because you need to unwind, this can be that place.
Best hot n honey wings in the area. Service was great. The manager was very nice and introduced himself to us. A lot of craft beers on tap as well.
New improved Otts is really nice! It's still really Jersey but the food is good and the prices aren't bad either. They even have a punch card for lunch.

Went here for St Pattys Day weekend so naturally it was super crowded. Parking is an absolute nightmare. You have to circle the lot- which has pot holes (and it just rained so it was muddy) and race people for spots. There was a line a the door for IDs. Half of my party was let in-- the other half were left standing outside in the line.. the guy at the door didn't say why.. I guess it was his attempt at crowd control? The inside was SO crowded, like sardines. The band was cool but kind of loud. The "dance floor" was so crowded you couldn't really even dance.. a bunch of younger girls dancing with their drinks spilling all over. Good priced irish trashcans! The security guy was really nice and funny. OH-- they also had some tables reserved at 9pm on a Saturday... seems weird, unnecessary, and unfair? Overall-- okay. I don't know if I'd go back. It was pretty clean. Except the bathrooms... a bunch of drunk girls left their drinks on the floors and sinks..

Dive bar but one that knows it's just a dive bar. Ott's is definitely not trying to be anything it isn't. What you get? Expect a "diverse" crowd-bikers, college kids, girls that are dressed up for no reason. Cheap drinks. Cheap food.

Ott's is the reason they invented the saying "It is what it is." Seriously, what you see is what you get. Not a great beer selection, but they've got beer. Food is there but it's nothing to write home about. People are hanging out, just chillin'. Bartenders who won't let you address them with "sir" or "miss." Just say "hey." It's been a solid choice for getting out of the house when the electricity bailed out a few times this summer. Or a few years back when my sister turned 21 on a Tuesday. Or when my friend's wedding ended early and we needed to continue the binge. Quizzo Wednesdays always promise a good time as do the Megatouch tuneskeeper and gaming devices. The new outdoor patio and bar is almost a bit too classy for the raggedy indoors, but I'm not complaining. This is definitely our neighborhood spot.

UPDATE: Very nice response to this post. Michelle came over and apologized and made it right. Will put this restaurant back on the list to try for another time because of how nice and accommodating they were. My first and last time I'll come into Ott's!!!! We ordered Ott's tots loaded. We got little cheese, where's the bacon, and the chili too spicy to eat . Ordered 10 wings, not hot heat cooked wise and very hard and dry. We left the whole order on table.

Rude male bar tender. I support the Eastern Football Booster Club every year. I have purchased multiple gift cards. I decided to actually use the Eastern Gift Card Offer at Otts which was listed as an eligible vendor for a food purchase and was told by this particular male bartender/manager that it was ineligible. I have no words. Other waitresses have let me use this same gift card in the past. I also called before I came and told this male that I was told it was permitted. He did not care. If you do not support Eastern Football then don't do it. Do not scam people into going to Otts Berlin when it gets poor to mediocre reviews at best. There are much better sports bars in the area with much better food.

The Ott's in Delran is my standby, but this one does the trick if I'm down in that neck of the woods (awesome farmer's markets!) The burger was okay, the bartender was sweet and quick to get us more beers. I understand there's an outside area but it was too cold for us to be out there...inside is very dark and dreary so that made me sad :(

I came here for the first time back in March after a softball game. I'm used to the Ott's in Medford so I was pretty surprised walking in and seeing how big this one was in comparison. The menu is the same as the other Ott's so the consistency is nice, great beer specials, plenty of TV's around if you're there to watch whatever game happens to be playing. All around nice staff and very clean atmosphere!

entered 5:30 and asked the two hostesses about 'happy hour'..they looked at each other quizzically, confessed ignorance and said to each other 'guess we should know that'...anyway it extends 'til 7 and all starters (a big choice) are half off, a good deal...whole place is bloody noisy, with a share of drunk regulars being greeted by an abundant staff...ahi tuna was excellent, quesadillas were packed with chicken, wings were disappointing and not helped by a poorly chosen 'maple' sauce...nice selection of micros scrawled on a board, six bucks a piece...they graciously allowed us to take out a fourth 'starter' at the same half price...the whole (limited to burgers, sandwiches, etc, nothing fancy here) menu was most reasonably priced, everyday and easily found pub grub you never feel particularly good after eating...it serves it's purpose but 50/50 i'll pull in next time passing...

My husband and I prefer this Ott's to the new Voorhees one. We love going there on Sunday afternoons. They have a huge bar with lots of places to sit and be able to see a tv for sports games. The beer selection is great and we like the seasonal cocktail and food menus.

Three stars is about right! Ott's is a fairly uninspired but reliable establishment with a pretty decent beer selection and predictable menu. Whenever Dogfish 60 is on tap I'm a happy girl! Boyfriend and I shared old bay fries which were good. I got hot and honey boneless wings which were a little underwhelming. I wish they were covered in more sauce and also the sauce should have been a little thicker as it was kind of runny. My companion got a pork roll egg and cheese sandwich which he said was delicious and certainly looked it. I could have done without the live music they had going on on a Friday night. I feel Ott's would do better with a jukebox perhaps. I'm not sure how many times I'll come back with places like the Jughandle or Picalilly close by, but for some beer and bar food it's a solid choice.

If you're looking for good food, fun, and drinks... this is your place! Smokin hot bartender there on Saturday nights... sometimes we go just to see her. Witty banter, long hair, and BIG.... Personality
Had shrimp tacos that were delicious. Also the wings and Hawaiian tacos were really good. I like the atmosphere of the semi outside bar. All you. An eat crab legs are a great deal. Service was great.

LIKES: nice big wrap around bar..lower drop ceiling painted black...they resisted making common mistake of painting exposed hvac and leaving it natural metal. DISLIKES: the area with the cathedral ceiling is FAR too bright...the space behind the bar is too big ...its actually distracting how much space there is because the bartenders pace around and bang into each other like a bunch of wind up toys....we ordered food and were not impressed at all...especially since it and we were cold....I was expecting much more since they had an opportunity to get it right.....but its early and they just re opened....I liked the newly remodeled outside and inside....just needs tweekin

My elderly parents were craving a good burger. My husband & I were looking for a casual, local place where we could bring our teenage kids for dinner, and still have a nice Sam Adams seasonal. I was shocked when I walked in, as it had been about 5 years since I'd been here. It has been completely remodeled. Gone are the dark walls, hardwood floors, bar neons, etc. What I felt gave it character, made it friendly & comfortable. The place is marble & bright tangerine walls, fancy light fixtures & tile. Not exactly my cup of tea, I'm more a neighborhood tavern kinda girl, but I remembered they had very good bar food. Apparently that changed too. I don't really want to get into the dirty details, because I'd end up sounding nit picky, but they ended up taking $15 off our bill for inedible soup & mussels. The rest of our food was "just okay", not great but not awful. Service was horrendous, actually had to go up to the bar to complain, which is not something I ever do. Do yourself a favor & scratch this one off your list. I will never go there again.
Great food , great atmosphere. Tony was an excellent server. Definitely will come back .

We walked in Saturday evening about 6pm; the place was surprisingly not busy (of course we now know why they weren't busy, because it the service was AWFUL). For starters, the music was insanely loud-which is fine for the later crowd, but not for dinner & conversation-everyone was yelling at each other to be heard over the music. We should've left then. The "hostess" looked like she wanted to be anywhere but there, and seemed a little annoyed that she had to seat us. The waitress came right over and took our drink order, and when she came back we were ready to order, but she didn't ask. She literally set the drinks down and left. So we're waiting & waiting for her to come back and then we see her sitting at a table on her phone. We left. As we walked out, the "hostess" just gave us a clueless look-absolutely no attempt to keep us there. BTW, we love Ott's Vorhees

After living in the area my entire life, this is the first time I have ever been to this Ott's. I walked in with not having very high expectations other than having a good time in a chill atmosphere. The first thing that turned me off was the cover for a band that wasn't even playing yet. If the band was playing, whatever, I'll pay for the cover. But if they're not even ready yet, it's ridiculous. Next, I stood by the bar for 10 minutes waiting to be served. As a bartender in a very high volume establishment, I understand getting backed up. This was not the case. Four bartenders walked by, looked at me, and continued chatting up with their coworkers. The bar business is about customer service. Well, apparently not here. The only good thing about my visit here was the waitress that took care of us when we sat at a table. Friendly and timely. I'm glad we got her, since the other waitress looked miserable walking around. If I ever come back, I'll be looking for her!

Philly/Jersey- this is the BEST sports bar! Was in town visiting friends and came by on a Sunday afternoon. Our server- Lacey- was AWESOME! Great recommendations on drinks and food, and such a great upbeat personality. Service is impeccable! Be sure to check out their daily specials. Lunch special on Sunday is 1 pound of wings for $7. Lots of drink specials during game day, too! Will definitely stop back if I'm in Philly again.
Great spot, awesome bartenders, GREAT midweek specials. Extensive interesting menu - small rear deck but nice. Pool table.
