It's alright. I had the sweet and sour chicken but the sauce tasted more like ketchup and there was not anywhere near enough rice. Good service tho!

Something was disturbingly wrong with the food we received. The food WAS delivered hot & packaged well. We ordered the Yum-Yum Chicken, General Tso's Chicken, and the Crab Rangoon. We ordered these items based on the reviews and recommendations of folks on Yelp & NextDoor. The good: they do provide cutlery, soy sauce packets, and fortune cookies. The food was packaged well and prepared quickly. The white rice is good. My husband liked his spring roll. The bad: the Yum-Yum Chicken was actually inedible. The texture was kind of chewy (fatty...maybe?) but definitely not how chicken is supposed to be prepared. It wasn't crispy at all. The sauce was a fish sauce (call me crazy but isn't Yum-Yum Chicken supposed to be a Yum-Yum sauce? It seriously wasn't anything but a fish sauce.) It wasn't that I hate fish sauce that made it inedible, it was the texture. It was offensive to the senses. It was like eating a sardine. My husband ordered General Tso's Chicken. Surprise! It wasn't a General Tso's sauce. The chicken was chewy, the sauce was sour and bitter. The Crab Rangoons truly are HUGE! And if you like Crab Rangoon for the crab then you don't want to order these, it's mostly just cream cheese. Personally, I love cream cheese. But I didn't order fried wontons with cream cheese. I can't believe we spent $30 for this food + delivery. The delivery experience was excellent, I'm very happy with that service. But I would never recommend this place. It was our first & now our last time eating here. And I want to make sure that everyone is prepared for a hit or miss experience. Because the good reviewers obviously had a good experience. Just be prepared to be disappointed so that if your food is good then you'll be surprised! I am so disappointed because I was craving Chinese food. And I couldn't eat anything but the rice without wanting to throw up for the rest of the day. It soured my appetite and my stomach.

Upon arriving the gentleman serving us was very kind. Service was great. I ordered the yum yum chicken and the hot & spicy beef. Food was hot and came out quickly. I also enjoyed music being played. Definitely recommend.

First time trying because my normal place of 10 years is under new Management. I can say that I now have found a new place to patronize. I understand how others can say that the customer service was not up to par because the young lady did not greet me and had no personality at all. She seemed like she had had a long day and didn't want to be there. The food was absolutely more than what I had expected. The service was fast and they had a lot of variety however I only get the plain fried rice and crab Rangoon.

While I generally agree that The Rice House has as diverse a menu as any restaurant without tables or chairs, I have to take exception to the glowing reviews it has received in this column. Granted the food is ok, but that is about all you can claim for it. The staff is as diverse as the menu and the concept of a receipe is foreign. Generally speaking the food has it's chops but is a long way from being great. The menu is printed on the wall and is extensive, the cashier, ordering people don't have a great deal of patience even when no one is in line behind you. Not good, when there is so much to decide on. While I did not try the soul foods offered, or the famed St. Paul Sandwich (egg foo young on thick toast, with mayo and god knows what else), the standard chinese fair was fare. The prices are not cheap, the service is not fast, and the care with which your order is made seemed to be a function of how the staff felt that day. Would I return? Maybe if ever I were so far north on Lindberg again, I would stop by, but unless my Garmin is fine tuned I will miss the restaurant and the driveway. I won't really miss the food.

My order was very good. Their food is very delicious, but they have to improve customer service. I did not have any problems today, but as a local restaurant, many people are not very happy with the service they've received and I want to make it known.I truthfully was not going to order from here but I was having a craving and wanted their hot braised sauce and fried rice. It was delicious as it was before. They are consistent with how they make their food, but not consistent with how customers are served. Please make service better so you can continue to get the support!

It's pretty good I thought my food tasted like onions and my boyfriends did too if u don't want to spend your whole check on Chinese food I would suggest goin to Lisa's great food great customer service I just didn't like it

Order wrong after asking several times if my order was correct. Very poor customer service, Folks act is if they are doing me a favor. When I called to complain folks asking for a ticket number, I never received a ticket number, For sure I will not be back too many other options.

Great food, really busy though so I suggest you call your order in. Don't worry if they answer then hang up on you a few times, that's just how they are. When your food is good I guess service doesn't matter. Great menu options, although for Rice in St Louis their about $2 higher than everyone else, but the food is good.
Delicious and cheap - adding bacon to a st. paul is genius. I would give it 5 stars if they added egg drop soup to thier menu since that's my kids favorite part of chinese takeout.

If I could give this place 0 stars, I would. I ordered with friends via delivery per one of my friend's recommendation on Sunday, September 5. Considering this is my first time ordering Chinese food that's not Panda Express in 3 years, I was very skeptical. My friend boasted about the rice. I went on Yelp and saw all the negative reviews and was leary but went forward with placing an order. I ordered the Pineapple Chicken Fried Rice. It was hot when it arrived and had adequate pieces of canned pineapple and actual pieces of chicken and not the mystery meat generally associated with Chinese restaurants. I dumped 2 packets of cayenne pepper into it and dug into it. It was good but very filling. So I finished a quarter of my half order and placed the rest in the fridge for a future lunch. Well that lunch was today. I heated my rice in its box since it didn't have the metal bars on the side. It was nice and hot after 1 minute and 20 seconds in the microwave. But since I had soo much rice left over I dumped it into a bowl to eat it. When I dumped it into the bowl and looked onto the bottom of the box the first thing o noticed was the black sediment generally associated with use of old grease. Hoping and praying that that wasn't the case I took a bite. Immediately the taste of old grease filled my mouth and overwhelmed the actual taste of the rice. I cursed and threw it in the trash. I definitely would never order from here again because clearly from recent reviews and from my own experience, they do not clean their grease for frying up things.

We found this place via Groupon and we're definitely going back again. The prices were so low, we had to order the next day's lunch to take home to make it easier to use our whole Groupon. I had the Angry Bird St. Paul Sandwich. This is my first time having any sort of St. Paul sandwich. I would have tried the regular St Paul, but the photo on their web site of this sandwich really caught my attention. Not as spicy as the name suggests, but the flavor of the patty was just what I wanted. I should have looked for some Sriracha to top that. I have to believe that these sandwiches are their specialty - it really shows in the flavor. The crab rangoon is a triangle fold with only a moderate amount of filling, so you have to be careful how you eat it so you're not eating straight fried wonton. I do prefer star folded, just because it holds more filling, but these were decent. They also had some varieties I've never seen that I wanted to try - philly steak rangoon and that day's special was a pizza rangoon. The pork egg rolls had a very good amount of pork. Not too much, but more than I've seen anywhere before. The rice was just right. The stir fry dishes were sauced and seasoned well. I have not eaten mine yet, but my wife's sesame chicken was very good. Overall, it was a good amount of food for not a lot of money. They have a surprisingly large, but bottled/canned only, beverage selection. Everything from Jolly Rancher Soda to Chrysanthemum tea. The dining area does have tables now (as opposed to earlier reviews I'm seeing).

Took a long time for takeout. Made everyone's else's order first and came back to me like they forgot my order. No worries, but then I got home and they forgot my egg rolls and the orange chicken was atrocious. Zero orange taste and the tiniest amount of rice. The amount of soy sauce left my mouth hurting and made me super thirsty. Philly wontons were the only good thing. We tried it and we will never go back.

5 star massive Ultimate St Paul sandwich for $5.50 I never had a St Paul before that I actually liked, but they add bacon. The also have bacon fried rice that I did not try. The place is dive with no place to eat. However, for tasty cheap Asian-Soul food... I must say it is A-OK based on 1 St Paul sandwich...

OMG. I thought all take out Chinese restaurants are all the same. This is head and shoulders better than average. I need to mention mad props to Sylvester T for his review mentioning this place. I saw the menu picture and it listed the "Ultimate" St. Paul. I love St. Paul sandwiches. I was doubtful but intrigued!?! I must admit that when I here superlative advertising my bullshit detector goes into overdrive. But I had to try it! It was incredible. The best St. Paul I have ever had. First the upgrades: Texas Toast and BACON! That made the sandwich. The bread held up to the egg fu yung patty. There was also dill pickles and mayo. There was every ingredient imaginable in there. The only complaint was that the patty was a little dry. There was no grease on it or released upon biting into it. It was very unusual. I also tried a small order of the Ultimate fried rice. It was delicious. Again, everything imaginable was in that rice. Also the meat and fillings were well distributed it was delicious to the last bite. I am not sure, but I strongly suspect that they use MSG from the incredible flavor. You may want to check on this if you are sensitive. They also had various crab Rangoon available on the menu. I picked up the Philly cheese steak Rangoon that comes with cheese dipping sauce. These were sublime! Other things to note: 1. Take out only. Plenty of benches no tables. That is a shame. 2. Rewards program. If I read it right you pay 100 bucks they give you 10 bucks back. That is a pretty good deal and there is one in my pocket, because like Macarthur "I will return..."

Ordered Full order of Chicken Lo Mein. The Lo Mein tasted burnt like it was already cooked and warmed over in the wok. It smelled like dry urine which was attributed to the large mushroom slices that were borderline bad and should not have been used. I have been coming here for years but the quality is really going down on most of their dishes. Don't get me started on the outdated phone ordering process.

Be cautious when ordering from this business. They are charging you more than the listed price on their menu. I placed a catering order of 3 pans of food. They charged me approx $20 more (total) than the price listed on the menu. I realized it after they were fixing a mistake in my order. The manager was contacted and her response was too bad, either leave the food here and we will give a full refund or take it for the price we charged you. She did not care about the listed price on the menu. If I did not have an event, which obviously she knew,I would have left that food there. This business will never see another dime of my money. If i could give negative stars I would. BEWARE!! of this fraudulent business.

Food: 1/5 Service: 2/5 I read the reviews on Yelp and then found a Groupon, so I decided to give it a try. Needless to say, I definitely will NOT be returning. We ordered the atomic fire chicken and szechuan beef, both which were supposed to be spicy. The atomic chicken tasted more like sweet and sour chicken. The chicken itself was fine, but the breading was soggy and sauce was definitely on the sweet end. Almost resembled orange chicken. The szechuan beef wasn't spicy at all. The beef strips were tough and difficult to chew through and the sauce tasted like a mixture of other dishes combined. It tasted NOTHING LIKE szechuan sauce. After 3 bites, I threw out my lunch. I'm not sure how this place has received a decent rating, the food is really terrible. The lady at the counter was super nice and helpful. I rated the service 2/5 because I felt it took way too long to receive the food for a carry-out joint. (We waited 10-15 mins.)

delivery was great but man even the ticket they had attached Didn't even have the order I put in so no fried rice I got a little thing I of steamed rice and I'm not gonna lie this was like a bag of chips when I opened up the container of chicken ( every time I've ever gotten Chinese food it was full) but man you could've stuck in a fist half a fist in there it was so open/empty at the top. and i did the dinner order 2$ more with no side! I feel and obviously sure feel like that wasn't worth "bigger portion so i thought" it with the amount given. but hey THE FLAVORS WAS THERE! that's about all that was good lol. but that's worth 2 star, so get the sauce and cook your own food at home and DONT order through delivery service with them. the order won't even go to them right or they didn't cook it right / ring it up there self

Overrated in my opinion. The st. paul is delicious. The chinese menu items are lacking in taste. I had the jerk chicken sandwich and it wasn't anything near what jerk chicken tastes like. It was just super hot with peppers. Friendly and fast service. Not a favorite.
My brother in law ordered hot braised chicken. When he got home and looked, it had NO Sauce at all. Just deep fried chicken nuggets. It was the Highway 67 location. Not recommended!!!!!!!

We were told the food would be done in 5 minutes. It's been over 20 minutes so far. We should have known better from the dozen people all waiting around and no one was leaving with food. I will update the review if we ever get our meals but don't tell people 5 minutes when the wait is 20 or 30 minutes. There's plenty of chinese places around here to choose from we chose this place because it looked nice. Big mistake. UPDATE: it took 27 minutes. Food isn't even cheap for two meals and 4 egg rolls (egg rolls were not included with the meals) it was $25. The rice portions were small too. We ran out of rice before we ran out of the food. The food was really good so I'm giving it 2 stars I'm just disappointed about the time and rice portion. If it's 30 minutes tell me so I can run errands and come back. There's actually a place across the street we will try next time since they did not look busy.

If there was a way to give this place less than 1 star I would have. The rice house is not cuisine at all actually. I can't believe anyone actually enjoys this heaping mess of soy garbage. My stomach is not trained to eat this mess and I am AA. smh - Someone suggested this place to me and I was thoroughly disappointed. I'm writing this in the middle of the night bc I can't sleep thanks to an upset stomach caused by this place. I wouldnt send a pack of wild animals there

We ordered a 5 piece of regular crab Rangoon last night at the Maryland Heights location for pick up. When we got home and I bit into the first one, there was no filling. Literally, nothing. So we opened the other four and it was exactly the same. These had absolutely no filling at all. It was just deep fried breading. The picture I attached proves it. The chicken fried rice was decent, nothing special, and the buffalo chicken fried rice was identical but with hot sauce poured on top. On top of the fact that it is ridiculous to pay for an item with zero filling, this was our first time in the restaurant and we were hoping to finally find a decent Chinese food restaurant in the area. I had a great experience at the Florissant location in the past but this was nothing similar. Very disappointed.

I definitely thought this was the other rice house down the street. I ordered beef and broccoli combination plate, but it looks like veggies with five pieces of beef. I order hot wings and they are huge, looks like turkey wings instead. Needless to say, I've programmed the other "the rice house" number.

What is going on at the Rice House on Hwy 67? This past year everything I've ordered has been too salty, I mean set your tongue on fire salty. I tried to order with instructions "light on the salt & soy sauce" but rice is really dark so you know it has too much soy sauce. Needless to say I'm looking for another place to get my fried rice fix.

Very poor customer service. I picked up my order of all vegan items and I received all meat items. I called them from work and explained I am at work and can not come back today and would like a refund the girl says she cannot do a refund until the food was returned. She told me I could come back anytime this weekend. Are you serious you want me to drive around with food for days. She even said she had my correct order so she knows she gave me the wrong order. So I gave these people 18 dollars for stuff I had to throw away. I will never go back

Best Asian/Chinese in St. Louis hands down! I'm glad this place opened up in Florissant. Everytime I come back, the family and I have to visit this place. My favorite items are the fried gizzards (best seasoning), jerk chicken anything, and the philly cheese wontons. My wife always gets a St. Paul sandwich, either the Ultimate or the Angry Bird. The kids get the typical - fried rice, crab rangoons, and wings. All in all, everything are must-haves. The owners are friendly. They are a husband and wife team. The place have always been busy on weekend nights but they always get it right and serve fast.
I'd say the best fried rice in North County. I love the other sides they have as well.

When I tell you this food was soooo good, I mean it! My job had The Rice House cater lunch for us and it was the best Asian cuisine I have ever had! I will definitely be referring them to everyone I know!

I really liked it. The best part is my wife and I got more food than we could eat for $16. We had a Groupon too so it really only cost us $10. There are a few things holding it back. 1) There's no where to sit. We had to eat in the car 2) The crab rangoon is horrible. My one huge pet peeve about Chinese food is when the crab rangoon is all crunchy and hardly any filling.
Check it this spot! if you are looking for that good rice! The food is great and the egg rolls are delicious......I had the sweet & sour chicken combo and it was sooo goooood! Check them out today!
Good food, at a decent price. Excellent variety, including multi ethnic!
This place is always packed which makes no sense because the food is absolutely horrible. If you eat here expect a belly ache, that is if you can get passed the grease ridden, tasteless food.

Order somewhere else. Too expensive and they give you a childs side of rice with your order. Not worth it when other places are a buck or two cheaper and actually give you a pint of rice with your meal.

The fried rice was pretty good... however thats the only positive thing i have to say. They told me my order would be ready in 15-20 minutes. I came back 30 minutes later and they said it wasnt ready yet. I went back to my car (not much sitting room inside) and waited another 10 minutes and asked again.... it still wasnt ready. I asked how much longer it would be and they said 10 more minutes.... Of course 15 minutes later it still wasnt ready. Long story short it took over an hour just to get some fried rice and a saint paul sandwich. The rice was pretty good, but the main reason i wanted to go there was to try the angry bird saint paul sandwich. Ive always loved saint paul sandwiches, so i was intrigued by the idea of their angry bird. However when i ate it, it wasnt at all what i expected. It was disgusting. I'm thinking that i just got a bad one since it seems to be pretty popular. Not sure that it was cooked thoroughly? But I am sure that it gave me food poisoning!!! I ate this on thursday evening and I got diarrhea friday morning and had leave work early. It's now sunday night and I'm still sick.

Ever since I moved to Florissant I've been wanting to try this place because I drove by it every day. After finding a groupon for the Rice House I knew it was time to try it. My favorite to order at any Chinese restaurant is General Tso's. Their General Tso was probably the worst I've ever had. I also tried their Jambalaya Rice which was just ok. We probably won't go back to this place. It didn't satisfy our Chinese food craving at all.

Using lard to cook my veggie fried rice disgusting ill never come here again, why would you do such a thing if I'm asking for veg fried rice then I should get it but instead your giving me that garbage with no reason why at all how dare you, it makes me wonder what else your lying about, for shame you should really be making better food and not half stepping your guests.

Love this place however since they stopped delivery and I can't drive anymore I no longer purchase from them. Even when I am out in a auto, I will not stop there. Of course they could care less I am only one person. Bye it was nice knowing you

The Rice House is located in a small strip shopping center on North Lindbergh. If you aren't careful you may miss it. The establishment prides itself on its St. Paul sandwiches and its diverse menu. When the owners say they serve Asian Fusion Cuisine, they mean it. The Rice house has hamburgers, "stupid thick pork chop" sandwiches, lo mein, fried rice, fried noodles, egg foo young, chop suey or chow mein, hot braised dishes, duck, jerk chicken, ribs, livers, gizzards, hot wings, and even a pho dish or two. This place is small! Don't plan on eating here. Plan on doing the following: 1. Walk in. 2. Turn left. 3. Look at the menu and tell the owner (Sunny?) what you want. 4. Pay the man or his lovely wife. 5. Take a seat on one of the 5 benches. 6. Wait for your name to be called. Not doing any of the above may result in inefficient service or someone getting hurt. Today I had the ultimate St. Paul sandwich. Let me break it down for you. Its a huge egg foo young patty a little larger than a grown mans fist. The ultimate patty is made with beef, chicken, shrimp, pork and ham. The patty is then laid atop a piece of Texas toast that has been smeared with mayonnaise and topped with pickles and thick cut bacon. Finish this behemoth off with another piece of Texas toast and you are down. I added a slice of cheese for fifty cents. If you are feeling adventurous or have a death wish I recommend jumbo sizing your St. Paul or getting it on a jumbo butter croissant. Hell, do both. I brought my St. Paul back to work and managed to eat half of it. I am writing this review from under my desk with only the light of the monitor to keep me company. Without its warm glow I might be forced into a food coma. The food is good and was described as the best rice in St. Louis by many of the regulars.

Unfortunately, the teenagers are too busy having a conversation to take orders right. My husband ordered a shrimp combination plate with steamed rice, extra bean sprouts, and a side of broccoli. When we get home and sit down to eat, I have fried imitation crab drowning in sweet and sour sauce, a small scoop of rice with 10 bean sprouts, a burned spring roll, broccoli that tasted like chicken grease. My husband's ham friend rice wasn't amazing. And the fried wings are flavorless. The only thing they get right is the Angry bird. Anything else isn't worth your time. I tried to call my order in I around 5 but couldn't because the line was busy. I tried to call about the mix up in our order and the line is still busy. Needless to say, if this were the first bad experience I could overlook it but the last few times have been less than decent.

Rice was excellent until the opening of the other 2 sites. I got food on Saturday 23 and my rice was super greasy and my wontons were under cooked. Ive ate here alot and this is my 2nd time that ive had a problem with the service / food here. Two orders before me were either messed up or they had to be remade. Ill never eat here again. To be so expensive for rice the least thing that can be done is the employees could have a smile on there faces and my food can be cooked right

We ate their for the 1st time. Friendly staff, huge variety of food. We enjoyed everything we tried. Looking forward to going back to try other items on the menu. I'm looking forward to Taste of St. Louis I understand they will be there.

This place has went down hill to me. At first, when it was just the owner at the one store on linbergh, the food was amazing. It seems since he started branching out, the service and food has not been up to par. I think they lost my service.

Kenny runs a World-Class Operation! The Rice House in North StL serves Great Food with an extensive menu for All taste buds. If you need Catering for an event & you are READY to place that order - Call Kenny!

Last time I went there is was very busy, hot and confusing.... seemed like nobody knew what was going on. I had a take out order through grub hub and said that when I got there. They looked behind and didn't see anything. I sat and waited for like 15 min on a bench and then went back up and behold.. my order was on the shelf the entire time. Go figure, but food is decent but not worth the headache to get it.

This place used to be my go to for good fried rice that used to only be in the city. Well that was years ago but over the last few years they have gotten so cheap with the portions but the prices steady going up. A box of chicken fried rice is damn near $6 then they charge you for sauce when they only give you a few. Last order we placed was both a month ago. Total was $45 so a nice amount of food ordered. They put 6 sauces in bag for all that food! Then the boxes of rice are smaller than when I go to the city and get same thing for $3-$4. It's just sad that they over charge for their food and to be honest the quality has gone down. I'm never going there again. Every time I tried to give another chance they go up in price and it's just not worth it. I'll make the drive.

There may be places that have an item slightly better, but pound for pound, this place is awesome. The only place so far I've been able to find St. Louis city style Chinese cuisine, in St. Louis county, save one place in Woodson Terrace (that I will not mention here) So far the fried rice, egg foo young, and god help me the pot stickers have been incredible ! Very expansive menu, so a lot left to try, but so far, no complaints....well one, I wish they used slightly larger shrimp in the shrimp St. Paul sandwiches ! LOL Try this place, you won't be disappointed.

Just went for a second visit and now I remember why I didnt like it the first time. Got orange chicken w fried rice. Crab rangoon, and the cheeseburger egg rolls. Orange chicken was soggy, chewy, and literally swimming in horribly sweet sauce. Fried rice was edible but was a really small portion. Crab rangoon was worse than a buffet, slightly overcooked shell with very small amount of filling. Cheeseburger egg rolls were the best thing and I'd give them a 6/10. Cooked well but the flavor was just ok. Wouldnt go back.

Something changed here. I think it must be the cooks in the kitchen. Apparently they can't correctly read the orders on the tickets anymore because lately constantly they keep messing up the order prolonging how long the order takes. Making half the order cold why they scramble to fix the mistake. It's absolutely ridiculous ESPECIALLY for the price that I am paying for Chinese food. Most of the time the cashier's are rude and unprofessional. I'm going to skip this place from now on definitely not worth my drive from south city.

I tried the Rice House out recently and to be honest, I was a little let down by the food. It is a small space but has plenty of options on the menu. I placed an order online to pick up via Postmates and the order was ready in a timely manner. The staff were friendly and accommodating as well. I ordered the Hot Braised Chicken Wings Combo Plate. The food wasn't the worst but it could definitely be improved. I was very underwhelmed by the quality of the chicken; especially for the price of almost $10. It was barely edible and I left disappointed wishing I'd gone to my local Chop Suey instead. Perhaps I picked a bad entree but I am willing to give this place another chance. I will update my review upon my next visit.

I ordered the Ultimate St. Paul sandwich and a half order of shrimp fried rice. The sandwich was so BIG, probably the size of my face. I wasn't expecting it but I was pleased. It'll last me a few meals lol. The sandwich was really good. Now the RICE has to be the best I've ever had and yes I'm from STL. I mean it tastes like they made my food with love and care. I will be a returning customer.

I just got food poisoned from eating a beef saint paul from this place. I called to discuss the issue with the manager to make them aware of the situation. I was referred to a voicemail box that was full and not accepting any messages. Food safety and contamination doesn't appear to be a priority.

OMG!!!! The best thing in my bag was the SODA!!!! The food stunk!!! They left the crab Rangoon off, went to pick it up & the order was cold!! The duck n noodles had no flavor the rice wasn't tasteful and I think the menu expanded which the quality went dwn in the basics!!! Over all not a good appetizing pleasure!

A little bit more expensive than your regular rice houses but really good food. Didn't take too long to place my order at all. They have a very lengthy menu, so take time to look over the entire menu and let someone else order ahead of you if you don't know what you want. Order came right up and no issues.

Used to be pretty good, especially with delivery. Sadly, they stopped delivering. Called in several orders, to show up and wait inside for 15-20 minutes each time. Quality of food has drooped off severely as well.

The first thing I will say is that I noticed how CLEAN this place is! It is very very clean. The menu has plenty of options. The food is fantastic and the staff are so nice! I will go back for sure! I also saw a groupon for this place. They are starting buffets on Saturday and Sunday!!!

My wife and I don't live in Saint Louis county but every time we are there and want Chinese we come to Rice House. Boneless hot braised chicken combo w/ 2 pieces crab Rangoon and with a side of 10 piece crab Rangoon. Love it!

First time ordering, (and then I ordered from the Dorsett location) they completely managed to miss a meal that I ordered. I went back and the manager fixed the meal, then proceed to talk to the cashier about my excellent parking situation (I parked crooked) which was caused by the car next to me being too close to the line. Extremely unprofessional and rude. Never going back or recommending it to anyone. I agree with everyone on here, I just wish I looked into it before placing an order.
The food at the rice house is amazing the chicken really good I also love the rice the rice house is so far the best Chinese food I've had so far I would definitely come back in the future
Best selection of rice around. They have a very extensive menu, you are sure to find something you like.

Tiny hole in the wall Asian restaurant with only take out, where the specialty is the St. Paul sandwich. A St. Paul sandwich is a St. Louis original that consists of an egg patty topped with pickles, white onion, iceberg lettuce and mayonnaise served on white bread. Lots of different types of meat you can add to their St. Paul sandwiches as well. Also have a bunch of classic chinese-esk dishes that have an added Cajun flare, including over 20 varieties of fried rice. I got a beef, chicken, and shrimp St. Paul sandwich and the Basil Fried Rice, and I was far more impressed with their quality than I was expecting given the run down environment that is The Rice House. I have never had a St. Paul sandwich, but it tasted a lot like a Big Mac and was very tasty. The actual restaurant itself was very run down and I would definitely not describe the staff as being warm or welcoming. It reminded me of a cheap take-out Chinese restaurant.

Most disappointing St Paul sandwiches ever! I'm always looking for a good St. Paul. For those who don't know what these are, it's an egg patty that contains meat, onions and bean sprouts usually served on white bread with mayo and pickles. Sounds plain, but can be quite tasty when prepared right. The two I've gotten from here thus far were way too over cooked and burned and quite soggy. I haven't tried any of the specialty St. Pauls like the Angry Bird one, but I won't be going back.
This place is horrible I wasn't suggest this place to anyone. The service here is horrid I wouldn't advise anyone to come here and eat.

I called in a carry out order on 10/30/20 & the young man answering the phone provided the best customer service I've experienced in quite some time! The food here is always delicious; it's our go to spot. But to call a restaurant during pandemic time and getting someone who asks how you are, repeats your order back to confirm it's correct and thanks you for your business is rare and highly appreciated!

Too many rules and guidelines for ordering food. I ordered Fried Rice that contained shrimp and I was told how many shrimp would be in the box..... The prices were very high for casual fast food and the wait was extensive
Good place to get some rice in St. Louis, affordable and filling, stop by here whenever I'm in town, service always great

trash.....don't waste your money. 4 shrimp in an order of steamed rice shrimp & w/extra shrimp!!! $4.00 charge for the extra shrimp.............no wonder they have all sales are final on the door............they would not make any money. i essentially paid 10.00 for a box of steamed rice w/4 shrimp. when i called...."oh you can have a credit" sssssseriously???

Good food but for some reason the "other" location on N. Hwy 67 has marginal service. Well at least for me. Maybe it's my luck but it just takes too long to get your food. Last week they actually forgot to put my order in. I noticed when my ticket number was skipped. Once I brought it to their attention there were no apologies, no nothing. Basically I just had to sit my ass back down and wait. Would have left if I hadn't already paid.

Yesterday was the first time I got a chance to go to this restaurant and I had the strawberry cheesecake crab Rangoon, chicken fried rice and the collard green gumbo. The location I went to was the one off of Highway 67. Now I did enjoy the crab Rangoon as well as the gumbo and the chicken fried rice was okay. Their menus pretty extensive and I will recommend it to anyone that likes variety in their choices. They've fused together some pretty interesting recipes from different cuisines and if you're patient you'll find one that suits you the best. I would recommend this restaurant to others.
This place has some of the best Chinese food I've ever had. Everything taste fresh ,the prices aren't bad, and the portion size is nice. This place is a definite repeat.
I love this place. Their Ultimate Fried Rice and Cheesesteak Wonton are delicious!!!!
Love ALL The Rice Houses! Cannot go wrong with anything on the menu! Please start making Hot & Sour Soup. I know you guys would put a home made spin on it!
We eat out every Friday. This was the most unappetizing meal ever. Rice was weird, chicken and crab ragoon were OK. The lady who gave us the food was great, keep her!

This review is for the new location on Dorsett in Maryland Heights. That location is not on Yelp yet. 12/12/15 Ordered: Combination Plate Beef & Broccoli with pork fried rice and an egg roll. & Daily Special General Tso's The Beef & Broccoli should be called carrots, onions, broccoli with a few pieces of meat. It was very bland. Hardly any seasoning. I didn't even see any garlic in the sauce. The pork fried rice was nothing special. A lot of soy sauce, very little egg and a few pieces of pork. Zero vegetables. The General Tso's Chicken Daily Special is served with steamed rice. General Tso's is supposed to be a bit sweet & spicy, theirs is just sweet. No kick at all. The chicken was also quite soggy. The portion of chicken is larger than the combination plate. The steamed rice is a VERY small portion compared to what they include in the Entrée. Maybe a quarter cup of rice. See pictures. Overall, it's overpriced for the portions you get and, in my opinion, it simply doesn't taste good. The service was friendly and quite quick. ***They put their combination plates in a styrofoam container and then put it in a paper bag...so the inevitable happened. The container leaked soaking the paper bag which then got on the seat of my car, all over the condiment packages, napkins and plastic ware. So therefore, I would ask for a plastic bag if you choose to order a combination plate.
Man this the second time I been here in two months and y'all haven't gotten my order right yet. I order shrimp fried rice with extra shrimp and get home and have ham fried rice. I don't eat pork!!!!!

My cholesterol went up when I walked in the door and looked at the menu. What mattered most was the food was so good. The waitstaff was helpful in helping me make a decision. Don't expect to eat at the location and the prices are cheap. Enjoy!

1ST TIME, LAST TIME. I ordered Vegetable steamed rice. Somebody forgot to cut up the veggies!!!! I had to empty on to a plate and chop the veggies. Did I mention that the rice had NO flavor whatsoever? the Duck leg was overcooked, dry. !st time, LAST TIME!
A very clean establishment. They have an extensive menu, with some gourmet Asian fusion options. Call in your order and be ready to wait a little. A busy and popular spot!

Love their rice and service is good . I don't eat everyone's rice so ever since my dad got it a while back , it's been a every 2 weeks thing lol (ikr bad) . I would say this is the best Chinese Food in St.Louis County . If your new , just try Any fried rice and there St.Paul sandwich's are A M A Z I N G . Egg Fo Young is great as well . But sometimes the customer service can be better . I just think they get a lil overwhelmed because of how busy it gets . But other than that , the food is great !

Philly steak Rangoon was delicious. Their fried rice has a smoky flavor to it which was really good. Beef broccoli was great. Used them for a catering event and they were on time and food was a great. Would use them again.

Curried Burrito - 5/5 Chicken Salad Sandwich - 5/5 Dirty Chai - 4/5 Espresso - 4/5 Service - 5/5 I come in at least once a week and I am never disappointed in the food, drink, and service I receive. The quality is mostly consistent and the atmosphere is nice and the noise volume is never too loud. The rotating art items and the little retail items made by local Boiseans give the place a great vibe. The food items are usually loaded and crafted with ingredients that go amazingly well with each other. The staff give you good suggestions if you don't know what to try and when you pick an item they give you a side of salsa, sriracha sour cream, etc that pair up nicely with what was ordered. The espresso is usually made to perfection, but the bad cup of espresso is unavoidable due to the art of making espresso, or being picky. Truly as good as a coffee shop gets.

I was in town visiting from Dallas and decided to stop here. It was an early morning so I knew I wasn't going to have a chance to try the next-door Goldy's restaurant. But this place did not disappoint. I got the bacon potato and cheese quiche and a regular drip coffee. Both were great. They had a lot of other breakfast options as well.

While we were waiting to get into Goldy's Breakfast Bistro they sent us to the corner for coffee...which you pay for and then can bring into the main restaurant when your table is ready. Which was perfect.....a nice place to sit while we were waiting and plenty of people just grabbing coffee and other light breakfast baked goods.
This space needs some attention and a breathe of fresh air. Dated seating, paint scratched off the walls, the space is hard on the eyes. Coffee was okay best.

I frequent this coffee shop often while waiting for a seat at Goldies next door. The staff has always been kind and fun. Art work on the walls, some locally crafted merchandise, board games and books available.

Great place to hang out, grab a bite or a coffee while waiting for your seat to open at Goldy's.. seriously the best marketing ploy by them since they always have a wait. Music is not annoying, lots of fun art and hand made gifts to check out.. overall great corner place in down town Boise

Tried a cinnamon roll with nuts and a chocolate chip cookie that looked really good in the case. It was awful. The cookie was stale and was completely lacking in salt so I was flavorless. The cinnamon roll was just average. The guy that helped me was really friendly though, hence the second star. Note to self... if I ever give this place another try, ask them how fresh the items I'm interested in purchasing are. Was salt added to the recipe? Baked goods without any salt are generally very bland. Not my personal preference.

I absolutely adore Goldy's Corner. If you order to-go from Goldy's Bistro, they'll bring it right over to the corner for you to enjoy:) the corner is open until 3 AM on Friday and Saturday nights, which is makes it one of the few late night food options is downtown Boise on weekends!! I like to stop in for an espresso shot before going out:) they also have amaaazing crepes, breakfast burritos, quiche, local fresh pastries, and a rad little gift shop of local trinkets! The service absolutely rocks, if you want a delicious surprise crepe or smoothie, they'll whip something special up for you (after they ask about food allergies first, of course!). They bring out your food and drinks, and when they can they take your dishes:) the prices, and the inviting, homey, kind atmosphere will keep me a regular for the rest of my days in Boise!

This is a new staple for me when I am in Boise. It is in a perfect downtown location and has that very "city chic" vibe going. I've been in only on Saturday mornings and the place is hoppin'. Cute little booth, vintage chairs, and all sorts of different kind of people. It's very homey and the staff treat you & talk to you like friends. I have ordered the regular mimosa and the sucker is HUGE. At first I was surprised at the price, but when you see the huge glass it comes in, it is worth it. Super yummy. The most recent time, I ordered a blueberry scone. They warm it up for you, and it is just delicious. They have ALL sorts of food and I can't wait to try something else next time I am in. If you need a cute little spot for brunch/coffee/ etc Goldy's Corner is GREAT.

Good spot for the overflow from Goldie's Breakfast Bistro, Goldie's Corner just a few doors down serves lattes, expresso and coffee along with homebaked pastries. Sorry to whine, but I have to gripe that the soy latte was watery: not with the substantial crema and strong expresso flavor I covet. (Granted, I've been living in Seattle lately, and Seattle coffee standards can be high.) The girls behind the counter were adorable, but not experienced baristas. The baked goods were stored and served in saran wrap, which did kinda lessen the aesthetic of dining at Goldy's Corner, despite the apt consideration to hygiene. I can say that morning I appreciated that Goldie's Corner was there, since it provided us a good spot to wait patiently for a table at Goldies Breakfast Bistro. But then, after waiting about an hour, I started to get grumpy. And this is when I started to suspect that maybe Goldie's had a more sinister plan. Two breakfasts. Yes. You heard me. Its basically a genius business move. Why expand the original dining room to shorten wait times? What if instead, customers would eat two separate breakfasts in one day? Think about it. With an hour to two hour wait times for Goldie's Bistro (and with a no reservations policy) hungry customers eat a first breakfast course at Goldie's Corner (coffee cake, expresso, banana bread) while waiting to eat the big breakfast at Goldie's Breakfast Bistro. Then, once seated, that full menu looks so good, and you've waited so long,... Okay. Round 2. Bring it. Genius. That's two breakfasts, and lots and lots of carbohydrates, folks. From a customer perspective, its not particularly cost effective or efficient to eat breakfast twice. Be forewarned that despite being sleepy, and in a haze of hunger, there are real consequences for these types of decisions,. Once the coffee cake, cinnamon roll and pancake frenzy has concluded, these things become painfully, painfully clear.

Here for the lavender lemonade mimosa. Veeeeery light hint of lavender. If you're not sure if you like lavender, this is for you. If you're a lavender lover (like me) you'll want to ask for another shot of lavender syrup Great service. Great location. Alert: are you a cinnamon roll lover? They have gigantic cinnamon roles! And caramel roles... Pro tip: if you're waiting to dine at Goldy's Breakfast (long lines because it's GOOD), come here to get a starter drink. It'll make the wait more fun. Best part? You can get your drink to go so don't feel rushed to finish it

First, I am not a coffee drinker so I can't comment on that but their mimosas and treats are delicious! They have day old baked goodies sold for a crazy discount and they are just as delicious. The cinnamon rolls and lemon tarts are delicious, the lemon tarts are perfectly tangy and the crust is so buttery and flaky and they warm up the giant fluffy cinnamon rolls. They have games too for you to play if you go with someone else and they have a little patio so you can people watch.

While waiting for a table at Goldy's we stopped by Goldy's Corner for a pre-breakfast cup of coffee. It is a cute little nook that is just off to the side of the restaurant. It is cozy and has a very chill atmosphere. Since we were from out of town we were unfamiliar with the area and didn't realize what a totally cool place Boise was, and especially the downtown area. We ordered a Breve' and wondered among the little trinkets they had for sell. I was delighted to find a little homemade novelty hand towel I plan on give as a Christmas present to a dear friend. We waited for about 25 min before our table was ready and thoroughly enjoyed our breakfast.

So much better than the hotel coffee I had yesterday - and I was pretty happy with that coffee. My vanilla latte at Goldys made my sleepy heart sing. The pumpkin bread was fresh, tasty, and a huge slice! Much more generous portion than most coffee shops. I'll be back tomorrow morning!

I don't understand why, if you can't manage to work up a smile for your customers while greeting them and serving them, why do you put yourself in front of people every morning. For God's sake, don't be so grumpy. The food made up for it and they did keep the coffee coming. Likely won't be a regular.
If you want dessert, local art, gifts, or jewelry, go to Goldy's. Everything is amazing, and I imagine it would be a great place to sit for awhile.

I've been here twice in the last year. First time for breakfast. Which was absolutely great. One of the better meals I've had with my wife. Second meal was so close to lunch time, my wife and I tried lunch. We had the mushroom cheese burger. It was ok. One of the few places that uses real cheese. Though the bun was bigger than the meat patty. With two drinks and a average tip it was over $ 30.00. I thought it was on the high side for what you got. The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 was mainly 3 reasons. High pricing. .Especially for lunch Cleanliness. .dust balls and lint hanging from air vents over my table. Though everything else looked clean. Wait time on food. Over if not close to 20 minutes.

This coffee shop offers mimosa by the glass and by the flight!!! Enough said! If that is not enough, know that mimosas are half off during happy hour, which is 17:00-21:00 (or closing, whichever is earlier) every day! Grab a seat at the outdoor patio and enjoy the view of the Capitol two blocks away.

Firts time in. I loved the food. It was really busy and its a small space. It was hard to social distance inside but no one seem to mind. The service was good. I had a chorizo tomato onion omelet and i i was very impressed with how much the onion and tomato tasted it was delicious. I wasn't to impressed with the sliced of sourdough French toast. My boyfriend had the steak omelet and he enjoyed it. The coffee was good. The short stack of chocolate chip pancakes where amazing.

I couldn't love this place more. Both the food and beverages are stellar. All the baked goods I have tried (a bran muffin, vegan sugar cookie, lemon bar) were fresh, moist, and just the right amount of sweet. Additionally, things are pretty reasonably priced and they sell day-olds for a discount. They brew Dawson Taylor coffee, and make espresso drinks with care. They also offer a wide variety of fresh fruit smoothies and other specialty drinks. They always brew four types of coffee, and it's self-serve with a bottomless cup, so you can get good and jittery, you can knock yourself out. My favorite aspect of this coffee shop is the friendly staff. They always make me feel truly welcome and offer a real, genuine human connection. They will go out of their way to help you decide between food options, will keep a tab open so you can linger all afternoon and keep picking things up, and are happy to answer a litany of questions. There are a few little tables, booths, and some comfy chairs and couches to hang in, as well as an odd little collection of cards and bags to peruse if you're waiting in line. Whether you're hanging out until you get a table for breakfast next door, or looking for a place with good coffee that isn't a total scene, I highly recommend Goldy's Corner.

Seriously the best mimosa in Boise! My friend and I got the lavender mimosas a while ago and I can't stop thinking about them! Can't wait to go back! I love coming here for a drink while waiting for a table at the restaurant next door!
Saturday morning, busy place with excellent service and essential coffee shop foods. Three sandwiches and two coffees was 27$. Kids got caramel macchiato they seemed weak and short of flavor.

Fun place. They know me by name and order. Friendly and welcoming. Smiling and friendly. Courteous and welcoming, even if your waiting for space at Goldies next door. Good place to study for college and degrees. Goid wifi. Also play chess and other board games that atr far from boring. Burritos run out fast in the morning. Close to Egyptian and other sites, main bus terminal or The Amsterdam or City Hall. So come to Goldys Corner and be ready!

This is the spot to go if you want good food, pastries, and a chill atmosphere. I do all my studying here and love the weekend hours. I have never had a bad beverage or pot of tea. The workers are incredibly friendly too. If you love cream puffs, pie, cinnamon rolls, cookies, cheese cake, no bakes, brownies, scones and more this is your spot. They also serve a limited menu of diner food after 6ish! I see people commenting that the environment needs a touch up but I disagree. Many coffee shops are too worried about looking cool and fail to provide comfort and quality dishes. My one complaint is the music can be flat out bad and on occasion too loud...
Wide selection of pastries/desserts and very, very generous serving sizes. Good, local coffee. Good prices. Very friendly. I wish they had more space for seating but that's beyond their control.

Mimosa will knock you on your face... in a good way! The Berries & Bubbly is pretty fabulous, but really any of their champagne options are! (The Sunrise is dangerously fabulous!)... Coffee is good, baked goods are yummy, and the customer service is wonderful! Tip BIG! :)

Autumn spice latte may be one of the best lattes I have ever had. Delicious! We had a super yummy caramel roll while waiting for our table to be ready next door at Goldys. Came back every morning during our stay in Boise.

I went to lunch here with my husband a few weeks ago for my first time, we ordered sandwiches, when I received my sandwich I noticed that it was dry and there was no avocado, which I had ordered, so my husband very kindly went to the counter and told the young girl that she forgot avocado, she replied by telling him that they didn't have any. Well, I had my heart set on what I ordered and so I didn't want to eat that dry $8 sandwich when I paid for avocado and didn't get it. So my husband asked her if we could get a refund on just my sandwich, he was happy with his, and the girl behind the counter very rudely said "there is nothing wrong with that sandwich, if you're not happy you can order so thing else"......I have managed a restaurant for 3 years and I was just completely infuriated with the lack of customer service. AND to top it, when we paid before we received our food we even left her a $5 tip on a $20 order of 2 sandwiches...... I called 3 times that week to speak to the owner, we was never in the restaurant at the time so I left 3 messages with no call back. I think it's safe to say that I will never eat at Goldy's again, it was undoubtedly the most horrible customer experience I have ever had.

I don't care for small coffee shops. The beans are over roasted, the coffee is too hot, and the baristas are pretentious. It's coffee. You don't have to be snooty. This place is the right amount of quirky coffee shop meets comfy seating. The Americana I ordered was perfect. The baristas were friendly and chatty. The customers were smiling and laughing. I recommend this place to everyone.

Goldy's was worth the wait! Sunday morning...yes, Sunday morning we decided to try goldys. Restaurant had character and wonderful breakfast options. I had fried eggs, bacon and peppa potatoes (which are home fries with onions and bell peppers with cheese on top). They offer mimosas that are nice size. Not to large... not to small. My guy had an egg scramble with basque chorizo and green peppers, sage sausage and hash browns. Waiter was pleasant and efficient. Once you get into the restaurant it's all good. With music, and fun artistic things to look at. I only took off one star because of the wait... there is a Goldy's cafe around the corner that you can have your coffee or beverage and wait to be called. Portion sizes were large. Large enough to share. Respectable prices for the food.

Stopped by for a coffee and was pleasantly surprised to find they had cold brewed coffee for an iced toddy. Got one to share with the husband for our sightseeing walk to the capitol building and it was too tasty to last very long. We stopped back by thinking to pay for a refill but the friendly barista said it was free. Nice surprise and nice place!
Great food, awesome drinks and happy hour. they also are open late on the weekends. the staff is incredibly friendly.

Great place to stop for a coffee/baked good. As for the food, I would not suggest the fish dinner or a sandwich. (Not to mention the fact that the staff did not seem to want to make the food because it was later?) But the overall feel inside is nice to sit and hang out.

This is our 5th and last visit. First 2 times it was great. Downhill each time since and today was the worst. Dark roast coffee was very watery. Purchased 3 different quiches, cinnamon roll, coffee cake, banana bread and 2 pot pies to go for a small brunch gathering. Quiche was old tasting, roll, cake and bread were dried out and the pot pies previously delicious were just ok. Only reason for the 2 stars is the friendly and personable good service received from the staff. Not sure if it was because it was a Monday and food had been sitting around. For almost $38 I expected at least one good item. Only thing not thrown out were the chicken pot pies. I would seriously worry about getting food poisoning here due to the failure to ensure food is rotated and fresh. Very disappointing as we were hoping this would be a good place for breakfast and lunch.

This is my favorite place to pick up cup of coffee in the mornings. It's also a great place to snag a pastry and hang out if you've got the time. The staff is friendly and the coffee is good. I haven't had proper breakfast here (I just go to Goldy's for that), but the half breakfast burritos are great. The coffee is decently priced but the food can be a bit pricey. There is also a little knickknack corner where you can purchase some local artists' work, a selection of teas, coffees, and funky magnets. This is a good place to get some odds and ends for your eclectic friends and family members.
Such a cool little corner! Got some swag and treats to boot! Cozy, and has great art!

Cool little corner coffee shop. It's a good place to hang out while you're waiting to be seated next door. I had a 40 minute wait at Goldy's, so I decided to kill some time here. There is a decent amount of seating. Not a ton of power outlets. Good selection of pastries and drinks. It gets pretty busy and noisy here, so not the best coffee shop to work at.

I have to give Goldy's Corner three stars for their outrageously-priced gluten free offerings. I appreciate the convenience of the various gluten free choices (baked by Amaru Confections) and don't get me wrong, they are quite tasty, however at $4 or more for a standard slice of banana bread, muffin or lemon bar, I don't feel like I'm getting my money's worth even with the gluten free mark-up that I'm accustomed to.

My friend and I were feeling the brunch lifestyle Saturday morning and decided to try out Goldy's. The actual restaurant had a 45 minute wait, and since we were already whipped up into a brunch frenzy we decided to check out Goldy's Corner. My buddy ordered the spinach, mushroom, and Swiss quiche while I had the bacon, potato, and cheddar casserole. Definitely filling, especially for the price (~$4 each) but nothing to write home about. The employees were very friendly though, and I definitely would like to try some of their delicious-looking baked goods.
The coffee is good and the people are nice but be careful of the pastries! Ask when they were made - they're often not very fresh. My cinnamon roll was hard as a rock and inedible.
Goldys corners is probably the go to place for all the customers facing an extra long wait to get a table at Goldys. Their food is terrible. Breads and cakes are pretty hard too.
Great! Gluten free pastries as well, made me happy! Nice, cuddly coffee shop attached to the famous cafe, and their food is just as good.
Great place to get an afternoon cup of coffee & a snack, and sit outside and people watch. The coffee was good and the barista was super friendly. I will be back.

What a brilliant idea. This coffee shop is adjacent to Goldy's restaurant. Goldy's restaurant is a popular breakfast place in the Boise area so when you have an hour wait. What better way to keep people nearby than to have a coffee shop next door. It certainly worked in our case. In case you get a little crazy they have snacks there as well. A selection of sundry items as well bandages, aspirin, and the like. Quite cozy and nice to hang out with friends. I believe they have wi-fi there as there was one person working on a computer in there but I don't know for sure. The restaurant around the corner takes your cell number and calls you when your table is ready. Very handy. I would come back here with or without going to the restaurant around the corner.
From out of town looking for a late night dessert after dinner. Got a Poke Cake & Chai latte. The cake was very dry and felt low quality. The chai latte was far too sweet. Wouldn't recommend.

The coffee is good, and the food is tasty, but the service was the nastiest coffee shop service I have ever experienced. I don't know if it was the particular staff (Emily served us) or if they were having a bad day, but there is no excuse for service this poor. I have been to this coffee shop many times, as I love how they have coffee ice cubes (so my coffee does not get diluted). The baristas were curt and rude. I will not be returning to this coffee shop, especially as there are many other equally tasty coffee shops within a minutes walk. I truly hope the baristas can learn to smile and have some basic customer service skills.

Stopped in for a cup to go... What a cute little place! Lots of people, but in a great Sunday morning social way. Their food looks amazing, like gigantic cinnamon rolls and scones! I was only looking for a cup of coffee though. Ordered a mocha. Simply wonderful!

Loved this place and the staff! Was in town for work and stopped in for my morning caffeine on the way to meetings. They had a great combination of coffee drinks - I had the Dirty Chai and it was great. Not to mention that the morning wait staff was so upbeat that they were contagious :-)
The coffee was delicious and the apple crumble muffin was a little dry. The decor and atmosphere were fun. The prices were really good for downtown.
Amazing! No idea what I ordered, but it tastes so good! It definitely has some potatoes in it.

Went in on a Monday morning that this joint was packed! Managed to get to bar immediately. Food was very tasty and they had great selection of items on the menu. Definitely the best spot for breakfast in downtown Boise.

Goldy's Corner is absolutely golden! For a coffee shop in Boise, it truly is an up and coming joint that will be the place to hang out for an early morning wake up call or a late late weekend night. I'll be sitting at one of the booths near the window, on a late Friday night studying until the live music comes in to play. In the meantime, women are preparing to assemble for a night of clubbing by splurging on the happy hour that's provided. Personally, I've never had the alcoholic drinks they make, but they look good. It's interesting, late at night when people are done dancing they'll come in looking for something to eat, and the large cinnamon rolls seem to be very popular. The coffee I drink is very sweet and is usually all I'll order. It's the White Macadamia Nut Latte. Very good. It's my substitute for Stumptown coffee. Most importantly though, is the Goldy's Corner staff. From the girls to the guys that treat you like a friend, who are truly respectful no matter who walks in. Well, unless you're out to cause trouble late at night and then you'll have to deal with Danny, you the man Danny! Then there's Alex, who was kind enough to give me a free drink card twice, thank you dude. Then there's the girls, they're down to earth and sweet, they're truly who you'd be happy with bringing your coffee to your table or chair. Everyone is easy going, but also know how to run a tight ship. It's perfect. Not very many people in Boise are aware that Goldy's Corner is separate to Goldy's Breakfast Bistro. They're both owned by the same owner though.
I got a bread pudding muffin from here to take on the plane. I didn't like the dates it had in it. Service was ok. They have a restaurant next door.

Disgusted !!!!!!!! Checked in at Goldy's restaurant for breakfast today around 12:00, and give them my name and cell number. Hostess says go walk around the corner to their coffee shop and they will call when our table is ready. We do and when we get there we order two coffees. One was a simple cup of coffee to stay, aka they give you a regular coffee cup and you take it to the air pumps and get what you want. The gal gives me a cup and points me to the air pumps. I see my cup is obviously dirty and still has coffee on the rim. I tell her this and ask for a clean cup. Yep, she takes my dirty cup and puts it right back from where she got it from, then grabs me the cup beside it. I call her out on it, and she tells me " I will wash it later". She says it's just some old drip coffee on the rim. She then mocks me to the guy making coffees. First and last time we will ever go to this place. A simple, oh sorry, and then put the dirty cup In the wash and I would have had no problem. Instead, yet another person got a dirty cup because she was too lazy to wash it. On a brighter note, when we got called to come back to the restaurant for breakfast, it was amazing. Amazing food, and we will definitely come back for breakfast, but not for the dirty coffee cups from the lazy employee.

I have spent so much time and money here because it's a great place to study or just chill. they have breakfast burritos, sweet treats, coffee, tea, cold drinks, fresh sandwiches, smoothies, and mimosas.

The two ladies working today are awesome! Super fast and friendly. Great at balancing urgency with great customer service. We put our name on the waitlist for their restaurant and walked around the corner to get coffee while we waited. The host gets your number and calls when your table is ready. Spicy mocha: cinnamon, cardamom, and a pinch of cayenne. Try it!

It seems this is the annex coffee joint space adjacent to Goldy's breakfast bistro, perhaps in place especially for those faced with a lengthy wait to get inside the namesake restaurant. It's a strange place to say the least. It feels more like a run down coffee shop from the early 90's (which I sort of think is cool and nostalgic). So, I suppose strange in a good way. I only had their iced coffee, but it tasted very good. They had a decent playlist going the day I was there. The staff are very nice and the patrons seemed on the youngish side, mostly millenials who ironically probably don't know what my reference to 90's rundown coffee shops means. This is a decent place to chill out. Their pastries did not look good. I observed that they served some alcoholic beverages (mimosas I think I saw) so maybe that might add to the draw here also. Check it out if you're in the area and need a place to relax for a little while.

Reviews looked great so we went to try it out this morning. The pecan caramel roll was very dry and hard. My husband got me a raspberry scone and it wasn't at all why I expected. It was this big flat square piece covered in a thick sugary glaze that was sooo sweet I couldn't enjoy it at all. Even my sweet toothed 4 year old wouldn't eat it. It was very crowded which is a good thing and not complaining there. The restrooms were filthy! Can't see us returning there ever again.
Always consistent. Great service. Friendly counter which is where I like to eat. The food is always spot on.
Best Dirty Chai I've had in a while. Friendly staff and th ey have HUGE cinnamon rolls. Will be back again and again.

Fantastic customer service today. Eddie was very friendly and provided some of the best service I've received from a barista in a long time. The coffee came quick and was delicious today. Thank you and great job keep it up!

My husband and I stoped in for a snack while waiting for a table in the main return to next door. I got the strawberry mimosa, he had a hot mocha, and we split a cinnamon roll. All was excellent, but we were too full to eat a big breakfast after. Either way, it was a win and we will be trying the main restaurant soon.

Mold in my bread pudding muffin. Mmm yup! A big ol' nasty bunch of mold right in the center after my daughter and I had eaten half of it. Was asked if I wanted something else by compassionate counter staff...but I.don't.think.so. First time here, first time in Boise, love that this is here to have coffee while we are waiting for our table next door. No stir sticks to stir large coffee though? Really? Mk...Good selection of beverages though.

Great service with a smile. I had the spicy mocha which was a creative mocha with cayenne pepper and had the perfect amount of spice. It wasn't hot enough but I am hard to please so I've given up blaming the coffee shops for that. Fruit crepe was good - they use pre-made crepes but honestly I could only tell because it wasn't warm. Comfortable seating, pleasant atmosphere. Loved it!

This is a great local spot downtown that you can get a quick bite to eat, coffee, or an alcoholic drink and get some work done on your laptop or meet up with colleagues for a group meeting. I used to love coming here in college to work on papers or homework and I still love coming here to get work done! The food here is really delicious and you can get breakfast-y goodness at all hours! Their breakfast sandwiches and quiche are among my favorites. The mimosas here are amazing and HUGE - the biggest in boise. My favorite is their lavender mimosa-- you have to try it! They also have amazing coffee drinks, and yes there's an option to make it "Irish" by adding coffee liquor. The staff here is awesome! Eddie makes the best mimosas but pretty much everyone I've encountered that works here is really cool and attentive.

Holy cow is this a tasty place for breakfast. I'm talking the best coffee, fantastic food, nice service. The seating is very limited but wait. It is worth it. The corned beef was incredible...so very fresh and salty...perfect. The potatoes and sausage were just incredible. I'm so infinitely sad that we were visiting. It's almost worth flying in just to eat there. Not joking...

Get the taste of Goldy's without the line. The pastries can be off-putting because they are wrapped in Saran wrap, but don't be fooled -- they are tasty and can be warmed up on request. I personally like the breakfast burritos, particularly the Italian and bacon ones. Don't be fooled by the size. They are VERY filling. Service is very friendly and attentive. The lattes are not as good as district coffeehouse or flying M, but are still quite drinkable.

Goldy's corner has been my go to coffee shop in Boise. The service is usually pretty friendly, and I'm able to post up for hours and do some homework. I am sad though that they don't have any vegan food options anymore. They used to have so many, and now you can't even get a bagel.

Best bakery in Boise!!! Service is excellent and blueberry scones are the best scones I've ever had that didn't come from Ceres Bakery in Kalispell, MT. Great atmosphere. A nice place to chill. Really casual and unpretentious vibe. The cookies are disappointing but all the quick-breads are amazing. Nice drink selection, too!

Good Family restaurant, girls night out, date and/or business lunch. Visited 4 times in the past 5 months. The good is great. Service is consistently good. Each time I have gone with a different group of people so I got a chance to hear what they thought of their meal. From the Tuna entree to the Kale& Quinoa Salad to the Chicken and Donuts ( with Mac&Cheese) and the Impossible Burger, everyone enjoyed their meals. I am more health conscience and the menu provides delicious & healthy choices (Gluten-Free, Vegetarian and Vegan). Never had their desserts but everything looks good. The bakery on the first floor has been crowded every time I've walked in.

Delicious as always! We always have the buffet when we come here and it never disappoints! Love it! Also whenever we have out of town guests this buffet experience is our go to... our friends always love it!

My son and I stopped by the Founding Farmers First Bake Cafe & Creamery for a quick breakfast before heading to an appointment at CHOP. I ordered an iced coffee and bagel with cream cheese and he ordered a donut and milk. The three year old was tickled pink that his milk came in a travel coffee cup, the same as my coffee. I did find it odd that my iced coffee came in a hot cup versus a cold cup with a straw, but not the end of the world. The chocolate covered donut was not good. I hate to say it that way, but the taste was completely off. It was doughy and somewhat flavorless. My bagel did not arrive until my son was well over half done with this bagel, it took quite a bit of time, especially since there appeared to be more employees in than customers. Not the best scenario when you are in a mild hurry and your toddler is not patient once the good is gone. The bagel itself was okay, but there was barely any cream cheese on it. I don't like a ton of cream cheese (I hate places that slop it on), but this had hardly any! On the flip side, my iced coffee was delicious, I would order that again if I happened to be there, but I wouldn't go out of my way to grab breakfast there again.

We have been to the bakery a dozen of times because my kids really like their donuts. They indeed have tasty sweets to keep us coming back. The bagel sandwiches were great as well (they stopped selling due to no time to prepare) But since day one, the service has been unbelievably slow and disorganized even when there are not many customers. Many times in the morning (between 8-10am) the donut racks are empty or lacking choices while nobody (including the kitchen staff I saw in the back) seem to care about it. When we were ordering donuts to go, the service person struggled to find a box, then the liner of the box, then tissue to grab the donuts because they were all out at 9am!? And when he finally found it, he just dumped the whole stack into a water jug behind him....i don't know if they are forever understaffed or what, apparently we can only rely on our luck to have a perfect donut day....

The donuts. All I can say is try them and you will be sold. The devils food donut is a must try. The coffee is also really good. Service can be kinda slow but it's worth it and it's easy on the wallet.

I stopped by during their "soft opening" last week and am looking forward to returning. The staff are very friendly and helpful. I loved the bright, clean, and rustic decor. The coffee was fresh and delicious. I also grabbed a creme brûlée donut that was so amazing, I haven't stopped thinking about it! Definitely stop by if you're in the area!

This has always been one of my favorite restaurants for brunch. I had never been to this particular location, and was a bit shocked at how delicious and consistent all Founding Farmers are. The food is soft, rich, and a complete delight. I had three rounds of food and each was better than the next. I was also impressed by the superb adherence to all COVID-19 safety precautions and excellent sanitation measures. Don't forget to sample the dessert tray! The butterscotch bread pudding was delectable. I look forward to returning back here and continuing the feast. Would highly recommend.

Terrible service. They seemed understaffed. Came in and had to wait 20mins before we were spoken too. After placing our orders we watched people that came in after us get their food before us. We continued to wait while none of the waiters noticed or cared that everybody else who came after us was eating their food while we had nothing. After brining it to their attention we find out that the food had just been sitting and was there for lukewarm when we got. Their gesture for bad service was a free donut. Its really a shame because the food was pretty good. Will not be coming back here.

I'm surprised how seamless my experience was here based on other reviews. I had no service issues and was happy with the desserts I got. We tried three flavors of ice cream: -Coffee: it was okay, basic. There were some frozen icy chunks in it (most likely from being scraped off the sides of their ice cream machine after churning). -Peanut Butter brownie: good -Texas Pecan Brickle: My favorite out of all three! This was just teetering on the edge of being too sweet for me, but the toasty pecan bites saved it. The flavor in this one is really good, and I definitely recommend it. I wanted to try their "Founding Spirits American Whiskey and Cornflakes" flavor, but they were out of it. Hopefully next time I'll be able to get some. Their waffle cones are crisp and fresh, with good flavor. Even though I just went in to grab ice cream for my boyfriend and I before a show, I caved and bought a doughnut to share as well because they looked BEAUTIFUL. I went with the creme brulee, which was good but not great. I'm comparing this to my favorite doughnut in the world though, the creme brulee doughnut from the Doughnut Plant in NY. The other doughnuts at Founding Farmers looked very alluring, and I would like to try some additional flavors in the future. Service was good, and quick. The cashier and everyone dealing with my order were very friendly. They had no problems offering samples or flipping my two cones into cups because we were taking them on the road. They offer metal spoons at the pickup counter if you're dining in. I also noticed paper straws of varying diameters. Great job trying to reduce plastic waste. When I'm in KoP I would stop by here for ice cream or doughnuts again.
The absolute worst service. Things have to be exceptionally bad for me to take time to write a review, and they were! Don't waste your time. I'd rather skip breakfast.

I don't understand why this place has only 3 stars. This is a great cafe w/ cool ambience and good food. I was skeptical b/c of the reviews but I am enjoying my columbus day at this cozy brunch place.

I gave this two different tries for breakfast before I decided on leaving a review. The first time I came in was a week or two after they first opened, and I got an everything bagel with cream cheese on the side and a coffee. The bagel I got was on the smaller side and hard as a rock - I'm talking like crouton hard. Borderline hurt the top of your mouth because the bread is TOO crunchy hard. But. Fine, you're still starting out, I'll give you a second chance. The second time I came in was this morning. I got a sesame bagel, and asked for the veggie cream cheese on the side. Also had a coffee and said yes, I'd like some room for cream. The cashier repeats to me that I wanted the cream cheese on the side as she types it into the computer and tells the barista that I'd like room for cream in my coffee. Apparently no one reads or listens. My room for cream gave me just enough room to pour maybe a tablespoon of cream in. When I got to my office, the bagel quality was better than the first time, but the cream cheese was on the bagel, and sloppily and unevenly spread at that. Also the veggies in the cream cheese were pickled? You need to warn people of that, I'm not sure that pickled vegetable cream cheese is a standard. Unless of course they gave me the wrong cream cheese too? I'll give them a third try, just because I like the coffee (when I have ample room for cream). But get you're bagel game together. Sheesh!

My family was visiting from out of town, and I took them here for breakfast. The girl behind the counter was fast and friendly. We were off to a good start. It went downhill after that. There was no place to sit. We finally found a table and had to wipe it down ourselves. We waited and waited and waited and waited for our food. In the meantime, we ordered donuts.
