The donuts were delicious! Finally, the food arrived...well, not mine. I had to wait even longer for mine. My niece's pancakes were burnt to a crisp...horrible. I cannot believe they had the nerve to hand that to people. My oatmeal was half cooked. We had to get our own utensils and go back several times to get syrup. That was before we realized the pancakes were not edible. This is a good place to go to if you want donuts or ice cream. But for a sit-down​ meal of any kind...do yourself a BIG, BIG favor and go someplace​ else. They are incredibly disorganized and the food was AWFUL!

They no longer have breakfast sandwiches, whomp whomp. And it takes them a solid 10mins to to give me a bagel with cream cheese. Maybe that's why they can't make fresh sandwiches anymore? Tough to stop by before work because they'll most likely make you run late.

Terrible service and disrespectful staff. A group of friends and I stopped in here after eating dinner across the street to grab a cup of coffee before closing time. We were clearly standing in line near the register figuring out what we wanted to order when one of the workers looked at us rudely, and placed a "sorry we are closed" sign up. We are very disappointed by the staffs uncomplimentary behavior. We arrived there and were ready to order at 10:37pm, and according to multiple signs the store does not close until 11:00pm. It was unnecessary to have turned us away that early. For a newer restaurant in the area, you would think they wouldn't turn away costumers, especially that far from closing time. Oh well, I'll never go here or to Founding Farmers restaurant. I will also make sure to tell my friends about the terrible service here.

The food here is delicious but the portions are ridiculously small for the price and the service is average. My wife and I had breakfast here on our anniversary and we were excited to try this place because we heard good things about it. We arrived at about 10am on a Wednesday, and the place was almost empty. We were seated promptly and soon our server came and introduced herself. We enjoyed regular coffee as we looked over the menu. I ordered the Valley Forge Breakfast (2 sunny-side up eggs, pork maple sausage, parmesan grits and toasted ciabatta). I also ordered a side of french toast. My wife ordered the pastrami hash with a small glass of grapefruit juice. The food arrived without the toast, and when we asked for the toast, it arrived 5 minutes later. The servers seemed distracted with changing the room over to lunch, so anytime we needed anything we had to wave someone down. So while the food is delicious, the portions are so small and the prices are ridiculous...$4.25 each for a regular cup of coffee. Our total bill for this small breakfast was $43.46. Ouch. So while we enjoyed the food, the service was ordinary and the portions way too small. We will not return.

I have been wanting to try Founding Farmers for a while, but due to the mixed reviews I figured that I would try here and then decide if I wanted to go to the restaurant another time. Sadly I don't think I will be returning to either. My boyfriend and I came in last night and each ordered a slice of cake. Mine took about five minutes to come out and his took about fifteen. He ordered cheesecake with cherries. After about five minutes one of the employees brought out a frozen cheesecake and told us it was frozen and that had to get another one from upstairs. When that one finally came down it took her over five minutes to cut a piece and scoop some cherries on it. Then she handed it to him with a snarky "sorry for the wait". I don't think we will be returning.

I love this bakery/cafe right next door to Home. The breakfast sandwiches are made to order and they're 5 bucks! They leave the fried egg a bit runny- how I like it so it makes for a juicy mixture of bacon egg and cheese - I get the brioche bun. It's grilled. I usually put salt on everything but they use a good fresh ingredients that need nothing else. The coffee is strong but not bitter.

Downstairs area is cafe, upstairs is restaurant. Cute atmosphere, lots of young professionals here for meetups and work. Free wifi of course. I got tomato soup and a caramel latte, both were delicious, paid $11. Would come back here to study again. Not much table space but enough to have your laptop out.

Warning, I was so wrapped up in my company and the delicious food that I lacked photos in this trip. I meet a few friends for dinner the other night. I made a reservation on Open Table. I LOVE being able to make a reservation. So major bonus points for that service. When we arrived we were seated within our reservation time. Our waiting Ryan, who had only been there a week was fantastic. He hustled for sure. My meal was great. I ordered the spatchcock chicken. It was seasoned nicely and it was not dry. The sauce it was placed on had great flavor! It was nice and hot as well. My friends both had burgers and they devoured them. My brother raves about the pot roast which he had DoorDash Ed earlier in the week. I loved all the small details, from the dates and numbers on their silverware, to their little creamer for coffee that came in a small silver carton. Their desserts were amazing, especially the peanut butter pie! There will be another visit back.

We were optimistic and had high hopes for this coffee shop when we drove by but was quickly disappointed after the first sip. The coffee my husband ordered was cold and burnt it was clearly sitting out all day. The latte I ordered was bitter and any semblance of caramel flavor was drowned out by the over powering burnt espresso taste. The donuts were subpar at best. Definitely do not recommend trying the bakery/cafe.

Saw mixed reviews here and I was surprised...I came at nighttime when it may have been a little less busy, but not sure if that made a difference in service or anything. I loved everything about this place! The decor is absolutely adorable, the service was fast, the menu had a great selection, and the items I tried were great! I had a creme brûlée donut which was delicious and even had the little crack as you bit into it, and I also had the espresso affogato which was amazing and had an adorable presentation. The only *tiny* downside was the coffee ice cream I had it with seemed to have ice chunks or something in some bites, but it didn't really bother me much. I also love the hours of this place, sometimes it's hard to find a cute cafe that is open past the evening. I LOVED this place and I will be back!

Probably the best donuts I have ever had especially if you can get them hot. Also ordered the eggs, toast and bacon and was dissapointed. Eggs were good but only two peices of almost burned bacon and one slice of cabiatta toast which was not good. For the price, dont bother.
Them Doughnuts...Definelty will be back here. All the reviews below mine are acurate...

Worst experience ever. We called and they said it'd be a 15 minute wait. We showed up, after inviting my mother to join, to find the wait is two hours. Said without even an apology. Not explanation that we could wait at the bar either. Jerks!

The service has been so hit or miss that it's hard to give the place anything above 3 stars. Once while dining at the bar area, the bartender was so stressed about being under staffed that she threw a glass at the floor. At the bakery downstairs, I once saw a worker put his entire nose in a container of cream cheese and then serve the cream cheese to me. It makes me wonder what kind of food prep goes on behind the scenes.

Was really excited to have First Bake come to KoP and I've been probably 6-8 times since its opening. Although there were kinks to work out when it first opened, the service and wait time has actually declined since our first few visits (*note*: the woman who handles the registers in the evenings is AMAZING. This pertains to morning/day visits). Most recently when I visited FB, there were 2 people in line ahead of me; I ordered a coffee, an iced tea, and two bagels (one with egg salad, one with cream cheese) and waited almost 20 minutes for that order. 10 minutes into waiting, a staff member came out to tell me they didn't have the cream cheese I wanted, and stared blankly at me after delivering that information. I watched as people restocked donuts, put away trays, restocked bread, but not once did someone say "your order will be out shortly" or ask what we were waiting for. When our order finally came out, they made chicken salad (not egg, as ordered), and my bagel had been toasted, buttered, and then cream cheese was applied. They were quick to fix the error, but it is confusing why these two simple orders couldn't have been made that quickly from the beginning. By the time we left, a huge line had built up at the registers. The time before that, it was a 20 minute wait for 4 milkshakes (they seem to only have one machine). It seems as if all staff have their "roles," and no one was about to roll up their sleeves and work outside of their allotted responsibilities. I couldn't tell if there was a manager present or not, because each person looked just as confused as the next. It's unfortunate because I enjoy their product, but I am in no rush to return.

Saw there were lots of mixed reviews about this place so I thought I'll share my thoughts to help people decide if it's worth going. Yes, it's true their service is slow but the food is just so so good, it's worth the wait if you have time (haven't had a drink there yet so can't say anything about that). The people there are always really friendly and loves to chat so I think that's probably why it's slow sometimes. But again, it can be kinda annoying when you're in a rush... I've been there many times now and every single time I would bring home their bread. Their apple walnut loaf is my personal favorite, and they have 50% off day old breads! Ice cream is very creamy and the waffle cone is very delicious. The glazed donuts are fuffy and light. If you love dark chocolate you would definitely love their glazed chocolate donut. Normally the chocolate glazed on donuts would be very sweet but this one is different! It tastes exactly like a dark chocolate bar.

Came in with my boyfriend on the way to the Philadelphia Premium Outlets for some shopping. We initially came here to have brunch upstairs, but when we arrived it was so packed, and we didn't call ahead of time for reservations, and the wait was literally an hour! We were hungry at the moment and just headed back downstairs and noticed there was a cafe downstairs that was also serving brunch and we could basically just seat ourselves at the bar. We sat down and were helped right away which was great! I ended up ordering the chicken and waffles and my boyfriend ordered the stuffed brioche french toast with bacon. When the food came out it was mouthwatering and the portions were huge. The fried chicken was so flavorful, I just wish the piece of chicken was a little bigger. The platter also came with scrambled eggs and a white gravy which was soooooo good!! I shared my meal with my boyfriend and he shared his french toast with was so tasty. It was stuffed with a cheese that tasted like the cheese on a danish and it was so incredible. The bacon was cooked perfectly and everything was incredible. I would definitely come back here if I am ever up this area again.

So I just walked out of the Cremery. It was a negative experience. I order a shake. The cashier coughs (I'm notpositive if she coughed into her hand) I was shocked she turned around the preceded to scoop out icecream for the shake with no gloves. Another employees is helpful and proceeds to get my donut,but boxed the wrong one.I'm glad I noticed and asked if she had gotten the right donut. She used the wrong receipt,but was nice and trying to be helpful. She drops it of on the counter in front of me and walks away. The other sales person is polite and helpful and I ask her if the shake comes with whip cream. She goes and makes a scoop of what I guess is "whipped" creme and Plotz it on the shake. The shape filled to the rim and with not cover proceeds to drips all over as I walk away.i also brought a donut and them noticed something bigger than a fruit fly flying around. The donuts are uncovered. I think the food at Founding Farmers in DCis great so I decided to try this location. I wont be back, at least not to the creamery. The shake is very think , very chocolatey, the big paper straw is not working at least for me. Glad u got a spoon. The shake has caused a mess. I'm throwing it away. I haven't even driven off yet,but the disappointment at this new location caused me to write this reveiw.
Just don't go when it's closing and you'll be ok. When it's closing you'll have limited options . You will be watched as an African American ! Don't order the jambalaya! Or the shrimp and grits .

Short staffed makes for slow ordering process and long wait for simple items. Breakfast items are great, WHEN they are in stock. They have been "out" of their flavored cream cheese for a few months but continue to advertise that they have it. Their latest excuse is "oh we have someone coming to make more today", as if they make it every few months and store it (yuck). This is the fifth or sixth time in a few months that I have encountered this issue, and have watched fellow patrons run into the same problem. When they first opened, they were excellent. The donuts are beautiful and delicious, and the actual breakfast and brunch items upstairs at Founding Farmers are exquisite, but they are really coming up short in the bakery/ "to go breakfast" department .

I stopped by before work for a quick bagel sandwich. They don't have many options for to go breakfast items that arent baked good, so egg and cheese with bacon it was. Everything was cooked perfectly, the bacon was extra crispy and the brioche bun was nice and soft. Even if they don't have a lot of breakfast sandwich options I think this could become my go to.

At the time of this review this place has a 2 1/2 star yelp review which I believe is wholly unjustified. We've eaten here twice now for dinner, getting something different each time, and it's always been really really great. The filet mignon is exquisite, as is the pot roast and the spicy fried chicken and donut. Service (at the bar anyway) is very friendly and welcoming. Will be coming back soon to try the short rib ragu.

I'm sorry to say but we had one of the worst dining experiences ever here. I ordered soup-it was cold and served with a dirty spoon. My husband ordered a breakfast sandwich which took 20 minutes to come out. It was served on the wrong bread and was barely edible. When he asked for utensils the waitress said to get Jen from the self serve section. Extremely disappointed. We won't be back. Wish I didn't have to add the star to be able to post.

First Bake, I am in love with your blueberry butter on a plain bagel... but you did me dirty this time with my breakfast burrito, which I was also once in love with. I wondered why my burrito sounded so solid in the foil and when I got home and unwrapped it, I discovered the bottom of it was completely burnt...

Never again really just due to the speed of service. First, I wasn't greeted when walked in. I could visibly see 4 employees. Didn't take my order for over 5 minutes and I was the only one there in line. And then it took the turtle making my sandwich almost 15 minutes and the sandwich wasn't even that great. If you are going to advertise your coffee shop it should be quick for mornings of people going to work. But it makes sense that no one was there because it wastes 30 minutes of your morning. Starbucks would have been a better option because I could have been at work by 7:15 instead of 7:40.

I have to echo others' reviews that highlighted the slow service. Regardless of the fact that we ordered 4 items, 2 of which required some labor, they do not have a great system. One person was behind the counter to take AND fill orders. Thankfully, we went during a lull and no one was ahead of us; I'd hate to think how much longer we would have waited if they'd been busy! The ice cream is very good. Rich and creamy, and the portion is generous. I ordered a decaf Affogato with chocolate ice cream, and enjoyed it -- though I would not recommend ordering it to go. They give you the espresso shot in a cup separate from the ice cream, and it wasn't very easy to maneuver. Rookie mistake. My kids liked their ice creams and hubby enjoyed his milkshake. The cafe itself is bright and chic and whimsical. I could see coming back to catch up with a girlfriend over a donut or milkshake...as long as I'm not in any rush!
Been there twice. Once for Lunch once for dinner. Meals are fresh and very nicely portioned. Service is good. Bar menu is unreal. Bakery is completely average meals are stellar.

Seriously how hard is it to get egg salad right? I've ordered it four different times and they've managed to mess it up each time. It's never made consistent or according to how you ordered it. I know why do I keep going back? The first time I had it it was so good. Every time the service has been super slow. 30 minutes to get egg salad and a water? I wanted to like this place but their service is terrible and they can't manage simple orders.

I've been to First Bake a few times now, even though I know I'm going to wait longer than I'd like for my order to be ready. The coffee is fantastic, and the bagels are very good, too. I live in the KOP town center, so it's an easy place to meet a friend for breakfast. My boyfriend and I met my parents for breakfast this morning, expecting 5-10 minute wait for our food, and waited FORTY FIVE MINUTES for 3 coffees, a soda, and 4 bagels. Forty. Five. Minutes. And no, the place was not crowded. I went back to the counter a few times to check on the order during our wait. The first time, the young woman asked me to tell her every single item on the order before she could check. The second and third times, they told me they were "working on it now." When the order finally came out, the bagels were not toasted, as we had requested, and mine had dulce de leche butter instead of peanut butter. I can't have dairy, so I brought it back to the counter. The young man disappeared for 5 minutes, came back holding the same bagel, and told me it *was* peanut butter. At this point, my blood sugar and patience were both low, and I told him that it absolutely was not!! He disappeared again, and when he returned, the bagel had peanut butter on only one half. I took the plate and asked him to bring a little to-go tub of peanut butter to my table, which he did, unsmiling and unapologetically. The young woman behind the counter offered us donuts for our trouble (which I couldn't eat, anyway), also delivered without a smile or an apology. I don't know what happened today, but as the wait at First Bake is always ridiculously long, I have to wonder about the management. Employees are clueless and seriously lacking in customer service skills. The coffee and bagels do not make up for the terrible service, and I will not be back.

Today was my second visit to the cafe. First experience was terrible but it was very soon after their grand opening so I thought maybe they would work out the kinks ...nope. Atmosphere: very nice decor but a terrible set up/ layout. They only have seating for maybe 20 people (2-3 tables and a small counter) in the cafe. We ended up eating in the car. Not sure why they don't take advantage of some of the open spaces to maximize seating. There is an odd counter next to the line where you can sit and get served but it's tiny and awkward as it is right next to the line. Service: there was a family of four in front of us and they ordered several items so it took a while to be served. We waited about 8-10 mins just to place our order (not too bad). When we started to order, the lady walked away to start gathering the order ..kind of odd since we were still in the process of placing the order. A line had gathered behind us that wrapped around the staircase. I am not sure why but our order took forever (2 drinks, 2 breakfast sandwiches). They need a better system or more hands to help. Also, they make no apologies for the slow service. Food: We ordered 2 breakfast sandwiches that were very greasy and lacking taste. The vanilla latte was good but the regular coffee was 'lumpy' and was not drinkable. My daughter got a chocolate frosted donut that looks delicious but it was awful ..very bland, tasteless. Would not recommend this place
I really don't know why First Bake Cafe & Creamery doesn't have five stars! All of the donuts I tried were amazing! The filled donuts were incredible and perfectly filled! so delicious!

Was there 11/21/2018 for breakfast with my daughter and grandchildren. It was terrible. Over priced, orders came out, they were all not as was ordered, replacements arrived after long delay, portions were meager. Complained to waitress and manager, they did adjust the bill but this was not about money. Manager blamed waitress, she was in tears. Overall not the way to run a resturant. No stars from me. Had to rate star, so post would be accepted Will never return.
This place is the best! The best donuts, ice cream and coffee in the area! And the staff is super friendly!

had a salted caramel milkshake to go the other day and it was gross. i dont know what all the hype was about when this first opened...i only ordered the milkshake and people behind me in line ordered more stuff than me and their stuff came out before my 1 milkshake. it was bland, not so salty or caramel. it tasted like vanilla with maybe half a squirt of caramel sauce in it. Also, I witnessed an employee being disciplined in front of guests, over leaving a full tin of coffee beans out on display. Even though they don't have milkshakes, I'd recommend duck donuts next door. they're faster paced in service and are nicer to their staff.
The food is good, but should I have to wait an hour for a takeout order on a Tuesday afternoon???

After finding out that the wait for brunch at the restaurant upstairs was an hour, my girlfriend and I ended up at seats at this Cafe on the first floor for breakfast. The cafe has bar seats that were staffed by a wonderful waitress. This turned out to be great decision. Instead of the expensive brunch buffet upstairs we had a reasonably priced 5 star breakfast that left us completely stuffed. We decided to share our orders. I ordered the stuffed french toast with bacon. She ordered the chicken and waffles, which comes with eggs. Her chicken was perfectly fried and seasoned and juicy. We just wanted a bigger piece. The eggs were perfectly cooked and the waffles were good. My bacon was perfectly cooked as well. My stuffed french toast was the standout star. The best french toast I've ever tasted. I think it was brioche and stuffed with a vanilla cream. It was soooo good. We devoured it and I wanted to lick up every bit of cream that had dripped on to my plate. Do yourself a favor and eat breakfast here as opposed to waiting in line at the restaurant above it.
I was looking for a good place to enjoy a coffee, sit, and work. I was a bit disappointed in the limited seating options. The nitro cold brew was not bad.

I was pleased to know that one of these restaurants opened in our area. I have been to the one in DC a couple of times and it was delightful Now the review. Yes I realize they are just opened but boy the staff is so not trained well enough. The line was longish in the cafe but not as long as the one in DC but the wait was 5 times longer. 5 people in front of us and it took 20 minutes to place an order. I was originally going to get takeout and was directed to the restaurant upstairs by the hostess at the door ( very nice decor and aroma up there - I will need to come for brunch next time. ) when I arrived I was told no takeout on Saturday, hmmm bad training perhaps that the hostess did not know? So the story begins. I returned to the cafe line to begin what would be an eternity to get food. The single person ( why not throw another person at the counter??? ) took FOREVER!! She was very pleasant but knew nothing about the food, prices and she struggled to find items in the computer. She had to leave the counter multiple times ( for each order) for help or clarification. I felt bad for her and would blame the management. And on to the management. The manger was buzzing around the floor while her staff wandered around dazed and confused. She was sure to align signs just so on the counter in front of these helpless folks. Not once did she step up to open a register or help behind the counter with her confused workers delivering the wrong items. There were also plenty of times a worker was just standing around waiting to run food from the kitchen that could have been put to use doing other things I am sure. And yes I got the wrong thing. I asked for a donut and they were mislabeled on the counter. I had to direct them to the right one. I guess I should have asked for a job. I felt so bad I wanted to help all the nice folks out. Now the food. Very fresh the banana cream donut was to die for. The bagel was fresh and the farm fresh jam amazing. Just do not get the bagel toasted. They warn you but it is grilled but it is on the same grill as other foods so it picks up that grilled cheese taste. Not pleasant. Please buy a toaster. Bottom line I will come back and give them another try but hope management is better getting this ship righted.
This place is great! Love the philosophy and food and coffee and amazing! Nice that there are good options in the mall.

The wait for the restaurant was a bit long so my friend and I decided to grab lunch at the bakery. We were told to sit anywhere and someone will grab our ordered but after no one came by for a bit we grabbed a couple of free seats at the counter. The food came out quickly while we chatted and watched the trays of donuts slide in and out of shelves. The food was ok and the donuts were not bad. The service was nice enough but not overly warm. Overall it was a nice experience but I am also looking forward to exploring other restaurants in the area.

Morning coffee and a bagel here is the best! $1.99 coffees and bagels! They offer coffee on tap every morning with the following milk options: soy, oat, almond, and possibly cashew. Other breakfast options include breakfast burritos, pancakes, waffles, eggs (most styles are offered), donuts, and more! My favorite on the menu includes their brûlée grapefruit and donuts. I believe the grapefruit is the same dish that's offered upstairs. The service is consistent. They seem to always be understaffed on weekdays and especially on weekends. It may take more than 15 minutes to get served, but I'm usually not in a rush to get anywhere when I'm here. They have online order options - if you're in a hurry that morning, it maybe best to order ahead for pickup.

This is is my go to spot. I made reservations for 10 am. They sat us down right away. The food is really good. My guests loved it. Our server Craig made the experience even more memorable. Thank you to the Founding Farmers Team.

We were in line which is right off the bat chaos. No one acknowledged we were at the counter waiting to be helped for 15 min. I wanted the breakfast burrito and my husband the onion bagel with scallion cream cheese. Guess what - they didn't have either. He just said "we don't have that" not a suggestion as to what we could get that's similar - nada. So we order completely different items from what we originally wanted. My husband ordered two mimosas and a second guy at the counter who didn't acknowledge us once chimes in and says "thats upstairs" ok well we just watched you bring the people next to us mimosas so....? Anyway long story short this place is a joke. I enjoy the brunch upstairs but it's incredibly pricey for a basic brunch. The downstairs portion is poorly ran and absolutely not worth your time and money. REVIEW UPDATE!!!!!! Marie from the PR department called me and issued me a refund as well as a gift card to come back. She was very apologetic and empathetic. I myself run a spa and deal with pissed clients all the time but getting them to come back is key and that's why I appreciated Marie's efforts
Not impressed with the desserts! The donuts are made in house and they were gummy and hard. So disappointed! Very nicely decorated.
Nice bakery and cafe! I love their latte and their restaurant! Will definitely recommend! Limited seating but vibe is good!

Amazing! The devils food was so delicious. Originally, I ordered one but after having it, I had to get another one! The chocolate was amazing and instantly melted in your mouth. It taste like the perfect moist chocolate cake you dream about.

Gave you guys another try First Bake Cafe & Creamery...wish I hadn't. When you order garlic and herb cream cheese on your bagel, but it looks like someone merely stood in the same room as the bagel and whispered the word "plain cream cheese". This looks like someone tried to apply cream cheese with a basting brush from 15 feet away. This is NOT acceptable. I took it in and made them fix it, but they STILL got it wrong. This is not garlic and herb (I'm just gonna assume you are still "out"'of that kind). Have your people ever prepared a bagel before?! Oh, and it's also not toasted, which I requested.

Such quick and friendly service! We were pleasantly surprised to find the First Bake cafe was a great spot for a quick business lunch. Originally we were hoping to have lunch upstairs but after the wait was so long we opted for First Bake. So happy we did - good lunch food and such pleasant conversation with the staff...yet enough quiet and privacy to get some work done. Thanks for bringing a little piece of DC to KoP.

Fantastic bakery and cafe! I visited the restaurant first for their brunch selection, but was also pleased by the bakery downstairs. The area is very well decorated and well lit. The items on the menu are affordable and locally sourced. There's free water by the seating area. I ordered a vanilla glazed doughnut for $1 and I gobbled it right up. The wait at the cashier did get a bit long when three large groups of people showed up. I guess they were unprepared to handle 20+ people at once, but that's understandable. I only wish there were more tables and seating so I could enjoy the atmosphere longer. I would definitely return!

Enjoyed my casual working breakfast here. Quality coffee in real cups with free refills. $5 egg sandwich on brioche. The maple donut was delicious. Personally I liked it better than Duck Donuts next door. All the employees were super friendly and informative. The free WiFi makes it a nice place to work but the seating was very tight. Felt like you were on top of other customers, especially at the high counter by the window. Will be back.

Was looking forward to trying this place for a "quick" treat. I placed my order for a root beer float and a scoop of chocolate ice cream at 1:52 pm, and I received my order at 2:15 pm. 20 minutes!? It was not even busy. Order was totally forgotten about. I also had to choose another flavor ice cream because the vanilla was "way too hard." This place needs a better system and more oversight.

Don't bother ordering here, though the food and coffee is nice they have a terrible management. Called in and Ordered some Burritos and coffee and when I got there, they don't even have the order in their system and took like ever to give me the breakfast. They took like half hour just got get me 2 caramel latte's which I call them and ordered on phone like an hour back so frustrating

Stopped by here on a whim as I was passing through kop looking for a bite that wasn't super processed. Was blown away with the food, prices and atmosphere. The downstairs looks like something out of an episode of portlandia. Super modern and hip but without the price tag. Food tastes fresh and well seasoned, coffee is deep and flavorful, And at $5 for a breakfast sandwich it makes you forget you're in kop. Will definitely return.

I am very impressed with Founding Farmers after the Guest Communications Officer, Amy, reached out soon after my visit to the cafe & creamery. She was concerned about my experience and asked to send me a gift card. I will be back to give the cafe another try when I'm in the area.

No fillers, just amazing desserts you can eat with quality coming first. Located near the spiraling staircase that leads to founding farmers, the bakery is located on the bottom. Very small space to gather around but this is a bakery to grab and go. Not meant to have large parties like a Starbucks to lounge around. Which is understandable as there just isn't that much space available to squeeze more table and chairs. Got a box of donuts with 6 different ones and man o man, eat them while there hot and you'll be on cloud nine. With that soft dough, you'll bite right into the strong taste of a fresh donut along with great toppings. The one with the icing on top was great for me because I like to keep things simple. I also tried the vanilla ice cream which tasted amazing. Instead of that strong sugary taste, it's subtle with the vanilla shining and a light, melt in your mouth bite. do me a favor and get it on the come, cause that way you'll get a better picture haha, definitely recommend.
This place is the best! The best donuts, ice cream and coffee in the area! And the staff is super friendly!

Went back and more of the same. Wait was horrific. 5 people I line at the cafe and it took, not kidding 17 minutes ( yes I timed it... ) Please Don't , repeat please don't order a fancy coffee. If anyone orders a late or cappuccino time will stand still. Everything stops like the Time Travelers Wife, as the person on the ONE open register walks to man the cappuccino machine. She then disappears to concoct a brew you will stand there motionless. Why they don't have anyone who can step in when a coffee is ordered is beyond me. Head to Starbucks or hope to your maker no one wants a fancy coffee. Everything bagel was dry and as hard as a rock. Other stuff was just ok. McDonalds would have been better sorry to say. Original review : I was pleased to know that one of these restaurants opened in our area. I have been to the one in DC a couple of times and it was delightful Now the review. Yes I realize they are just opened but boy the staff is so not trained well enough. The line was longish in the cafe but not as long as the one in DC but the wait was 5 times longer. 5 people in front of us and it took 20 minutes to place an order. I was originally going to get takeout and was directed to the restaurant upstairs by the hostess at the door ( very nice decor and aroma up there - I will need to come for brunch next time. ) when I arrived I was told no takeout on Saturday, hmmm bad training perhaps that the hostess did not know? So the story begins. I returned to the cafe line to begin what would be an eternity to get food. The single person ( why not throw another person at the counter??? ) took FOREVER!! She was very pleasant but knew nothing about the food, prices and she struggled to find items in the computer. She had to leave the counter multiple times ( for each order) for help or clarification. I felt bad for her and would blame the management. And on to the management. The manger was buzzing around the floor while her staff wandered around dazed and confused. She was sure to align signs just so on the counter in front of these helpless folks. Not once did she step up to open a register or help behind the counter with her confused workers delivering the wrong items. There were also plenty of times a worker was just standing around waiting to run food from the kitchen that could have been put to use doing other things I am sure. And yes I got the wrong thing. I asked for a donut and they were mislabeled on the counter. I had to direct them to the right one. I guess I should have asked for a job. I felt so bad I wanted to help all the nice folks out. Now the food. Very fresh the banana cream donut was to die for. The bagel was fresh and the farm fresh jam amazing. Just do not get the bagel toasted. They warn you but it is grilled but it is on the same grill as other foods so it picks up that grilled cheese taste. Not pleasant. Please buy a toaster. Bottom line I will come back and give them another try but hope management is better getting this ship righted.

I am from St. Louis and frequently visit Philly. I will be back here! First of all it's open so early....I got a crab Benedict and it was amazing. I'm not sure what the other reviews are about and the service and food choices but I had the servers talking and mingling with me. I loved it! Also got their chai tea which has stayed so so hot for me that I'm drinking it in the car still!

I am rating the Cafe only and my experience there. The 'Aztec' (latte) was a bit disappointing. Most of my Yelp reviews are positive so it is with a heavy heart that I say the Aztec was not wonderful. The coffee was bitter and I tasted no hint of chocolate, cinnamon nor agave. I was really looking forward to it. In addition, when I asked for additional agave to add (hoping to curb the bitter taste of the latte), I was told they did not have any and that the agave was part of the 'mix' for the latte. I will review the restaurant separately and I'm still looking forward to that meal even though my Cafe experience was not wonderful.

Extremely rude! First I went upstairs and asked to look at a menu. They said this is for brunch if you want breakfast it's downstairs. I said ok may I see a menu please and they said no breakfast is downstairs. I was looking for brunch but apparently I wasn't welcome to eat that. I went downstairs to have breakfast and asked for a menu. There were no seats available. I asked if they had any other seating and they told me to go upstairs for brunch. Looks like they have enough business and do not need any more.

Well, I thought I was going to Duck Donuts. I parked, then when walking to DD, we came across Founding Farmers First Bake Cafe and felt it would be a more chilled out atmosphere...and that it was. Comfortable arm chairs and coffee tables to kick back on. Ice coffee was excellent...some difference in opinion of what a "large" should be, but I'm ok with quality over quantity. We picked two donuts (ok I picked two donuts), maple covered and bananas foster...then noticed a creme brûlée and snagged one of those too. Simply amazing, they were light airy clouds of dough covered and stuffed with sweetness! Bananas foster was really good, unfortunately...that's it...just "really good." Stuffed with a banana cream with just the right sweetness. The maple...very good. What I loved most...it wasn't a sickly sweet low grade maple taste, but a light, thin coating with a subtle maple flavor. The creme brûlée was AMAZING...stuffed with a sweet cream and topped with caramelized sugar topping. You get a crunch on your first bite and the the bits of broken sugar spread out and every bite gave you a little sweet crunch. Big fan of this place. Service was prompt and friendly. The young man that served us even popped over and checked on us as he was picking up the area.

Was in the area and thought I'd give it a try despite the mixed reviews. Tried to order bagel and donuts at 1:50pm. The board says they serve "eats" until 2pm. Was told they aren't serving because it's after the time. I told them it's not yet 2pm but they had nothing to say. Poor customer service so I left. There are many other food businesses in the area that would gladly take my cash. Would have been a first time customer but will definitely not be back.
Great food but the service is what really made it. If you go, ask for Zhane. I can't even put into words how amazing she was! Thank you Zhane for making our dinner so enjoyable!!

I was sadly disappointed in my visit here. Kind of a cool spot, but the food just wasn't great. I've been looking forward to this visit for weeks, but in the end it was a letdown. What was most telling about our visit was that no one in our party of four finished their meals. They have a very expansive menu, which was nice, but I'm not sure I care to come back and try anything else. They went 0 for 4 in our group tonight.

I came here to grab something quick. I ordered a large iced chai latte with a shot of espresso and a plain bagel with bacon jalapeño spread. I received a SMALL HOT chai. I'm confused about what was so hard to understand between a hot and cold drink... She literally repeated it to me yet handed over the wrong thing. Secondly, she wasn't wearing gloves or sanitizing her hands which honestly disgusted me. How are you touching everything around you and then making my bagel... Overall, I wouldn't come back here or recommend them since the barista couldn't follow basic orders.

Excuse me while I shove sushi in my face even more often now! My boss told me about this place so my husband and I decided to go this past weekend and it was just was the tastebuds ordered! We had 4 rolls total- the killer shrimp, California roll, Unagi and Shrimp Tempura Crunch. Surprisingly the Unagi with eel in it was my favorite! The killer shrimp was a close 2nd! The great thing about this place is you can eat in, pick it up or have it delivered- it's pretty much the fast food of sushi but it tastes magical!

Sushi and service were excellent! The ordering process was a bit confusing for us first timers. Although we had researched the menu prior to arriving for lunch, we thought we could order with ease. However, the menu was written in various formats on different sections on the walls and leaning against the counter. It was hard to follow and decide what we had wanted. Once we did, it wasn't really clear how exactly we were supposed to order. Do we seat ourselves and someone would take our order, or do we place our order at the counter/ cashier. Finally, a very friendly member of the staff directed us to order from the counter. At that point, we paid, and were given a table number so our food could be brought to us when ready. Smooth sailing from then on, as our meals were prepared perfectly and the waiter, who had also taken our order was very attentive. The Sushi was beyond fresh and this will definitively become a frequently visited restaurant now that we're familiar with the menu and ordering process.
I think they are overpriced for what you get. It's a small place where you order like any fast food place. What I had was good and fresh.

I came here around dinner time on a Monday and it was unbelievably fast, about 5 minutes for a roll. The roll itself (a shrimp Avocado) was a bit expensive and not amazing, but still pretty good. The waiter was also friendly, so for service and speed, it gets that 4th star over average. If you want quick and don't mind the price, this is your place.
Everything here is great, and for the price you get a lot of food. I always get the teriyaki chicken rice bowl, and it comes to about 11 dollars and miso soup is included. Always delicious!

I come here for the chicken teriyaki. It's quite good. The sushi isn't half bad either. Not your typical restaurant. You basically order at a counter and they bring the food out to you. Some items are pretty pricey. This place is worth a try though.
friendly service, and some bangin' ass sushi!!!
Very cute little place with very good sushi and other great combos, I would definitely come back, I like the chicken teriyaki rice bowl and the very friendly staff
Me and 3 other friends at work made a "to-go" order of sushi combo + lobster maki + udon / tampura shrimp (total cost = $46). It was excellent!! Will come back here again n again n again.

Not entirely a restaurant.. counter order your sushi, and they bring it to your table. Great for a quick in and out lunch. I ordered the Fire Roll, which is a California roll in crispy tempura. VERY SPICY, and I dabbed most of the hot sauce dots off each roll, but very cleanly made, and very delicious. A must have for spicy food lovers and crispy sushi roll lovers, and at a great low price, $7.99 (very large roll) (** $10 minimum for credit cards)
If you live in Conshy get your sushi here. This is our go to spot and it never disappoints. Fresh. Friendly staff. Great selection.

A nice surprise for my lunch break! Clean and nice interior. I had one of the lunch specials-$2 off a bento. I had tuna and salmon nigiri, salad, and miso soup. The green tea was delicious too. Excellent! I was pleased to enjoy a quick and affordable lunch here. I will definitely come back.

Delicious sushi, quick friendly service, I'll definitely be returning. The prices seemed a touch high at first, but you get more sushi in your rolls here than many other places I've been, so totally worth it.

This place is a favorite of the guys I work with nearby. I'm not that big on going out for lunch at work, but they had me at sushi. We did the takeout option, though dining-in is different here. You order at the counter, seat yourself, and your order is brought out to you. I had planned on only ordering one roll, but they enforce a 10-dollar minimum if you wish to pay by credit. I ordered a spicy tuna roll and a California roll. It seemed like they use actual crab meat for their California roll. It was sushi. If the guys want to go here again, I'll probably go the rice bowl route, those sounded interesting and fun. Otherwise, I don't expect to come here on my own whim.

Stopped in here for lunch today. I didn't think it was that expensive. I got a shrimp tempura roll, miso soup and a house salad for $15. The place is cute for a take out sushi place. You can also order at the counter to eat in. The shrimp tempura sushi was tasty and fresh. The salad was good as well. I really liked the dressing. The miso soup left a little to be desired. I think it had one piece of tofu in it. I would go here again if in the area and in the mood for sushi. (Actually, I'm always in the mood for sushi.)

I've eaten here a few times. It's always just ok. But if your stuck in the burbs and need to have sushi. It's decent in a pinch. I would not recommend this as a great sushi restaurant. They're sushi is adequate, just above grocery store but not as bad as food court grade. Although it's priced as high as a freshly delivered restaurant; but it's not. The typical non-experienced tongues orders of salmon & tuna will be fresh. Clean. Good service but just overpriced adequate sushi. And they're usually out of anything too exotic.. like mackerel or squid. Oh my! Don't even think of ordering uni. They don't carry it. Oh they do have ikura but the serving size is small! All their sizes of sushi sashimi are SMALL. so don't come here hungry.

I've been going to Happy Maki for about 4 years. I think the sushi itself is pretty solid, albeit overpriced. My main issue with this place is that one of the employees talks with a fake Australian accent. He insists on keeping in character even though it's pretty ridiculous. Try the sushi, and try not to laugh when ordering.

I have been really happy with this restaurant. They always have great service and the food is always very clean and fresh! The cook there is so sweet! It is definitely an atmosphere that I prefer to be in. I will most certainly make sure to return!

I was pleasantly surprised by Happy Maki! Heres the flow: Go to the back of the restaurant to order, there is a chalkboard with specials and a menu on the counter ad on the wall at the right, place your order and pay then go sit. Just a note, don't try ordering Donburi, they don't make them anymore. They bring your food to you. The sushi rolls may seem expensive, but I found the bowls to be very reasonable. The roll we tried was they Happy Mango. The fruit on top was evenly balanced with the salmon and the salmon tasted very fresh! I had the Shrimp and Vegetable Tempura Rice Bowl, it was more than enough for dinner and reasonably priced at $10. The tempura was delicious and I got a good mixture of broccoli, sweet potato, and shrimp. We've grown too fond of the sushi place across the street to change allegiances, but if we want Japanese style Asian food or something other than sushi we'll be back to Happy Maki.

Finally good sushi has come to Plymouth Meeting. I have eaten from this place about 10 times. They consistently have great sushi. They are even available on doordash. The place is also very clean. Anyone who does not give this restaurant five stars is a sushi snob. This Sushi is just as good or better than what you can get in the city

Fast casual sushi joint. The sushi is ok, prices are decent. Its BYOB which is a plus and the inside looks nice. Mostly a take out joint. Conshohocken really doesn't have a lot of sushi options so it fills a need.

Happy Maki definitely fills a niche interest in the area: fast takeout sushi that is better than grocery stores and most Chinese places that also do sushi. There are a couple of things I really like about this place: - my wife doesn't eat seafood, and Happy Maki actually makes rolls with meats (cooked, of course), like beer teriyaki. Their vegetable rolls are pretty good too. - they have some pretty creative rolls here, and daily specials - the eating area, should you choose to eat in, is pleasant and clean On the downside: - their price point is a little high, pretty close to sitdown sushi places. It's not uncommon for me to spend $50 here on takeout. - service/friendliness is hit or miss If you happen to be in the area, I would check out Happy Maki, but not sure I would go out of my way. That said, I am definitely happy that this place is here.

Happy maki has the most fresh, unique, delicious sushi I've ever encountered. I take my son here all the time and he loves it. The rolls are a bit small for the high price but the quality makes up for it. The lobster roll has big chunks of lobster throughout. The angry scallop is spicy and delicious. I will keep coming back!

This is always my go to place for sushi in the suburbs. It sits as a hidden gem in this strip mall. I love happy maki for their fresh fish and uniquely and addicting roll options as well as their kind service. You are always greeted with a kind smile and hello and leave satisfied. Some rolls can get a bit pricey, but they do have a rotating daily special which allows you sample some of their classic rolls for a discounted price depending on the day of the week. They also do a nifty $10 lunch special with 1 raw and 1 cooked roll that is always a good option for lunch on the run. If you need advice for a standard meal for 2 and guaranteed GREAT experience, opt for the hiyashi, tornado and sunkissed rolls. You can thank me later.

We had quite the opposite experience than that of 'jenna c' and 'joe s'. We loved Happy Maki and didn't find it weird at all! We ordered the Philly sushi, the Shrimp Tempura Crunch sushi, and the Chicken-Katsu Rice Bowl. All were delicious.. and the Shrimp Tempura Crunch was an absolute winner for us--we highly recommend it! We will most definitely go back there and we're quite eager to try other menu items. The dining area is quaint and clean and the staff was friendly. We actually showed up 5 minutes before closing and they welcomed us and allowed us eat there past closing time. And who cares about the plastic ware!! It wasn't tacky at all and as long as there's good food in it, that's all that matters!! Happy Maki also sort of reminded of us of a mini version of Pei Wei Asian Diner (which is also really good), but with a much larger selection of Sushi. Finally some better eats in that area of Conshocken! A little pricey but worth it. :)
Delicious Tornado roll! Spicy ramen was pretty good. The yaki udon was delicious but had too many onions. Udon with fish cake was good as well. This place is a hidden gem. Staff are very friendly.

In short, come here for small portions, high prices, average sushi, and teenage service. I really like sushi, and really want this place to be decent because there aren't any other close sushi places. So, I keep going back here. Every time I go in with low expectations, and I'm somehow always disappointed. Their seaweed salad is about 1/3 of the size of other sushi places at the same price. The spring rolls were tiny and expensive. The sushi isn't awful, but it isn't really notable either. Make the drive to Blue Fin, it's worth it.

Happy Maki is okay, I suppose. It comes off as a hole-in-the-wall sushi place, and it is small and cozy inside. The staff is very polite and endearing. The food is meh. The bowl that contained my miso soup smelled like dish soap. This can be interpreted two ways: at least they're cleaning the bowls, but apparently they aren't doing so well enough. The smell, by proxy, made my brain think I was tasting said soap. I couldn't finish it. Their sushi was pretty good. Lackluster, really. I also got chicken katsu in a bento box - I had never had katsu. This was good in the scheme of chicken, though the other components of the bento box, not so much. I think the soap smell really set my tastebuds off. I'd be willing to try it again, as this was probably a one-time thing.

EDIT- I have decided to edit my post instead of update it, since I only wrote it a week ago. Despite my opinion of Happy Maki from my first visit, I decided to give them another chance because I thought the food was good. This time, I went with take out. I found the food to be virtually inedible. The sushi was mealy and unappetizing. Also, it's highly aggravating to open a small soup container to discover it is half empty. This was the case with the miso and the udon. Nothing here is worth the money. The portions are small and the food is not good. I will never go back. Here's the original post- How could I not like a place called Happy Maki? Come on, folks, that's adorable. Too bad the place is so odd, because I don't like it. I have always lived under the assumption that when there are no servers, the prices go down. Or that when you are housed in a suburban strip mall, the prices go down. Or when you use mostly disposable dishes, the prices go down. Or when a restaurant doesn't offer tap water, don't the prices usually go down? Are you noticing a trend, reader? This place generally does everything on the cheap, and yet their prices are fairly high. There are no technical servers. You walk up to the counter, order, and they'll bring your food to your table. Drinks are self service so at the counter they will offer you a choice of soda fountain or a bottled drink, including bottled water. Their tea and green tea options are limited to a bottle of Peak's green iced tea. Everything is plastic ware, the utensils, the soy sauce plates, the small plates. The only things not plastic are the dishes they bring the food on. I hope the rest is all biodegradable, cause they're producing a lot of garbage. The food was good, but not good enough to justify the prices. My miso was tepid and only filled half the bowl. The rolls were good, but certainly not great. The price is definitely not justified. Most of their special rolls are based off a California roll. For instance, the Dragon roll is a California roll with eel on top. That should not be $15, especially when the California roll only costs $4.95 Or how about this pricing decision. A spicy tuna roll is $6.99, a little bit steep, but not outrageous. A spicy tuna crunch roll is $8.99. The only difference is the addition of tempura flakes for $2. This place is weird. Everything is done on the cheap, and yet costs more than normal. Maybe they will work on this once they are open a little longer. I don't think I'm going to stick around to find out.

Yeah the rolls fall apart a little because it's so fresh! If you are used to supermarket sushi, then perhaps this is not your thing. Yellowtail and snapper were great. Who orders chicken rolls at a sushi roll place anyway? ... that's like going for Italian and complaining the hotdogs stink. Delicious, fresh and super accommodating to food substitutions/allergies. This was my first visit and I definitely will go back.
- good-fresh sushi and delicious - good size portions - fast at bringing out food - does not have Gluten Free soy sauce - small seating area inside - clean and great service

I've seen this place pop up a while ago but never went by... I am ready to write this after 2 satisfactory recent trips. I've had the chicken donburi which is tasty without being too salty as it often is and I love that they add vegetables to this dish! Huge plus for me. I've also had a couple rolls/makis from here and they make it neat and pretty without a ton of rice to make it appear bigger. I appreciate that. The avocado/cucumber and other ingredients used seem super fresh and, the raw tuna I have had there has been very fresh. We also tried the monkey balls once and liked it a lot! It's different and interesting in flavor. They have good lunch specials too! It's nothing amazing, but Conshi area lacks in casual Japanese spots so I am happy to have this nearby to fulfill my occasional cravings.

Okay, so the sushi here is just okay but the teriyaki bowls are pretty good and reasonably priced! My spicy chicken teriyaki bowl came with perfectly cooked sticky rice, plenty of flavorful, tender chicken sauteed with onions in a sweet and savory sauce, a side of shredded Asian slaw, and a small bowl of miso soup. The portion was also pretty generous, given the very reasonable $8.50 price tag. I was quite happy with the meal and loved that the chicken and rice weren't at all dry, which is often at other places. Will definitely be back to try the other bowl options.
I ordered from here 3 days in a row for the same rolls/food. I love the happy mango that I couldn't find in any othe sushi places!

Much better than the "take-out" sushi you get from the counter in the grocery store but not quiet on the same level as some of the other sushi places in the area. My take: a good place to go for some decent and quick sushi. Surprisingly creative menu, nice staff, clean eating area (if you choose to eat there). It can be a little pricey (depending on your order) but like a previous reviewer said would you really eat "cheap" sushi.....I think not!
Fish quality seems to have gone down (or is spotty / uneven). Really wish Conshohocken had a good sushi place...

I have to give this place props simply for being a fast-casual sushi restaurant. If you're looking to quickly fulfill your sushi craving, go here. They have a full menu and a decent daily special. There's nothing outstanding about the sushi, but I was satisfied. Prices range from $8-$20.

I went practically 30 minutes before they were closing one evening night, and they were still very friendly to me. It does have places to sit down in the restaurant, however you first go to the counter and order your food, such as like a Panera. I sat down to wait for my food, and they brought it out to me. I am not sure if that is regular practice, or they did that because I was the only one in the restaurant. There is a good chance at busier times that you are suppose to pick up your food from the counter. I only ordered one maki roll, the Happy Mango, and it was very good. I did not go crazy ordering a bunch of rolls only because they are a little over priced. Some rolls are about $3-5 more than other places I have been to that I know has good quality rolls. If the prices were a little less I would have tried out more. The best bang for your buck would be a rice bowl. You get a very reasonable amount of food, and a nice cup of miso soup. They have good sized cups available if you just want water, and the most important thing I noticed is that they were very clean! Even though it was closing time for them they did not make me feel rushed, and I overall enjoyed my meal. Also it is a BYOB if you are interested.

I pass this place on my way home from work and it's become my go-to takeout sushi place. While I'll agree with many of the other reviewers that it's a bit overpriced for a takeout sushi place, I've always found the quality good--in fact, the best I've found around here since moving from Center City. The service is friendly and quick and I've always found the sushi fresh. I'm not a fan of their miso soup, but have been happy with rolls. I can't comment on the California roll as that's never been a favorite of mine, but I enjoy the Sunkissed roll (spicy tuna topped with salmon) as well as the Unagi roll. I'd also recommend the Monkey Ball (deep fried jalepeno stuffed with spicy tuna and cream cheese)--but only if you're dining in (tempura doesn't travel well). I know, sounds weird which is why my friend wanted to order it, but it was definitely a great combo. All in all, I'd recommend giving it a shot if you live in the area.

Great lunch specials! I usually get the $10 spicy salmon roll and 2 pieces of nigiri ( I get the eel!). I love that you order at the counter and they bring the food to you. It's still presented really nicely and you have actual plates and nice chopsticks, but this allows us to go there and have a nice meal and be on the road within a 40 minute timeframe at most. I'm hoping to try the bento box next time I'm there as its only $10 as well.

The sushi is decent, but not great. It's definitely overpriced. For a take-out place, the decor and atmosphere are both nice. The staff is also very friendly and pleasant. I might go back here for the convenience, since it's really close to my home. But otherwise I'd probably go somewhere else to really get my money's worth.
I got the spicy scallop roll. It was great. I usually don't love sushi/rolls but this really satisfied me. I will definitely return.

Why pay more? With the price they charge...what is value? Seriously, just 5 minutes more drive, you can get better take out at Benihana or Blue Fin. I am not much fun of rolls anyway; but this place serves a little weird California roll to my taste...dried imitation crab meat was not so good at all :( I can just give two stars...but close to one actually!

Decided to give this place another shot...and I was shot down. I wanted to try the benchmark salmon avocado and spicy tuna. It took them 20 minutes to make the rolls (4 chefs in the back and it was not busy at all) and they were very sloppily put together. They were falling apart basically. The spicy tuna was decent but not memorable and the salmon avocado was not that fresh. At least it was part of the lunch special and didn't cost an arm and a leg. The waiter/cashier was pretty nice and had a very cheerful demeanor. For sushi, I'm heading to Bluefin next time.

Best sushi I have ever had. Love the spicy tuna crunch. Also loved the yellow fin roll. The egg rolls are delicious as well. Got the chicken teriyaki roll once and it was good I just prefer the seafood rolls. Overall everything is phenomenal. Have yet to have a bad thing. Always try a new thing when I come in because they have so much. My wife also loves this place as well we were not ones for sushi until we found here.

Great lunch deal. Delicious rolls. Was here for lunch and had the spicy tuna roll and Mexican roll. Mexican was just some spicy sauce in a California roll. But were tasty. Next time I may venture out to their specialty rolls. They had some intersting ones with fried calimari.

Chicken teriyaki bowl and Chicken katsu bowl both came with miso soup. The miso was average. The chicken rice bowls however had maybe five thin strips of chicken at the most, very skimpy. This was not worth $8.45 at all. We should've known when we didn't see anyone in the restaurant at 7:45pm, not a good sign.
This is a great little spot. Fresh, reasonable and friendly service. It's not high end but fills a middle of the budget sushi need. Will be back for sure.
This small but really nice fast casual restaurant was amazing. We had chicken teriyaki & chirashi sashimi & rice. It came with great miso/tofu soup. We highly recommended this restaurant.
I love the spicy tuna crunch ! Everything is always fresh, tasty, and the service is great.

The Sushi isn't bad, but it's overpriced for the quality and small portion sizes. The lunch special isn't a bad deal, but I'd rather drive 5 minutes more to Blue Fin on Germantown which has some of the best Sushi in the country. If you don't mind going to North Wales, Assi Plaza has excellent, fresh, mouth watering sushi for less than half the price they're charging here.

Down from 5 stars. I was referred to them years ago by a native Japanese friend who stuffed my belly my first visit. If I'm rating flavours: 5 stars. But my last 3 visits were disappointing. Their prices continue to go up which I could tolerate but their portions are questionable. Chicken Teriyaki Bento is a favourite. It's now up $4, from $14 to $18. I didn't used to care because I could have my fill on my lunch break and finish leftovers after work. But seriously, let's call it what is: Onion Teriyaki. I've asked for extra chicken but was told they have no control over how much I get. I opted once for Gyoza instead of sushi and I got two tiny bite sized fried bits with no sauce. The majority of the plate is an ice cream scoop size of rice and a cup of soup. The half handful of lettuce for salad is wilted if it's delivered. Not worth the money. Sorry Happy Maki, it's been a good run but I think I'm done.
Best sushi ever. Little pricey but worth it! M-w get there before 6 and its bogo!

I live in San Francisco and have had top notch sushi as the norm. I didn't expect Sf quality or prices, but after reading the reviews, thought it would be above average. It was not. The chirashi was miserable...75% rice, 10% radish spirals and 15% fish. The shashimi was only 3 types of fish and only 6 slices. They were very thinly sliced. I've never had a sushi chef cut sashimi in such a way! The highlight was the seaweed salad. Tempura was average, shrimp spring rolls full of lettuce and completely tasteless, served with canned industrial Chinese duck sauce and shrimp "dumplings" that I think you can buy at Costco in the frozen section. 2 stars because at least the thinly sliced fish was fresh.

This review is for the lunch menu. This place is quick and convenient, but the price you pay for that is high and the quality is sub-par for the price. I paid $13-14 for 4 pieces of Nigiri (Sushi) and a Spicy Tuna Roll. The Spicy Tuna Roll was okay but the Sushi pieces were lacking in quality. I tried Salmon, Tuna, and Snapper. Salmon was okay because the fattiness of the fish masks the quality. Tuna and Snapper were extremely disappointing. The Tuna had a bright red color rather than a deeper ruby as it should be. It's sad to say, but the quality of fish was comparable to King Buffet ($9 w/ tip for lunch). If it's not too far from you, go out of your way to go to Bluefin instead for lunch. Their comparable lunch combo is $15 and it comes with 5 pieces of Sushi vs. 4. Add in tip of $3 for a total of $18, and you have a much higher quality meal served with Miso Soup or a Salad. With that said, I'm willing to come back to Happy Maki but definitely not for Sushi. I'd be willing to give them one more star if their Bento boxes or Donburi is good.

I probably get something from Happy Maki every few weeks or so. I appreciate that there's a clean, not-bad place in Conshohocken to get sushi or a bento box. My only complaint is that without a coupon from the Clipper Magazine that shows up every once in awhile, it's pretty expensive. My favorite thing to order is the Chicken Katsu bento. Miso soup, katsu, rice, 4 small pieces of California roll and salad for soemthing like $14. It's not cheap, but it's pretty good comfort food. PS. The screens at the cashier aren't touch-screens. Trust me, I learned the hard way.

My wife and I love sushi and visit several sushi restaurants in the area around Happy Maki. We love Blue Fin, Sushi Cazu and several restaurants in the Lansdale area. Based on that, we were hesitant to try Happy Maki as we found near perfection elseware. However, based on the fact that Happy Maki is only a 2 min drive from our house, I have always wanted to give it a try. We went last week and found the entire experience horrible. The "style" of the restaurant is odd and based on this counter service, one would think the prices would reflect. But as the above posts indicate, the prices are not inline with the experience. Something about a soda fountain machine a few feet from where you are eating sushi does not compute. While a BYOB, they did not even offer to open our bottle of wine. The sushi (now this is a very bold statement) was the worst I have ever had in my life. Most was inappropriate to eat and made me feel sick the next day just thinking about it. The flavors, combinations, consistancy was just not right. While we did have decent service, I would never go back to Happy Maki. I would also never recommend this restaurant to friends and foes alike.
Love the variety of rolls that are offered. The price is a bit on the high side, but definitely worth it.
Sushi was fantastic! Great service and a very new an innovative menu. Would 100% come back and try more things. Lunch specials seem like a great deal too!

I got takeout sushi from Happy Maki. I ordered a spicy tuna and a philadelphia roll. The sushi was notably fresher and better than the order I picked up from the Stonewell a few weeks back for less money. Important when sushi places are less than a 5 minute drive from one another.... The inside of the restaurant is small, dark, modern and cute. I don't see it as being a great date place- probably just better to grab a quick lunch and they do have lunch specials. The guy at the counter was pleasant and it was an in and out experience. I'd be so bold to say that this is the best sushi in Conshohocken. If you want a sit-down experience and a higher quality product/more options then you need to head down to Bluefin2.

Happy maki is one of the best sushi places nearby. The service is always nice. It's more of a cafe place, so you go up and pay before you sit down and the food is served. There's rarely a wait for dine in as it is more of a take out kind of place. There are special rolls each day that are 2 dollars off. My favorites include the rose roll, the flaming (great for spicy-food lovers), and the tiger. Their spicy chicken teriyaki rice bowl is amazing too. I believe if you go during lunch hours, there are lunch sushi specials that include a cooked and fresh roll for 10$.
This place is awesome. I love their sushi bento. Their salmon nigiri is the best! The sunkiss roll and monkey balls are also really great.

Every time I choose this easy in/out Japanese sushi place... It never disappoints. The host/cashier is always so courteous professional & charming. The menu is elaborate especially considering the space of the restaurant is. Every *special* sushi roll I have tried is great! Food is fresh with nice presentation too! The prices are fair they are superior in taste considering you pay about that much at the sushi pre-made/packaged from trendy super markets. Atmosphere is low-key but has that Japaneseque vibey-thing going on.

Sooo I work in Conshy and there really are no sushi spots around besides this one. I was really excited to try this place out - I had high hopes and it did not disappoint. I would steady drive by as it is in a popular shopping center and finally came during lunch a few weeks ago with a coworker. It is an order at the counter and sit experience, which is good for a quick lunch. They bring your food to you at your seat once ready. We got edamame which wasn't that impressive and three rolls to split. The rolls were tasty. It was about $35 for all of that which is reasonable for sushi. My favorite was the spicy tuna crunch. There's ample seating or you can order out. I'll definitely be back!

Very consistent sushi and bento boxes. Our kids have been eating here since they could chew solids. The rolls are yummy and the chicken katsu is as good as I've had it on the east coast for under $20.
Very happy I tried this place. The staff were friendly and my rainbow roll was beautiful and delicious. My only complaint was the size of the salmon nigiri.

Happy Maki brings a new style of dining to the Philadelphia area. People do not see much of what they offer. People often complain about the high prices of their sushi based on the services they offer. What is actually happening is neglect for why they do things the way they do. They purchase the same expensive ingredients as high quality restaurants and bring their west-coast style of rolls to the Conshohocken area. Their prices reflect what a typical sushi restaurant prices their sushi while understanding that it would be more if their customer base chose to dine at a restaurant. Tip is expected from those types of restaurants but here at Happy Maki their goal is to provide the same sushi at a faster and efficient rate. Their attempt is all done while keeping the prices quite balanced. So, if you honestly calculate the prices of eating sushi along with tip you save a few dollars and eat high quality food. Also understand that the restaurant is more geared towards take-out. Overall this restaurant brings a unique style that is actually a new experience for all.

The sushi is pretty good here, It's not blue fin or Osaka but decent. They lost stars because their service is super slow! It's taken over 20 minutes before when they weren't busy! My pickup orders also are not always ready when I arrive. Also, their a bit over priced for their portions.
$$$ for a to go place. I say to go because the atmosphere/decor has zero appeal. Sushi is good but It's priced as if you were sitting somewhere nice and getting the true sushi experience.

Complete and total underwhelming meal. The only single saving grace was the salad dressing. The salad was warm and obviously from a bag. I have never had frozen tuna, but I did tonight. It was an odd pink color, ice cold to the touch and had zero flavor. The crunchy spicy tuna roll was incredibly under filled and over priced. 6 individual pieces of sashimi and a loosely and lightly filled roll for $25. If I could pay $50 to get the last 30 minutes of my life back and my stomach pumped for a complete do over I would in an instant. Never again, Never ever again. On to the next one.

I love this sushi place. It's clean, has a cute ambience and the food is awesome! I just went there over the weekend and I tried two new dishes- their "Happy Chicken" salad which is crispy chicken in a mango sauce over greens- the dressing is SO good. I also tried their new Sunflower roll which is spicy tuna with crunchy tempura flakes on top- I love the crunch!! My favorite roll is the Tornado in which they fry potato sticks and pile them on top of the rolls, and their Money Ball is so unique in which they fry jalapeno peppers, cream cheese and tuna together- it sounds weird but tastes SO good! Their udon is really good too with the broth really light and flavorful. All their sauces and dressings are house-made. For a cheap, fast, delicious sushi place, I always come here!!
Always good quality. Sometimes the actual serving size of the fish itself is quite small. See the attached image...for $15 I would want a reasonable size piece of salmon in all of my rolls.

Pretty good sushi in the suburbs. Like Seve's reveiw, would you really want to eat cheap sushi? They have unique rolls, including one that comes out on fire! I particularly like the fact that there's no waiters, save acouple bucks on tip. they bring you the food out to your table anyhow. Service is always pleasant. ummm, craving some monkey balls, fried jalapenos stuffed with cream cheese. YUM!!
Do NOT get the ramen!!! It's watered bowl broth and ramen noodles with a cracked egg in it... cheap and not worth it. The sushi on the other hand was great. Got the California crunch.

Stumbled across Happy Maki this past weekend, I honestly had never noticed it before. I'm picky about my food and while I enjoy sushi I like everything cooked (not a raw fan). Tried the Killer Shrimp Roll and Angry Scallop roll and both were absolutely phenomenal. I thought they were prepared perfectly, I liked the presentation but best of all they were delicious. Happy Maki may be a little pricey but it left me a happy customer.

I love this place and grab the teriyaki chicken bowl at every opportunity. It's a hole in the wall restaurant and very unassuming, however, on the inside, it is clean, the food is fresh and delicious and the workers there are friendly, professional and efficient. They are willing to tweak and customize their dishes for you as well. It's tiny inside with only a handful of booths along one wall but the delicious food and friendly service make up for it. I've never had a bad experience here. I love it. It's the perfect place to grab lunch.

I have considered getting a job here just so I can eat here every day. I could eat at Happy Maki every day for the rest of my life. I love the Spicy Tuna Rolls, Yellowtail Rolls, Angry Scallop Rolls, and Sunkissed Rolls. The Bento Boxes are great, but the sushi here is what it's all about. I ordered a house salad and didn't expect much but it had a homemade ginger dressing that is fantastic. I love everything I've ever tried here. Plus they have gluten free soy sauce if you ask!

The sushi was pretty good. Nothing really that special but better than a lot of other places. My real qualm is with their pricing. They do have some good deals at certain times of the day, but I paid $8.50 for one (8 small piece) philly roll. If it was amazing sushi I might be okay paying that, but for pretty average sushi I think that's way overpriced.

Went here the other night with my boyfriend and let me tell you, this place is a hidden gem! We had no idea it was here; tucked away on the side of the shopping center! So, the atmosphere was cute- we weren't there at a super crowded time, but there were only two booths open. I didn't expect the type of ordering/service that it was, but I didn't hate it. So I ordered the Gyoza and the killer shrimp roll (with soy paper wrap) and my boyfriend got the monkey ball appetizer, and two rolls (I can't remember the names currently). He said his rolls were okay, nothing too out of the ordinary. However, my killer shrimp roll was everything I've hoped and dreamed for. It was so delicious and they were super accommodating with my soy paper wrap. The gyoza was crispy- just how I like it. The only downside was that we ordered a one of the special rolls from their "special board" (we went on a Friday) and we didn't realize until after dinner that they didn't give us the two dollar discount for ordering off of the specials board. And in the grand scheme of things.. it was two dollars; Not even worth losing a star! The service was friendly and fast! It was so good- I have a feeling it'll become a regular stop for us!

Stopped on the way home for a dinner here --- food was good but portions well under for the price paid. We ordered three rice bowls with different options - Chicken katsu/ veggie & shrimp tempura / chicken teriyaki bowl . Fresh maki rolls as well as Spicy Ramen Served with miso soup as well as rice. Food was fresh and served hot. Three pieces of chicken katsu/ with pickled cabbage in a bowl mainly filled with rice Veggie/Shrimp Tempura bowl with picked cabbage and ONE shrimp Too much rice and too less meat -- but overall it was a nice restaurant & good food.
