reviews.title: Good for BUDGET trip
reviews.text: I book two rooms there on 9th July, 2015. Hotel manager was soft spoken and helpful in nature. Rooms were also nice. We took breakfast, it was tasty and average in price. Littlebit problem in cleaning of towels. We asked for more towel, but he denied. WiFi was free but not useful in the rooms. Location is also good, near to mall road and market. I would recommend the hotel for budget peoples.

reviews.title: Nice room, horrible crook staff
reviews.text: I went there off season with 7 other girls, we took 2 rooms, for 1000-1000 rs each (4-4 people), and the rooms were beautiful, covered with wooden panels, and the bathroom was spacious also, but the towels were full of stains. When i asked for a clean towel, it had even more stains, We only spent one night there, because the girls were cold and decided to go to south. I decided to stay one more night alone , and i discussed with the receptionist guy that i can take a much smaller room alone for 500 rs. I asked the receptionist guy to fill out the form and write it in the registration book, but he said no no , its ok. We even shook hands, but luckily I didnt pay in advance. After the others left, i went to the market for one and a half hour, and when i returned,it was already dark. Then the guy knocked on the door and wanted more money. We had a big argument over it, but he denied what we agreed on. What a spineless crook. I asked ok, so what was our agreement about??? He said: that u can leave your baggage here for 1 and a half hour for 500 rs.... This guy thought he could take advantage of me just because i was a woman alone and it was already dark outside. Luckily a foreign couple arrived and he went to do the registration with them. Then I grabbed all my stuff and ran away before he returned with his friends. I don't recommend this hotel to anyone, no matter how beautiful the rooms are, go only if you are not alone or if you like being ripped of. I went by a cycle riksha to the other side of the lake to a small villa, where there were wonderful people, very honest ones, who didn't want to take advantage of a female traveller. The rooms were more frugal compared to himtrek, but i didnt mind it, i only paid 250 for a double room and I really loved the hosts.

reviews.title: Great room in a great spot
reviews.text: When we arrived at Kuwadro at Haarlemmerdijk both Johnny and Goran took their time to introduce us to Amsterdam. Every day our refrigerator was filled with new stuff that tasted great. The Haarlemmerdijk and Haarlemmerstraat is a fantastic area where you can find lots of specialiced shops.

reviews.title: Super B&B
reviews.text: Stayed here for 3 nights with my girlfriend and we loved it. Met Goran upon arrival and he was brilliant in giving us information about amsterdam,things to do and how to get around. The B&B is in a nice busy area about 10-12 minute walk from central station and about 15 minutes into centre but trams nearby. Our room was stocked with plenty for breakfast each morning so we were never hungry leaving for the day ahead. The steps up to the room are steep but that's definitely a common trend in every building in Amsterdam which we learned in our time there! Would really recommend this place to everyone,nice,clean,comfortable and a top class host

reviews.title: Fair room, good location, thin walls
reviews.text: Room was clean and well attended, with a decent breakfast selection refreshed in the fridge daily. Mattress was very comfortable although we both felt the pillows were rather too big. Only negatives that have lowered the review are that the walls are very thin so we did hear a lot of noise coming from the family that live in the property and were woken up on one occasion - can't be helped with young children I'm sure, but not exactly ideal when you've spent €560 euros... And the heating often wasn't switched on, which left the room cold when we returned. Can't fault the location though, and we did receive a friendly welcome off Goran who gave us tips for visiting the city and a map. Would recommend for location and simplicity, but be aware if you're a light sleeper who doesn't plan on having an early start each morning! Also very steep staircase, typical of old Amsterdam properties!

reviews.title: Perfect Place
reviews.text: We have found a treasure with this apartment & having stayed here in November, we have booked another 3 visits over the next few months.. Location is superb, apartment is spotless with all mod cons & extras that make all the difference.. Thank you for sharing your gaff it's awesome 😊

reviews.title: Felt like home, we were sad to leave!
reviews.text: We fell in love with Amsterdam and this accommodation! This was my first experience with a bed and breakfast, I must admit we were slightly skeptical to begin with as we weren't sure how private the rooms were, however immediately upon arrival we knew we had made the right choice! The owners were incredibly friendly, they provided us with a detailed map of Amsterdam which included places to eat and other tourist destinations. They tidied up our room on a daily basis and filled our fridge with fresh food for breakfast the following morning. They even let us use they're washing facilities, anything we needed, they were on top of it, and privacy was definitely not an issue! Beds were super comfy and the location was perfect, walking distance from everything. We stayed for a total of 2 weeks and did not want to come home! Thanks for everything Kuwadro! Wouldn't stay anywhere else in Amsterdam! See you next time!

reviews.title: Lovely B&B in nice area and good base to explore Amsterdam
reviews.text: Exceptionally clean, comfortable room, good breakfast, tea and coffee in the room, even easter eggs and chocolate daily. Really helpful host that took time to explain the area and the attractions of the city and marked it clearly on a city map the places we were interested in seeing. Great location for exploring the city. Good access for Trams, Buses, Cycle hire and near to the central station (15 minutes easy walking). Some great boutiques, bars and restaurants within easy walk. . We were also able to leave our luggage at the B&B securely after check out time.

reviews.title: Very central - Loved it
reviews.text: The place is beautiful. They have 2 bedrooms on the 3rd floor with a kitchen in the middle. The room is large and tastefully furnished. Only drawback is the steep climb to the third floor. Location is great. few minutes walk from Central station. there are couple of good pubs down stairs. The owners are great and they keep the place neat. Love to come back...

reviews.title: Great vacation in Amsterdam
reviews.text: Our stay in the hotel was really comfortable.The room was cleaned every day,breakfast was great.The staff was kind and help us a lot to get we wanted to.The centre of Amsterdam was close,so you can walk all over great places.This place makes you feel different ,in the atmosphere of the city you can feel all of the energy of art’s gteatest from the past.Makes you want to come back!

reviews.title: Amazing Amsterdam
reviews.text: We visited Amsterdam this weekend and had an amazing time. What a beautiful City that is overloaded with culture, it has such a positive vibe. We stayed at Kuwadro for 2 nights, this place is in a great location in arhat her boutique setting just minutes from the centre. We were met by Goran when we arrived who was very helpful and gave us some great tips on places to visit, he even helped with our luggage. The room was spotless and well stocked for essentials for the weekend and fresh fruit was delivered each morning. We were shocked after we left Kuwadro to hear Goran following us on his bike as we had left our iPod in the room, that is the level of service you get from these guys.

reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.text: Great service. So friendly and helpful. Nikki who meet us when we arrived was super. She chatted with us and told us whats around, best to do, gave us map. It is a 10-15min walk from central and really easy to find with their map emailed. quiet street so perfect for sleeping during day after partying. we forgot something and they have agreed to post it to us (thank you). I have been in Amsterdam before and stayed more central but this has been the best, the cheapest, the cleanest. really liked this place :) Mini fridge was great and the nespresso machine saved me from my hangovers... big thumbs up

reviews.title: Great Stay
reviews.text: I stayed here last week with my partner, we both really like it. We had a lovely room very comfy bed & nice modern bathroom. We really like that there was a coffee machine & that the breakfast was in the room meant you aren't tied to times. Each day our fridge was filled with fresh orange juice, bread, meat, cheese, fruit & yoghurt. Perfect start to our day. Johnny was a great host sat down with us on arrival & chatted about where to go on the map - really helpful. Kuwadro is located in a really nice part of the city we really liked walking through the Jordaan area. It's also only 10-15 mins walk from Central station.

reviews.title: Location/Service/Breakfast-- top notch
reviews.text: We stayed in the Jordaan location for three nights over the weekend, and couldn't be more pleased. The proprietor accommodated our arrival time and took the time to sit down with us, asked what we wanted to get out of our weekend, and to make recommendations (an experience we certainly did NOT have with other bnbs). Our room faced the street, Haarlemmerdijk, which is a gem of a street in itself. Location was easily walkable from the train station and really in the heart of it all. We were thrilled with the range of breakfast items and this was our favorite accent of the bnb, to me this really sealed the value of it all. No complaints at all, but do be aware that this is situated on a busy (but wonderful) street so if you can't sleep through the fun, that may be problematic. 10/10 would come back!!!

reviews.title: Not the quietest stay
reviews.text: The b&b in its entirety would have been perfect. Great location that was walking distance to all attractions. It was clean, bright and plenty to eat. Unfortunately we were woken up daily and early by a small child running about, sometimes screaming and generally being a small child. I appreciate this can’t be helped if you have a small child, but we paid €407 for 3 nights, it’s not the cheapest. Had earplugs for road noise, these didn’t help inside! It’s a shame.

reviews.title: Good place for lunch & relaxing stop between the rocks
reviews.text: Food slightly overpriced for what one gets, but one is paying for the location - convenient between the rocks. They also have rooms, too, which look great and available at negotiable rates. Just ask the owner what she can offer -- and greater discounts can be obtained for longer stays.

reviews.title: Charming place!
reviews.text: Charming hotel and especially the owner! She is fantastic! It has a perfect location for climbing both Lion Rock and Pidurangala Rock. Peaceful and calm hotel with a fantastic breakfast. Can really recommend this place!

reviews.title: Perfect location and service
reviews.text: The location of Thal Sewana is perfect for climbing either Pidurangalar Rock and Sigirya Rock. They are both working 10/20 minutes walking distance. A Tuk Tuk to the golden temple in Dambulla is around 2500LRs return. The owners of thal sewana were very welcoming. It a nice place, great curry ! If you are getting at Tuk Tuk from Dambulla to thal sewana them tell them it’s on the other side of Sigirya rock as we had some confusion. It should cost you about 1500/1700 Rs

reviews.title: Convenient accommodation option near Sigiriya
reviews.text: This accommodation is highly recommended if you want to visit sigiriya and/or pidurangala. Both are within walking distance of this place. The rooms are functional, the food is decent and the caretaker is friendly, helpful, efficient and speaks English. If you are not careful, you might even bump into a wild elephant - I just missed one!

reviews.title: Excellent little place!
reviews.text: This homestay exceeded expectations! We arrived late after a long day of travelling and were met with a friendly welcome. Breakfast was included in our price and it was prepared for a time that suited us and was great! We had fruit and eggs and toast amongst other things. The family that runs this place are so genuinely kind and the son was happy to help us by calling train stations and sorting out our transport back to Colombo. We were made to feel like one of the family especially when we were being introduced to the sons family and waving them off goodbye as they left. I was also allowed to have a go at driving their tuk tuk on the track outside! The location was fab, a 5 minute stroll to Pidurangala rock and a tiny bit further for lions rock but not massively, both are visible from this place. After we climbed the rock we did take a walk into the closest town, it's not too far but I would recommend a tuk tuk if you were tired like we were at that point! We chose to eat dinner and lunch at the homestay and food was very cheap but tasted amazing! It was so delicious. The rooms were a nice size and the internet worked well considering you are in the middle of the jungle. The best part of this stay has to be the owners, they go out of their way to help you and get you anything you need (she even gifted my sister some cream to help her insect bites!). At the end of the trip we hugged goodbye and were waved off like we were one of the family. Would 100% recommend this place, have no negative comments.

reviews.title: Restaurant well situated, 300m from Pidurangula entrance.
reviews.text: We stopped here for lunch on our way back from Pidurangula Rock, to the main street to get our bus back. We were served very quickly. The food was good but honestly, the portions were very tiny and it was a bit expensive for what we got. So I can't say that this restaurant is value for money, but after the walk of Pidurangula, if you are hungry, this place is well situated so it is very convenient to stop here.

reviews.title: Fabulous breakfast on return from pidurangula!
reviews.text: We came here for breakfast on our way back from climbing Pidurangala rock. The food was lovely and very well priced! The people who run it were very helpful and gave us useful advice on the busses etc. This would be a great place to stay if you were here panning to climb Pidurangala for sunrise (which was awesome)!

reviews.title: Fantastic stay
reviews.text: The location is great, and this small property makes you feel at home. The manager Arun and his friend were very friendly and always accommodating our requests. The environment and their Sri Lankan breakfast are the best. Thank you guys, we will definitely recommend it.

reviews.title: Best Stay in Sri Lanka
reviews.text: Great owner, family and staff! They did everything to make our stay as good as possible and arranged transportation when we needed it. Really good breakfast and quite some a-la-carte options for lunch and dinner as well. (Try the cheese and chicken kottu and the vegetable rolls!) Location is a little bit out of 'town', but very close to the two rocks that can be climbed! They have kids and they played with our baby all day and he loved it! For dinner they prepared a special meal for our baby and he loved it and ate it all! We really do recommend this place!

reviews.title: Good lunch spot
reviews.text: We stopped here for lunch after climbing the nearby rock. We had nice fresh juice, sandwiches and ice cream. It’s the only place close by and it’s worth stopping after a hot climb. It has dinner as well if you climb in the afternoon.

reviews.title: Honeymoon Trip
reviews.text: Me and my wife stayed here for 1 night at the start of our honeymoon. The location of the home stay is brilliant as it’s a 5 min drive to lions rock which was our first site seeing attraction, however it is down a long dirt track road with no lighting so you aren’t able to venture out at night unless you have a driver. The staff there were extremely friendly and welcoming. The bed was really comfortable but the room could do with more attention. We were provided with welcome drinks and a small Christmas present on check out. There is WiFi available and the breakfast was delicious, really traditional Sri Lankan breakfast.

reviews.title: The perfect accommodation in Sigirya
reviews.text: Great accommodation and location, we recommend it to everybody who wants to discover Sigiriya. With special thanks to most wonderful hostess we met during our trip to Sri Lanka. We would certainly stay here again. Arriving in Thal Sewana felt like an oasis after all the hustle and bustle of the big cities. The accommodation feels really homely and is very clean and well maintained. The location is perfect between both rocks. The room and bathroom were very clean. It all looked brand new and also has the best shower (even better dan the one we have at home). The porch is wonderful to sit and enjoy the beautiful garden and the delicious foods. All the food is home-made and really flavourful and tasty. The breakfast is the best we had during our trip with al large variety of fresh products (springhoppers, pancakes, fresh fruit, eggs, different every day). You taste the love Washanti (the hostess) puts in her food. She makes you feel welcome and takes the time to give advise on what to do and see but also to explain about Sri Lanka and its religions. In different reviews we saw that they wished they could stay longer, therefore we booked for 4 nights and didn't regret it at all. The perfect place to stay and we would recommend it to everybody! Thank you Washanti for making our trip to Sri Lanka so special.

reviews.title: Wonderfull stay
reviews.text: Wasanti, the manager/owner of the place is the main reason my stay was so amazing. She was so kind, gentle, friendly and caring. The food she made was really good and she even packed us a doggy bag that we ate the day after. The hotel is like at maximum 15 minutes of walk from Sigiriya! The room was really clean. We felt like being part of her family as her daughter works with her and it is a small hotel. It was like renting a room in a Sri lankan family. Wonderfull experience and cheap!

reviews.title: Staff is incredibly nice. Food is delicious.
reviews.text: The woman who manage the guest house is amazing and sweet. The dinner was delicious and the breakfast very good too. The room is simple but has everything you might need. The location is in the middle of the jungle so very quite but has a lot of insects especially in the evening so bring mosquito repellent spray.

reviews.title: Great value for money
reviews.text: Located only few meters away from Pidurangala Rock and sigiriya. Very well loacted and rooms are clean. Special thanks to Anil and his colleague for providing with food and directions. Very helpfull. Would recommend this place for anybody. Keep up the good work. Will visit again for sure.

reviews.title: Perfect stay at thal sewana
reviews.text: We wanted to visit pidurangala and sigiriya rock and also to be located in a quite place. The staff also deserves special mention as they were extremely helpful and nice. I recommend this place 100% 5 min walking to pidurangala and 20 min to sigiriya rock.

reviews.title: Perfect host and meal !
reviews.text: We stopped at thal sewana to have lunch. The owner is incredibbly nice and would do everything to please you. Above that, she is a very good cook ! We loved it so much, we decided to go back in the evening. I highly recommend this Place, perfectly located to climb the lion rock and the Pidurangala.

reviews.title: Typical lunch in a peaceful place
reviews.text: We didn't stay in the guesthouse but it s located between the two rocks . We had lunch after climbing the 2 rocks and the food was excellent : the chicken kottu was delicious ! The owner was really friendly and it was a pleasure to talk to her. We recommend it if you want to eat or even drink something ( juices were really good too) after the hike but somewhere more genuine than the cafeteria of the park.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Very very very good, very nice, clean and friendly!!! If you will pass this place, just stay here ;-) They will do everything for you... No matter, what you want... And out is very close to small rock of Sigiriya!

reviews.title: Great Lunch spot between Lion Rock and Pidurangala
reviews.text: Great homestay with clean, quiet rooms and great food! We stopped for lunch on our way to Pidurangala and took advantage of the charming garden and good WiFi. The owner spoke great English and was very flexible re. food allergies. The portions of food were smaller than most places in Sri Lanka, but still filling.

reviews.title: Wonderful 2 days.
reviews.text: We stayed here for 2 nights on our tour of India. What a fantastic place to stay. Such an incredible home and wonderful welcoming family. A place of peace after some hectic days. Delicious meals taken with the family, who were so interesting to talk with and learn about India, their culture and way of life. We so enjoyed this aspect of the stay. Lovely large room, with good facilities. Really enjoyed the walking tour of the rubber and coco plantations and learning about the plants and environment. A must in anyone's trip.

reviews.title: A most pleasant stay in a really exceptional site!!
reviews.text: We arrived very lat in this privately owned Manor on a huge plantation. The proprietor, a very educated and cultivated medical professor waited with his family with the dinner which we took together with him! In the conversations we learned a lot about the christian minority's life in southrn India. The room was spacious, calm, with views only on the palm trees. You can sleep with open windows, because it is cool outside! Beautiful bath of grey granite. - Next morning the owner made a private tour over hs plantation with us, explaining all spice plants and the cultivation of trees and fruits - really interesting! I only can recommend this place because it gives you the rare opportunity to learn to know a member of the Indian upper class personally!!

reviews.title: Memorable stay
reviews.text: We spent three nights in the beautiful home of Matthew and Rosie. The house has many beautiful teak features with a huge terrace to enjoy a glass of homemade juice or beer in the evening. The bedroom was spotless, air conditioned, great shower and tea making facilities. Three delicious home cooked meals a day, produced by Rosie and her daughter in law Tina. All dishes explained and true authentic Keralan flavours. We enjoyed a visit to our hosts rubber plantation and coconut oil processing plant. Fascinating for us Westerners and fully explained by Matthew’s son Vivek together with his two bright and delightful little boys. We made two visits to the surrounding plantation and were simply overwhelmed by the variety of crops produced. The family were all so welcoming, warm and a joy to spend time with.

reviews.title: More of Vivek and Tina please!
reviews.text: This is a difficult review to write because we have very mixed feelings about our stay. Matthew is very attentive but rather domineering so that one feels just too directed at times. He told us on our arrival that he only lets one room at a time because otherwise the guests ignore him and talk among themselves. We did not find that to be the case in any homestay that we used. We loved the visit to the church and to the school and his driver took us for a wonderful day in a national park with an enjoyable picnic. However this was at the expense of a planned and paid for visit in our itinerary that would have been led by our own, excellent driver. Dinner was rather late at 8.30pm in the evening and when we came down all the doors to the outside were locked and the inside seating area dark so we felt that we were intruding. When we had the chance to talk to Vivek and Tina, the younger generation, it was less formal and we feel that perhaps they should take the lead in the homestay business to give a more inviting feel to what could be an excellent homestay.

reviews.title: Wonderful Homestay
reviews.text: This is a wonderful Homestay with a lovely family. The house is really comfortable and the food was delicious. Even though it was raining heavy while I visited that didn't stop Vivek & Matthew showing me their fascinating plantation.

reviews.title: A truly unique homestay experience with a genuine and hospitable family in beautiful surroundings
reviews.text: We had a magical 2 nights at the Planters retreat. The family hosts went out of their way to make us welcome and comfortable and we had a truly authentic Keralan experience. The cuisine was extraordinary and the surroundings fascinating and we learnt so much about the culture. There is plenty to see in the near by forest and some interesting trips to do. Our room was very comfortable and the atmospherevery relaxed and welcoming. It's an amazing retreat and definitely worth the interesting car journey :-)))

reviews.title: Brilliant Homestay
reviews.text: Spent 1 night at Planters Retreat as part of a VJV tour of Kerala. We were not sure what to expect but Matthew and Tina made us very welcome and their home is just lovely. Our room was massive, comfortable with a terrific bathroom. Matthew took us to visit a coconut oil factory run by his cousin and to see his rubber plantation. The trips were interesting and we got an insight into the local economy, the use of coconuts and the problems faced by the local population. Matthew and Tina were great company and we also enjoyed meeting two of their sons Thomas and Joseph who were really good hosts. Our experience was a highlight of the trip and it made a lovely change from hotels. Well worth it.

reviews.title: An interesting homestay
reviews.text: We were welcomed graciously by Dr. Matthew and his family, and we enjoyed learning more about healthcare in India as well as about the challenges of running an organic plantation. We had a tour of the plantation and marvelled at the diversity and complexity of running such a venture. We enjoyed a trip to the nearby dam, and the wonderful picnic that Tina provided for us. We felt uncomfortable eating in splendour at a folding picnic table while our guide and driver sat behind the car for their lunch. Coming from New Zealand, this just does not feel right but we simply had to accept it. Tina catered beautifully for us and we enjoyed getting to know her delightful little boys. We enjoyed being in a family home, though quite a formal one. The wifi did not work for us, but otherwise it was a very comfortable stay.

reviews.title: A good home stay stop
reviews.text: Dr Mathew and his family run a fine homestay, with pleasant ,if not exciting, air conditioned rooms and quite acceptable bathroom facilities and a relaxing lounge if you have the time in the evening. The good doctor and his family conducted us around the one time full rubber estate , which is now diversifying to meet modern requirements , and gives his guests a warm insight into a planters day. The homely meals were splendid , This is a good night stop , whether we should more enjoy an extended stay I am not sure .

reviews.title: Unfriendly ..impersonal
reviews.text: The room was furnished with second hand or old unwanted furniture. What were we paying for. there was a horrible dark coloured bathroom suite (old) the host did give us a interesting and informative walk around the plantation and arranged for us to go on a lovely drive to a dam with a picnic. He and his son ate with us....but not relaxed We wanted to sit on the verandah...nowhere to sit in garden or in our drab bedroom --however the hosts grand children were continually going up and down on trikes etc.,,no relaxing with a book here. Don't think the host deserves guests...

reviews.title: Outstanding Hosts, Superb Food, Hugely Interesting
reviews.text: Stayed at this beautiful plantation for a few nights and we were genuinely sorry to leave. Mathew and his son Vivek showed us round the plantation and explained the working of the different processes, includung a short visit to the coconut oil plant just down the road. The rubber tapping and the production of sheet rubber was also a unique experience. They also arranged excursions for us and we were accompanied by Sajess (hope the spelling is OK) one of the plantation´s workers who made the outing to Siruvani dam an unforgettable experience. The food prepared by Mathew´s wife (sorry I have forotten her name) and Tina, Vivek´s wife. Words cannot decribe the flavours put on the table. Every meal was different and one delight after the other. Vivek - if you read this, I hope the aquaculture is a success - you deserve it

reviews.title: Lovely setting. The plantation is an intersting experience.
reviews.text: A beautiful property set within lovely gardens and plantation. Or room was huge and the bathroom a good size. The large well furnished verandahs were peaceful to sit and read or snooze in my case. The hosts were very welcoming. The ladies of the house made food which aimed to give us a taste of different types of Indian food, some we had had before some was new to us, it was all enjoyed. The host's son showed us around the plantation which was fascinating. There was a much more diverse range of crops than I had expected. The descriptions of rubber and cocoa production were very interesting. I was impressed by Vivek (son) he appears to be an astute business man. We were taken for an all day safari to a local forest and reservoir. A picnic lunch was provided along with tables, chairs and an umbrella for us westerners. We had a lovely day and expected to pay for the drivers time and petrol, but it was complimentary, although we would have been happy to contribute. A very enjoyable stay in some of the most picturesque scenery we encountered on our three week trip.

reviews.title: Mixed Feelings
reviews.text: We stayed one night during our month visit to S. India. We were warmly greeted by our charming host and owner (a retired medical man) who showed us to our spacious rooms. The property is large and beautifully constructed with much teak in evidence. The garden grounds and estate beyond are all well tended and most attractive. With this being a 'home stay' we had thought we were going to join in with the family for their meals - however the guests had their own dining room, the food was placed on the table and the contents explained by the lady of the house. We then ate while the doctor stood behind us. Frankly we felt rather uncomfortable - we would have liked to have eaten with the family - having one of them standing over us made us feel awkward. Maybe this is the custom in India. But don't get me wrong - our host was most attentive, very cultured and most interesting to talk to. The following morning, before departing, we had a tour of the estate which was most informative and well worth the time. Our driver was delighted with his accommodation and food which he shared with another driver. If we go to India again we'll try another homestay or two - I didn't have the feeling I had stayed with a family - more like being in a hotel with an attentive house manager. Sorry, but there you are.

reviews.title: EXPERIENCING PLANTATION LIFE AND KERALAN CUISINE
reviews.text: We only stayed for a few days but it felt as though we were part of the family, meal times were a real treat with a chance to experience genuine Keralan cuisine. Our trip to nearby Siruvani Dam was a highlight of the holiday with a sighting of a herd of elephants in the hills where were completely alone. Enjoy a relaxing stay in a beautiful setting.

reviews.title: A nice stay
reviews.text: When we arrived at this Holiday Inn Express in Culican we checked into the reception and they not only were friendly but they had my reservation on hand and because we arrived in the morning we made a special request if we can get breakfast for two (even if it did cost us some money) plus also for us to get several "upgrades" in which we did. The bedding was nice. The pillows were soft. The bathroom had nice running hot wáter. I would give this two thumbs up.

reviews.title: Clean and new
reviews.text: The hotel is new with big rooms. The hotel won't honor the reservation, something typical in Culiacan. I reserved a suite but was occupied when I arrived to the hotel..didn't like it but I'm used to it.....don't bother reserving a suite... The hotel is near (walking distance) to a restaurant and bakery...also they have complementary shuttle to the airport. I found some condoms at my room, like 10....thank god they weren't used codoms.

reviews.title: Easy to find.
reviews.text: The room was OK but they left a lot to be desired. There was no fridge, no microwave, no coffee as one would expect in a IHG hotel. The hotel is pretty new so maybe that alcove with electrical plugs will have a coffee pot, a microwave etc. next time. I probably will not find out. The complimentary breakfast was excellent. A good variety and good service. We crossed the street to a fast food that was terrible for dinner.

reviews.title: Perfect for a business trip
reviews.text: This hotel is not far from downtown but is in an area where three are not many options regarding restaurants and entertainment. Nice rooms, which lack a fridge and a microwave, just a coffee maker, but pretty neat and clean. This hotel has no pool, and the exercise room is small but will help you with your daily workout routine. Service is excellent; all employees will give you their best effort to make you have the best of your stay. Breakfast is delicious, freshly prepared with Mexican and standard American options as well. For lunch, there is a restaurant next door named La 20, not a fancy place, but a trendy seafood place which corroborates that you should go where locals go, serving excellent, inexpensive, fresh seafood.

reviews.title: Clean and good service
reviews.text: Good quick and clean rooms and bathrooms. Close to highway and safe at 1 am I heard someone try to put their key card in our door then knock by the time I got up to look out the peep hole no one was there. Called downstate concierge and they sent security up right away. Very pleased with service.

reviews.title: Wonderful Stay
reviews.text: The hotel is located at the outer part of the City but considering the traffic is not bad. It is just next to the Bus Terminal. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The room side is big considering Express and well equipped. The internet was perfect and so was the breakfast selection. The parking space is ample and though the hotel doesn't have a restaurant but just across the road in Panama great Sinaloan cusine. Enjoyed the stay and good resting after business.

reviews.title: Very nice hotel with a full breakfast included!
reviews.text: This hotel is perfect for a quick business or family trip. The rooms feel new and are a very good size. The breakfast buffet included with the room is perfect with plenty of hot and cold options plus very friendly staff.

reviews.title: New building....$67 usd...great morning breakfast...secure parking
reviews.text: This was my first stop in Culiacan. I usually zoom by on my way to Mazatlan or Los Mochis. I will be stopping here from now on. A great town with nice facilities. Even though this town is the center for the Sinaloa drug cartel it has a nice feel to it. There is security everywhere so you don't have a wary feeling as you move around. We stayed at the new Holiday Inn Express and were very happy with our room. This room was as nice as our room at the Matilda in San Miguel de Allenda which was $600 a night.

reviews.title: Great value for money
reviews.text: The hotel is new, the staff is friendly and the bed is super comfy. It is still has that new smell. Decor is pleasing. Totally get your money's worth. Thumbs up. The only drawback is its location. It is far from good places to eat.

reviews.title: Avoid this place, you might get mugged
reviews.text: I chose this hotel because in the past I had good experiences at other properties BUT this time has different... At 1am (yes your read right) I got a call for the front desk telling me that "the comandante from Culiacán" was calling. To make the story short this person ("the comandante from Culiacán") had all the info you leave when check in and he asked me to leave the hotel at 2am in the morning because there was an "operative" Fortunately I made a mistake when I was going down to the reception and realized that nothing was happened... immediately I went back to my room and left a few hours later. People for this hotel is colluded with "the comandante" and they are going to give away your name and data... So don't stay at this place, others you might get mugged or something worts might happen

reviews.title: very good place to stay , friendly and easy accessable
reviews.text: a very good and well placed hotel safe , secure and well priced good , clean sized room with good amenities and appliances provided polite staff day or night ( and right across the street from Panama resturant :) hope to revisit soon

reviews.title: Good business hotel
reviews.text: I stayed here for three nights during a recent business trip to Culiacan. I found the holiday Inn to be a comfortable, modern, and friendly hotel, with good parking. I recommend the seafood restaurant next door. The breakfast was pretty good. The gym could be a bit bigger but it will do in a pinch. Culiacan is a friendly city.

reviews.title: Great stay, value and service
reviews.text: Stayd here just a view days, but it the service, quality and price that you expect from a holiday Inn express. Breakfast included (you can start having breakfast at 06:00) Room was clean and spacious enough. Would definitely Como back again if I am in town! Just a quick tip, if you want to visit downtown or eat out you have to take a cab, the only place in walking distance is Panama.

reviews.title: perfect for bussiness
reviews.text: straight forward clean rooms as expected. Great breakfast service and if you want more options accross the street from a great restaurant and around the corner of a small bar. Very convenient in everyway.

reviews.title: Clean, nice, location
reviews.text: Had to get some work done near by and this hotel was a great option Clean room and barhroom, good service and very good restaurant across the street Hotel has complimentary breakfast and with a good variety of choices Only stayed for one night, but definitely would come back

reviews.title: Consistently Very Good with Great Breakfasts
reviews.text: Recently stayed in the HEI Culiacan and was not disappointed. Hotel is nicely appointed; has a helpful staff; very clean; and has great breakfasts. It's located off of one of the major arteries in Culiacan. I would recommend leaving your car at the hotel parking lot and take a taxi; they're very inexpensive. Culiacan is in the middle of a major street renovation now and driving is a definite challenge. If you want a great, personal, reasonable taxi driver, I highly recommend "Carlos" Unit 29 with Radio Taxi at 667-3051510.

reviews.title: For a relaxing moment in a luxury place
reviews.text: This relatively small hotel is on the edge of a larger family resort, yet it seems that it catered mostly to adults. Our sunset view room was very large, spotless and luxuriously appointed, one of the best ones in which we have ever stayed. The open air infinity pool was very quiet with a great view, yet, at the end of July, it was too hot to swim laps. The thalasso pool with its numerous strong jets to massage every muscle was wonderful and put you in a relaxed mood. The breakfast buffet, with its mix of Japanese and western food was excellent. The afternoon tea and afternoon end Champagne moments were wonderful additions. The service was surpassing the already high Japanese standards; most staff spoke English, from a limited to a perfectly fluent level - it was not a limit, ever. There are numerous restaurants to choose from in the resort, but the ones at the larger resort are more catered for families. The prices are rather high, and the food is less of a price:quality value than the room at the Busena Terrace Club is. What is a nice addition is the quietness of the area and the lack of the Muzak that is so ubiquitous in American hotels and resorts. A wonderful place to relax in luxury for a couple...

reviews.title: Not worth the price - disappointing
reviews.text: The facility was nice enough, being on the beach. The rooms were quite outdated and the "thalasso spa" was such a disappointment. Basically just a glorified jacuzzi. The dining options are quite lame for a resort this expensive, and even if you book at the Terrace Club you have to go to the main resort (which is wayyyy too crowded) for a decent breakfast. The restaurant at the Terrace Club itself is pretty bad and bland. The hotel also has very arbitrary and annoying rules - you can't wear a robe around (it's a beach resort?!), you must give your phone to the front desk, can't take pictures around the pool, can't swim at the beach... Overall found the facilities a disappointment and the service very poor. Save yourself the money and go stay at the Ritz two minutes from here, where it's actually the service and ambiance you're paying for!

reviews.title: Beautiful Setting on Nago Bay
reviews.text: The location is great. The Terrace Club is on Nago Bay on a private cove. The property is only about 5 years old and is very well maintained. The front desk staff was amazing. From check-in, to arranging meals, transportation and activities they were always eager to help. Our ocean front room was very large. Equivalent of a king sized bed (two twin+ beds pushed together), full seating area with sofa and chairs, mini-fridge, nespresso coffee maker and dining counter. Large balcony with a day bed and a table and chairs. Double sliding doors which let you enjoy a sense of indoor/outdoor living. Great bathroom layout. A moveable wall can be opened, so you can see the view from the bathtub or closed for privacy. Double vanity, separate water closet and nice shower. Nice outdoor pool area though it closes early except in the summer (6pm). The spa has a separate Thalasso Pool which is open later, but that is really not for recreation. There is a nice small workout area with a few stationary bikes, two treadmills and a small studio for yoga, etc. Book treatments such as massages and facials in advance. We were not able to book all the treatments we wanted during our stay due to no availability. That was a disappointment and surprising as the hotel did not seem full. The therapist we had for facials was very good, and the private treatment room was very nice. The larger sister property next door, The Busena Terrace, is a family friendly resort with multiple pools and restaurants. They also have a nice public swimming beach and various water activities. You can use the facilities at both properties, and they have complimentary golf cart service if you need a ride. Breakfast was included. They also have complimentary tea and desserts in the afternoon and a happy hour from 5-7 with free wine, Champagne and snacks. While we enjoyed our stay, we have come to expect a few more nice touches from a resort with these prices. While nice, we have had more memorable stays in Indonesia and Thailand. That's why I could not give it 5 starts.

reviews.title: A most relaxing and recharging experience
reviews.text: Spent 4 nights at the resort. All aspects of resort were of a high standard. The food was excellent. Complimentary breakfast, afternoon tea and evening drinks all commendable. Lovely views from public spaces and room. Spacious, comfortable and quiet guestroom. Thalasso treatment was fun and effective. The only downside is that the beaches adjoining the hotel are quite littered from rubbishh washed up from the ocean.

reviews.title: Ultimate relaxation and paradise
reviews.text: Absolutely echo the reviews about The Terrace Club from all those who have commented on its EXEMPLARY service. It made our Honeymoon worthwhile from start to finish - so much so, that we extended our stay by a few days! If you can handle the 90 mins or so to get here from Naha Airport, then definitely stay here. It definitely is the jewel in this series of hotels: adult only, unlimited use of the thalassotherapy pool, food prepared with wellness in mind using locally sourced produce, peace and quiet, ocean views, spacious Club Rooms, golf buggy to take you around the resort, butler service, turn-down service with weather report for the next day left on the bed.. HEAVEN. Getting here... The Hotel has a shuttle bus that goes between its hotels free of charge. This needs to be booked in advance, so if you land at Naha Airport, easiest would be to take a taxi to the Naha Terrace (a sister hotel), which is about 20 minutes away, then take the free shuttle bus to The Terrace Club - make sure you book. You can also take an Airport Limousine Bus, which stops at the neighbouring Busena Terrace Hotel, but note that it stops running around 4:30pm/5pm from the Airport, so if your flight gets in later (like ours did) and you haven't booked a shuttle from the Naha Terrace, you're at the mercy of a long distance taxi, which was around 14,000 Yen (approx. £80) one way (!). Our stay... Every single member of the team at The Terrace Club and all the restaurants across the resort made our time special in Okinawa. They remembered what we liked to eat, where to buy things, where we'd like to sit, helped with sunburn creams and first aid (!!), nothing was too much to ask for, because they would find a way to make it happen, despite the language barrier. Our Club Room facing the Ocean was worth every single penny, with stunning colours and views, and wonderful weather we were blessed with whilst there. A private balcony where we could sit and catch some sun, read and take in the ocean air. Food and Drink... I must emphasise the kindness and care shown by ALL staff at the hotel in relation to my food intolerance (gluten). Everyone was absolutely brilliant. I was given special cookies during the Afternoon Tea to accommodate - without even asking! - and staff members remembered my dietary issues throughout the stay. Our dining experience at the Japanese restaurant at the neighbouring Busena Terrace Hotel was made all the more personal when the restaurant actually RE-CREATED AN ENTIRE MENU just to accommodate my gluten intolerance and gave us menus printed on beautiful paper to take with us. The chef at the Teppenyaki restaurant and the Italian restaurant were also equally informative and helpful about gluten free options on the menu and what could be done gluten free. All were very good dining experiences. We loved the food options at La Tida, which was a buffet of western and Japanese cuisine.. Buffet with anything and everything going! The dessert counter would make anyone smile just looking at it!! Things to do... If you have time - perhaps on a rainy afternoon - the Craft store at the resort runs a Shisa making and painting workshop. We did this and the lady in the store (Tsuboi) is so lovely!! We really enjoyed the workshop and she made it all the more enjoyable for us with her encouragement and descriptions of our 'masterpieces' :D Awesome staff.... There are so many staff members who made our stay at The Terrace Club enjoyable. We wish we could name them all. We must mention, Natsuko, one of the English speaking staff members, who was kind enough to help us with all sorts during our stay and leave us a beautiful memento of our honeymoon in our room (a framed photo of us) along with a rose and card. We were (and still are!) so touched by this. The gentleman who drove us from The Terrace Club to the Busena Terrace at the end of our stay to catch the Airport Bus was kind enough to express farewell wishes in English, which we could tell he very much wanted to say. ~~ We left Okinawa with heavy hearts, full of love and adoration for everything about our stay at The Terrace Club. Okinawa will always hold a special place in our hearts. If you want relaxation, this is the place to come.

reviews.title: Fabulous resort
reviews.text: Wonderful staff who strive to privide excellent service. Enough staff speak English to make your stay comfortable. Fabulous breakfast or lunch at adjacent sister hotel only a short walk away. Shuttle also available. Happy hour at 5 PM and afternoon tea at 2 pm with free drinks and snacks. The Thalasso spa pool is fabulous. Lovely beach but swimming in ocean & outdoor pools not permitted until April 1st. Lots to do in the surrounding area.

reviews.title: Excellent service !
reviews.text: I stayed there for the 2nd time. Service is always excellent. Staff is always very helpful and customer centric. Rooms are large, cleaned and very comfortable. Food is tasty and closed to fine ‘cuisine’. Nice pool and spa. This is a very good place to relax, a real five star!

reviews.title: One of the best hotel ever
reviews.text: This hotel is the perfect romantic vacation spot. Great service with excellent facilities. Champagne lounge and free thalasso facilities were a great plus for a day with bad weather. The hotel is located on a private peninsula shared with its sister establishment the Busena Terrace. The terrace Club is secluded and very quiet

reviews.title: Unique experience~!
reviews.text: Stayed for 2 nights in early July. Brilliant well furnished ocean view spacious room. Great hospitality. All staffs are sincere, attentive, and helpful. They even manage to help us to make last minute dinner reservation at a nice teppanyaki restuarant. My resort package allowed us to have breakfast at either The Terrace Club at Busena or The Busena Terrace. Also grant access to all facility at The Busena Terrace which is a few minutes transport on golf-cart. Well maintain facility. Highly private beach and a unique spa pool to refresh your body. Quality hotel guests that respect the public space and enjoy the peaceful and quiet environment (No cellphone ringing or iPad video playing where you may find in other family resort). Free afternoon tea mini buffet and free-flow drinks happy hour. We never feel bored even if we spend the whole day within the resort. Best suited for couples and small group of friends (no child under 13 served in this property). The Busena Terrace is better fit for family group. The only shortcoming is that the curtain is relatively thin to block the sunlight that wakes me up before 6am. Well, I am a light-sleeper anyway. Very refreshing and relax stay. We could have spend another night with no regret. Memorbale vacation with every penny well spent . Job well done by the Terrace Hotel group. Thank you~!

reviews.title: Our vacation in okinawa
reviews.text: People are friendly, that is it... hotel is like a ghost town. I see the staff working but what are they doing?Hotel is little dirty, food is terrible. Badest hotel we have had in years... the hotel is now 5 years old but it looks like a hotel from the early nineties. It is not allowed to wear swimming gear if you go to toilet at the pool. Have to wear a robe. If you have tattoos you should lie in your shirt at the pool. If you smoke it is not allowed to smoke outside... if you have a headache they do not help you? Welcome to the terrace club!!! 😫

reviews.title: Bubble and blue sea
reviews.text: Great room, on a lovely peninsula. A range of pools and beaches in the complex. Free champagne at sunset was a welcome surprise. Disappointing that no hotel restaurant would take a booking on the same day and no one alerted us to the fact. That inconveninece forced us to explore the area which turned out to be a stroke luck.

reviews.title: Very relaxed stay
reviews.text: We stayed 2 nights in June. The room was perfect to stay 2 people; very convenient and well furnished. Overall services are great, and the place was very quite and relax. We would like to come again!

reviews.title: Excellent services, great for laid-back...
reviews.text: Stayed 2 nights in 10/6-12/6, room no.3707 which is sunset view deluxe, view is fantastic, room is spacious and clean, complimentary water was good enough...The hotel itself like a serviced apartment, luxury, quiet and excellent services for our stayed, of course the room price was high...The restaurant was awesome for dinner and particular healthy breakfast, service and taste more better than their sister hotel which is near by next...I think only drawback was the room was a bit dated, the toilet seat flush by yourself, not electrical, and no master control on the bedside, floor lamp also need to switch by yourself...The private beach's view was great but not for swimming, and the water spa "Thalasso" is a bit ostentatious...but overall, great hotel and better for laid-back !

reviews.title: Great place to spend the winter
reviews.text: The Terrace Club Wellness Resort at Busena This is an upscale facility, one of the Terrace properties, and adjacent to The Busena Terrace Beach Resort, but is a separate building and facility. It has many very nice amenities that add to the enjoyment of the stay. Our 5th floor room had a beautiful view of Nago Bay through four 3' wide by 8' high windows that open to our private terrace. The open studio-style room is large and comfortable, with Western style beds, chairs, ottoman, coffee table and sofa. The floor is hardwood and tile, with an area rug in the sitting area. We had two double beds with nightstand and lamps on each side. A large flat screen TV and DVD player with remote are provided. The shower and toilet are in separate rooms with their own doors. The large tub is between the bedroom and 2-sink lavatory. It can be open to both sides, or sliding doors can separate it from the bedroom. Unusual for Japan, the shower is separate from the tub, and water cannot be allowed to overflow. There are many toiletries provided: shampoo, conditioner, lotion, razors, toothbrushes and toothpaste, Q-tips, shower caps, soaps, bath salts and more. Terry Cloth robes, nice slippers and comfortable cotton pajamas, as well as a hooded cotton jacket to wear to the spa or pool are in the closet. The closet is large, with lots of drawers for clothes, which makes it convenient for longer stays. Free WiFi and LAN will connect you with the internet. Our stay included breakfast or lunch. You can choose daily whether to have breakfast in the Club dining room, or buffet lunch at the La Tida restaurant at the Busena Terrace Beach Resort (a short walk up the road, quick shuttle ride, or walk along the beach). Either meal service is awesome, so many selections it's difficult not to overeat. The breakfast emphasis is on a healthy diet, but taste is not sacrificed. There are many different breakfast foods available at the buffet: granola and other dry cereals, with many different toppings, such as raisins, cranberries, mango, prunes, yogurt, aloe jelly cubes, sliced almonds, pumpkin seeds, etc.; then a whole table of Japanese breakfast foods, including mozuku seaweed (not readily available outside Okinawa) buckwheat soba, and all the usual toppings; a bread table with various pastries, breads, rolls, plus jams. Honey is dispensed from a honeycomb. A salad table, with greens and multiple salad condiments and dressings; a fruit table with many freshly-cut fruits (my favorite was pineapple); an orange squeezer makes orange fresh juice while you wait. A daily smoothie is always healthy and (usually) tasty. In addition to the extensive buffet of health-oriented foods, an egg dish is chosen from a menu of six varieties - all are interesting and delicious, but I usually choose "Today's Special". One great feature of the Club is the Thalasso therapy facility featuring a warm salt-water massage course. There are multiple stations, about 14, with strong jets of water that massage different parts of the body from the feet to the shoulders. Some stations are hot, some warm, and one is cold. The one that massages your feet soles is my favorite. After spending a half-hour or more, you move to the steam and/or dry sauna. After that, there is a unique cooling off room where you can doze as you relax in a dark room with "healthy" air. We took the introductory 90 minute lesson, and have enjoyed the facility daily. The staff is universally polite, respectful and helpful, it is a pleasure to interact with them. It's a little strange having everyone greet you with a smile and a bow, and another bow or two as you walk away. And after a day or two, they know your preferences for breakfast, coffee and evening drink. This is a welcome characteristic that sets the Terrace Club apart from many other hotels, although politeness and respect seem to be endemic to Okinawa. Two other features deserve mention: Tea Time, 2-4 pm with coffee, tea, and a selection of light snacks; and Cocktail Time 5-7 pm, with draft Chatan Harbor beer, wine, cocktails and a selection of light snacks, including cheeses, fruit, nuts and desserts. Both are presented in the Library/Bar. They were included in our program, and after a big breakfast or lunch, can easily tide you over until the next day. After Cocktail Time, a pianist plays relaxing jazzy music 6:30 to 7 and 7:30 to 8. The bar stays open until late. If you want a dinner, the Fine Dining room serves a selection of entrees and set courses with a French emphasis that will leave you satisfied. There are also a Chinese restaurant, an Italian restaurant, and several speciality restaurants at the Busena Terrace Beach Resort, such as a Japanese and the La Ti Da buffet. The concierge can make reservations for you. More information is available at their website, and a promotional video is available.

reviews.title: Best Birthday Ever
reviews.text: Long story short, this place is awesome. Pros: Awesome customer service Beautiful decor, timely service, beautiful property, food (especially breakfast at Cafe Terrace), Cottage accommodations (spend the extra $$--it's worth it with the outdoor shower), activities on site, reasonably priced, everything in walking distance, awesome customer service, awesome customer service, feeling as if you got great value for what you spent. Cons: bugs native to Okinawa being on site (I have a phobia so not so great for me), having to go home Also note that the tattoo policy (covering up) is strictly enforced. I have one on my shoulder blade and forgot for a split second as I was on the beach and I wanted to get in the water. A lifeguard was pretty quick to remind me of true policy. Not a deal breaker by any means but something to be aware of

reviews.title: An Excellent Stay
reviews.text: The Terrace Club at Busena is a small and exclusive part of the larger Busena Terrace Beach Resort. Staying in the Club section of Resort provides you with access all facilities in the Resort, not just the Club. It is expensive but in this case you get what you pay for: a very large well-proportioned room with everything you would expect in a 5-star resort. Staff are friendly and very helpful. Breakfast, afternoon tea, and happy hour complete with French Champagne is included. There is also a very well-stocked resort convenience store located the next to the Club which frees you from depending on the minibar for supplies. Much appreciated. In my mind, the most outstanding feature of the Club is the Thalasso Pool. It is essentially a very large Jacuzzi or rather a very series of interconnected Jacuzzi pools with differing temperatures and water pressure pressures. If you progress through these pools in a particular order the effect is supposed to be therapeutic. It may be, all I know is we found it to be very enjoyable. The resort itself has an excellent swimming beach and a large number of restaurants and shops to choose from. Highly recommended if you want a relaxing stay in an upmarket beach resort without leaving Japan. One thing to remember, the Club over 60 km from the Naha Airport. Going by taxi will cost just under 20,000 yen. If you want to save money take the bus. There is a regularly scheduled resort bus service to the Club and other resorts in the area. Much cheaper and just as quick.

reviews.title: Utterly disappointed
reviews.text: I paid a whopping price for this supposed-to-be a most luxurious resort hotel in Okinawa, but was sheerly disappointed with this place. Three reasons for my disappointment: 1. Beaches and oceans are average, not spectacular 2. Hotel architecture, lobby and lounges are too ordinary, bland Japanese buildings. 3. Restaurants' foods and services are not that great. Horrible services and foods at the fake Italian restaurant.

reviews.title: Typhoon preparedness excellent
reviews.text: We stayed during Typhoon Goni. Watching the efficient preparations for the oncoming storm was fascinating. All done with the calmness and efficiency of a location used to dealing with these types of weather. However, staff remained on duty, were kind and courteous and helpful. The hotel has a lovely balcony view of the bay and overlooks its private beach. The rooms are spacious with open bathrooms (that have sliding doors to render them private). Good dressing area. Tons of facilities as the hotel is part of a larger complex with two other buildings (this one does not accept young children). The Thalassotherapy pool is fantastic. So much so we used it several times - even during the typhoon! Best massages ever...

reviews.title: Overall Excellent Service
reviews.text: We stayed 6 nights at this hotel and both my husband and i received very welcoming service from start to end. All the staff we met spoke English - in some areas like Spa some staff may have limited english speaking ability but then we did not really use it but still did not limit our enjoyment. The room was large with good views and every day anything items that was used whether soap, napkin, water or anything it was replaced. Overall cleanliness and servicing of the rooms were very high. The staff we found overall very helpful. As the breakfast is a healthy option we were informed we can also go to the sister hotel next door for a larger buffet with greater choice if we wanted. We did one day but we found the breakfast at the Terrace club had all the range of food we wanted to eat and the staff was always welcoming and attentive. The reception staff i thought were superb - there was several ladies that we would greet on our return from the day and their welcoming smile and welcome back made is so welcoming. They would recommend local restaurants for us to try and book for us. One day one local restaurant was not answering the phone (it was around 7pm so i assumed they were busy) so we were equipped with 3 restaurant options in case this one did not have a table. On arrival the lady at restaurant knew who i was as reception continued to call and booked the last table for us! They even keyed in the locations on our GPS on most days and ensured we knew where we were going each day in case we needed some help. The price is quite high for this hotel but i think on reflection, the service we received and the standard of service we received actually reflected this small luxury hotel status. We enjoyed our stay very much and i think it was due to the level of service and attention we received this that made the overall stay memorable and enjoyable.

reviews.title: A Haven !!!
reviews.text: A recommendation from a friend. Amazing ocean view, a must try Thalasso pool, and the never failed- Japanese hospitality. The staff was extremely attentive only wish most of them had better ability of speaking English. Ms.Kinjo and Ms.Takatani were absolutely a huge assets of Busena. Not only they speak English well and being helpful, their kind attention of offering all in best it could be, it simply was heavenly !!! Dear boss at Busena, Ms. Takatani and Ms. Kinjo both deserve a promotion !!! I'll definitely go back.

reviews.title: Amazing hospitality, room, and service!
reviews.text: We stayed here only for one night for my husband's birthday. We were blown away by the hotel. Our room was beautiful and spacious. The cocktail hour had a huge selection of drinks and snacks for free and we enjoyed the piano player. We dined at Chula-la, the Italian restaurant, and it was delicious. The entire staff was hospitable and we felt like royalty, not to mention they all spoke wonderful English. I will recommend this place to anyone looking for a nice place to stay in Okinawa.

reviews.title: A wonderful conclusion of our Honeymoon
reviews.text: Stayed there from April 10th to 15th 2016. Despite the weather not always playing along we had an awesome stay. The staff was very professional, friendly and helpful, especially in the light of us not speaking more than 5 words of Japanese. What amazed us most was that they always knew who we were, without ever asking for the room number or a valet slip. The restaurants and bars on the resort were great as far as we tried them. There are also a few places within walking distance at nearby Kise. The spa and pool facilities are clean and very enjoyable. I recommend to rent a car at Naha Airport, in order to get around. There are a few activities nearby, but if you want to go explore it's advisable to have your own wheels. The driving style on Okinawa I found very relaxed. If it weren't so far for us to travel there, we'd make this our annual R&R destination.

reviews.title: Extremely terrible service and discrimination
reviews.text: It is supposed to be a private club with excellent and exclusive service, we came here for our wedding and expected much more than what we experienced. - The staff here speak poor English and treat foreigners with poor attitude, you can feel a huge service difference from them to local vs foreigners , even in front of your face, if you are not Japanese, you would be discriminated and treated with a poor attitude all the time during your stay - the hotel room is spacious but it is ridiculous that you can’t even invite your guest to the room even for a short 10mins visit. It was our wedding trip n we mentioned at the beginning of our booking, there r two of our friends who would like to have a short catch up with us but were blocked and banned at the entrance. Despite the fact that we were there to pick them up and it was a windy rainy night. - the food was just soso and the spa service is highly overpriced, you can have a much more professional and luxury service in anywhere in the city, at a half price of this All in all, if you r expecting a 5star service, you will be highly disappointed. If you are not a Japanese, you would only be seeing many ugly expressions on their faces every day. If you have having some special events or occasions, don’t choose this hotel. They have too many restrictions and you won’t like the discussions with them. There are many more better choices which charge more reasonable than this! Even a 3star does better than them ( to foreigners maybe)

reviews.title: Odd place
reviews.text: We stayed in an apartment. Things are basic and old, which was fine, but oddly arranged and somewhat disfunctional. The owners try hard I think, but their efforts are hit and miss. The storm door did not close unless you hefted up the handle, which could easily be fixed by aligning it correctly. We were told that Internet was intermittent. It was non existent unless one went outside to the east of the 'farmhouse'. This could be easily remedied. There is no office. The owners seem to live in one of the cottages behind a house, and perhaps a tent or 2 set up on the far side of the property. It's an odd place with toddlers outside mostly unsupervised. There was no interaction or communication with the owners/management except by an older, somewhat weird, gentleman who came to chat us up a few times. The backyard area is a mess with odd green camo barriers set up, kids toys, and some old barbecues which didn't appear serviceable. There was also a bonfire area filled with construction debris. This backyard goes into the woods and could be a lovely place. A guide to tv stations would be helpful as well as some information about the area. There was a bundled stack of old tourist information newspapers on the porch of the 'farmhouse' which looked as if they had been there for months. There were no coathangers in the closet. Was told we would get an email the day before arrival with check in info but it came the afternoon of our arrival, which was problematic for other guests who arrived at night, with no cell service, and were clueless as to what to do. Would not stay here again.

reviews.title: Great value, charming cottages
reviews.text: We enjoyed our 3-night stay at the Sunset Motel in August. We didn't really expect anything considering it was the high season and the rates were surprisingly reasonable. We were therefore delighted to find that the cottages were clean and nice, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The location is removed from the noisy tourist locations without being too far away for convenience. Those who want to be in the middle of it all will want to look elsewhere, but for those who want to get away from the crowds, it's a great choice. And there is in fact a beautiful sunset! We would absolutely choose this spot again on a future visit. Only drawback was that the internet was spotty at best, but we were able to use it in the reception for free.

reviews.title: Charming
reviews.text: We stopped at Twin Hill Cottages on our way home from Canada. We stayed in the Jayden Xander. The cottages are charming and cute. Everything is clean and it was nice for my daughter and her friend to have their own room. As I write this I am having a cup of the complimentary coffee, enjoying a glorious Maine morning on the front porch.

reviews.title: We really enjoyed our stay
reviews.text: We spent a night here and found the cottages charming, clean, and private. The bedding was a little faded, but we really enjoyed our stay. The bed was comfortable and the pillows were nice. The shower was great, but you need to run the water a while to get it hot. Cottages near the end have trouble getting wifi so we didn't have data, but that could be an easy fix if they add a repeater.

reviews.title: Quirky but very clean, knowledgeable owner!
reviews.text: We stayed two nights in the yellow cabin (no. 1), which is one of the larger units and contains two separate bedrooms. The decor is nothing less than quirky, but the beds and bathroom (toilet, sink, bathtub/shower) were very clean and neat. The shower had AMAZING water pressure! The a/c units in each of the bedrooms were relatively quiet; we did not hear any noise from Route 1 which is very closeby. The beds and pillows were comfy, all of them were queen-sized, which was a delight for our two children who were traveling with us and were tired of sharing a bed. They were also happy that there was a second television in their room. All in all, we felt like we were staying at a friend's house, not at a hotel. The owner Roland was very nice and knowledgeable, giving us valuable tips about activities and places to eat (Helen's and Sylvia's Café). This was a very pleasant surprise; thanks to the Maine Travel Maven and her article "Cheap Sleeps: Budget lodging near Bar Harbor and Acadia National Park, Maine".

reviews.title: Basic and good value
reviews.text: The cottages are basic but quite spacious compared to other motels I've stayed in, especially the bathroom. The cottage was clean and comfortable enough for one night but it was a shame that there wasn't a proper hairdryer and the wifi didn't work, think we were too far away from the router (purple cottage). Location was ok, close enough to centre of Ellsworth, about a 15 minute drive, but a bit further to Acadia and Bar Harbour. Perfect for one night though next time would probably stay closer to Acadia.

reviews.title: Very nice, clean and affordable place. Courteous staff. Strongly recommend.
reviews.text: Just one word, awesome!!. Convenient location. Good amenities. Friendly staff. Clean and comfortable. We stayed there for two nights. The beds might be a little small if you are over 6 ft. But overall great value for the money you pay.

reviews.title: The price was right
reviews.text: We were looking for a clean, affordable motel near Bar Harbor ME. I found this one on TripAdvisor. The owner said he would give us more restaurant information after we paid him for our room. We stayed in room 5, which he said was an upgrade, and we appreciated the kitchenette. However, there were no dishes pans, or anything to use in the kitchenette. I had some things with me so we were fine, but I would rather have cooked eggs in a pan than the microwave. The room was fairly clean, but I needed to wipe the fridge and clean the microwave better before use. I also cleaned the inside of the bathroom door, as there were unknown drips down the door....which is close to the toilet. We stayed two nights and although I wish the hotel would have been closers to Mount Desert island, it worked out well. No ice available that we heard about, no Laundry facility. Despite the negatives, if needed, we would stay there again. The price was right, the bed was clean, and we enjoyed the kitchenette. The bedroom was separate with a door. Could be a positive for some.

reviews.title: Not enjoyable
reviews.text: The young owners were pleasant and attempted to rectify issues, but did not give it their full and professional attention to ensure we were satisfied. We did come in to a very clean and well kept cottage. However, we realized the hot water was not on. I notified the owners who, that evening, changed out the water heater located one unit over and serviced the last 3 cottages. After that we still did not have hot water. The next day they worked on it again assured me it was fixed. when we returned from a day at the National Park, we checked and it came out warm, but never got hot. Within 5 minutes, there was not even warm water. By then it was 10pm, so we went to bed. The next day (departure day) there was still no hot water. We left early in the morning never to return. The very small desk heater did not keep us warm the second day/night since it got down to high 30's after then assured us that the small unit should keep us toasty. They also never fixed the outlet in the bathroom. They seem to work hard and want to succeed, however, they need to address issues quickly and follow up as professionals. The cottage was $115 per night and without hot water or great heat the entire stay it was not worth it.In addition, they advertise a TV, but there is no cable and there were only 4 DVD's to play. All of which were killing/action movies. Just poor amenities with entertainment. The wi-fi hardly every worked, although they did tell us that we get better reception closer to the main building. And, I would not recommend unless they run the facility in a more professional manner.

reviews.title: Interesting...
reviews.text: If you like to drive right up to your little cottage door, then this motel will have some appeal to you. It is clean. It lacks modern amenities, i.e., hair dryer, outlets for chargers, etc. It has a refrigerator, microwave, a TV (did not use), bathroom, bed, desk, AC - window, lamps and a fan - very basic. It is decorated with a personal touch. Unfortunately, due to small quarters, I put some of the items in the drawer, so I would not bump and break - especially from the bathroom shelves. The double bed and pillows are sufficient, but lack comfort. The AC is noisy, but then so it the highway running by motel, so take your pick. The bathroom is small - small shower, especially. Water was hot - good. I just don't know what to say about this place as it was clean and very reasonably priced for the area. I think it is okay for a one night stay for one or two people. The owner checked us in, gave us some advice about Acadia National Park and recommended restaurants in the area, which we appreciated. After that I would say he is a "hands-off" owner - never saw him again. Lobby door was closed and you had to ring a door bell to contact him. Just left the key in the cottage. Interesting. So with all of that being said, if you are looking for a reasonably priced and clean motel only, then you might this motel. When driving north of Ellsworth on Rt. 1, there is a steep hill down and then up, the motel is right at the top at the corner of the appropriately named road - Twin Hill Rd. There is a lit sign on the left, if you are arriving after sunset. In the day time, you absolutely could not miss as the cottages are Easter egg colors. Very noticeable - can't miss. Ask for one away from the highway if possible. Oh, it is non-smoking, but there is a small outside deck with an ashtray, if needed. Internet? Yes, but did not work while we were there. Apparently the purple cottage is too far from the main router or something. Anyway, I wouldn't count on it.

reviews.title: S Small Surprise
reviews.text: Found this motel late in the day when most hotels were full and only $$$ hotel rooms were available. We found a cottage with 2 twin beds for less than half the cost of other places. Room was a cottage with a covered porch. Room was small but adequate for our needs. Bath was spotless with all new fixtures. It is a no frills motel that won't break the bank. Clean and comfortable.

reviews.title: Sweet Ticky tacky cottages
reviews.text: We stayed in the Orange one they really tried to make you comfortable they had a coffee pot left danish for the morning a microwave with popcorn a refrigerator and funny little decorations around the room. Not really my cup of tea but something different that I'll remember.

reviews.title: Cute place, great rates, reasonable doge policy
reviews.text: Clean, cute, nice people running the place. Very reasonable dog policy - $10 charge and please crate the dog if you leave him in the room. My dog and I enjoyed having our own little house with our own door. Only (minor) drawback is the location. Sunset Motel is in the general vicinity of everything, but not close to anything specific, so everything is at least a short drive. However the rates were about half of many other similar places that were closer to town or Acadia. I saved $70 and had to drive 10 minutes for dinner. Not a problem really. ps. Yummy sweet rolls in room for breakfast. I ate them both.

reviews.title: Ok
reviews.text: Had to stay here as I arrived on Columbus weekend holiday period and as a Brit never thought it would be a problem. How wrong was I?? The whole of the region seemed to be sold out from Friday to Sunday. I suppose I was 'lucky' to find this place which looked like an oversized beach hut, found on a UK holiday resort. Irrespective of the price the owner was friendly and helpful and despite his claims of potential week WiFi signal we managed it and we were the second furthest away from his router. The inside was clean and he'd made an effort with snacks, coffee machine, microwave, popcorn and a working TV. Wasn't worth the $95 inc tax but it was holiday season!!

reviews.title: Visit to Acadia National Park in Maine
reviews.text: My wife and I spent a few days exploring Acadia National Park. The Sunset Motel is outside Ellsworth, 25 min. from the island.The distance was not a factor here, the drive was smooth.
