Noise is not a real issue as you are tucked away below the noise levels. You will receive a lovely warm welcome from the owners with plenty of information on bus timetables, things to do and see etc. So handy to visit Cinque Terre, Portofino etc and most places you can get to by ferry in Rapallo. The campsite is well kept, clean toilets and showers, lovely pool, wifi and great pizzeria. Most of all we loved the smiles from the owners and were sad to say Ciao! We will be back! ....

reviews.title: Nice camping
reviews.text: We arrived wet from the French rain. It was a pleasure to be received by very friendly people. Our outwell concorde xl fitted perfectly in the spot we received. A small but clean swimmingpool for thd kids, good pizza & pasta. Enough for some days of holiday before we travel more south. No issues with the noise from traffic nearby. Suppose it's best to stay low in the park.

reviews.title: Superb campsite with excellent hosts
reviews.text: This is an excellent campsite. It is a little far from the main tourist hub of Rapallo (easy to cycle in but probably a 30 min walk) but that is the only minor issue. On arrival we were made to feel very welcome, and they gave a choice of plots. It was very hot whilst when we were staying, so we were glad for the plot in the shade! There is a good atmosphere around the campsite, and everyone is very friendly. They keep it clean and the shower/toilet blocks were always excellently kept. There is a lovely pool, and the onsite restaurant is amazing and you will not find more reasonable food and drink anywhere on the coast!!! A freshly made margherita pizza was only €5 and absolutely delicious. I would recommend getting a plot nearer the entrance of the site - not only are you nearer the facilities but there is a motorway close to the rear of the site which can be noisy. Thank you for an excellent week!

reviews.title: Camping Miraflores
reviews.text: Just got back from a lovely trip to the Italian Riviera, where we stopped at Camping Miraflores. We looked for somewhere else to stay for ages and everything was so over priced for that time of year so we decided to stop at Camping Miraflores.for 100 euros a night. We stopped in a superior mobile home with a friend and 18 month old son. The mobile home was perfect for us, it had air conditioning, kitchen, living room, a shower and all the items you would need to a few days apart from an oven (it had gas hobs). The owners were lovely, always helpful and their English was perfect. The swimming pool was cleaned each morning and closed at night. It had a small playground and you felt safe their. As there isn't many reviews on this site I thought it would be full of Italians, but me met and heard a few English people, The only thing that annoyed us was that their restaurant was only open from 7:30Pm which they told us is normal but it was a pain. We chose to take public transport from Genoa to Rapallo which consisted of a bus (6€), train (€3.30) and another bus (€1.50). It was cheap and pretty smooth apart from the heat. So i would recommend it for anyone on a budget.

reviews.title: Great value and friendly staff
reviews.text: Found this campsite by chance on our first night of a roadtrip around Italy. We stayed 3 nights for 35 Euros per night for 3 adults with a small campervan and large tent. It was 3 Euros extra per night for electricity. The staff spoke perfect English which helped a lot and we could buy boat trip tickets from the reception desk which saved a bit of time at Rapello port. There is a small pool with sunloungers (swimming caps must be worn), a bar/restaurant with free WiFi and a play area for children. The showers only have hot water from 7.30am until 11am, but I never had to queue for a shower. It is located near to a road so there was generally background noise, but it was such good value compared to other campsites that we overlooked that issue.

reviews.title: Perfect location to visit the Tigullio Gulf
reviews.text: The camping is located very close to the highway but there is no problem with the noise. Even if the location is not so beautiful, it is perfect as base camp for the oneday visits to the amazing places in the Tigullio's Gulf. Only 25 minutes by walk or 10 by bus and it is possible to get the train for Camogli, Santa Margherita Ligure, 5 terre, Genova. The managers are very nice and helpfull. We stayed here with the motorhome in December and the services were perfect. A restaurant quite close to the camping is suitable for a good and cheap dinner. In summer time it may be too far from the seaside.

reviews.title: very friendly staff but location could be better
reviews.text: The staff at this camping is very friendly. They help you wherever they can, and at least one staff member is very fluent in many languages, which greatly helps with communication. I disliked the location because it is very close to the motorway entrance, which results in quite some traffic noise, also caused from a nearby truck carpark. If you just sleep there, it's ok, but be prepared for at least some noise. We had a "classic mobile home" for 50 Euro/ night for 2 people. That price is ok, but not particularly cheap. Putting up your tent is much cheaper, if you are on a tight budget. Our mobile home accomodates four, but we found it tight with just the two of us in it. There is a separate kitchen attached in front of the mobile home for your personal use, including a fridge and freezer, a gas cooking unit, and most of the necessary basic kitchen equipment. I would say it has everything you need, but not much on top of that. The private shower/bathroom is inside the mobile home and has a small quantity of hot water available only. Otherwise, you can use the shared showers that have more hot water available. There is an electric heater inside the mobile home for beginning and end of the season that works well (and is needed if cold). There is not much to do at the camping - so if you are looking for some entertainment, you need to go somewhere else. There is a swimming pool (was closed in October). For a fun camping time (tent or mobile home), I'd recommend to go somewhere else. We were just sleeping there for which it is all right. Shop around though, you might find better value for your money.

reviews.title: Perfect little campsite
reviews.text: This is honestly one of the nicest little campsites I have ever been to. I'm in no denial that the showers could to with a little bit of tlc, But the whole atmosphere and staff here easily compensate for this. Firstly we were greeted by an incredibly friendly woman on the reception who kindly gave us a code for free wifi and told us roughly where our pitch was. After this her husband (presumably) led us to our pitch on his moped, despite it being a little bit small it was very quaint and located in a nice place. This campsite is ideal if you would like easy transport into the centre as it is only a 20 min walk away. The restaurant is incredibly cheap and if I'm honest sells probably one of the nicest pizzas I've ever eaten!! (Only €4.50 too). All in all love this campsite it's a little gem!!

reviews.title: Good camping, certainly for a few nights
reviews.text: We stayed at Miraflores two nights. We booked a couple of dives in the Portovino marine park and needed a camping to stay. The reviews I read were not all enthusiastic, but we were quite content. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Our spot had good shade all day. It was small, but what would you expect on a location close to the coast? It was relatively quiet, certainly for an Italian camping. I have to admit that our Italian neighbour was playing 'classic' Italian songs (which are not my favorite......). But they were so friendly, and stopped not too late in the evening. Remarkably I didn't hear much of the highway that actually is located directly next to the camping ground. There is a small swimming pool, sanitair is ok, the little restaurant serves good pizza and the atmosphere is nice. What more do you want?

reviews.title: Quiet, friendly good for relax!
reviews.text: Nice garden area good in a morning seat and have a breakfast with birds!Malika (owner)she look after everybody and always smile!Hope next time got more time to relax,the staff is always smile and help if u need something,hope next time they speak more English!!:)));)))

reviews.title: Lovely place to stay
reviews.text: We went to this place to hire motorbikes as we were staying next door, the owner is a lovely french lady who was very helpful, we liked her so much that we decided to move there (even though we had another night paid at the other place). The room we stayed was really nice, big and comfortable with a very strong fan which was great as it was super hot in Samui. It is so close to the beach, you can reach Lamai Beach within less than a minute. The swimming pool is a plus, really nice and clean. The whole place is lovely and very well looked after, all bushes are trimmed, the grass cut etc. Furthermore there is a social place where people can drink, eat and have a chat, that was really nice. We ended ip staying 3 nights there and hired bikes on all days, Malika helped us with tips of where to go and she gave us a map too. I would definitely recommend the place to friends and if I go back to Samui I will stay there again. Another bonus is that Lamai Beach is amazing, so beautiful with all the rocks. There are also lots of nice places to eat and drink. Because it's not in central Lamai it's quiet, and you can walk to central Lamai in less than 10 minutes.

reviews.title: Great value
reviews.text: We booked a fan bungalow with cold shower. To my delight we had a hot shower which was a bonus. The bungalow was clean and comfortable. It had a nice little alcove to store your luggage so it felt quite spacious. The bungalow was well sealed with screens so there were no insects creeping in. It's very close to the beach and a short walk to the main street, however we rented a scooter from reception so this wasn't a problem. The staff and owner, Maria, we're friendly and helpful and really made you feel at home. I thought this was excellent value for money and would stay here again.

reviews.title: Close to the beautiful beach
reviews.text: The resort looks well kept. There is different types of accommodation. We had a fan room with our own bathroom and hot shower. The rooms are okay for the job of sleeping but not the cleanest in the world. But we only stayed one night so we were happy. Short walk around the corner to shops and straight down to the beach. Walk a bit further down to get to the nicer sand and beach area.

reviews.title: Green Canyon-PARADISE!
reviews.text: we were really lucky because we choose Green Canyon .it is the most nicest place,which i have ever seen.if you have an image of Thailand like a small world,another world,like a small paradise on the earth,Green Canyon is right to stay.here you cam feel soul of thailnad,unbelievable beauty,feel nature!hammocks beetween wild mango-is a dream.We photed this place a lot.Marri is a bos.she is from France.and i think she created ideal place on busy Samui.the thing is not about only atmosphere and territory,staff here is best too!...i f you want have a party it is better to go to Chaveng.but this place cost this.night life is just night life...but this place is only one^)grandmother and grandfather is really close to bungalos go many yimes there and in differnt time!it is magic.thanks to Mari a lot ,thanks a lot to the charmest french people!Samui won't be so bright witout this place and people!all my best!!!

reviews.title: 3.5 Stars
reviews.text: I wish I could give this place 3 1/2 stars. The owner is very nice and welcoming and the reception and garden are nice. Less than a 5 min walk to Lamai Beach. However, the standard room was very stark and the walls were a bit stained. It seemed like bugs could get in through the bathroom window so we kept that door closed. It's also a bit far from everything, but that may be a good thing for some. Transport on the island is a bit expensive, so if you're looking for a scene of any sort, better to stay at Chaweng Beach. Otherwise decent, cheap place.

reviews.title: Friendly staff with great location
reviews.text: Stayed here for a few nights,was made very welcome by the Thai staff who spoke English and the lovely French woman (owner maybe).stayed in a fan bungalow which was fine,wasn't too hot,no creepy crawlies got in like other places that I've stayed at around Thailand.Had a refrigerator with free waters on arrival.had the American breakfast which nice.just off Lamai beach and a few restaurants market etc nearby,nightlife was a 10min walk was a bit dodgy with no footpaths and motorbikes whizzing everywhere.would definitely stay again.

reviews.title: Excellent budget bungalows
reviews.text: Perfect rooms if you own a budget. Maria lovely owner friendly and helpful and friendly Thai staff. Over all perfect excess to shops and beach within minutes. Cheap scooter rental aswell with no hassle or questions. And when ever we needed a taxi Maria always sorted it out with any hesitation.

reviews.title: Cute!
reviews.text: Lovely comfortable room with lots of facilities to use: kettle, fridge, crockery and utensils, plus others. Free wifi and great location, just seconds from the beach. Don't bother to eat at 'the restaurant' as it is over priced and not of any great quality sadly. Overall a very enjoyable stay and would recommend. Oh and if you like sheep you'll like all the little "sheepy" extra touches!

reviews.title: Backpacker escape..Perfect!
reviews.text: Friendly French staff and brilliantly situated bungalows in a peaceful garden area. Lamai is much more chilled than chaweng and if you are looking for a cheap place to stay this place is perfect. Right on the beach and with a few shops and bars dotted around we loved our stay here

reviews.title: Close to the beach
reviews.text: OK service. Got a nice bungalow after I had to upgrade the first day because of ants everywhere (I had to pay for this myself.). Bathroom is very simple but clean. Got used to the shower which was placed right beside the toilet. Hot water. Close to the beach, nice garden, ok american breakfast, unstable wifi in the rooms. Recommend it for backpackers and people who travels on a budget, you get what you pay for. Would stay again.

reviews.title: Fantastic!
reviews.text: I absolutely adore this place. It is peaceful, out in nature, yet convenience stores are righy on the corner. It is one minute away from the stunning beach and it is very close to the popular lamai. The staff was wonderfull and I will definitely be coming back!!! Thanks!😁🙏

reviews.title: Definitely recommended for a young couple, just take the aircon room with a fridge.
reviews.text: We're 27 and 32 years old and had one of the newer bungalows. Nice room, with all the basics you need, aircon, fridge and hot water. Location is superb, 5 minutes from the Lamai beach, 10 minutes from Had Lamai (Lamai main street) and just enough from the main road so you get a decent night's sleep. Motorbike rental 200 baht with no deposit, laundry service with return on the next day and a decent american breakfast (recommended) in the garden bungalow to start your day. Staff very friendly, owner as well as the janitor/gardener all ready to help. Definitely recommended!

reviews.title: familyfriendly, relaxed and nice place!
reviews.text: We had a great experience at this place. Laid-back, relaxed, very nice staff and nice location.We rented the familyroom. When you travel with kids it is perfect., nice garden, great pool ( 5 metrs away)and a 2 min walk from the best part of the whole beach. If you don't like the resort/chigue/unpersonal places and not the toeristic/crowded hotels this is a good choice. Malika arranged a tour for us and our todler and two thai woman showed us the nicest spots of Koh samui by car, It was a great day and they were very sweet to our child.. Thank you!

reviews.title: Great location, quality and service
reviews.text: There was a french lady co-owner who greeted us on arrival and made us feel so welcome throughout our stay to the point where it felt sad to say goodbye. The bungalow was with a fan and cold shower and very reasonably priced for the area. They offered scooter hire which was slightly more expensive than other local places, but was well maintained and no fuss. We have been on the road for 5 months and would come back here in a heartbeat.

reviews.title: Pretty little bungalows, good value for money
reviews.text: This is my second stay here. Bungalows are basic but clean and in beautiful gardens. Beach isn't that great, lots of debris and dog mess. Quite a lot of wildlife roaming around in bungalows but what do you expect living in jungle surroundings? Nice continental breakfast with excellent coffee. I highly recommend eating at the roadside 'Sunee Restaurant' a short walk away towards the 7 Eleven. Cheap and tasty food and welcoming staff.

reviews.title: Highly Recommended Budget Accomodation on Lamai Beach
reviews.text: I stayed here for four days at the end of June 2011. For the price charged it is excellent value with direct access (less than 5 minutes walk) to the southern end of Lamai Beach. The main tourist area of Lamai with shops and restaurants is approximately 10 minutes walk. Accomodation is cabin/bungalow style with fan/Aircon/TV and ensuite facilities. Rooms are made up daily and the owners and staff are very attentive and courteous. However, the cabins could probably do with a refresh on decor and it seems like the establishment has recently changed ownership - so renovation is probably forthcoming. As the accomodation is cabin style, if you have problems with geckos and insects coming into the room it may not be for you. Also the owners also have a large dog who barks at you in the drive way if you return late at night, but doesn't do anything else. Overall, I was very satisfied and would stay there again the next time I'm in Koh Samui. Highly recommended. The establishement offers the following facilities: 1. Reasonably priced cooked breakfast 2. Free wifi in reception area, some of the closer bungalows are in range. 3. Very reasonably priced laundry service 4. Tour organisation and vehicle hire Also worth noting that the hotel advertises a pickup service from the nearby airport in Koh Samui, fine if you fly in from Bangkok, but if you arrive as a lot of people do off the ferry from the mainland into Na Thon, you will need to take a taxi or songthaew (the red pickup trucks with bench seating) for the 15km journey to Lamai. The meter taxi costs about 400 Baht (€10). Vendors sell tickets on the ferry for around 100 Baht for private minibuses that drop off at any location on the island.

reviews.title: As it says on the tin...
reviews.text: Initially booked 1 night as we weren't sure what to expect from such a cheap resort (at least they're honest about it in the name!) but ended up staying 3 nights. The bungalow was basic but absolutely fine with a fridge and A/C, bed was a bit hard but you can't have it all! Pool on site which was nice to cool down in and the lovely Lamai beach is literally a 2 minute walk away. There are restaurants and shops (7-Eleven down the road and Makro across the main road) so you really do have everything you need nearby. If you're happy to be near the beach without being on it for a fraction of the price, choose here.

reviews.title: What a good surprise
reviews.text: The best deal for the price in Lamai, the owner arranged transport from the airport. We arrived and were welcomed by the owner Christian, a French guy who gave us all the information on places to go on the island. The bungalows are very clean and in the middle of a tropical garden. The beach is 5 minutes away walking. Not luxury for for the price exceptional.

reviews.title: Lovely place to stay!
reviews.text: So when we arrived, we got dropped off on the main road and told to walk down an alley. bit strange but when we reached the property it was gorgeous. Little huts dotted around with beautiful greenery and literally 5 mins walk to the beach. The huts are nice but dont expect 5* for the price your paying. The beach itself was lovely but i was expecting it to be sand not pebbles so walking on it was a little sore but you get used to it. There are some lovely resturants along the beach to chose from which are good prices and all sun beds/ umbrellas are free. The sea is gorgeous. The only negetive i have was the hotel never seemed to have any staff about, there was a bell u could ring but felt rude doing so unless i had too. Nice place to stay to see town and beach.

reviews.title: Avoid here at all costs!
reviews.text: Would not recommend this to anyone. Arrived around 9 pm to be greeted by staff who took 10 minutes to find out which bungalow we would be staying in. Paid for our stay only to be told they had no change so would need to give us it the next day. Got to our bungalow which was a family deluxe room. There was a small double bed and a tiny pull out couch. No way would it fit four people as was stated when booking. Enquired about buying tickets at reception- no one could help us. Next day, asked to speak to the boss. Boss came to meet us two hours later. Brought an extra bed as she agreed it could not fit four people. However, the extra bed left little space in the room. Beds were very uncomfortable. Left here one night early due to the disappointment.

reviews.title: Bad service-cosy bungalow
reviews.text: We were a couple of nights there, i know that you get what you pay but even in the cheapest accomodation i am used to friendlt staff that try to do their best, I asked to the owner for clean beadsheets and they sayed no cause the room i was staying at was too cheap for having clean sheets everynight. The bungalow was basic but cozy.

reviews.title: Cute bungalows in a quiet garden
reviews.text: Cute and clean bungalows in a well maintained garden. We stayed in the simple kind with only cold water and no aircon, but they have ones with aircon too. The bungalows are in a quiet and serene location slightly away from the main tourist strip, a short walk away to many restaurants, bars and shops. Close to the beach, great mountaim view. The owner is a friendly French guy and his sister also owns a good sushi restaurant in town.

reviews.title: Very good location
reviews.text: The bungalows are away from the main ring road and in the second row from the sea. So it is just one minute to the main road and one minute to the sea which makes the place very quiet all time but you can reach everything within minutes. The amusement and shopping area is a nice 10 minute walk away. Staff is super friendly and helpful, my bungalow was very clean and the price was very reasonable. I stayed 14 days and enjoyed every single day!

reviews.title: Bed Bug Problem- But put right Hotel
reviews.text: Arrived to quaint tree house accommodation at about 9.30pm dumped our bags and went for a meal after the ferry from the mainland. On our return we crashed on the bed only to find ourselves itching, after we turned the lights on there were hundreds of bed bugs crawling over the mattress and on the walls. Didn't get much sleep that night as you can imagine, and couldn't speak to hotel staff as the reception was shut until the morning. Staff and manager rectified problem the next day and upgraded to a more expensive bungalow for free (including fridge, TV, and air con) with complimentary breakfast the next morning. However we were then told we could not have the key for the aircon. Was a shame the original treehouse hut had problems as it would have been nice to stay there a second night, but glad the staff could sort the problem out the following morning... Just need to re-stock the bite cream now.

reviews.title: nice n quiet stay
reviews.text: This is a nice quite little place to stay in Ko Samui. If you are looking to stay around the party area, this is in the total opposite direction. It is less than a five minute walk to the quite white sand beach. The room was OK, it was by no means great, but I have seen much worse. The bed was comfortable. We did have a bit of a mosquito problem (well my wife had a mosquito problem as they left me alone) and that was annoying, having to keep killing the bugs every few minutes. The staff is very friendly. While we were there, it appeared as though they were remodeling the rooms, putting up stronger new walls (hopefully they'll keep the bugs out). Again, it wasn't amazing, it wasn't terrible but well worth the cheap price.

reviews.title: Super relaxed friendly french staff .. 5 mins to beach.
reviews.text: Outstanding. Adorable rickety bungalows on poles , plenty of space to relax, staff keen to help booking things, but also keen to give you your space. Lovely. Wifi might not reach your bungalow, so what? Go sit in the beautiful gardens.

reviews.title: Bad even for the price
reviews.text: While the garden looks very nice, the rooms leave much to be desired. My wife and I are backpacking around the world so we are used to budget rooms, but these rooms were unacceptable. The first room we booked looked fairly nice, but we quickly found that the shower drained VERY slowly. During our showers we found that mold and some other unknown substance was floating around on top of the water. The water backed up inside the bathroom until it covered the entire floor and threatened to spill out into our room. The staff was kind enough to move us into another room for the second night, but we found the same issue and to add to the problems we found an ant infestation inside the bathroom and the TV didn't work. For less than 800 baht we found much better rooms elsewhere.

reviews.title: Great location, friendly staff, tranquil setting.
reviews.text: I stayed in a chalet with fans, had I known there was A/C properties available, I would have upgraded. Would benefit from having a fridge in chalet. Staff are excellent, led by the lovely Malika, great setting in lovely, tranquil gardens, with a swimming pool. Cheap motorbikes for hire on site, located 2 minutes from beach. Overall, great place, great price, great stay. Would definitely recommend.

reviews.title: Cheap bungalow
reviews.text: We booked 3 rooms for 2 people at this place only for one night. The price was very cheap, less than 10€ per person. The bungalow was very small and the bathroom wasn't the best but the garden was very nice and quite. Unfortunately it's located quite far from the nightlife's place but if you are looking for a peaceful place in Samui for a low price this is the right place to go!

reviews.title: Loved it
reviews.text: Lovely bungalows surrounded by a gren garden! Clean and well occupied - AC and hot water. The place is 10 min walk from Lamai Center and 1 min walk to the peaceful and quiet beach. The only thing that bothered us was that despite that staff was friendly in general, they didn't allow us to make a phone call for our next destination... a shame.

reviews.title: Value for money
reviews.text: + Nice bungalow for cheap price, 500BHT Scooter rental at reception Very pleasant French lady owner Very nice staff and service Direct beach access - Mosquitos everywhere Overpriced breakie at reception, better go to town A bit of a walk from main street about 15 min

reviews.title: Very good room and great dining
reviews.text: Six of us booked this hotel at the last minute from Cane and were very happy with the rooms and service. The staff was friendly and the manager was very helpful in booking a tour of Normandy for us. Good food and excelant beach front dining.

reviews.title: Good Location
reviews.text: The hotel is in a good location for visiting the D Day beaches and museums. All the staff we saw were friendly and helpful. Room was small but clean but be warned that the walls are paper thin! We ate in the restaurant one evening and the food was lovely. We had quite a long wait for our mains and the waitress brought us a complimentary starter to share. It is a nice hotel for a short stay but I wouldn't recommend for a long stay due to the size of the rooms and noise from ajoining bedrooms.

reviews.title: Visited once again
reviews.text: Over the last ten years we have returned to this hotel five times for longer stays. And are likely to do so again. The hotel is well located with the boardwalk and beach in front. This allows for long and nice walks and also for a good point for visiting the D-day beaches. The staff is highly professional and friendly and the kitchen had good quality.

reviews.title: Good quality, beautiful view...
reviews.text: Beautiful views from the front room, cozy and clean blue room with double bed and living room part with small TV. Very spacy bathroom, cleaned every day. Good coffee, poor wifi. Overall a nice 4 day stay in Normandy to have a lot of fresh air by the sea... :)

reviews.title: great stay
reviews.text: Wonderful stay. Food, rooms and staff were great. Rooms were pretty small but still had a lot of charm, and I can't really complain because the ocean was literally right outside my window, haha. Food was incredible. Staff were very friendly and helpful, always went the extra mile.

reviews.title: A perfect getaway location
reviews.text: We went for a romantic getaway - returning to Clos Normand after about 5 years. The hotel is just as quaint and beautiful - the location is perfect. After 12 hours of travelling and sight seeing in Caen - the glasses of wine on the terrace over the beach, in the sunshine were very welcome. The staff were very welcoming and our lack of french language didn't phase them, thankfully. We ate in the resaurant the first night of our stay, it is always busy with locals as it is an excellent sea food restaurant. We weren't over keen on the menu - but that was down to our personal tastes, not the fault of the hotel. What we did have was superb and couldn't have been better. After dinner we went for a walk along the promenade. We went out and about the second day, it's a perfect location to explore Normandy and the reminders of its history are at every small town and traffic islands. I also adore the little casino's in each of the coastal towns. The only small quibble I would have is that when we got back there were no parking spaces left, it must have been a busy night. The room was small, but spotless, and overlooked the beach, right on the edges of Sword/Juno beach. A very compact bathroom, but fully functional and spotlessly clean. We slept with the windows open just because we could, and the sea was so close. Breakfast both mornings was a delight, and the staff contstantly replenshing the supplies. The hotel is beautiful, and quaint, and fairly quiet. The staff were excellent and helpful. What surprised us on this visit was the lack of English visitors in the whole Normandy region, the hotel too are missing their custom. I will be doing my best to get enough money together, and time off work to head back again next summer - it was a lovely short break to recharge the batteries and relax - perfect!

reviews.title: Right on the Beach
reviews.text: Le Clos Normand is located right on the boardwalk. In fact, its terrasse is on the beach side of the boardwalk. Our rooms were Channel-side and offered a delightful breath of salt air and great view. The rooms are tiny as are the bathrooms, and there is sign of age, but everything was very clean and the beds were quite comfortable. We ate dinner and breakfast at the hotel. The dining room is outstanding! All hotel and restaurant staff were very friendly and helpful.

reviews.title: Nice hotel by the sea
reviews.text: Older style hotel with small rooms but some with views over the sea. Staff were very helpful offering to carry our friends bags upstairs. The fish dinner we had that night was delightful and reasonable. Only had bottled beer in the bar but this maybe because we were early in the season. Parking was available in the courtyard upon request. To cold to sit outside but the hotel has tables von the beach front that would be very pleasant on a summer evening

reviews.title: tired but functional
reviews.text: Obviously a busy family hotel and showing signs of wear and tear. Rooms were clean although bathrooms could do with renewing. Building obviously gets heavy use and it's after mid season so to be expected. Very quiet at night - not street noise... until early morning when the pipes started up; very loud plumbing sounds and as other guests have commented walls between rooms are think enough to hear people talking. No trouble to park outside and location is central.

reviews.title: Le Clos Normand
reviews.text: We spent two nights in this lovely hotel. The best aspect of the hotel is its location directly facing the beach with just the promenade in front of it. A sea view room is worth paying for. Staff were extremely friendly and helpful and the overall atmosphere of the hotel was very welcoming. We had dinner in the hotel one evening and found the food excellent though typically rich. We struggled to finish and had to abandon the Tarte Tatin. Our room was small but comfortable and although the bathroom was small, the shower was good. One criticism was that the soundproofing could have been better in the rooms. St Aubin itself is quite small but it is well located for visiting the surrounding area, particularly the D-Day beaches.

reviews.title: bad experience to be avoided
reviews.text: this hotel is really not at a reasonable standard for 2014 travelling: rooms not only too small, bathroom nearly 1,5m², but on top of that no insulated walls at all, so you here everything from the neigbouring room (conversations, toilet, snorking, .... The old fashioned restaurant menu looks good, but very restricted and several items are not even available. We were served full lobster gratiné, the lobsters were very tiny and small, for sure less than 300g alive, but for a price of a jumbo lobster (around 50 EURO). The boss did not show any customer oriented attitude, just arrogant; when we made the remark to him, he said 'yes the kitchen chief is compalinting also' and then he added smiling 'but they are inexpensive'. Bad answer from this guy, who doesn't care about his clients.

reviews.title: Visited Restaurant
reviews.text: Visited this restaurant for lunch whilst on our way to Normandy Beaches. Very pleasant and welcoming. Sat outside with beautiful view surrounding and out to sea whilst eating our Mussels which were gorgeous. Staff were very accommodating. Prices very reasonable.

reviews.title: Nice hotel by the sea
reviews.text: We were travelling back home and wanted to stay by the sea. It was quite late and this was the only hotel we found. They had a four bedroom and it was nice. Quite big room with one double bed and two pull out beds. Quite comfortable. The furniture and beds were a bit old but still nice. The bathroom was big with double sinks and a bathtub. Nice bathroom with bathrobes. The hotel is not the newest but it is nice and it is directly on the sea. Unfortunately we did not see the sea when it was high. We just saw it when it was out. Unfortunately our room was at the backside so we hade no view. But I am sure the rooms with the view of the sea are really nice. The staff is really nice. There is free wii-fii but it did not work in our room. We had to go to the lobby to make it work.

reviews.title: Friendly welcome....return visit after a few years
reviews.text: This was a return visit for us after visiting the hotel many times in the past .The welcome was very friendly and helpful as we arrived much earlier than anticipated and room made available quickly. As people have noted the rooms are small but views more than make up for this ..if you request a sea view.The food was good and well presented but the menu smaller than remembered.Breakfast was buffet style and substantial. My only negative comment is the fact that the walls are thin and most things can be heard from next door room ie speech and flushing of toilet.

reviews.title: Gourmet
reviews.text: Perfekt in every way with a surprisingly elegant kitchen. It's location right on the beach is hard to beat. Go there to relax not to party. Try their selection of calvados and enjoy a nice breakfast on the terrace.

reviews.title: Lovely!
reviews.text: We have just returned from a week in Normandy where we stayed at this charming hotel. The hotel is on the beach promenade in the pleasant little village of St Aubin sur Mer. When we made our telephone booking the girl advised us that the room available was small in size but we found it was comfortable, spotlessly clean, lovely pure white sheets and towels with a tiny bathroom and a beautiful view over the sea. It was lovely to go to sleep and wake up to the sound of the waves. We stayed on a bed and breakfast basis but the hotel does have a very good restaurant and we did eat there on our first evening. My only criticism of the hotel was their wine list was on the extravagent side so we spent the rest of the week eating in different restaurants, some in St Aubin sur Mer and others in the neighbouring villages. We really enjoyed our stay. We loved the fact that you could walk for miles along the promenade in either direction and explore the other little villages and it was also a good base for visiting further a field by car. We came home relaxed and our batteries recharged.

reviews.title: A fantastic stay
reviews.text: I loved this hotel! I had the chance to stay three nights at this hotel while touring Normandy and loved my stay. The hotel and rooms were spotless, my bathroom had recently been renovated to a high standard. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The food was excellent.

reviews.title: You can smell the sea!
reviews.text: The first thing we did when we got to our room (which had a lovely 'beachy' decor) was open the window and let in the smell of the sea. We didn't have a room directly facing the beach but on the side but could still see the water without having to lean out the window too far. The room was fine although the shower cubicle was the tiniest I have ever used and the walls were paper thin - could hear everything the two old ladies were saying in the next room - including hearing one sing the other to sleep! We had a half board booking so had dinner in the dining room which was absolutely fantastic - a lovely view of the water and the waitress was very good at explaining what everything was (my basic French is not good when it comes to seafood dishes). Everything was delicious and of good quality and quantity as was breakfast the following morning. Our delightful stay was topped off by a romp with a very friendly puppy in the pretty garden on our way to our car (parking available out the back as well as along the side street).

reviews.title: pleasant hotel in sweet seaside town
reviews.text: We stayed two nights at the Clos Normand during a three-day weekend to visit the Normandy landing beaches. It's a very pleasant hotel, with a nice restaurant. Being that it's right on the beach, and in a well visited area, it's a touch more expensive than what you'd pay for the same hotel elsewhere in France. The rooms and bathrooms are small, but attractive, well appointed, and comfortable. The town of St. Aubin was one of the nicest of the seaside towns we saw in the area, with pretty villas right on the water-front. However, the beach itself is bit thin and strewn with seaweed. Further to the west, the beaches are much wider, wilder, and tempting. You don't have to eat in the restaurant, but we did and the food is quite good with a full price range of menus. Breakfast is pretty standard hotel buffet: fruit, cereal, yogurt, pastries. Note that St. Aubin is on Juno beach, with Gold to the west and Sword to the east, so perfect if your main interest are the British/Canadian beaches (the `North Shore' regiment from New Brunswick landed right in front of the hotel).. Omaha beach is a good hour's drive along winding roads. If you are in a hurry, and more interested in the U.S. beaches, then maybe you should look for a hotel further west. I'd make two complaints: the walls between rooms are a bit thin and I could almost follow a conversation in the next room, and the wi-fi didn't work when we were there. The staff said it had been down for a few days, and they didn't seem to be in much hurry to get it repaired. But the tourist office 5 minutes' walk away had free wi-fi, so we could at least check our emails.

reviews.title: Tiny rooms, decor dated
reviews.text: This hotel has an absolute beachfront position, with a terrace on the sand of Juno beach, scene of the landing of the Canadian contingent in 1944. The hotel dates from around then, is my guess, and the structure of the building means that the rooms are very small. Since they would have had a bathroom down the hall when constructed, the inclusion of a tiny modular WC/shower/basin makes them even smaller, with nowhere to sit but on the bed. But for a seaside holiday, when you are not going to spend much time in the room, it's (just) OK. The hotel has a quite upmarket restaurant, but there are half a dozen more casual options within a 5 minute walk. Parking available, and you'll need a car as the town is 20 minutes from the nearest railway station in Caen.

reviews.title: Le Clos Normand is Normandy's best kept secret
reviews.text: on our way to Caen, in Normandy France we decided to leave the main road and head for the beaches. From Caen we took the road D17 direction Ouistreham and followed road D514 direction Ouistreham to St Aubin-sur-mer. A most charming and beautiful little village on the Normandy coast. As we were travelling mid-week it was easy to book a room and dinner on the spot. The receptionist was very helpful and friendly. We booked a special offer for the room including breakfast and dinner, in total we paid 95 euro per person per night. That is relatively cheap once you realise that the restaurant of the hotel is serving excuisite food. Breakfast can be ordered in the privacy of your own room. There is a big terrace in front of the hotel on the promenade that is sheltered from the wind and is most enjoyable for afternoon tea or pre-dinner drinks. Our room was a suite, with two bedrooms with TV, a spacious bathroom and separate toilet. All very clean and well maintained. The view from our room was amazing; overlooking the beach and the sea. Since there's no traffic in front of the hotel the tranquility and peaceful surroundings struck us the most. The restaurant is excellent and a delight for discerning travellerers who appreciate good local food of high quality. The Chef takes pride in serving local specialities like plateau fruits-de-mer with local oysters from St Vaast, other shellfish, muscles and shrimps. A must for seafoodlovers. Or try the 'tripes de Caen', or tarte de pommes with Calvados. Service was most friendly and very attentive to every wish. Only minor point were the prices of the wines and other drinks on the menu. Very expensive and extra to the bill. But the total of your consumptions depends on yourself, of course... in the morning we walked around the village, very charming and we discovered a life of luxury and memorial buildings behind the dyke. As well as turn-of-the-century villas and charming streets. This village looks like a filmset, so authentic and still untouched by modern tourism. We were very impressed by our stay at 'le clos normand' and we will be back. If only for the superb oysters and lobster!! "Le Clos Normand" is highly recommended for a short stay especially for foodlovers and families with little children who enjoy the sea and the beaches and the French good life.

reviews.title: Exceptionally Rude Host, a ruined stay
reviews.text: We stayed at this hotel at the end of April 2012, after having visited Saint Aubin Sur Mer last October and staying elsewhere. What a mistake to book with this hotel. We booked via a well known internet site and I specifically requested a sea facing room, but on arrival we were shown a room at the side of the hotel and on asking about my specific request they advised they had emailed us about that and received no response back from us. Of course we couldn't check that as we had no access to our emails on holiday and on return home, there wasn't any email from them. What can I say about this hotel? It doesn't smell good. They say its non smoking but every day it was easily evident to smell cigarettes in the hallway. Added to that was stale smells such as cooking. Not nice. The entrance foyer. Is so dated. Has awful red net curtains up at the windows and dirty dated carpet and furniture. The room - the walls were so thin we could here the TV in the next room and the couple talking to their dog. Yes, onto pets. A couple in the next room to us had their dog with them. Not such an issue but it was when they took it to the dining room every time they ate. However, this all pales into insignificance when on the second evening we decided to book a table for dinner in the evening. The menu looked great. I asked for the ravioli and was told they didn't have any. My partner asked about the steak and was told it came with pasta (odd choice and on suggesting french fries we were given a withering look, so he ordered the veal instead which again came with yes you guessed it - pasta). The starters arrived. Mine was langustines with grapefruit salad and toasted bread. It wasn't good with soggy toast and a pretty lame excuse for a salad. I advised the waitress it wasn't very nice but she wasn't interested and did nothing about it. On to the main course. One veal with pasta and one lamb. The veal and pasta were mediocre. But the lamb? It was a huge rib of lamb which hadn't been cooked correctly, so that on attempting to cut it was difficult but to eat ? Forget it. I spat out the first mouthful. My partner felt the same. Remember this was a 25-28 euro meal. It wasn't some burger from McDonalds it was meant to be exceptional cooking (we'd paid much less in another restaurant the night before and the food was amazing). We explained to the waitress it wasn't edible. She fled. The other waitress came she couldn't understand what our issue was, instead she contacted the Hotel owner. Here the evening went into what can only be described as a scene from Faulty Towers. The Hotel owner appeared and his first words to us were "I wasn't meant to be working this evening, I was at home with my children" in other words how dare you disturb me. What a rude and inconsiderate thing to say to guests in your hotel? He listened to our complaint and we advised him we wouldn't pay for the meal - and he sneered that other people had eaten the lamb that evening and didn't complain and that "he knew his chef" we argued that he should find the meal and taste it and let us know. He said he'd get right onto it. Instead he waltzed off speaking to other french guests in the dining room acting all friendly and like you would expect a Hotel owner to act. Eventually around 20 minutes later he came back to us, no apology, no offer of anything else to eat, no drink on the house, no explanation, nothing. His last words "I wish you a good evening " through grated teeth and not in the least bit sincere. I should also add here not one member of staff in the restaurant offered us any other food, or apology they just ignored us as though we'd committed a crime. No deserts or coffee or would you like to order... Just ignored. so rude. We left disgusted. In the morning when we went to leave and pay our bill he appeared from the bar area, with a croissant stuffed in his mouth watching as we asked for the invoice. There again were no apologies. Awful owner, wouldn't recommend to my worst enemy.

reviews.title: Amazing value and incredible service!
reviews.text: We booked this hotel on recommendation from a colleague. Seriously, the experience was incredible. For an incredible price we had private rooms with a view onto the beach, a four course dinner and a breakfast. First of all, the hotel is right on the water. Across the boardwalk they also have a terrasse for meals and drinks, etc. literally on the beach. If that wasn't enough, the entire hotel is fresh and inviting. Decorated in maritime colours with large windows, it is very inviting. The staff is incredibly helpful and friendly. They get to know the guests very quickly. At dinner, the experience is clearly five star. Excellent servers bring courses and courses of incredibly prepared, unique local specialties. Yes, as another comment mentioned the drinks are expensive, but would be on par with any restaurant in Paris, even something of a must poorer quality. For the calibre of the restaurant, the drink prices were reasonable. The server quickly suggested the right wine based on our meal, and we were quite impressed. Possible the best meal I have eaten in a long time. The rooms were nice, although a bit small - perhaps because we booked single rooms. If you are a large person, ask about the size of the shower when booking a room. The breakfast was also quite good, including pastries, bread, cereals, yogourts, jams, coffee, tea, juice, milk, etc. - once again in their excellent dinner hall overlooking the sea.

reviews.title: Short visit
reviews.text: We had a great room with sea views from two windows. The room was lovely and warm as was the bathroom,it was a very chilly windy day!! Very good powerful shower. The staff were friendly. We had a very nice meal in the hotel restaurant overlooking the beach. Would love to go back in the summer.

reviews.title: Lovely location, very nice hotel
reviews.text: Stayed here two nights. The rooms were bright, loved being able to open the window facing the Channel to hear the soft surf at night. Very clean. Didn't even turn on the TV. Dining room had a good menu and the food was well prepared, not over-priced. Lovely breakfast with made-to order eggs. Plenty of parking, Good location to explore the D-Day beaches moving from the eastern end to the west. This is not a high-end luxurious hotel, rather a comfortable, cosy, homey-type place. Loved it.

reviews.title: memorable
reviews.text: I could not recommend enough this place. The food and the service were outstanding!!!

reviews.title: Perfect location
reviews.text: We arrived at this hotel by bicycle after half a day cycling in the rain. We were warmly welcomed and the staff was helpful in drying our clothes. It is in a very nice village overlooking the sea. I did not find the restaurant to my taste however, I am sure that there more restaurants in the area but as it was raining we decided to use their restaurant. The restaurant did not look very clean and flies were around windows.

reviews.title: Small beds. Good restaurant.
reviews.text: We stayed here for two nights while driving the D Day roads. (We didn't see the American cemeteries or a couple of other things due to the government shut down!) The nicest thing about the hotel was that a lovely promenade was right outside of the hotel. Very nice for walking and views. We had a room on the seaside with a large window looking out to the sea. If you are of average or larger size, I would try for a different hotel. Maybe they have different beds in different rooms, but I don't think so. My husband is over six feet tall and the bed was pretty uncomfortable. The room was so small that you could walk around the bed, but that's it. No room for even a chair. The restaurant had good food....a whole fish and a steak that were excellent. The place must be run by a family that lives there, as the kids and a dog are running around. That was kind of nice to see, though.

reviews.title: Wonderful Location
reviews.text: I have stayed at this hotel before. This time I was guiding a group of travellers for D-Day 70 and wherever one went in this area, it was full of veterans and people who wanted to pay their respects. The Clos Normand was fairly full but this did not detract in any way. One can sit on the beach terrace bar and know that you are on the Juno beach which featured importantly on June 6th 1944. 70 years on, at 6:30am, I looked out of my bedroom window to see the beach swathed in sunshine, a wonderful setting. The rooms at the hotel cannot be described as capacious, they are small but appealing in a rustic sense. The restaurant is good, we ate here for 4 nights as a group, the house wine, particularly the Chardonnay is well acceptable. Breakfast is quite satisfactory with home made, fresh squeezed orange juice. The staff are really hospitable and friendly. The one downside was that WIFI is only available in the reception area, but really, does one have to have accessibility all of the time? I can recommend this hotel, I shall certainly be back

reviews.title: Good hotel for families
reviews.text: We stayed for one night on our way back from the Vendee. St Aubin is only about 20 minutes from Ouistreham (also known as Caen for some strage reason as its a good 10 miles to Caen) from where Brittany Ferries operate a service to Portsmouth. St Aubin is a lovely seaside village. The Clos Normand is right on the sea front and all the rooms have a sea view. We were given an excellent room designed for families. It has a main entrance leading to a hallway with the toilet and bathroom (which is a very good size) accessed from the hallway. It then has two separate bedrooms one of which is again of a very good size and the other has room for three single beds but doesn't leave much space. We booked half board. The dinner menu offered good options for 'free' and also allowed you to upgrade to a-la-carte options for reasonable supplements. It's a typical up-market French restaurant and therefore the food is very well presented and cooked to perfection. The kids had plenty of options for their food. Whilst it's not cheap to stay here I highly recommend it. The price is the only reason I've rated it as Above Average rather than Excellent.

reviews.title: Nice rooms - very good restaurant
reviews.text: We booked the Le Clos Normand just for one night using bookings.com. The hotel was easy to find, as it is located directly at the esplanade of St. Aubin. The welcome was professional and warm-hearted. The look and feel of room 207 (siedeview to the ocean) was maritim (blue and white) and cosy - allthough the room and especially the bath was quite small. We had dinner at the hotel-restaurant - outside facing the ocean: great view! The dishes (fisch, seafood, desert) tasted excellent. (3-course menue: 25€; large bottle of spring water: 6€) I would recommend the hotel for a romantic weekend.

reviews.title: The pipe that never sleeps
reviews.text: Good location on the broadwalk. Walls are thin like paper, we could hear every conversation, every toilet flushed. There was a pipe, I think heating pipe,somewhere in the hotel which made an horrible noise all night. We woke up like 10 times. We hear other people complaining, trying to turn water on and off to keep the pipe quiet. We won't come back unless there is some serious renovation done.

reviews.title: Amazing Lunch at the Restaurant.
reviews.text: We were in town for the D-Day ceremonies. This happened to be the first restaurant of a few that we visited that week, and the one to which every subsequent restaurant was compared. Fabulous presentation, amazing food. Not to mention a fabulous patio overlooking the channel. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Good outweighed the bad
reviews.text: Le Clos Normand I stayed for three days at this hotel in late may,2015. I was able to get a beach front room and it had a fantastic view of the beach. The rooms were bright and clean. I thought the walls were probably the thinnest of any hotel I've stayed at because of the noise you hear from the next room, but I think it's mostly an older crowd that stays here who aren't really interested in staying up late, so it wasn't really a factor. I did find on the second day that there was no hot water when I went to take a shower around 8am, so it might be best to shower the night before. For the most part, I found just about all of the staff was very freindly, from the groundskeepers to the people behind the desk and in the restaurant, except on the third day. On that day, I returned about 5pm from a day of touring. I pulled into a small courtyard in back that's in addition to their regular parking on the side. I went up to my room and freshend up. I then went down for a cold beer. When I drove in, all the staff was at a table in that courtyard and were still there. So I went up to the reception desk which is right in front of the bar and stood there, waiting for someone to come in. A middle aged man came in the door and stood there and just put his hands together behind his back and looked at me and didn't say a word. I finally asked if it was possible to get a beer. I'm sure he was either the owner or the manager or both. So he poured me a beer and to his credit, he took his time with it to make sure it was filled to the brim with beer and not foam. I ate two nights at the restaurannt here. They had no menus in English. I've been to France several times and there are a lot of words I'm familiar with, but except for the key words for beef or fish and a few others, I was lost as to what it said. The waiter on the first night was a young man who only knew a few words of English and was of no use. The third night, the owner or manager guy waited on me. He offered to translate anything I needed help with, but I did not get a warm fuzzy feeling from this guy. I said thank you on the way out and heard nothing in reply. The food I did have there was good and not too highly priced. There are a few other restaurants a short walk away. There's also a casino not far away, just up the street which can serve as a landmark when your trying to find this hotel. The wifi connection in the room was so so with occassional loss of signal. Going down to the lobby didn't improve things much. They had a small tv with a good picture and several channels to choose from. So all and all, with the great view and most of the staff being freindly and nice accomodations, It was a good stay for me.

reviews.title: Very enjoyable stay
reviews.text: We were in Normandy recently and stayed at Le Clos Normand. Although the room and bathroom were small, it was clean and well located. We had a room overlooking the beach and with the windows open we had a spectacular view. The restaurant serves excellent fare - the desserts are out of this world. The staff were great - friendly and knowledgeable. If we ever return to this part of France, we'll be sure to stay at this hotel. The food is excellent, the location is perfect, the rooms are clean, the staff are friendly (even to us non French speaking clientele). What more could you want?

reviews.title: Ya get what you pay for
reviews.text: I've been here before and honestly, you get what you pay for. No it's not a Hilton hotel but at least it's a place to spend the night for cheap and considering the location (right in the heart of Clifton Hill) you can't go wrong. Yes it's a little outdated with the tacky furnitures and curtains but it's clean and cheap and it's no where near close to an experience at a hostel (if you've stayed in one before y'all know what I'm talkin about). So, if you want the luxurious experience with the fancy view of the falls and don't mind spending an arm and a leg there's a Hilton down the street. If not, this place is not too bad. Save the money for shopping! And..... casino? hehe :P

reviews.title: nice little hotel great location
reviews.text: Have stayed there before and never had any issues clean rooms easy access to Clifton Hill and casino and Mr. Lee was excellent anything i needed had no issues I can't wait to stay there on next visit.

reviews.title: Terrible hotel!!!
reviews.text: We've arrived at the hotel late at the evening when reception was already closed. It took 15 minutes to the owner to answer his phone, but finally he came to check us in. The room that we've got looked like someone sleep on the bed 5 minutes ago. Later we saw a Japanese guy passing by our room with Folding Mattress, so it was clear that we've destroyed his night. The room was not clean, no air conditioner and no hot water!!! The owner behaves like he is doing you a favor. The most terrible hotel I've been!!!!

reviews.title: Amazing location, great price!
reviews.text: Conveniently located close to everything you could possibly want to see in Niagara. The rooms were clean, we basically had the pool to ourselves, the owner was kind & courteous at all times. We are even going back this summer, thats how great a time we had! (side note: if you're used to 5 star, 200$+ a night hotels, this place won't be for you. you get what you pay for, but it is very clean & very well kept).

reviews.title: No one there and Phone number posted on window
reviews.text: I arrived with another family at 9 pm March 9th, 2019 and found no One there the light in the front office on. No doorbell only a note saying call this number. I called they do not even have an answering machine set up.I called repeatedly. Weird part no one answered but the number called my cell.. No voice on another end. Really Disappointed by several factors. the place looks abandoned/ filthy and just not a place to ever return to. Waste of time going .. We had to scramble around to find a place ..

reviews.title: Basic and a bit worn out
reviews.text: Niagara Family Inn was cheap, you get what you pay for, and location was right next to the Clifton Hill. Very easy to walk to the Falls and for example Skylon Tower. It seemed a bit shady at first but actually it was quiet to spend the night in. We had a good night's sleep. The room was old and worn out, very basic. The sheets were clean as well as the bathroom though the place kind of made you wonder if it really has been thoroughly cleaned up. Probably just a feeling, but it's not nice to have one. The only actual inconvenience was that they did not have a luggage storage that most hotels, hostels and motels have for the customers to leave their luggage in when either waiting for the time to check-in or after having already checked-out but spending another day in town before the bus/train/plane leaves. We arrived about two hours before the 2 pm check-in and wanted to leave our luggage there to start exploring the town while waiting for a room. We ended up leaving our stuff to the reception, where they probably were left unattended because at times there was nobody at the reception. After the 11 am check-out the next day we did not want to leave our luggage there as they did not have an actual space for it, though our bus didn't leave until later in the evening. We had to come up with other arrangements.

reviews.title: NEVER AGAIN
reviews.text: Poor to no access to manager when unruly guests were in a family fight at 3am. No phone, Bathroom Not Vented, not able to use wi-fi in room, toilet paper was pretty much see-thru, we were two and there was no room preparations for two people.(1 very thin soap),(towels for one). For a Motel that appears to be full almost each night(due to price), There is poor money management to upgrade basic comforts. The pool was not clean. When we checked in and asked for a larger room, we were told that the owner gave them to long term guests.(workers from the restaurant). Again Very Poor Money Management going on at this place.HHHHHmmm

reviews.title: HORRIBLE-FILTHY
reviews.text: Need I say more? just in case I have attached photos lest you think I exaggerate. Run down, dirty halls and then the bathroom was worse (see photos). Who knows just how filthy the bedroom floor was-you can not tell with dark color carpet. Sheets were surprisingly very bleached white. They tried to charge more than the booking.com said would be charged. charged $10 to park across the street next to the $5 a night parking lot. We just went to the casino and stayed up all night. Did not take shower. We just went home.

reviews.title: Decrepit but clean linen and towels
reviews.text: I stayed with my family in a 2QB room for 1 night. I had called the hotel earlier verifying the reservation even though I booked through Hotels.com The picture of the hotel lobby that I found online is misleading. The reality is nothing like it. The room I was in (#6 on the second floor and near the "Reception") was decrepit and in dire need of renovation. Carpet was very dirty and in urgent need of replacement. The general condition of the hotel too seemed run down. I was charged USD 10.00 in cash for parking by a person called Rahul at the front desk and told to park in the parking of another hotel across the street which had a sign saying Full Day Parking $5(CAD) so it was a rip off. We did not fight it as it was a small amount. However, the linen and towels were surprisingly clean and the beds were comfortable.Toiletries and hair drier are provided. There was hot water and water pressure was good. Internet was okay. We did not put the TV on. There was no coffeemaker in the room and even after requesting several times for one, and even saying that we were willing to pay for it, we were not provided one. The big plus is that it is within easy walking distance to Clifton Hill and Hornblower cruise. However, there are at least a dozen other hotels in the same area. Another plus is that there is a very good and authentic Indian restaurant in the hotel, but it was accessible from our room by walking the entire hallway and then down some very small and risky stairs. I would not recommend this as wheelchair friendly. There is a picnic table tucked away under a tree at the side of the reception booth which was being used at night by people I don't know for what purpose but it made me uneasy. I needed the hotel for a few hours sleep only but I would definitely shop some more and choose another place if I visit Niagara Falls Ontario again.There are far better ones available for the price I paid for one night (CAD$152) to Hotels.com

reviews.title: Horrible!!!!!!!
reviews.text: This hotel we paid over $200 a night and in the room we had a bed that was to small for what we were told, a dresser we couldn't open, a tv that didn't have more than 5 channels and a bathroom we couldn't turn around in and a view of a brick wall out the window.... what we DIDNT have was: Garbage can Kleenex A chair Pen Paper Phone Clock Extra toilet paper Fridge Coffee maker You will regret staying here I think this is where cockroaches go die and the birthplace of crack..... and please if you decide not to read this and you do stay there make sure if you leave the window opened you get some hobo stab insurance cause they will try to get in!!!!

reviews.title: Not Worth the Money
reviews.text: The only good thing about this place was the location. I was also excited about the pool and called to ask if they had one. They told me yes, but when we arrived two days later it was a surprise to find they didn't even have a pool. I wouldn't be so mad and disappointed if they didn't lie about it. Our room was incredibly small and didn't come with more than 2 towels, proper hand soap, conditioner, a hair dryer (which they said it did come with), a fridge, or even a remote controller for the tv. Our view out the window was a brick wall. They don't have a proper ice machine just a cooler they fill up so when we went to get ice it was all melted water. The worst part of this was that I booked my room online and the website told me it would be 360$ and when I got to the hotel they charged me 450$. WAY over priced for the low quality that we got. I will never be back.

reviews.title: How much time do you spend in the hotel when visiting Niagara anyway?
reviews.text: It's been a few years since we stayed at the Niagara Family Inn but our experience was pretty good. We had four kids with us so we stayed in the family room with three double beds. Sure the place is older and doesn't have all the amenities the newer hotels have, but we found the clerk to be helpful and didn't have any issues with noise or anything for the three nights we were there. They allowed us to let the kids have pizza by the pool in the evening. The beds and bathroom were clean. TV was crappy and there was no phone but honestly, all we really did was sleep there anyway. It is great for the rates and within walking distance to the falls. I had to choose July 2012 as the date, but we actually stayed the year prior to that.

reviews.title: Disappointing and bad service
reviews.text: I got here after a 2 1/2 hour drive and was exhausted. I was desperate to get into my room and the owner kept interrupting me to go on his cell phone. You have to park across the road which is incredibly inconvenient. Wifi doesn't work, and got a total of 2 channels on my TV. The room has the bare necessities. A bed, crappy TV with no remote, bathroom, and 1 soap and 1 shampoo. The only saving grace was that it was very clean. But for $91, I am never going back.

reviews.title: Great location, decent place
reviews.text: The location could not be better; it's literally right by Clifton hill, there's a mini "alleyway" by the parking lot on the pool side to quickly cut onto Clifton hill (ends up right by sugar mountain). The rooms were clean and were what was expected. Overall we felt safe and happy with the stay. The manager was very lenient with the rules and we went for a late night swim.

reviews.title: Bare bones but clean and central
reviews.text: Okay, so my friend and I, who are huge Boz Scaggs fans, needed a place to stay on July 24 in Niagara Falls. Of course, we left it too late to get a decent rate for a cushy place so we were pretty happy that we actually found a place for less than a hundred bucks that night. The Niagara Family Inn is very basic, I mean really basic, very Spartan, one soap, one shampoo, thin towels, old furniture, etc. But it is clean, the sheets were soft and very white and the beds were comfortable. There is a pool, we didn't go in it, but some people were enjoying it. It was very clean and the water clear. There was a Korean restaurant attached to the hotel, since the owners are Korean but we didn't go in. Because we were coming from two different locations we had two cars for one room, but the owner was very gracious and gave us a dashboard tag for the second vehicle for free. You must be up-front about how many people are sharing the room. One couple sounded a little unsure how many people would be in the room and the owner made no bones about the fact if he found out more people would be in the room, he would charge them double. Hey, he's running a business, and it states quite clearly that a room with two double beds is for two people max. The location is very central, just one short block north of Victoria Street. It is right where all the action is. If I had a family and was traveling on a budget this would be a perfect place to stay. We are used to staying in more upscale places but it definitely gave us somewhere to lay our heads when vacancies were few and far between. Usually places we would stay in for $100 a night were going for $230+. There was one issue with the table lamp on the bedside table; the socket was loose and wobbly and I didn't feel comfortable turning it off the normal way so we unplugged it. We told the owner and he thanked us, so if you are in room 3 and the lamp is fixed then good but if it's still scary wobbly, then I'm going to be disappointed.

reviews.title: What do you get from a 2 star?
reviews.text: Well you get exactly this: The hotel is in serious need of an update, but everything in the room worked just fine. It was clean enough, but not sparkling. I don't think the maid came in once while we were there, but no biggie, we were only there for a couple of nights. There is an Indian restaurant attached to the hotel so the scent of the cuisine kind of permeates everything, so if you don't like that don't come here. Can't beat the location, easy walk to Clifton Hill. Staff extremely friendly and polite. I give it a good rating because I paid for a budget hotel and got exactly what I expected and paid for.

reviews.title: Don't go
reviews.text: We are NOT picky people when it comes to hotels, as long as it's clean we're good. This place is just gross. Super small rooms, holes in the walls, microwave from 1980. We found garbage under our beds, and not just a piece of wrapper or something, there were pop cans and a pop can case. Fries behind the nightstand, blood stained towels, and the best part! DRUGS in the nightstand drawer! Seriously, that happened, 4 roaches (the pot kind not the bug) in then drawer, thankfully we found this before our 3 kids did! Our tv wasn't working, so we asked to have someone fix it, said they'll be right up, no one came, (don't worry we fixed it ourselves, and your welcome for that) parking is 10$ a night even though the guys running the lot are charging anyone else 5$ The only plus about this place is the location, it is close to Clifton but so are a hundred other places you could stay

reviews.title: Worse motel ever.
reviews.text: Very rude, unfriendly staff. This is worse motel - NOT 3 star hotel you can stay in Niagara, nothing to do with the family.I was about to cancel after I pay 75$ and see the room, but I was refuse by the owner even I found somebody to take over the room.Next time even if the owner pay me to stay, I won't do it.Worse motel ever.

reviews.title: Reasonable price
reviews.text: best service, Clean rooms, affordable price, good food. Housekeeping staff was nice and helpful. I ordered food and the quality was good and the food was delicious. I will recommend to all of you guys to visit this place.

reviews.title: newly renovated
reviews.text: they recently renovated the motel, new bed sheets, amazing smell, 3 shampoos and 3 conditioners, the have an ok fridge (okay their fridge is horrible) and a not too good tv, but overall it's really good. they got a new owner who is really nice. did I mention there is free wifi. it"s attached to an amazing Indian restaurant too, plus it only costs 100$, amazing for its price

reviews.title: House Keeping Fail to do job. And Management did not care.
reviews.text: two adults. ! teen and a child 2 years old stayed in Room 3. we found juice bottles under beds.& chip bags. there was even half drank water bottles in cupboards. I wrote my name in filth in drawers and cabinet. The place had not been vacuumed at all We heard several guest screaming across the lot at all hours. .I brought it to the management they just disregarded it.I even took our garbage out and recycled/ plus stripped beds. I took pictures and then asked for management come see.Pubic hairs in a drawer and upper right corner of the room.No comment no apology and they walked away. sad really good location. Minutes from Cliftonhill

reviews.title: Average motel--but clean & great Value close to the Falls! :-)
reviews.text: I actually booked this room for my son and GF (young 20's) visiting from BC as for $57+$10 for parking it fit their budget. The property is only 2-star but had good reviews for comfort and value so we booked it--and my son and his GF were very happy with the room, clean, comfortable and excellent location for them in the Clifton part of Niagara Falls! The area was "a bit sketchy", especially compared to Fallsview but the price was 1/2 of even the cheaper alternatives. The kids had a blast and had no issues/complaints re the rooms--so was a great choice! :-)

reviews.title: Kashish
reviews.text: I've been there for one week from 1 January. The place was excellent rooms were clean and close to all attractions in Niagara Falls. It has great Indian cuisine restaurant the food was really good and affordable. Must give it a try.

reviews.title: Disgusting
reviews.text: There was no window in the room, couldn't even sleep in it...It gave me nightmares!!! Never go here, it was a waste of money and couldn't even get it back!!! The pool was green, it was a shack.

reviews.title: Bait and Switch- there is no pool
reviews.text: Shame on the hotel owners for showing a pool on the Expedia website and they have poured gravel into it and covered it over. We booked this hotel as we saw a pool. It has long since been covered by gravel and a patio-this wasn't done a couple weeks ago . The owners either want to draw people in knowing they can't cancel or are inept, On a positive note the room was very clean however it had three electrical outlets but only 2 were operational. Do not expect a view there are bars on the windows. Location is great- you can't get closer to Clifton Hill. If you want basic (yes I mean basic) accomodation and a clean room this works. I hope the owners update the pictures and represent their property correctly- No one likes a bait and switch. If the owners do not change the pictures they are intentioally misrepresenting their property and should be assamed of theirselves.

reviews.title: Nothing Family about the Family Inn!
reviews.text: ABSOLYETLY DISGUSTING! First when I check in, I couldn't. No one was working at the front desk. I walk into the motel and up and down the hallways and no one to be seen. I went to the attached restaurant and no one in the restuarant knew where the check-in person was, even though they are owned by the same man. Come back a few hours later and the line is forming and he is checking everyone in. He (the owner) tells everyone "you like your room; very clean room". Im sorry, if you need to go out of your way to say that, there is something wrong! Which there was. We go to our room and find pills and burnt foil in one drawer and a condom package on the floor. I report this and ask for a new room and he wouldnt accomodate me. He said "his guy mustn't have cleaned everything". We come back from a day of sightseeing and find the owner going up and down the halls and making us feel like we were being watched by a prison guard. Not fun! The following morning, our check out date, I was going to open the door and I find the owner patroling the hallways and he sees me and comes over to my door, says 'do you have a dog?' while trying to open my room door! I put my foot down on the base of the door and held the door. First- there was someone changing in my room, second- thats rude! I said no and that I was packing and going to start to load up my car to leave. I couldnt pack up quick enough and get out of there! I wouldn't even let my dog stay here!

reviews.title: You Get What You Pay For
reviews.text: Writing this from the hotel right now, Wifi is great and free. TV is ok, but needs more channels. Front desk folks are very nice. Room has a fridge and microwave. It's clean, but the chair is broken and the room needs lots of minor repairs. Door locks with a key. parking is $10 and there is no pool. Indian food at the onsite restaurant and a nice patio. Parking at other hotels here is $15 or more. Chain hotels run over $200 a night. I paid less than half that. Bottom line-if you are watching pennies this place is just fine.

reviews.title: Location location location
reviews.text: It is very important to remember that this motel is booked because of the location and the very cheap price (for the Niagara Falls area). The room is allright, the bed is not comfortable, but the restroom is actually fine, eventhough the water temperature keeps changing.
