reviews.text: hubby and i went to lake george for our 2 year anniversary, it was a last minute decision to go. hubby called all over 2 nights before we went up. most places only would do 2 nights minimum when he called the owner said they did 2 nights but decided he'd let us just do the 1 night. it was beautful view and everyone was very friendly. loved the cabin yes it was a little small but hey what do you expect? your in half a cabin but it was so cozy and very romantic for us. loved the fireplace and the best part was the night we were there, there was a fireworks show so we grabbed one of our blankets out of the car and sat down by the lake to watch them best view of fireworks ive ever seen. all in all i would totally go back there if we ever make it back to lake george.

reviews.title: Ultimate Relaxation
reviews.text: This was our first trip to Lake George and we loved it! We stopped at a couple of resorts before going to Alpine Village to compare rates. When we drove into Alpine Village we knew we found our place! The cabin we rented for the week was quaint and had a spectacular view of the lake. It was rustic, but clean and suited our needs. The beach area was very well kept as were the grounds. The Alpine Village made us feel like we were visiting family, rather than staying at a "hotel". The kids were perfectly content just swimming in the lake or playing ping pong. The breakfast was economical and very tasty!! We had a wonderful, relaxing vacation at Lake George and we will definitely be going back and look forward to staying in room 47 at Alpine Village!

reviews.title: Its like camping with all the comforts of a Motel!!!!
reviews.text: Me and my family just got back from a four day stay at Alpine Village. Ernie and Lillian could not have been nicer people. I did not tell them that my son was Diabetic and that I would need a fridge. Right away they brought one up to our room. This is a rustic lodge with cabins right smack dab on Lake George with a great little dock and a view to die for. I traveled with my husband,our 14 yr old and my 83 yr old father. Then my brother and nephew came up and ended up staying a night too. If you have small children, this is the place for you. These folks have everything your looking for if you want a fun but peaceful lake vacation. DO NOT miss the breakfast in the am!!!! Wow a ton of food for a small price. We will be back in the fall. I thank you Ernie and Lillian for a great vacation. We all had a fantastic time and look forward to visiting again. I live in Rhode Island and have stayed all over New England. Even though its kind of rustic, that is what you want when you stay on a lake. Go to the Hilton if Luxury is what you crave, but dont miss a chance to stay at this great little place. You will leave with a feeling like you just stayed at a summer camp. Loads and Loads of fun!!!!!!!

reviews.title: We only went to the fantastic breakfast at their restaurant.
reviews.text: We had read about how good it was, and it was delicious. On Monday, July 6th, I had the bacon, eggs, hash browns and toast, AND blueberry pancakes (which my daughter and I agreed to share on top of our meals), and orange juice. An hour later, I was stuffed. It was the best ambiance, the view looking down at the lake in the early morning, and surprisingly, there were only a few other diners. Our waitress was very friendly and attentive. Four of us ate for $37, my daughters having an omelet and eggs over easy, while my wife only had a bagel.

reviews.title: Our new vacation tradition!
reviews.text: Alpine Village was exactly what we were looking for. With two kids we wanted a carefree vacation spot and that's what this is. Safe and kid friendly and very relaxing. The restaurant offers breakfast only and it's very budget friendly and great food. You get to know the staff and they are a pleasure. We have already booked again for next season!

reviews.title: Great family getaway.
reviews.text: We are going back this year with even more family in tow. We fly into Albany and rent a car and drive up. There was a lot to do. The kids had a great time. Not gonna lie...it is rustic and things are outdated. However, you are not going there to expect a Hilton. It has charm and character. Great views for your morning coffee. The t.v.'s in the rooms are not the best and there are no video games. The town is so cute and great places to eat! We are looking forward to our week in August coming up.

reviews.title: excellent
reviews.text: We went to celebrate my husband birthday with my family. We had a wonderful time Lillian and Ernie were very helpful , we had to extend our stay. It was very sad when we came back to Queens.

reviews.title: Great Atmosphere - Great Value
reviews.text: This is one of the best kept secrets in the Lake George area. Although it is a resort with cabins, pool and lakeside activities, the breakfast s are open to the public. The food is consistently good and very reasonably priced. Our server left a full pot of coffee to indulge in after taking our order. My french toast and my wife’s egg whites were done perfectly. The workmanship and rustic appeal of this place is similar to what we experienced in our trips to Switzerland. Be sure to check out their website.

reviews.title: rustic resort with beautiful view
reviews.text: Stayed at the alpine village resort in late October and could not have asked for a better time. The views of the lake are remarkable especially with the fall foiliage. The resort itself was as expected rustic. If you are looking for the ritz and want to be pampered- go somewhere else. Read several bad reviews about the owners and was expecting the worse. Not a problem. They were very hospitable and seemed like generally nice folks. Cleaning service was prompt with ample towel supply. Fireplace in the cabin completed a great trip and would visit again.

reviews.title: no thrill log cabin
reviews.text: We booked a cabin at Alpine Village because we wanted a log cabin that's right on lake george, we also booked the week after their peak season to avoid crowds. When we first called Alpine Village to book, a very old man answered the phone, he was friendly, I asked for a log cabin, and he asked if I'd like the option of having a fire place or lake view, of course I went with lake view, provided my credit card information and dates. We had a long day upon arrival, and called the office around 8pm to let them know that we shall arrive around 11pm, the man who answered the phone says good thing I called, because the office closes at 10pm, then he provided very detail steps on how to locate our cabin, since it'll be dark when we arrive, he also said he'll leave the lights on in our cabin, and leave the key in the lock. We arrived around 11pm, found our cabin, settled in. The interior ceiling of the cabin was newly done, but everything else is old. The bath tub has plastic inserts to cover up the old tub, the vent in the bathroom is super loud, the towels leave small white lint all over our body, and the shower curtain keeps coming into the tub when the water's running out of the shower head, because the curtain is too light and the draft from the water keeps bringing it in, the air conditioner was very loud and actually blew out dust, the fridge is loud, too. We did have a lake view, our cabin was about 100 to 140 feet away from lake george, there were 2 lounge chairs on our own deck, there's a private beach with about 10 lounge chairs, there are boats and kayaks for rent on this private beach. Because we arrived after the office was closed, we ended up checking in on the second day. The wife of the owner was in the office, she mentioned that there's a 11% tax for credit card payment and no tax for cash payment. I gave her the total in cash and she had trouble counting it. I asked for a receipt and was giving a hand written note that's a quarter of a 8"x11" paper. The owner or the owner's wife did not care to speak to us or have any eye contact, but that's how lake george is when your skin color is not white. Ice from the ice machine is not free. We also found out there are cabins with fire place AND lake view! We would have rented that if we knew about it!

reviews.title: Wouldn't go back
reviews.text: We just got back from a week at Alpine Village Resort, and won't be returning next year. The accommodations were ok ... I wish I had know that a two bedroom unit with a kitchen wouldn't have a tv room. It weird to walk in the room directly into a bedroom, and have the kitchen attached to it, with no door or separation. If we wanted to watch tv with our family, we had no choice but to all lay in bed. Our room was pretty clean, but the AC is only in one bedroom (our kids room) and is a wall AC, so we sweated in our room while the kids froze in theirs. Our big problem was actually the other guests. We were in building H which contains 4 units (2 upstairs, 2 down). You all share the front porch, and enter through the same door. We were unfortunately there while 2 rooms were being used by one huge family that took over the front porch, and stayed outside drinking, yelling, cursing and fighting until 3am. We complained to the owners, but I don't know if they did anything about it, because it didn't make a bit of difference. My husband and I were woken up an average of 3 times a night. And having 2 young kids didn't make this a fun vacation. I thought it would be a family friendly place, but drunk belligerent guests does not scream "family vacation" to me. The beach area was small ... and always packed. We ended up going to the public beach. The towels were terrible, and the showers were the worst I've ever used. No water pressure. Also, as someone else said, the rooms were smoke free, but I smelled smoke a lot. Also, parking was terrible. Sometimes there were just no spots left. I think our experience was tarnished by the other guests, but I wouldn't stay here again because of that. And I wouldn't recommend it. I also don't understand how someone can take cash only, and have no money on hand to give change. I gave the owner $850 when my balance was 825$ and she couldn't figure out how much change to give me. She actually said "Ok, so I don't owe you any change, right?" I'm thinking that they could use someone slightly more business savvy in the office.

reviews.title: Had a Great Time!
reviews.text: We made reservations at the last moment, after booking the room I saw the reviews on this sight and was hesitant. I am so glad I did n't cancel at this property purely based on the reviews left here. We stayed in half a unit and I have absolutely NO complaints! I had two interactions with Lillian, both pleasant. Check in was quick and easy, our room was very clean. Clean sheets, towels, tub, toilet, floor, etc. The pool was extremly clean, and not overcrowded. The beach was clean and offered a great view of the Thursday evening fireworks. We ate in the restaurant, and the food was excellent and reasonably priced. This property is close to town and offers breath taking views of the lake for the price. As I told the owner, we will be back.

reviews.title: Great Place
reviews.text: nice family location, Ernie the owner is there to help you in anyway. Yes Cabins are a bit rustic but most are in Lake George. Clean rooms, great breakfast- best deal in Lake George. We have stayed here 3 or 4 times-whenever we do go to Lake George we stay here. Book early though as it is always full!

reviews.title: It was just what we wanted.
reviews.text: We went last minute looking for a motel. We wanted rustic as it was my guys first time to the adirondacks and he is from florida. We stopped at several motels and we came back to the Alpine. The price was great since it was pre-season. It was clean, the bath recently remodeled and a great view of the lake. The owner ( an older gentleman) was very friendly and helpful. We bought firewood, lit a fire in the stone fireplace, we had a fridge and a great view of the lake. It was a great place for the weekend and I love the memories. I will say our room was clean but the cabin we looked at next door did smell of cat urine or something.. so i can see how someone could be disappointed with that. Our room was great!

reviews.title: Best Breakfast and View
reviews.text: This beautiful lodge is open to the public for breakfast and we loved it. Very reasonable and we sat on a small balcony where we had a beautiful view of Lake George. Peaceful and private. We liked it so much we also checked out a cabin and have planned a vacation there.

reviews.title: Spoiled by inaccurately described rooms, and astoundingly rude owner.
reviews.text: On the upside, the location is nice. This didn't, though, offset the downsides. The 2-bedroom cabin was really a one bedroom where the living space had been converted into a second bedroom - there was nowhere to sit together. Oh well, we can live with that. It would have been nice if we didn’t have to clean the dirt from the inside of the fridge, though. Far worse was how we were treated by the owners/managers. My partner checked us in on arrival and when she returned to the car she reported that the woman who did the check-in (one of the owners) was surprisingly curt and abrupt. Not a hint of any sort of welcoming attitude. Again, oh well... We wanted to rent a rowboat so I eventually tracked down the other owner/manager to whom I gave a cash deposit and took away a set of oars, required for the boats down by the lake. I asked him if the procedure was that I return the oars when we had finished with them, since we needed them for that day as well as early the next morning (the oars are kept in the office which doesn't open until 9am, itself rather an inconvenience). The owner confirmed that this was fine. That evening we went out to dinner and on return discovered that someone had been into our cabin and removed the oars. I went to the office the next morning and mentioned this to the same woman who had first checked us in, who to my shock addressed me to my face as “the culprit” who had not returned the oars. When I pointed out that the person who had given me the oars had confirmed very clearly that we could keep the oars until the second day she basically accused me of being a liar. When I protested she literally turned her back on me and walked away, calling back that she was keeping our cash deposit. We left in disgust. So if you don’t mind rather shabby accommodation and rude and abusive ‘hosts’, have fun in the Alpine Village Resort! But you won’t be seeing me there.

reviews.title: Back for Our 2nd Year in A Row!
reviews.text: We visited Lake George and stayed at the Alpine Village the same time last year. You can see my previous review for specifics, but my review is basically the same this time around. We had a great time! We had such a great time last year that we were looking forward to coming back as soon as we pulled out of the driveway! This year we added an extra night and stayed for 4 nights/5 days - we are already talking about making it a week next year. This year we stayed in a 2 bed cabin with a front porch and back deck. I loved this room. It had an "updated" bathroom with great water pressure in the shower. Basic toiletries, but since you will likely bring your own it didn't matter. Each morning i had coffee on our deck overlooking the lake and each evening we had cocktails there as well. We had a small fridge that we kept stocked with snacks. One night we used the BBQ down by the lake. I am not sure what people are looking for when they get a room on lake george. Most of the "motels" there are similar in the fact that they are old and in need of updating. For the price we paid, in PEAK season, we couldnt have gotten better and we can't complain! We spent the days on a row boat on the lake and my 6 year old daughter could've fished for hours (and did!) on the dock. It is the kind of place that is reminiscent of days gone by, if you want glitz and glamour - good luck finding it elsewhere (go to the Sagamore) - if you are looking for long lazy days on the lake then Alpine Village is great. AV, is 1/2 mile from downtown LG and we took several trips there for dinner or walking around. It is close to all churches, markets and grocery stores too. My only complaint is that there could be some more amusements onsite - the ping pong table is great, but perhaps some horseshoes and bocce. The owners, Lillianne and Ernie, work their tail off. I respect them for their work ethic and honestly, although i know they have a reputation for being gruff, we've mostly only experienced their pleasant side. Like I said, we are already planning on a week stay in August 2013.

reviews.title: Nice, rustic, old style log cabin lodge and cabins
reviews.text: We recently stayed here for 2 nights; booked two adjoining rooms in the main lodge for a party of 4. The lodge and cabins are built on a hillside, approx. 1.5 acre property that is lake front. The buildings were built from the late 1930's to 1940's. This was exactly as I expected it to be ............. rustic charm. Ernest gives good, accurate descriptions of his rooms when you talk to him on the phone. They do not have a web site that is capable of making reservations, and I do believe that they book things "the old fashioned way" with a ledger and hand written receipts. We received just such a written receipt in the mail about a week after making the reservation. The rooms in the lodge are basic but clean. Ours had a small refrigerator and air conditioning and a relatively new looking shower insert. There was also in room heat which was needed in Oct. The lodge rooms are arranged on the 2nd floor on either side of a central staircase; you walk up a this large central staircase and the rooms are located on either side, down an open "walkway" which looks down on the living room/common room. Country decor that you would expect in an Adirondack style lodge. My only negative comment is that this is an older style lodge and like all older lodges/hotels/B&B's the rooms are not soundproofed. The open stairway leading to the 2nd floor does not lend itself to quiet either. In "full season" I imagine it could get kind of loud at times; people downstairs are easily heard in your room. I was prepared for this and came prepared with earplugs and a small "sound conditioner". The bed was comfortable and all the people in the lodge for the two nights we were there were quiet and respectable. Alpine Village has a small "beach" with lounge chairs, a restaurant that is open during the main tourist season (closed after Labor Day weekend) that is popular in the region for breakfast. Nice view from the covered back porch and Adirondack chairs. There are approx. 10-12 cabins of various layouts on the property; you would have to contact Ernie & Lillian for descriptions as each is a bit different in their layout. Only the lodge back porch and cabin #10/!11 (which is a dublex that can be rented separately or together) have an unobstructed view of the lake as far as I could tell. Some cabins sit back a bit from the lake and the only view would be a bit through the trees, but only a very short stroll to the lakeside. Overall a very nice place to stay as long as your expectations are in line with a rustic (but clean) log cabin style accomodation. Ernie and Lillian are nice people.

reviews.title: We enjoyed lake george.
reviews.text: First time at Alpine Village, after reading the prior reviews wanted to experience it for myself along with family members. We enjoyed Lake George very much, the property is large and has a lot of potential. All the cabins my family and I stayed at neither of them had a living room. Everyone had to hang out on someone's bed. The cleaning situation could have been better, so we were prepared with wipes and air fresheners. Ernie seems like he tries his best to make everyone happy. The rooms carpet seem as if it had not been vacuumed ever. I found empty bottles and debris under one of my kids bed. Which means they never vacuumed before we got there.. It is a very rustic place and although I will never stay there again, overall we had a great time and made the best of it. The pool needed repair and the mosquitos in the area needed immediate attention. The water pressure in the shower was so bad I almost got burned with the hot water not being balanced. We were there for Hurricane Irene, the main lodge had a generator but none of the cabins had electricity for 18 hours. They say no pets allowed but they have their own dog running around the property. The only good thing about this place is their main lodge breakfast it was awesome and reasonably priced.

reviews.title: Rustic and serene
reviews.text: This is a very special place tucked away on the beautiful Lake George. The owners obviously take pride in their resort and go out of their way to accommodate your every need while you are on vacation there. There is great variety in lodging, from a lodge room to small cabins, to larger housekeeping cabins. I have been here twice and will be back again.

reviews.title: AWFUL! STAY AWAY!!! OWNERS ARE IN IT FOR ONLY THE $!
reviews.text: Where to even begin... I checked into alpine village with a large family reunion. Upon checking in I was told that you can only put $100 on a credit card the rest needs to be CASH?! Whoever heard of such a thing, sounds a little weird to me... Next I go up to my room where the air condition does not work... Not to mention the rooms are absolutely disgusting. I find the owner and let him know that the air was not working. He gave me every excuse possible of why it wasn't blowing cold air. Finally I told him it does not work!! He then proceeds to come back with a knob for it thinking that would solve the problem... it didn't obviously. He then tells me he is going to show me another room for a little bit more money. $250 more money!! I said i was not paying that because his air condtion was not working in my room. He then reels and deals me to pay an extra $100 (which I never payed) We get into this room and it is not very clean but whatever it was vacation. My daughter than arrives with a friend and go to lay down and check there beds... There was HAIR, DIRT, and A CANDY WRAPPER on the sheets!!!!!!! The next morning my daughter goes to ask the owner Lillian for new sheets bc hers were not clean, Lillian says okay she will bring them right up. Next thing I know there is Lillian knocking on the door telling me we are nit picking the room and we can get out! She tells my daughter she is "unprofessional and stupid." She leaves and next comes Ernie yelling saying we can have everything out of the room at 11 and can leave. Finally my husband got him to calm down and showed him the issues and he said "I'm sure there candy wrappers in your bed at home" UNBELIEVABLE. We made him look under the bed where it was so disgusted with globs of dust and dirt, no one have vacuumed in years. Also the air condition in this room had an inch of dust on it. We checked to see vacancy at other places so that we could leave this dump but unfortunately no where else had vacancy for my boat. Ernie let us stay and said "if we say one more thing we are out!" Also if you go to bbq I hope you have water shoes bc it is soaking wet all the time down there. Ernie and Lillian were the rudest people. You would think they would be happy getting over making everyone pay CASH! Please DO NOT stay here. All of my family rooms had issues, one had to change there bedding with stuff they brought from home and also found a used butter knife on the TV. Alpine Village is a joke and you can spend your money much more wisely! This place is a dump and the owners don't appreciate or want to make there customers happy.

reviews.title: Charming and rustic
reviews.text: We stayed here for 3 nights with a family group of 16. We has 5 groups and stayed in 4 different types of accommodations. All were clean and suited each groups' needs just fine. We didn't get warm-fuzzies from the owners when planning and booking but, maybe because we didn't need anything special and didn't get too disruptive, all of our interactions were uneventful. We had a great time at the lodge: played games on the huge porch when it rained, played volleyball, took the canoe out, swam, and had great family meals (take out) under the gazebo. It's not pristine or upscale but not dirty or run-down either. I will definitely stay there next time I go to lake George.

reviews.title: A great family experience !
reviews.text: My husband & my son and his family had a wonderful time at the Alpine Ernie & his family made us feel right at home. Our grandchildren can't wait until next year. The rooms were clean and comfortable the maids gave us fresh towels every day. The pool was great & the lake was beautiful! We enjoyed the fireworks what a beautiful sight. We want to thank Ernie, Lillian & Jay for our wonderful vacation. See you next year! Our grandchildren are looking forward to seeing Katie & Will again.

reviews.title: Weekend getaway
reviews.text: We needed to get away from the hustle and bustle of business ownership. We found the Alpine resort to be not only very accomodating, but also clean and neat. Though it is rustic, it is very well kept and very well maintained, every light bulb was lit ,The owners and staff were wonderful to be around. In our opinion one of the adirondacks best kept secrets. Can,t wait to book for the next relaxing retreat. The in house breakfast is an added bonus for a price that can,t be beat. T&J Church Wynantskill N.Y.

reviews.title: below average
reviews.text: Thought that the negative comments were exaggerations but they were spot on !Dirty towels, linens and rude owner (lilian ) told me one price and cabin on the phone only to find that I was over charged and my cabin was given away to a returning guest. Shame on you !!! We won't be back.

reviews.title: Dirty Shack.....
reviews.text: Planned to stay a week, left after one night......You get 1/2 a cabin, the room is tiny and filthy, bedcover and drapes look like they haven't been cleaned in ages, carpet was filthy and stained. Bathroom was also disgusting, shower curtain had mold on it. The fireplace is an accident waiting to happen, check smoke detector if you decide to stay at this dump. We could hear the other guests in adjoining cabin/room shower,flush,cough, everything!...Then share outside common porch with them, very awkward. The beach does not have white sand, it's raked dirt and shared with a private boat mariner, water is murky and full of weeds, needless to say, very unappealing..imo In my opinion, this place is a DUMP!, to avoid at all costs!.....Just read the multitude of Bad Reviews, find a much better place for your precious vacation time somewhere else, there's a ton of them available.

reviews.title: Will NEVER go back!
reviews.text: Check in at three...NO. The elderly woman owner kept putting us off saying it was being cleaned. Forty-five minutes after the check-in time I inquired again..this time with the cleaning ladies. They said it was ready. Went to get a key from office and again had the not-so-nice owner say she did not have a key..but finally found one. There were ants and sesame seeds/crumbs on the table in kitchen. Carpenter ants in bathroom as well. After a couple nights I SAW a mouse run across the room under the bed I was sleeping in. The next night a smaller baby mouse actually jumped out of my luggage bag. Mouse droppings were on my clothes and all over the kitchen upon waking up. I brought a shirt covered in mouse droppings into the office and asked if there were any mouse free rooms. I was yelled at and told by the woman "this is the Adirondacks and they are all over my house when I return from Florida". I also mentioned ants. She she, "what do you want Earnie to do, spray?" I said spray what, and was yelled at again. I said I have children and don't want toxins on top of everything else. I was actually blamed for "bringing food into the place" . Go figure, it has a kitchen. Next day, I noticed 3 rotten oranges left behind from previous people on top of a cabinet. Everyone I spoke to agreed that their place was dirty too. Since we brought our boat, we were thankfully out on the lake all day and not so much in the room..At times, sitting on the deck of our building, we could smell sewage! They really need to get people in there to update and make this a more pleasant stay. Towels actually ripped they were so paper thin. It does have potential for being a great resort since the location is excellent. Earnie was quite helpful, as he fixed a running faucet in the kitchen and a leaking pipe. Stay away if you want clean rooms that are rodent free!

reviews.title: Charming
reviews.text: Just returned from 3 nights at Alpine Village in Lake George NY. This is a lovely property, well kept, nice pool and beach. We went with another couple, and we had a "duplex" cabin with a shared porch. It was perfect for allowing each couple their own bedroom and bathroom but gave us a place to gather for drinks and evening chats on the porch. The cabins are very rustic....a bit of a step back in time. However, the air conditioner worked great, the bed was comfortable and there was cable television, so it was perfectly fine. Breakfast is served in the main building...delicious and inexpensive! $1.75 for one egg and 2 slices of toast! T The property is on a bit of a hill, so getting to our "duplex" was tough for me as I have trouble walking. There are plenty of cabins though, and not all of them are up the hill. So, if it's an issue for you, just ask when you reserve for a cabin that is easily accessible. It was very apparent that many of the guests come back year after year and I can see why. It's a reasonably priced resort in a great location on a beautiful lake.

reviews.title: Do not give this place a try!
reviews.text: I booked a room here in June 2012 for a 3 day stay in September for a friend's wedding. I had read reviews (good and bad) and thought I would try the place out for myself. The owner asked me to send a check for half the total as a deposit. A little strange but ok. When we arrived to the motel on Friday afternoon at 3:15 pm there was a sign on the office door that said "be back at 4pm" and a phone number at the bottom of the sign. Since we had to be at the rehearsal dinner at 5 on the other side of the lake, I called the number and told the man that answered who I was and I wanted to check in. He said, " Well I guess that sign didn't mean anything." I said, "Well you left a number to call and I need to check in. We have a dinner to attend at 5pm and need to freshen up." He said," Take a deep breath and go look at the lake." I replied, " I don't want to look at the lake. I want to check in." He said, "Fine, I'll be there in 10 minutes." After looking around at the dark, dingy, musty smelling lobby I began to think I had made a terrible mistake. The gentleman arrived about 10 minutes later, telling us he had an emergency to attend to. I gave him my name again and he couldn't find my reservation. He asked if i received a confirmation and I said that I had and that it was at home. He replied sarcastically," That's a good place for it." I was so shocked I couldn't believe this man was chastising me for something I have NEVER had to do at any other hotel or motel I've stayed at. I have never been asked for a reservation/confirmation receipt! I explained that I had sent my check in June and even showed him the record in my check register. He even asked me how did I know his wife received the deposit check and I said that I knew because I had gotten the confirmation receipt in the mail! He said that his wife must have made a mistake and he didn't have a room for us. He asked me if I knew what room we were supposed to be in and I said, "15 or 16" He kept asking me to spell my last name which I did 4 or 5 times and kept looking at a chart on a desk stating we were not on the chart. He told us they were completely booked for the car show that weekend and there wasn't anything available. Another guest for the wedding walked into the lobby and heard my conversation and whispered to me, "They said the same thing to me." Apparently their reservation system leaves much to be desired. I was beginning to feel panicky as this was an important wedding for us to attend and now were being told they didn't have a room that I reserved in June! I was not happy! I felt like he kept looking for ways to blame me for him not keeping good records. After our insisting we did have a reservation, he finally said that he did have a room! So out of the blue a room appears?? He looked into a rusty file cabinet in the office and finally found the carbon copy of the our reservation. He said," I have a room with a queen bed available. It's room 16." And I said, " Yeah that's my room." He offered an apology but the damage was done! The room was something out of a youth summer camp and not a good one. Indoor/ outdoor in carpeting in the bedroom, white wash clothes stuffed into the crevices at the ceilings in the bathroom and bedroom, a door between our bedroom and another room that was so thin you could hear everything that was going on, a coffee maker and microwave that looked like they were from 1985, and no coffee for the coffee maker! The towels were slightly larger than a hand towel and worn so thin I would have used them for rags. There was only one very tiny trash can and that was in the bathroom. A cloth shower curtain hung in the bath with a note on the wall asking to keep the curtain inside the tub! There wasn't even a plastic curtain to keep the water in! The windows were dirty and filled with spider webs and dead insects as was the light in the bedroom. I expect the Adirondacks to be rustic but not disgusting. As for the service...we asked for someone to look at our TV since the picture went fuzzy. The woman in the office, I'm going to assume this was Lillian, said that it was because of the storm that went through but we told her it was like that before the storm. She said that she would have it looked at. When we returned to the motel later that day at 8 pm, the TV was still fuzzy, so bad that you couldn't see numbers on the football players' jerseys. So, back to the office my fiance went. He came back with the man who almost didn't check us in, after looking at the connection in the adjoining room, he determined the cable booster had been unplugged by the previous guests. The room hadn't been cleaned yet after the guests left. The owner said we could watch TV in that room if we wanted to! I wasn't about to occupy a room that hadn't been cleaned from its previous guests and reeked of cigarette smoke, even though the motel supposedly has a no smoking policy for all its rooms. By the way, our room had an ashtray on the table! The wedding was the highlight of the weekend but this poorly managed, archaic motel with rude, uncaring owners was just unacceptable! Please do yourself a favor and try another establishment. This place needs Hotel Impossible!!

reviews.title: Overpriced and Filthy
reviews.text: It was very dirty, there was mold in the bathroom which smelled like a urinal, and a hole in the screen door was lazily plugged with paper. The floors looked like they hadn't been vacuumed in 20 years and the furniture had layers of dust. For anyone who says this place is clean I dare them to take a glance underneath the bed in their room or look out the window which looks like it hadn't been cleaned in years. The beds were extremely uncomfortable, each person in our group complained about the state of their mattress--6 beds, not one of them was comfortable. When we reserved the room they also did not mention that the rooms were railroad style. So we had to walk through the other bedroom to use the bathroom. Additionally, they would only take cash or personal check, but then display the visa and mastercard logos on their office door. And they require a credit card to hold the room---but you can't pay for the room on the card. The cheapness of the owners continued when we asked if they had a couple packets of sugar and said "we could buy them in town." There is a restaurant on premises AND we stated that we forgot to pick up some sugar. The dish soap in the kitchen was watered down and the stove wasn't working when we arrived but, to their credit, they did get it working once we complained. I think if they hired a few more housekeepers this place could be great. Check out is at 11 and check in is at 3, in those four hours the room should be thoroughly cleaned and everything should be checked to make sure its working properly--but this obviously doesn't happen. They should also invest in some new mattresses. The one upside is that the grounds are beautiful and there is a great view to watch the Thursday night fireworks. So if you aren't planning on spending alot of time in your room and you don't mind dust, mold and a greasy, unclean kitchen--this might be the place for you. Oh! And there are no pets allowed, which was great for our group b/c many of us have allergies but when we arrived there was a dog and cat in the main lodge. I also found dog hairs on the carpet in our room.

reviews.title: shock and awe
reviews.text: Great location and small private beach with rustic setting of log cabins and main lodge on Lake George. Breakfast at the lodge each day was ok, basic and wait staff was most pleasant. When making reservations we were quoted a price which was higher than website. When we noted that, adjustment was made the day we arrived. They only take cash when checking in so bring money! The room was a typical log cabin with fireplace, widow AC, and old fashioned screens on windows and door. Alpine Village is a great place to be, cheaper than other locations and that is where it stops. Our room really had not been cleaned thoroughly from the previous guest or others we suspected. Although there is no smoking permitted in the cabins, when we entered the room, there was a smell of cigarette smoke masked spray and by the AC on full blast and a rug that looked like it really needed vacuuming. The next morning I awoke with a major sore throat and swollen glands. I noticed the AC filter and casing was filthy and probably had not been changed/cleaned for a long time, the blind above were caked with dust and the floor had not been vacuumed or cleaned for a period of time. I asked Ernie to attend to this. He quickly got housekeeping to take down and wash the blind, vacuum the floor and he changed the filter. Housekeeping leaves a lot to be desired. I was there one day and the only thing that was done was the bed was made, new soap and towels (paper thin) were replaced. That took all of five minutes at best. There were no cleaning products for the toilet, tub or sink or even a vacuum cleaner on hand. The tub ( which had black mildew on the treads), had not been cleaned for the entire time we were there. I asked another house keeper to come in and vacuum (you can't do much to a rug with a stick vac), mentioning there was dirt tracked in from the beach and hair on the bathroom floor. It was given a lick and a promise at best. Housekeeping is sorely lacking. There is no excuse for lack of cleanliness. After having read reviews before we got there, I brought my own, wipes, Lysol, clorox all purpose cleaning solution, insect spray. They all came in handy. The bedding , not only sheets, really had to be freshened up and washed. Without the AC on, there was a body odor/funny smell. It was like camping out but in a log cabin! To be fair, we had been there years ago and the place was now much improved in terms of modern bathroom, not 1930's metal shower stall., improvements made with ceilings and lighting, fridge in the room, and an outdoor pool replacing the old tennis courts. The setting can't be beat. Should you stay at Alpine Village, just take precautions mentioned and do tell Ernie about it. He will try to make things work and wants to please. Bypass his wife Lillian. By the time we left, our room looked good! We showed it to other guests and they said it looked better than theirs!

reviews.title: Reunion
reviews.text: Ernie required a 200 dollar deposit for our 4 day stay. No where on his web page did it say,”No Pets” My wife and I drove over 14 hrs from central Kentucky, upon arrival we were told No Pets, our dog would have been in her little container/kennel. I am a disabled Veteran and this stay was an Army Reunion. The owner/Ernie said no refund on deposits for cancellations under 14 days. My wife and had to find other accommodations. It was my fault for not calling prior, but it would have been nice, better business practice, if No Pets was mentioned on the web page!

reviews.title: Bed bugs
reviews.text: There were bed bugs in our room. I brought them home in my suitcase, and I had to deal with the long process of getting rid of them. It ruined my summer. We had one of the duplex style log cabins. Be VERY careful and check your beds.

reviews.title: You're On The Lake
reviews.text: This is our fourth year in a row coming here. More family and friends in tow. We've been coming to LG for over 30 years. Stayed at many places. Alpine is on the lake in a cove with calm water. You can walk on Alpines beach,which is lake beach sand and will harden up with lots of rain,float or swim over the natural grass a few feet under the water and only a few yards off the beach,to a clam cove area of LG. I say because you can't swim at any other hotel on LG the waves and wakes will exhaust you. My kids love fishing off Alpines docks. It's the best place to stay. Yes we are in the Adirondacks. It is rustic. It's been serving vacationers for over 70 years. As I said before...Relax and Enjoy

reviews.title: great breakfast, great prices, understaffed dining room
reviews.text: We ate here for 3 breakfasts because we enjoyed the food and ambience so much. It was very picturesque, the building was pretty and they served ample, very good food, but the wait staff were short handed and we had to wait awhile 2 of the days. It was the best place we ate breakfast in terms of the food.

reviews.title: Hard to find lovely rustic retreat
reviews.text: We usually stay in Maine in a similar log cabin style resort and know it's hard to find this kind of environment, where you just mellow out as soon as you see the main inn and cabins. It has a beautiful location with lovely lake views and well tended grounds. Our room was clean and comfortable, room 48, near the pool. Ernie and Lillian were very cordial towards us and as landlords, we know that sometimes whatever you do it's not enough to satisfy some people. I have a hard time understanding the nastiness of some of the reviews and fortunately, I had not read any of them before reserving our room. We only wished we could have stayed longer and look forward to going back and savoring being at the Alpine Village. Ernie also told us about a great restaurant when we asked about German food, and our dinner at the Pumpernickel up the road was excellent. Being an inn keeper is very hard work and the owners deserve more respect than some reviewers have shown; I'm fairly critical in evaluations usually and I say thumbs up here!

reviews.title: Alpine Village is so much fun!
reviews.text: We have been staying at Alpine Village for years, and we have not found anything that comes this close to an old-fashioned family vacation. The real log cabins are unique, rustic and quaint. The beach is perfect for our 10 year old and toddler, very shallow and calm. The grounds are always so pretty and the view from the lodge and dining room is spectacular. It's family run, the owners always there to help, and very reasonably priced. My daughter has friends she sees every year, because so many families return year after year. We have stayed at other places, but just can't help but to keep returning to Alpine Village.

reviews.title: will definitely come to Alpine Village again
reviews.text: Glad I didn't fully believe "A trip to Hell would have been a better experience." After reading all the other reviews, which were very good, I decided to take a chance and booked a 2 bedroom cabin. The rooms were very clean and could not find a single bug, certainly not a cockroach. I was told cockroaches can't survive here due to the very cold winters. Also, the entire resort is very well kept and their breakfast is simply outstanding. We will definitely come back to ALPINE VILLAGE again.

reviews.title: My Family Stays Here Every Summer!
reviews.text: This was our 7th year straight staying at the Alpine Village. My family travels with our friends and we usually get neighboring cabins. This is NOT the Waldorf Hotel by any means. If you are looking for that good luck anywhere in LG. It is a simple, rustic place that is reasonably priced and well maintained by good, hardworking people. We particularly like the view of the beach to the lake, the swimming pool, and the location to town. The place has plenty of parking. The restaurant in the lodge truly does make a great breakfast which is moderately priced and very convenient. The family that runs the place (the Ipish family) are nice people. If you are nice to them, they are usually nice to you. The rooms are reasonably clean but have a cabin feel to them. Some rooms have fireplaces, others have kitchens. If you have a special need for kitchen appliance ask before you book because the supply in each of the rooms is inconsistent. We have never had any major problems and the staff is very accommodating. WiFi does suck, but I was told the motel plans to upgrade next year!

reviews.title: Cheap and cute
reviews.text: I was nervous after reading some of the reviews. I was pleasantly surprised when we arrived though. Although the bathroom and beds could of been cleaner the cabin was cute and reasonably priced. I brought Clorox wipes to wash down the bathroom and brought a sleeping bag which I put on the bed. The cabin we stayed in had a double bed and a twin bed, a small fridge, and a TV. The beach is nice, and the walk to it was better then some of the others I've had to walk down to. The beach chairs are wooden which were a little uncomfortable. I brought my own chair so I used that. You can use the canoe or rowboats after putting down a $20.00 deposit for the paddles. We ate breakfast at the resort and were very happy with it. My one complaint would be that we didn't get our debit card back after we checked in. We thought we lost it while at dinner. The next day while we were in the office, the man said he had been looking for us all day/night. We were back in the room by 8:30pm if they had left a note on the room door to go to the office we wouldn't have had to cancel the debit card!!!!

reviews.title: Great place we loved it! I just went the week of July 12 to July 20 With the family and we had a great time. Great price and the
reviews.text: We had a great time rooms were clean and we had fresh towel everyday ! It you like plush troweled I would recommend you than your the breakfast is ok d For the most part and very reasonable! We will for sure Jo back next year!

reviews.title: Real Log Cabin vacation
reviews.text: 37 years ago we spent our HoneyMoon here. We have been back many times with our kids and now for long weekends by ourselves. Very picturesque property. Nestled into a hillside are some dozen or so cabins built circa 1930s or so. They are real log cabins with stone fireplaces and adirondack porches with chairs all facing the lake. The main house is full of memorabilia. Breakfast is a hoot with flapjacks and eggs called by a dinner bell!$5 gets you all the wood you can carry for your fireplace.This all happens under a canopy of massive evergreens.It is located a mile or so up the road from central Lake George.Bathrooms and tv are basic. Beds are ancient but comfortable.Just bring extra pillows and blankets. Have to say that even with its age and basic facilities. Alpine village will give you great memories as it has for us and our kids.

reviews.title: A Great time even 25 years later!!!!!!!
reviews.text: I started going to Lake George in 1986(when I was 15).. As life moves on this was the first time I have been since 1998(Iam now 39).. The place is filled with fun and a great atmosphere for children. I highly recomend this place for a great vacation or reunion for family and friends. I will be calling the owners in January to book for next summer....

reviews.title: Hell would have been a better experience
reviews.text: We were told on the phone that the cabin has a lake front view, 2 fireplaces, internet, and is secluded and far away from everyone. We drove down there in good faith but when we got there, we realized that the cabin was so small it can barely fit the double bed, the fireplaces were not working, it was right on the highway and you can hear all the traffic and the entire complex was small like a very seedy motel, unmaintained, dirty and filled with bugs and not wilderness bugs either but big cockroaches and ants. When we chose not to check in and asked for a refund, the owners became hostile and rude. The woman brought out her husband who was uneducated, loud and refused to admit that they lied. He kept screaming and cursing and attempting to scare us. They basically ruined our trip. They give the area of Lake George a bad name and should be ashamed of themselves. Just because they are running their business into the ground doesn’t mean that they should lie and take advantage of unsuspecting tourists. Go there at your own risk.

reviews.title: I Never come back and recommend stay away from this ,I' don't want to say ,hotel
reviews.text: I would have to say that my stay wasnt as welcoming as I imagined. I made a reservation in advance and asked regarding a crib and when we arrived I was charged $5 a day. Noone told me over the phone that a crib is going to be addition money. The owner is very unfriendly and not sympathic. The hotel seems like its 50 years old and since then never remodeled. The towels look old and it seems like they never been renewed.We left our bbq sticks at the rest area and when returned they were missing. Approached owner she said thats impossible and the next day came back saying its possible but didnt even apologize. I have been to Lake George over a dozen of times but this is so far the worst hotel I have stayed in. Would never recommend this to anyone. The lake is wonderful.

reviews.title: We Are Already Planning Next Year's Visit!"
reviews.text: We just returned last night from a long weekend at the Alpine Village (8/13-8/15) and are planning to return next year! I read the reviews on here before we left for our trip and some of the negative ones really had me nervous. When I got there and experienced it for myself i knew that i wanted to write a review and describe our visit once i got home. My husband, 5 year old daughter and I decided last minute to go to Lake George during the busiest time of the year. Alpine Village is sold out from May through mid October. We called them based on a recommendation we received. They had a cancellation that was just received so we were able to snatch up that cabin. Lillian was the person my husband dealt with to make the reservation and she was quite pleasant. Despite some negative comments here, she was very nice to us the entire weekend. Our room was sufficient. It had a queen bed, chair, desk, decent size mini fridge, dresser and fireplace. A window AC unit and bathroom with shower/tub, sink and toilet. The rug was stained, but the room overall was what i expected for a lakeside cabin. It was confortable and provided what we needed. Btw, i didn't see any bugs, rodents or anything else that wasn't supposed to be in our room! We had a covered porch that was shared with the family in the attached cabin. We had plenty of room to sit there and have wine and enjoy the scenery. Alpine VIllage is ideally located. It is about a mile to downtown LG and right on the beach! we had our own sandy beach with very comfortable resort like beach chaise lounges. We had access to a dock, several row boats, canoes and kayaks were at our disposal. My daughter fished off the dock and row boat and caught her first fish. She was thrilled! There is a nice swimming pool with tables and chairs surrounding it as well as a covered picnic area and several grills for cooking out. There was also a swing set. The main Great Room offered a wonderful breakfast for the best price anywhere with a full view of the lake. There were plenty of chairs on the main building deck where we could take cover from the sun or rain and still enjoy the beautiful scenery and spend time with the other families. There was a ping pong table and it was in constant use. The grounds were impeccably maintained and made a very good first impression. There was not a single piece of trash anywhere on the property! The owners work hard all day and obviously take great pride in their property. The only thing that i didn't like was that they could use more games, maybe horseshoes and another ping pong table - the one they had seemed to be monopolized by one family the entire weekend. I also wish that there was a small store in the great room, just big enough to sell some snacks/sweets maybe a bottle of wine. But there was a general store right up the road and like i said the village was only a mile away. If you are looking for more amenities or more hotel like accomodations, this may not be the best option for you. But our weekend there was reminiscent of old time family vacations in the mountains. Very relaxing, fresh air, long days outside and plenty of kids for playmates. We plan to go back next August, this time for a few more days!

reviews.title: relaxing and enjoyable
reviews.text: we were very pleased with our stay at Alpine Village. There was a real effort to make us comfortable in every way. Ernie the owner is a wonderful guy. It was a heat spell and the pool was clean and inviting. Clean, homey, not elegant

reviews.title: Come here if you like throwing your money away
reviews.text: We had never been to the Lake George area but came on a last-minute whim for the Columbus Day weekend, as pretty much everything else around Vermont / New Hampshire was booked. If you haven't been to Lake George before, it is chock-full of aging "resorts" scattered all around the lake, which may have been nice in the 80s. There are a few that I am sure ARE nice, but you have to fork over several hundred dollars for those. This place charged $100 a night, with a two-night minimum. As others have said, they state over the phone they prefer cash (so they don't get hit with credit card merchant fees I guess). It is an old couple that runs the place, and they probably should have given up the business years ago. The first place we were put it is literally less than 50 feet from the road, so you hear cars zooming by at all hours - not what I would say is relaxing. There are the "fireplaces" in those units, but no wood provided and I would be afraid that it doesn't have proper ventilation - it seemed very ramshackle. We moved to a "lakefront" unit that was above the pool, with no fireplace, but at least it was quieter. Neither unit had a kitchen, so I'm not sure which of the ones others are talking about DO have kitchens. We tried to back out of staying here, but the owner/manager said if we left he would charge our card. Everything here is nickel-and-dime. No coffee provided, no filters, one old disposable cup. No breakfast, I guess because it was late season. No ice for free - the machine takes coins. No "do not disturb" signs, so we were about to have intimate time and then the housekeeping lady banged on the door in the morning, so there goes that. We had no heat the first night, because apparently the owner had the breaker shut off. To my knowledge, all the units are "duplex" units so it is difficult to have any true privacy / quiet. We had a loud family next to us, with people stomping up and down the stairs all night and all morning, and when the shower runs, it is a deafening sound, as if the water is pouring out feet away. The WiFi also was very poor, except for if it was late and no one else was using the signal (can't handle multiple users at once). So, what did we get for $100 a night? A roof over our heads, and that is about it. It was NOT a relaxing weekend, and we will never come back here.

reviews.title: Love Alpine!
reviews.text: I just got back from another perfect vacation at Alpine. My family & I have been staying here for a number of years now, and each stay just gets better then the last. Ernie & his family have never been anything but very kind, and they work very hard to make sure their guests enjoy their stay. I've stayed in the main lodge, and log cabins, and each time was very pleased with everything. It's very charming and rustic, everything a resort in the Adirondacks should be. There is delicious breakfast in the main lodge each morning with amazing prices, and friendly service. The beach is well kept, great for fishing, docking your boat, and offers rowboats to take out on the lake. The best feature is the porch on the main lodge that overlooks the lake. My family and I love to sit out there. Alpine is conveniently located close to the LG village, and Bolton Landing. Some of my best memories are from Alpine Village. I wouldn't stay anywhere else! Thanks Ernie & family!

reviews.title: Will keep going back!!!
reviews.text: This was are 2nd time we stayed here and plan on going back every year now. I found Alpine Village on the internet last year. I read all the reviews and can only agree with the ones that are good. The log cabins are rustic, the rooms were clean both times we stayed and the real fireplaces are a bonus.The main lodge has a resturant and the food is quite good. The resturant does close in late October a week or two before the owners close up for the season. The views from the cabins are great. A great place to sit in the morning and late afternoon and watch the sun come up and go down. The beach is clean and there is a boat dock that you can walk onto and take in the lake and the view of the mountains which by the way is breathe taking. Ernie the owner is very nice and has been very helpful whenever we had a question on where to go and what to do. He knows Lk George like the back of his hand and his recommendations have always been right on. Alpine Village is great place to stay and would recommend it to anybody.

reviews.title: Cozy
reviews.text: This place is by far my favorite type of lodging. Nicely furnished and nice people. Breakfast from 830-11, we stayed in room 1. It had three beds: 2 fulls and 1 queen. Nice little kitchenette. Needs some entertainment when weather is bad : i.e. Board games or cards. But the grocery store and rite aid has cards and games.

reviews.title: Not as bad as most reviews stated.
reviews.text: For the price its not bad at all $1300 for a 7 day stay for 5 people. Right on the lake cant complain with the price. Every other resort in the area with lake and dock access is atleast double the price. Most of the reviews ive read people are expecting a luxury stay on a budget. Ive stayed at places a bit worse for the same price. The owner can be a bit grumpy, but i think its cause people complain about stuff as posted above no free coffee, no free fire wood. Its a budget resort again. For the price i would stay again of visiting lake george. Thurs nite great view of fireworks from beach at resort as well. 2 min trolley ride into town also which is $1pp.

reviews.title: Very Unique Traditional Experience. Old Fashioned, Not Fancy, But Fun. Recommended.
reviews.text: Booked a week's stay in log cabin number 10. The entire resort is a bit of a throw back - almost like it's in a time warp. Not for a person who needs a lot of amenities but if you want to and want your family to experience a real "country" visit this is a great place. Cabin #10 was very close to the pool and beach area. Its balcony overlooked the lake. The cabin with two double beds while very basic and similar to cabins at the National Parks, had a working stone fire place, modernized bathroom and a mini-fridge and microwave and a coffee maker that all worked fine. Many places on Lake George have long and narrow properties with motel style rooms lining the sides of the road going to the lake. Alpine village is a large property with more of a crescent layout. The main lodge is at the top of the road, but the way the property is laid out - no lodging is too far from the pool, grills or pool. The main lodge lobby is all logs and very traditional. The breakfast restaurant which is in the main lodge is more reasonably priced than any other breakfast around. It has a nice menu and some outdoor seating overlooking the lake. All together the hotel was a great experience in spite of the sand-paper towels. The pool area was very safe and secure, the property very well maintained. Enjoyed the week tremendously and was happy we stayed here. Must bring your own beach towels.

reviews.title: Loved It!
reviews.text: After reading some of the negative reviews, we were almost "spooked" enough to cancel our reservations for this resort- but we decided to give it a chance, and were we glad we did! We would have missed out on a really neat place to vacation. While the "rustic" log cabin lodge resort is not for everyone, it was exactly the kind of place we enjoy-from the exposed log walls in the lobby and even the bathrooms, to the gorgeous stone fireplace, and our favorite, the wrap around porch with huge log posts with a lovely view of the property and lake (where we could also relax with a paper and cup of coffee and watch the kids run around in the grass and play ping pong)-this resort was very homey and comfortable, with definite character. It is not a luxury hotel, and definitely not a cookie cutter chain hotel, but a neat place for those looking for something a little different. Being just a short way north of the "village"- and surrounded by trees, this resort seemed secluded from the crowds, which was nice. Although the private beach area is kind of small, it is still right on the lake, and enables guests to wade into the lake for a swim, or jump in one of the boats provided and take a ride out on the lake-which we did every day and enjoyed so much. The location on the lake was great. The pool was nice, and having plenty of grass for the kids to run and play was nice. There were just enough other guests to provide opportunity to meet new folks if you like,and the kids to find playmates, but is was suprisingly quiet and uncrowded in the resort. We enjoyed cooking out on the grills provided and had a picnic dinner in the pavilion one evening. The rooms are a little on the smaller side (we had a 2 room suite in the main lodge), but clean and nice enough, and most of our time was not spent in our rooms anyway-we had no complaints about the rooms. As for the owners, and some of the bad reviews- we had nothing but good service and and both were very courteous and friendly. Ernie even took the time to sit and talk to us a few times, telling us a bit of the history of the resort. We really enjoyed this resort and would definitely stay again and our first trip to Lake George was great, we loved this area and the lake.

reviews.title: Relaxing
reviews.text: The good: After reading mixed reviews before booking, I wasn't sure what to expect until I walked in the door to our cabin, a two bedroom unit. When we did walk in the door, I was pleasantly surprised. It looked very clean, cleaner than most motels I've stayed in. It was very cozy,,and the covered porch was equipped with two Adirondack chairs. Bathroom was spotless as well. Owner was very friendly. Fresh towels were provided every day by the house keeping and they also made the beds every day. Porch was relaxing. Ours had a view of the beach and lake. Alpine village is close to town, but far enough outta town to be away from noisy crowds. The breakfast at their breakfast restaurant was extremely delicious. And was very cheap compared to other places in lake George. The waitress was very friendly. And there is a beautiful view from the restaurant of the lake. For as old as the place is, they really do a good job maintaining it. The Bad. . . Use of the canoe was nice, but they said their kayaks were" not out yet" for the season...that was upsetting because I was looking forward to kayaking. ...there WAS bed bugs. ! This place doesn't wash their bed sheets and blankets apparently or something. It was annoying for us to wake up to dozens of bites on our bodies from these bed bugs, especially our baby. .When we booked, we were told that they" had a big beach"...the beach is not big at all. In fact, it was smaller than all of the other resorts in that area....there was a large family, about twenty five people (adults and children) staying there the same weekend (housed in about half of the cabins, from what we learned they were regulars at the resort ) and the WHOLE TIME we were there they "hogged" the pool. I mean, these people just would not leave that pool at all, let alone leave the resort. We felt awkward enough about using the pool, jumping in on their family get together, that we didn't even go in the pool, which by the way closes at 7. Pretty early for a resort in my opinion. I guess I'm suggesting that there should be a sharing the pool policy, and should stay open later as well. Maybe 8 or 9 instead of 7pm. OVERALL, it was very relaxing. Its not dirty "appearing" like others have said it is, except for the bed bugs. That, and the early closing of the pool are the only two reasons that we may not be returning to Alpine Village. And it's unfortunate too because it's a really nice place. We just don't want to put up with bed bugs. And would have liked to go swimming after return.ing from a long day of activities in the town. Thank you Alpine Village. But we may be staying somewhere else next time. :/

reviews.title: Just what we wanted
reviews.text: This was exactly the type of relaxing, rustic experience we were looking for on our stop-over in the Adirondacks. The atmosphere suited us perfectly. If rustic is your ticket, a log cabin here is the spot to go. If fancy is your ticket, well, what are you looking at rustic resorts for?

reviews.title: Never Again!!!!
reviews.text: Went to Alpine Village in July of '09, nothing fancy, nice. The pool was NEVER open! Owners "seemd" alright. We we're going to go back in October, but called to get room Rates and off season rates occording to them are $79 or $89 whichever they feal like charging you a night. The rates on the internet say $59 a night. And when we we're their IN season they we're $79 a night. Will never go back Earnie And LIllian are not very nice people. They change their prices whenever they feel like it, they are very rude and they shouldn't be running a buisness. Both had screamd at me on the phone when i calld to reserve rooms and lillian went as far as to hang up on me not once, but 5 times and then had the nerve to tell Earnie that i was very rude to her on the phone. They belong in a nursing home not running a buisness because they have no idea whats going on. Both are incapeable!!! For people to comment about lillian as much as they do they will soon find out that Earnie is just as bad. Oh and as far as their excellent breakfast goes... the Cook Quit so their will be no more breakfast. Don't know how the cook could work for those two anyway. Don't know how anybody works for those two. They probably get paid different every week, because lillian don't remember the pay rate. It would be a very nice place if new owners would take over. Because if it wasn't for the owners i would deffinitely love to go back!

reviews.title: Rustic, but not in a good way.
reviews.text: I'll start on a positive note. The grounds and scenery are fantastic, but that is about where it stops. We were fortunate to have caught Ernie (the owner) in the office when we arrived to check-in, otherwise we would have waited quite some time to be attended to. The "ring bell for service" sign didn't seem to be too effective the remainder of our stay. We were asked to pay in full upon arrival. I have never encountered that at a hotel and have traveled to many, many places all across the country and in other countries. We were allowed to use a credit card to pay (however it was only half our bill, the other half had been sent via check prior to our arrival to "secure our reservation"). And we were informed about how they get charged a $0.25 fee for every credit transaction, almost as if we were being scolded for asking use a debit card. We received a standard key to enter the room (no swipe, no problem there), however without the help of the guest staying in the room next to us, we would never have been able to lock our cabin door. The rooms (or at least ours) needed a serious facelift. Which I found ironic considering when we checked in, the owner told us that it was "one of the nicest rooms". The carpets were dirty looking and consistently damp. I refused to walk around the room without flip flops or slippers. The bedding was old in style (but that is to be expected for the log-cabin atmosphere). The sheets were clean, but the mattress was hard, creeky and the pillows were flat as could be. There is no actual closet, just a shelf with a hanging pole. The window treatments were stained in spots and yellowed (I imagine at one point they were off-white). The windows themselves were in desperate need of cleaning... there was actually a quite large, dead spider encrusted on the window. The towels in the bathroom were thin and occassionally stained, I ended up using an extra beach towel I had brought with me. The shower curtain needed to be washed and stuck to you when you showered (so gross)-- I couldn't wait to shower when I got home!! The room rates were inexpensive for the area, now I understand why. I think if they replaced the carpets, window treatments and shower curtains and got a better cleaning staff; they could double their rates and be full year round. The concept of the "log cabin" style is perfect for the area and the location and scenery are wonderful, but more attention must be paid to the interior of the rooms!!

reviews.title: Nice place if your looking for something on the "rustic" side
reviews.text: First let me say that I'm a bit of a "hotel" snob. For most places I travel to (Caribbean, Las Vegas, Myrtle Beach) I like a more upper class resort (ex: North Beach at Myrtle) with higher end furnishings and ultimate amenities. That being said let me just say I was happy with spending a night at Alpine Village. My husband and I decided to take a spare of the moment motorcycle trip to Lake George. Have to admit I was a bit nervous because it is August, weather has been awesome and when I did look on line most hotels were booked. My husband didn't seem to have an issue with this. So off we went. When we got into Lake George, weren't very many vacancies (as I had expected). My husband did ask about the Holiday Inn but I told him the price on-line was outrageous and wasn't paying that for one night. So first place we stopped was definitely "old" and a "dump" just looking at the outside of it. (but can't be so choosy when you did spare of the moment). So, I asked. They wanted $259! (they did accept AAA discount though). So, I got back on the bike and told my husband lets move on. We made jokes we would be buying blankets and end up sleeping in a park somewhere. Anyhow, saw vacancy at Alpine. Pulled in. Let me just say I was greeted with a friendly smile, how can I help you, etc. I thought the staff to be very friendly. They had one room left for only one night. I was like great, that's all we need it for. He told me it was a room for 6ppl I said we only have two. He quoted $175 which at this point I was fine with (it was getting late) then when I asked about AAA, he said they don't honor that. I said okay, let me just tell my husband to park the bike. I started to turn around to go tell my husband and he said he would only charge $135 if we only used the one bedroom (which that is all we needed). I asked if he "preferred" cash or credit. He said cash and to make it $130. It was down pouring at this point so my husband asked if it would be okay to park the bike under the awning and he said fine. The Room: We expected this to be old and dated and it was but to our surprise it was pretty clean and as far as the main concern (bathroom and bedding) This was very clean. We were in the main lodge on the top floor. The bedding on top looked new. I was very surprised to see newer flat screen TV's. One in each bedroom. Okay, so some stains on the rug (have seen this even in higher end places), window screens were dirty (I'm not sleeping on those), bathroom looked like newly tiled floor. Tub, sink and toilet all clean (some dust on radiator). I do agree they could use some better towels and noticed the adirondack chairs on the deck probably could be replaced. We didn't use the pool so can't really comment. Grounds seemed nice to us. Beach did look small but again, we did not use the beach so can't comment on that.. We saw quite a few different families use the grills and pavillion area and they seemed to be enjoying it. We thought for the money and for one night, the place was perfect and actually made us feel more like we were at a lake in the mountains. We enjoyed the atmosphere. Both my husband and I grew up with going to Lake George many times as kids. We have brought our kids here and hope to bring our grandchildren some day. It has been like a tradition. In summary, I think if you like that rustic feel when you stay in an area like this, Alpine Village is perfect for a long weekend trip ( 3 or 4 day trip). If you like more amenities, more up to date furnishings and decor, you should choose another resort or perhaps a vacation rental on the water which is probably what I would prefer if staying for a week with family.

reviews.title: Great Time, Very Relaxing
reviews.text: We had a very nice time. The cabin was small, but we knew that going in. It was rustic but by no means was it dirty. Just be sure you confirm your reservation and have them send you confirmation by mail. Their reservation system is antiquated and you can get lost in the shuffle very easily. I think most of the resorts here are the same, though. We luckily had no problems and the view, lake and pool were fantastic. The breakfast was the most affordable and best meals we had while we were at the Lake! It was a very relaxing week :-)

reviews.title: So much fun!
reviews.text: This was our families first time in Lake George ever. I was a little apprehensive based on mixed reviews but I have to say I was so pleasantly surprised with everything. The price is very fair, abominations are lovely. It was quiet, clean, and had just what we were looking for. There's so much to do and the location of Alpine Village is so close to everything your want to do. You can rent oars for their kayaks, row boat and as long as you return them you get the deposit back. Beautiful fireworks can be seen on Thursdays from the lake access. Lillian and Ernie were very pleasant as was their son, his wife and their son who was about 9 years old and played with our kids. Everyone else who stayed there was super friendly and nice to chat with. We always go away as a family in the summer and everyone agreed that this was the best trip yet! We've been to Ocean City, Maryland, Delaware near Rehoboth Beach, Montauk, the Jersey shore, etc and lake George is number 1 in our book. We went to Scotty's lakeside for half a day to visit our friends who were staying there and still we preferred Alpine Village. We loved the rustic feel, the quietness, the fairness in price, the cleanliness, the balcony, fridge and microwave, location, etc. Would love to go back next year! While there we rented a boat, went horse back riding, arcade, the track in Saratoga, awesome dinners. A great family vacation for all ages. My grandmother and a family friend her age also came and had a blast.

reviews.title: Left right after checking in!
reviews.text: Rooms were dirty, spiderwebs, insects, yellowed curtains, broken glass pane on window, dirty windows, bathroom door had no lock, toilet leaks and causes water all over floor, no locking screen door if you want to keep front door open and keep kids inside. Ernie actually chided us and said well you're going to have to watch your kids, they need to listen, their ages were 7, 2 and 1and they are well behaved but there were so many things wrong in the room my husband and I would've never been able to sleep making sure they didn't hurt themselves! We said we were leaving and Ernie said no I'm kicking you out try and find a more affordable cleanly hotel, well we did exactly just that and saved ourselves $300.00 in the process. Pinebrook Motel, great room, clean, nice pool, extremely friendly owners, very caring. You couldn't pay me to stay at Alpine!!

reviews.title: Better than expected
reviews.text: After reading some of the negative reviews, I was a little concerned about what we might find at the Alpine Village. I was very relieved when I walked in and found our cabin to be clean, and especially important to me, had a nice updated bathroom. The bath towels were very thin, so I was glad I heeded the advice of another reviewer and brought some from home. I also brought pillows and blankets. The "galley kitchen" had a mini refrigerator, a microwave, a sink and a coffee maker - nothing else so bring coffee cups, utensils, paper towels, and paper plates. There is a sign on the door that warns NO COOKING in the cabin. (There were no smoke detectors in the cabin which might explain that rule.) I found the bed to be quite comfortable and slept very well the two nights we were there. I wanted a nice rustic cabin and that is exactly what I got. I was disappointed breakfast wasn't being served as so many wrote good things about it. They still had the sign out stating breakfast was served and open to the public. As far as the price, we spoke to another guest as we were checking out and found he paid $20 less per night than we did. And he had a lake-front cabin while our cabin was next to the road. He had talked to Ernest and negotiated a lower rate since it was off-season. Wish I had thought of that. Also worth mentioning is that they installed a new septic system and are still working on finishing up the project.

reviews.title: Relax and Enjoy!!!
reviews.text: It's 830 in the morning,the Kids are still sleeping...You are sitting on a Adirondack Chair with your Significant Other,on the Main Lodge balcony,overlooking the Lake and the Beach...A Carafe of coffee brought to you by the Waitress...do I really need to continue??? Ok, I will...how about having your Boat at Alpine's dock,or a Pavillion with Grills...Just fill your Coolers, Relax and Enjoy!!! Can't wait for August

reviews.title: Ripped off
reviews.text: I arrived and the room I had reserved and had paid for was given away. The owner lied, was hostile, and would not admit mistake. Instead of trying to correct it in a nice way she was really rude. Eventually I was given another room, but not lakefront as I had reserved.
