They must have read the prior review about a lack of plates as there were a ton of little plates and bowls. Dinner (fish and risotto) was fabulous...they obviously employ a great chef. Our room safe did not work (as a prior reviewer said) and the electricity went out in the middle of the night briefly (I only knew because I was awake). The room was beautifully decorated with hand painted pictures, bedpillows, and a decorative bed runner. Room was large so we were able to spread out all our rain drenched clothes from the Falls. There was a gap between door and the outside, and the beautiful large window has no screen (nor do other hotels); therefore, we had a few bugs but it's impossible not to in a jungle. The trash can to hold the bathroom trash and toilet paper was too light weight and would fall back when you tried to open the lid so I propped the lid open. There are many locals staying here so its perfect to not be surrounded by only tourists, and one day they even had Guarani Indians selling crafts. The pool was small with sloping edges so it had a wonderful feel more like a jungle pond versus a hotel pool. There were a number of children in it when we arrived, so it was a bit green; it was cleaned well the next morning but for me it was prettier to look at versus wading in. Overall I would definitely return here.

reviews.title: A nice place to stay
reviews.text: A short bus ride into town, not that’s much there. The rooms are fairly large, very clean and well maintained. The food in the restaurant is excellent and so was the service we received. The grounds surrounded the accommodation have a number of private ares to relax in and the pool was a bonus.

reviews.title: Nice setting, friendly staff
reviews.text: Stayed here for one night to explore iguazu falls as most would when visiting this region. Room was massive but space in furnishing which I didn't mind. Staff were excellent and tried to speak English and accommodate my needs. Would recommend staying when visiting iguazu.

reviews.title: Il Pueblito
reviews.text: Great place to stay. Clean rooms with a bath ( and a plug!). Restaurant offered good variety of meals. Bio centre was an added bonus. Bus or taxi to Iguazu Falls right outside hotel. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Amazing hotel to experience Iguazu Falls and Jungle
reviews.text: El Pueblito Iguazu Hotel is an outstanding hotel to whom is looking for experiencing the Iguazu Falls, the selva misionera (jungle) and the flora and fauna to the fullest. I was amazed for the top level service my family and I received at the hotel. The restaurant offered a delicious variety of meals, the staff is super friendly, the colonial style rooms and facilities are very clean and very well furnished. This hotel must be considered as a four stars. I will definitely come back. Very recommendable.

reviews.title: Fantastic hotel with spacious rooms
reviews.text: We stayed here for two nights while visiting Iguazu Falls. We then were unable to fly out due to fog in Buenos Aires and did not hestitate to book another night at the hotel. Massive rooms, swimming pool and lovely rainforest surrounds. Only downside is Wifi and restaurant could be better.

reviews.title: Charming and spectacular service. A boutique experience.
reviews.text: We stayed few days at El Pueblito and we had a fantastic time. It's is a charming hotel with a little church, a mini zoo and a lovely pool surrounded by the jungle. The service is very personal, and warm, the food good and even with gluten free and vegetarian options. They even have tours to the falls and shuttles to the airport.

reviews.title: Beautiful rooms but no WiFi in the rooms
reviews.text: We were meant to stay at the Americano Hotel however apparently there was some issues with having running hot water so we were shuffled to the hotel instead at about 8pm in the evening. It sounded a bit suss but our tour guide/transfer guy advised it would be nicer and newer. We were pleasantly surprised. The rooms were very spacious and felt more like a retreat than a hotel room! The only downside is there is very limited savoury breakfast (just some ham and cheese and bread) but a lot of sweet breakfast items and there's WiFi in the main public area only (and its slow) and not in the rooms which were located on the other side of the hotel which was a bit annoying. Dinner was very delicious here in the hotel. Get the steak (the malbec reduction is amazing!) and the Alamos malbec. We also went downtown one night which costed 60 pesos one way via taxi.

reviews.title: Refreshing
reviews.text: We came upon this nice hotel while visiting the "Bio centre". We were accomodated next door in a very poor hotel. We immediately packed our luggage and moved in to this fan-tas-tic, familiar hotel, which is kind of a thema park about the history of Misiones, the Northern province of Argentina. The hotel has a friendly, helpfull service. It is well located in a unique jungle site. The restaurant serves delicious meals and has it's own wine cellar. In short words: A TOP HOTEL!

reviews.title: Restful Haven
reviews.text: This was a great hotel. The rooms were spotless and huge with good heating. Initially we had a few problems with the safe etc but this was quickly resolved. The staff were friendly and helpful and had good local knowledge. Breakfast was included and was lovely and one night we had dinner here and had a great meal. The grounds are gorgeous and beautifully maintained. The swimming pool and barbeque looked like a great spot to just relax. There is a pond and some jungle. You feel like you have all the privacy in the world as it feels luxuriously secluded. It has a special boutique feel.

reviews.title: Beautiful setting and lovely hotel
reviews.text: We weren’t expecting much from n Iguazú hotel, other than something simple. We arrived a bit early and they invited us to look round the gorgeous gardens. These include pond, pretty boardwalks, an area with feeders that encourage hummingbirds and a butterfly house. There is also a rather cramped area with reptiles, not unusual in South America, but not great for the animals. There is a lovely small pool and several shaded sitting areas in the garden. The rooms were a complete surprise. Enormous and beautifully decorated- two huge double beds, aircon, a safe, plenty of space to put everything, a desk and chair and a small balcony. Hand painted cushions on the bed with local wildlife on them. Staff were friendly, breakfast was standard. As for the review I read about no vodka in the hotel... this is Iguazú, it’s all about nature and natural beauty. There is a bus stop directly opposite with regular buses into town for 18 pesos each way. It’s safe even at night and you really don’t need a taxi. Staying out of town is nicer as town is a little ragged at the edges. The hotel is also nearer Iguazú than town and the front desk arranged us a taxi to the falls ( which for 4 of us was only £2 more than the tourist bus and at our convenience). All in all, a great place to stay.

reviews.title: Grubby
reviews.text: Totally disappointed. This was sold to us as a 5 star hotel but it just rates 2 stars at best. On arrival there is a small unmade road, which was very muddy due to rain the night before. We sloshed our way to our room, through a really nice setting. (No complaints about the surrounds). Our room was a good size with a great big bed. However, on opening the bathroom door things went down hill quickly. We were greeted by half empty shampoo & conditioner, shower gel and lotion bottles, obviously left over from previous guests. The toilet roll holder was hanging off the wall, the toilet seat loose. We were given a generous 7 tissue in the box and the walls were FILTHY. (Looked like they hadn't been cleaned down in years). The shaving mirror was on a tilt. We decided to put stuff in the safe and of course it was locked, so had to walk back to reception to get a key. WI-FI DID NOT EXIST in the rooms, although did work in reception. Decided to go to the bar, but this must be the only Hotel in the world that doesn't have Vodka! (Wife ordered hot chocolate but they didn't have any, although the next day she tried again and got some). There is a small zoo in the grounds but the animals looked cramped for space, especially the large crocodile that only had 2 small fiber glass pools to swim in. Tried the restaurant on the 2nd night and it was actually pretty good. (Although still no Vodka). Staff overall were pretty good (Except the barman). I'm torn about this place. It has beautiful gardens and surrounds but is really started to fray around the edges in the rooms.

reviews.title: Friendly hotel in a great setting
reviews.text: I'm scoring the hotel 5* for our experience within it's official category which reflects on how well we were greeted and looked after as well as the accommodation and setting. We really enjoyed our stay and would recommend El Pueblito to people who enjoy nature as the grounds are amazing - set out with all kinds of flora/fauna and wildlife. The accommodation was excellent and the staff were always polite and helpful.

reviews.title: El pueblito Puerto Iguazu
reviews.text: Small hotel, gorgeous rooms with gardens, pool area, with lots of retreats and relaxing areas. It also had snake area with 10 different types of snakes and yacares. park, lake, plants vegetation room with exotic plante, great service and ambiance!!

reviews.title: Jungle Retreat
reviews.text: The hotel was booked for us by our travel company who try to promote ecologically sustainable and locally owned and operated businesses. What an unexpected pleasure this hotel/resort was! A hotel that grounds itself on sustainable ecological practices and promoting local cultural heritage... There was a great local history book in our room - I had not appreciated that European presence here dates back to the 17th and 18th centuries, particularly the influence of the Jesuits... Our very spacious room overlooked rainforest and a small chapel. As it was early January we also had a nativity scene and lovely Christmas door decorations... Part of the hotel complex is a forest and bio-centre with an interesting walking trail that leads around a small lake (inhabited by wetland birds), through a humming bird house and a butterfly house to a small zoo with a variety of pythons, some small armadillos, a jacare caiman (crocodile) and tortoises... Forests around where we live tend to be quiet, so nothing prepared me for the chattering South American forest! The hotel has a very inviting swimming pool and now and again local Guarani craftspeople sold handcrafts in a hut specifically provided. We enjoyed our breakfasts and ate evening meals there - all more than adequate. Over meals we chatted to fellow guests and enjoyed swapping stories and experiences. The dining room had a large aquarium - especially enjoyable for families with inquisitive youngsters. All-in-all, a great place to base yourself as you explore and enjoy the Iguazu Falls and surrounds.

reviews.title: Pleasant hotel, a little complicated to access
reviews.text: Stayed here for a night in March while visiting the majestic falls. The room was large, and reasonably comfortable, although a little bit on the Spartan side. Should that be smaller with the same amount of furnishing, it could have looked more appealing. We had a torrential rain that night, and the electricity was gone for a while so unfortunately it was even less welcoming, but I am ignoring that bit now, I assume the AC would work faultlessly otherwise... The staff was kind and helpful, really appreciated their support. The not so great side of the hotel is the location. It's a real challenge to go anywhere. You need to have your wheels or taxi to go to the town, or to a bus station which is the essential hub if you want to go to either side of the Falls. The other downside is the WiFi, you need to go to the reception if you have to use the net, as the one in the room is useless

reviews.title: Recommended
reviews.text: A very comfortable hotel. Clean. Spacious. Quiet. Friendly and helpful staff. It’s approximately 2km from downtown (Centro). Buses run every 30mins or taxi is only 150 pesos (we took the taxi several times). The restaurant serves a simple but tasty breakfast. Lunchtime & dinner have a good menu (& nice wines) all at very reasonable prices. The pool is shallow (safe) and refreshing. The “eco park” (unexpected) has an interesting range of snakes (including very large pythons!) & butterflies. It’s not 5 star but it’s very good value.

reviews.title: Lovely stay
reviews.text: I arrived early from the airport to just drop off my bags, and they let me check in early and then helped me get on my way to the waterfalls. Alan actually described to me the best way to tackle the waterfalls, which routes were the ones to start with and others that I could skip based on time—which was very helpful! The room was clean, the water hot, and it was quiet despite being on the main access road. They helped me find s driver who also made the rest of my stay a lot easier, having that contact. Overall, nothing but good things to say! Large property, family friendly (appearing, not from my Own experience).

reviews.title: Great place!
reviews.text: Great place, service and location. Stayed for business and the place was awesome. We were a group of more than 50 people. Great rooms, location. Close to both airports and easy to find on you way. Fully recommended.

reviews.title: Accommodation
reviews.text: Lovely big room and a little balcony as well. No wifi in the rooms was the only negative of this place. Wifi in common areas was strong though! It is 3km walk into town but felt very safe doing this walk. The Biocentro was ok and you have free access if you stay here.

reviews.title: Great hotel
reviews.text: Very nice hotel, friendly staff, beautiful rooms, nice swimming pool and jungle feeling:-) only tip, breakfast can be with a bit more variation, but was good! We had a great time at this hotel and great place to visit the falls!

reviews.title: Friendly and accommodating
reviews.text: We stayed here as a base camp for an Iguazu Falls tour. It was very conveniently located to the Falls and Puerto Iguazu. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Our room had three twin beds which we requested and they were VERY comfortable. The hotel has a small bar where we enjoyed our afternoon beers and Cafe Lattes (excellent espresso machine on the premises). As we had traveled for 40 hours from Los Angeles, we enjoyed the restaurant on premises. We enjoyed a delicious and very affordable meal (with an excellent bottle of wine). We would definitely come back and enjoy these facilities.

reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: Stayed here for 2 nights during our tour. The rooms are big and beds are comfortable and toiletries are supplied. However the breakfast is terrible and nothing other than the fruit seemed fresh. It consisted of damp cereal ,stale breads sliced cheese and slices of ham, an assortment of sweet slices and sliced fruits. I think that some love injected into this area would be an improvement. We would probably not stay here again given the choice.

reviews.title: Good value
reviews.text: A basic but very clean little gem of a place, with great service and fantastic food. It is on the Argentinian side of the Iguazu Falls, which can be reached by a 20min bus journey, with the stop right outside the hotel.

reviews.title: Amazing Experience
reviews.text: I spent 2 wonderful nights at El Pueblito. Everything was perfect and the service was amazing! The hotel is built in colonial style, surrounded by nature, jungle and wildlife. Food is also great, I will definitely go back soon!

reviews.title: Lives up to the reviews
reviews.text: Per previous reviews, this hotel doesn't look like much on the outside but once you step through the front doors you'll find a quaint hotel with large, tile floor rooms. Beds are comfortable, not as hard as the usual Argentine mattress (but why have thick comforters in such a hot climate?). A small pool warmed by the sun sits next to the bar(also small). Great garden with walking trail which we had no time to fully explore. It's quite far from restaurants within walkable distance so we dined twice in the restaurant for dinner. Menu has a small selection but the Thai soup was wonderful, but a different variation in that it was thick. It was slightly spicy with a reasonable amount of shrimp and some mushrooms and tasted wonderful. Large portion for 190 pesos. The steak was not as tender as we've become used to when dining in Argentina despite requesting rare (which it was). The vegetarian pasta was a disappointment. Essentially a bottom of pasta layered with a thin coating of puree vegetables (unidentifiable from my perspective), covered by another thin sheet of pasta topped with lots of melted cheese. The pasta was very tender but I expected more vegetables and more flavour (overwhelmed by the cheese). Breakfast is as described previously. One morning we arrived at 9:20am (hours are until 10am) and there were no plates, cutlery; the eggs were cold, the fruit was almost all gone. We had to ask the waiter for plates, cutlery even though he saw us sitting there. All in all a very positive experience at the hotel.

reviews.title: Wonderfully landscaped property, great accomadation
reviews.text: fantastic property with birds galore and extensive jungle landscaping. Great room.Included buffet breakfast was good but a shortage of plates made serving yourself difficult. Great flan cake, I devoured 3 pieces. I ate two nights in the hotel disappointing mini hamburger but an excellent over sized NY steak

reviews.title: Loved this place.....
reviews.text: We stayed at El Pueblito for 4 nights in November. It is designed on the original buildings of Iguasu and is set in a tropical garden. We thought it was beautiful. We had a spacious room upstairs overlooking trees and the little chapel. Yes there are muddy roads all around - this is Iguasu - and if you have the time to walk around the area not many people here have the benefit of sealed roads near their houses. The staff at this hotel are very helpful and it is a short and inexpensive ride in a taxi to restaurants in the town. However dinner at the restaurant is a reasonable quality if you don't want to go out. The breakfast has lots of fresh fruit - and sweet cakes which is the Argentinian style - it's the local experience. The swimming pool is pleasant - music can be a bit loud at times. Overall a very pleasant experience. We would definitely choose to stay here again.

reviews.title: Fantastic eco stay!
reviews.text: The rooms here were large and well furbished - with the ensuite being particularly large with its own full size bath as well as a separate shower. There are many public areas in which to relax - including the pool, not the deepest but handy to have a dip, as well as the walk through the "zoo" - really enjoyed seeing the butterfly house and the crocodiles. The staff were professional and tried to assist - with some language barriers given my Spanish is not good. Do not expect much in the way of mobile reception - this provided difficulties for us as we tried to contact some fellow travellers staying elsewhere in Iguazu. It was also difficult to book taxis - fortunately there were many passing by and happy to be flagged down.

reviews.title: Met our needs
reviews.text: The staff was terrific. There was a complimentary shuttle to and from the airport. Rooms are in separate building from the reception dining area. Infrastructure needs some work as both safe and air conditioning malfunctioned. Rooms were comfortable quiet and clean.

reviews.title: Relaxing and very quiet
reviews.text: I had two nights at this Hotel. It was perfect, friendly staff, quiet and the grounds are gorgeous. Wi-Fi was a bit touch and go, but its quite remote. Food was great and quite reasonable. A very comfortable stay

reviews.title: Beautiful accommodations, wonderful concept
reviews.text: We spent 3 days at this hotel. Rooms are big, decks and common areas are comfortable, and staff are friendly. It was wonderful to experience nature right outside our room! We appreciated their triple-bottom line (people, planet, profit) approach and policies. The hotel is new and has some details to iron out (such as placement of electrical outlets and shelving) but the manager was very receptive to feedback and took notes to address what we pointed out.

reviews.title: El Pueblito
reviews.text: A beautiful serene place to stay. Rooms are very big and the room my sister and I had contained 2 queen beds which were very comfortable. It is very clean and had tea/coffee making facilities. Awesome!

reviews.title: Can't say much more!
reviews.text: Most points have been covered in previous reviews - huge room, best breakfast we had in Argentina with fresh fruit and scrambled eggs. The young men on reception were very helpful and all staff were pleasant. It is outside the town and taxis are required to go into restaurants at night. It is on a dual carriage way with no pavement so walking is not really an option. Enjoyed our stay.

reviews.title: Beautiful place to stay!
reviews.text: Loved staying at El Pueblito. The rooms were beautiful and the BioCentro was wonderful. It felt like we were staying in our own mini rainforest lodge. Rooms were cleaned every day and presentation of the room was gorgeous. Reception service was great. Everyone spoke enough English to be able to assist us (our Spanish is beginners level). The only issues we had was 1.) finding the bus stop and 2.) ordering a taxi back to the airport. We wanted to catch the bus to the city and was told to wait across the road and wave to the bus. No one told us there was a bus stop across the street and walk about 5-10 minutes towards town. We waited for ages and no buses would stop. Eventually we decided to walk to town, and coincidentally found the bus stop. Maybe just need to be a bit clearer i.e. or even draw on map where it is. Issue 2 was when we ordered a cab back to the airport. We asked the hotel to call a cab. The man at reception told us it'd cost us 300 pesos. We said that was too expensive. We caught a cab from airport to hotel for 260 pesos (we know this was expensive but had no choice). He then came back and told us 250 pesos. We accepted however this was still more expensive than amounts other drivers had offered us a few days earlier. Was disappointed that we were being ripped off, and our hotel didn't bother to assist. You would think the hotel would know how much it should have been and told the taxi driver 300 pesos was too much, without us having argue it. Oh and we emailed requesting airport transfer the day before we arrived, however did not receive a reply to confirm or to advise one was not available. For the amount of money you pay, I think airport transfers should be available. Apart from those minor issues, this hotel is amazing. I would 100% stay here again 😊

reviews.title: Corner of paradise in Iguazù
reviews.text: Staff are amazing, extremely helpful and most of them speak English. Rooms (we stayed in a triple) were spacious and with AC, they were also clean for the country standards. The restaurant offer a small choice of dished and the prices are slightly higher from the average but quality is excellent. Breakfast very generous and delicious. The whole property is just a dream.. you can hear jungle noises all day, relax near the pool.. the atmosphere is so peaceful and there are very little mosquitos! We did not want to leave!! El Pueblito is not in town, which for us was a plus as Port Iguazu did not appeal to us when we went past by car.. however, it is not far should travellers need to go in town. Reception can arrange taxis. Thank you to all the staff in El Pueblito, you were amazing!

reviews.title: Serenity and great food.
reviews.text: This is a unique spot that prides itself on environmental awareness and sustainability. Our room was spacious, comfortable, and the decor was in keeping with the basic, natural theme. The food was excellent with no excessive frills. Instead of being handed a wine list our marvellous waiter took us straight to his cellar so we could choose ourselves. To our surprise when ambling about the gorgeous gardens we came upon all sorts of reptiles including alligators In thinly masked confines. It was a unique and wonderful experience and Lucia makes the best capirinha I have ever had! A treasure.

reviews.title: Excellent value
reviews.text: A little hotel with large clean basic rooms some of which are close to nature. I did wonder if screens would be needed at certain times of the year. A welcome drink of fruit water was offered on arrival. The breakfast was good but a bit boring since we stayed for four nights. The staff were pleasant and helpful. We also enjoyed the chapel, the bio centre and the butterfly house. It was not difficult get to the falls from the hotel nor into town for an evening meal. If we were to return to Iguazu Falls, we would be happy to stay in this hotel again. I also found the staff to be very helpful when I was arranging our booking by email from Canada.

reviews.title: Great ambiance; very bad breakfast
reviews.text: The location of the hotel is fine - on the national highway towards the park. Since the national park is the main attraction here, the location away from the city centre does not matter. There is an easy bus that goes to Puerto Iguazu (city) for 13 pesos, from right outside the hotel. The rooms are huge and the beds are also large. Bathroom facilities are all good too. WiFi is free. Works very well in the reception area. Works in the room too but sometimes it switches on and off. Breakfast is very poor. Breads and pastries were stale on both mornings. The cornflakes were soggy as though they had been left out. They also do not provide large size plates - only small tea plates so there is barely any place to take any food. Either way, breakfast was bad and needs severe improvement. Further, they do not recommend drinking tap water here. In any place that does not recommend drinking tap water, bottled water must be provided at no cost (it is the case in any other hotel I have stayed). They make you pay for bottled water and there is nothing else around from where you can buy anything. Water should have been provided at no extra cost. There are also no other food options around and therefore you will be compelled to eat in the restaurant here. Unless you have a car and can go to the city centre. Service was good. They gave us a two hour extension for a late check out. Since it is a touristy town, the options are all probably limited to this kind. While the hotel is good, location is alright, breakfast needs improvement.

reviews.title: Very friendly and wonderful room
reviews.text: Room was large and comfortable. Area was beautiful. The location is central. The staff is very friendly and many speak English. They do not hesitate to help. The only downside is the restaurant which I would not advise for meals outside of breakfast.

reviews.title: Nice hotel but could be better
reviews.text: This hotel well located halfway between the airport and the downtown central area. The room was large, bed was comfortable, and WiFi was strong. The whole atmosphere was nice. It has their own little zoo exhibit with turtles, fishes, ducks, butterflies, snakes and crocodiles. Unfortunately, our room’s AC was weak, the window was unable to open (even though the outside temperature was cool at nice), and the toilet water was running the whole night (we were too tired to call maintenance, fell asleep as soon as we hit the bed after long day at the falls).

reviews.title: x
reviews.text: The rooms were huge, but a bit noisy, I could hear every step of the people in the room above. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Food was pretty good, although breakfast was a bit slow being set up.

reviews.title: Great rooms and service, pity about the food
reviews.text: Nice hotel with large rooms and pleasant surroundings, including an Eco park with butterflies, hummingbirds, snakes etc. Service is good, price of bottled water is steep. Unfortunately the food is very ordinary

reviews.title: A surprising resort just out of town.
reviews.text: Much to my surprise, this is a well designed resort hotel in a very beautiful setting with a butterfly house and small zoo attached. While it is a good 10-15 minute taxi ride out of the centre of Peurto Iguazu, the hotel setting and features make the distance worthwhile. The restaurant has good local food at reasonable prices, and breakfasts are more than adequate. The rooms are air-conditioned and spacious with good beds. A very relaxing and enjoyable three nights here.

reviews.title: Second floor only plz..
reviews.text: The hotel is cute and well priced. Native ppl think the name is kinda stupid tho..lol Pro: Good breakfast.(had fruits, salads, egg, ham, cheese and breads etc..) Tasty dinner for good price. Their fish was very tender and tasty. Relaxing and you feel like you are in tropical jungle. Con: Shower is a bit of a struggle cuz when you shower the water flows out to toilet and outside of shower zone... mosquito. We stayed in the first floor so there were a lot of mosquitos in the room. They have this electric mosquito killing? Plug in the room which works.. but I would rather not use it cuz who knows what effect would that cause to human body in the long run.. Need to ask for second floor. Not close to the center.. so to go to a market you need to take taxi which cost about 100 pesos (2.5 usd)

reviews.title: Loved this place!
reviews.text: This is more than a hotel, it's a retreat! The rooms are HUGE, clean and have all the extras (balcony, air conditioning, TV, toiletries, safety deposit box, free WiFi, etc.) The staff are lovely, very friendly and helpful. The restaurant is also very nice and has a wine room at the back. The food is tasty and not overly expensive. Breakfast was really good with lots of choice. The pool.areas is beautiful and there is also a little church on the grounds as well as a biopark which you get free access to as a guest. There you will find a mini 'zoo'. The location is around 25 minutes from the airport and 15 minutes from the Brazilian border so great for doing both sides of the Iguazu National Park.

reviews.title: Great option
reviews.text: Great option in puerto iguazu. It is closer to the brazilian border, on the way to the iguazu park. Price is fair and the service is very good, breakfest is included. The pool is awesome, the rooms are literally giants, and there are also bathtub on them. Attached to the hotel there are a biocenter with some animals (alligator, ducks, snakes). 10/10.

reviews.title: Great Hotel
reviews.text: The hotel is situated within ten minutes of the Park. The hotel is clean and comfortable with a lovely bio-park. We were on motorcycles and even though our motos were parked in front of the hotel they were secure. The hotel has security and cameras. What really makes the hotel is their staff they are professional, polite, and friendly. The staff that works in the garden and pathways are artists and were pleasant. The receptionists Alan and the morning receptionist were excellent persons. The restaurant staff, Sergio, Lucia and another young man that loved motorcycles were excellent in professional service and friendliness. Sergio was excellent in suggestions of wine coupled with meals and desert. Truly the staff makes the hotel a good stop on the way to see the most fantastic waterfalls ever.

reviews.title: Amazing stay
reviews.text: Spent 3 nights in this hotel and this was absolutely fantastic ! The room was huge, the bathroom was great, and we had a hammock just outside our room. There is also a swimming pool and a little open air bar behind it... There is also an "eco centre", which we loved. The only 'complain' I would have is the restaurant food which is really not great, but eh, it was okay (apart from what they called a bruschetta, which in reality, was just a piece of toast with veggies on it...).

reviews.title: Na
reviews.text: Great hotel , great service perfect location . Food was great , we ate dinner at the restaurant 3 times and food was gourmet. Very friendly staff . Rita the receptionist was very efficient, Friendly,and helpful. Would stay here again .

reviews.title: A quite paradise in the middle of nature
reviews.text: The hotel is a peaceful haven and gives a wonderful sense of being in the park. It has a not to be missed Biocentre with crocodiles, snakes, fish and importantly a wonderful butterfly sanctuary when you can see amazing butterflies close up and hummingbirds in another open sided enclosure. The staff are super friendly and helpful, breakfast plentiful and fresh and the rooms are large and airy. Bathrooms could do with a little updating which is why a 4 not a 5.

reviews.title: Lovely quite eco hotel
reviews.text: This was a really nice hotel to stay at.The rooms are huge. The natural environment is really nice. The trees and lake outside the room and the birds make the whole stay pleasant. There is a walk around the lake with exhibits of a number of local animals, butterfflies, snakes and plants. The restaurant was nice and food and drinks reasonably priced. A good choice of place to stay while in Iguazu

reviews.title: Great hotel
reviews.text: Yours is a great hotel, the staff is friendly, the rooms are well appointed clean and quiet, good breakfast and good lunch and dinner menue at the restaurant, nicely landscaped gardens. Loved your Orchid and butterfly greenhouses. We were very sorry we could not stay longer, as we found your hotel to be very relaxing. The location is also very good, as it is not too far from the Iguazu falls and or the downtown core.

reviews.title: very beautiful
reviews.text: Very beautiful hotel, located few minutes walking from Spanish Steps and Vatican City. Great room, large, clean and with decorated ceiling. Rich buffet breakfast in the morning, helpful staff. We loved this hotel, we will definitly come back.

reviews.title: Do NOT recommend
reviews.text: While this hotel is located near Vatican City and Spanish Steps, I would not recommend a stay at this hotel. The rooms were smaller than US hotels, but we managed. However, when the hotel says it has "air-conditioning," it is referring to an open window and a teletubbie looking dehumidifier. We had to sleep with the window open to generate cool air and the traffic noise kept us up most of the night. Friends who also stayed at this hotel had mold in their room so overwhelming that they had to frequently leave the room. The staff at the hotel was not friendly or helpful. There are many other hotels in the same area. Keep looking!

reviews.title: Stay away from this hotel
reviews.text: Information about this hotel is misleading from web description. Ara Pacis is overpriced , filthy , smelly place . Peeling wallpaper everywhere, very tiny washroom, spoted mattress , Do I need to say more ? We ordered pick up from Fiumicino , driver was 40 min late with old no air conditioning Jaguar , we paid 55 euro . There is small clean buss - 40 euro.

reviews.title: Avoid headache and hassle. Don't stay at this hotel.
reviews.text: DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL. My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel in August 2006. We had a confirmed reservation, but when we arrived, they told us they would have to send us across town to another hotel because they had no rooms. The staff person assured us that the other hotel was "much nicer," and pointed to a spot on the map near the city center. They said they had "made special arrangements with this other hotel to take us in." Much to our dismay, the other hotel wasn't much nicer, and even worse, it was located in a totally different part of town than they claimed. We were very disappointed because we could have easily stayed in this much less popular part of town for much less money. The next night, we insisted on being sent back to the Hotel Ari Pacis. They stuck us in a tiny room with broken air conditioning. I travel all the time, and I've stayed in a variety of hotels in the past, but this was by far the worst hotel experience I've ever had in any part of the world in my life. If I were to take a guess, this hotel actually owns the other hotel. The Ari Pacis overbooks intentionally because it's at a lower price point. The other hotel (The Hotel Borromeo) may be under the same umbrella ownership. It's at a higher price point though, so the owners of the Ari Pacis may simply overbook the cheaper hotel, then send the excess guests across town to the other hotel. Whatever is going on, it's a very shady operation, and I don't want any other travelers to have to deal with what my we had to deal with. For your own sake, please DO NOT STAY HERE. If you have to pay more for a comparable hotel in the area, stay in the other hotel. It'll save you a lot of headache and hassle.

reviews.title: Great deal and location, not a 5 star.
reviews.text: We stayed in this hotel for 8 nights. While the hotel itself is not top luxury, we didn't mind due to the price and location. Bonus that there is a bus stop right infront of the hotel, and walking distance from everything! The staff was of average attitude, not what you expect as cheerfulness and deisre to fufil all your requests but they where helpful. Breakfast was a so so array of pastries, cereals, meats and cheeses. Our tv and heater worked and we had a beautiful balcony in our room. This hotel is not a 5 star luxury resort, but as I said I didn't mind since we spend little to no time in the hotel and most of our time exploring the city. The location is the reason why I will return, only a 5 minute walt to the Vatican and many other Roman points of interest!

reviews.title: This hotel is grotty, smelly, unfriendly and misleading from web description
reviews.text: My husband & I chose this hotel for our anniversary as from the description on the website it appeared perfect. When we arrived, the man on the desk was unhelpful, rude and did not care less whether we were there or not... The room was smelly, wallpaper hanging off the walls, no doors on the wardrobe, a large hole in the window with tape on the crack. The bathroom tiles were dirty with unsightly white splashes all over. The shower was broken from the wall and you had to hand hold it to use. The internet did not work in the room. The double bed was 2 singles pushed together which were hard and uncomfortable. Do I need to say anymore, do not stay there and I wish I had read the reviews before we did.. only good thing was the location and breakfast was eatable.

reviews.title: Worst hotel ever!
reviews.text: The pictures on the website looked nice and for the price, it seemed like a good deal. WRONG! The first night our AC was broken so they switched us to another room. When we got back to the hotel after a day of sightseeing our room was covered with ants...all over the bed and hearboard. They tried making us stay in another room which was the size of a closet! I have stayed in hostels better than this place.

reviews.title: Loved the Ara pacis
reviews.text: My friend and I stayed at the Ara pacis on July 26 for 4 nights we had a twin room which was clean and comfortable. We had air conditioning hot water, and the breakfast was great especialy the cappuccino. The staff were friendly and helpful plus there was a new lift, the hotel was idealy situated for all the main sites of interest. We both had a brilliant stay in Rome made even better by the Ara Pacis staff and hotel

reviews.title: Perfect for a short stay
reviews.text: First, we moved to this hotel after our original hotel The Borromeo (see my review there) didn't have enough rooms for the weekend and we hadn't booked in advance. The Borromeo was much much better in every aspect but this place wasn't too bad either. Yes, the place is dingy, the walls are crumbling, but it's clean and doesn't smell. There's no AC, which was a bit of a problem in end of June heat in a room with no windows but it wasn't unbearable. We switched rooms upon arrival to one with a shared terrace and that made it all worth it. The sunrise was breathtaking from the balcony and it was a perfect place to start the day in beautiful Rome. The hotel is also located just 5 min down the street from the Vatican and only 10 min away from the Spanish steps so it's a pretty good base for exploring historic areas. All in all, it's a great option during high season when everything is booked or pricey but if you can find them, there's definitely better places around for similar prices.

reviews.title: good service and prices
reviews.text: Just came back from Rome and very impressed with Rome,its history and culture heritage! Fantastic shops and even the weather in this period which i advise becouse its so beatiful all aroud before Christmas!! Not so many turists aroud, i felt very comfortable while walking around the city. The staff in the hotel was so courteous with me, helped me to find russian-speaking giude and russian tours to Rome and to Napoli. Only positive emotions from all my trip!

reviews.title: Not the place for me
reviews.text: I was supposed to stay at the Borromeo but willingly moved to the Ara Pacis because my room at the Borromeo wouldn't be ready until 2 hours after I arrived (my stupid mistake for switching hotels). I was dirty and tired from traveling and did not want to start my adventure in Rome sweaty and smelly. I was told by the front desk clerk that their other hotels (all in the same chain) were just as nice. He told me he'd find a ride for me--which he did...a friend of his I believe. Not a hotel employee...a friend. She was nice enough but still... It was located near the Vatican though I wanted to be closer to the Forum. My fault for accepting. Anyway upon arrival at the Ara Pacis I wasn't impressed. The desk clerk was extremely gracious and kind. I had absolutely no problem with the hotel employees. They were all very accomodating. The clerk gave me a double room with a balcony. However, upon entering, my heart sank a bit. My very well-worn room with scratches and brown marks on the wall smelled extremely stale and moldy; the carpet was thrown together on the floor in approximately 14"by 14" squares and not glued down (I could see the cement floor underneath); the bathroom...oh dear...the bathroom. It's ridiculous to even call it that. It was the size of a large closet and the shower, if you can call it that, was simply a drain in the floor with a shower head attached to a wall...less than a foot from the toilet. There was no separate shower space. It was sink, toilet, shower head, shower curtain, drain. The toilet and shower shared the same floor. That's right. The entire floor would be covered by water because THAT was the shower room. Basically, the bathroom was a shower with a toilet in it. When I got into the stale-smelling room I opened windows on the balcony to let in fresh air. I figured since it was a balcony I didn't have to worry about the security of having the doors wide open since the room was on the 4th floor. However, as I was getting dressed a maintenance man came through a little removable gate on one side of the balcony to spray the plants and flowers. Not a big deal...unless you're a single woman getting undressed close to your wide open door! (The room was a bit crowded so I didn't have a lot of room to change) I was horrified. I quickly closed the door and curtains. After this I tried calling the Borromeo to see if I could still have my room (I'd only been in the Ara Pacis for 20 minutes or so) but was told the room had already been taken. Yeah, sure it had. I didn't feel like putting up a fight since I had made plans with friends so I decided to just stay in the room as it was only for one night and consider it an adventure. I was paying $140 per night and expected something similar to the Borromeo which I have stayed in before. The Ara Pacis was not that place. It's very close to the Vatican and St Angelo and there's a bus stop across the street if you don't feel like walking to the Forum, Colloseum, Spanish Steps, etc. I'm sure there are rooms that are fine in the hotel as evidenced by the other moderate reviews. However, I won't stay there again.

reviews.title: Checked out early!
reviews.text: I think the title says it all. Before I berate this place let me highlight the positives.....the location is quite convenient, so if that is your main pre-requisite then you may not be as disappointed as I was. Our "double room" was so small I had to put the room chair on top of the wardrobe so that my wife and I could walk past eachother. The toilet didnt flush properly (always a great feature), and there was no 24hr service man to fix it. Then there was the shower (if you are a robust person say +90kg you would not have fit into it), which had no water pressure and the hot water ran out quickly. Front desk service was surly to say the least. Finally, given the aforementioned points, the room cost me 175Euro which was the biggest insult. Had it cost 80-90 I could not complain, but that price was ridiculous. It is obvious they are taking advantage of the location and general popularity of Rome. We checked out the next day (one day too early) and moved to a better hotel 500m away and stayed there for 140Euro. Happy travelling Marvellous

reviews.title: Horrible Place - Avoid this Hotel!
reviews.text: When we arrived at this hotel, we were hoping for someone to help us w/our bags since the hotel was actually on the 3rd floor & only few people could fit in the elevator - the receptionist was rude & annoying. The rooms weren't ready yet therefore; we had to wait in non-air-conditioned cramp lobby. The room was tight but it was clean. The bathroom looks nice but they could have invested their money on unclogging the shower stall & bleach to clean the molds on the shower stall floor. Within the family, we got 3 rooms for each family. All 3 rooms had portable (barely working) air conditioner. One of my aunts, her husband had to empty out the water tray every night from their room's portable a/c otherwise, the a/c will stop working. The other aunt couldn't sleep because she said, "there's a ghost" in her room. She saw her daughter got pushed off the bed (but no one else was around her) & her daughter asked why did she (my aunt) pushed her off. The breakfast wasn't bad at all; I think that's the only good thing in this hotel. Though I must admit the location is really great! Very close to the Vatican, the Basilica, Spanish Steps, etc. Oh yeah, our 2nd night the electricity went off, the front lobby said “because all the room's a/c was on & the fuse couldn't handle all.” It's been happening everyday/night for 4 nights! Our last night in this nightmare hotel, the fuse went out again around midnight & almost all the guest went to the front lobby & no one was there for 15 mins. The front desk guy tried to fix it for 2 hours around 2:30am, the fire truck arrived at the front of our hotel & finally the electricity came back on. I know that this is the worst "hotel" any of our family members ever stayed in and because of the high peak season, we couldn't get any other hotel (and they know this) we paid almost $200 per night! When we were all checking out, we asked if we could get a little bit of discount because what we all went through (all the inconveniences) & the guy said, we should of check out the first time the electricity went off. If you want to come to your hotel and relax after long day excursion - HOTEL ARI PACIS IS NOT the hotel you want to check-in. There's a hotel across this hotel & seems to be a lot nicer! AVOID THIS HOTEL!

reviews.title: Do NOT stay here
reviews.text: Although the building is elegant and in a good position the hotel is in a state of disrepair. The air-con was absolutely useless and no attempt was made to fix it; the wallpaper was peeling off the walls and the carpet was in holes. The attitude of the day manager was unbelievable - he was rude, disinterested and just shrugged if you asked him anything.The breakfasts were rather special too - in a country that prides itself on its coffee, the muck that they served was beyond description. It was no better than some of the hostels my son had just stayed in in Morocco and a lot more expensive.

reviews.title: Hotel Ara Pacis well-located, but beware of air-conditioning
reviews.text: When the Hotel Ara Pacis advertises ‘air conditioned public areas’ that does not imply that all guest rooms are air-conditioned—some are and some are not. When they first put us in a non-air-conditioned room, I complained and, with a faint sneer, they moved us to an air-conditioned room. The hotel was in a safe neighborhood and was well-located for sight-seeing, especially the Vatican sights. But when you first arrive, beware that it is located on the other side of the river from the Ara Pacis monument, not next to it, as the ads imply. The breakfast was adequate—the server, though hard-working, could not be made to understand that we wanted our coffee hot and our milk cold. The elevator worked fine during our visit.

reviews.title: Don't waste yur money
reviews.text: This hotel is a disgrace. It was filthy, falling apart, peeling wallpaper, paint chips everywhere. Everything is worn, frayed and smells. It is an absolute fire hazard. To their credit they did try and move our rooms, but it was insult to injury. They ended up moving us to another hotel, at their expense, that was acceptable. They also charged 50 euro for airport pickup when the regular cab fare is 40. It was a rough start after a long flight.

reviews.title: Good location, lift still out of order
reviews.text: We (family of 5) stayed at the Ara Pacis March 27-31, 2004. We found the location to be quite good in a quiet area, away from the crowds. Easy walk (3 minutes) to taxi stand at Piazza Cavour. Walking to major sites possible - Vatican 10 minutes, Colloseum 25 minutes, Via Veneto 20 minutes, Spanish Steps 8-10 minutes, Trevi Fountain 15 minutes. Not having a lift (except for luggage) got old after the first trip up 106 steps. We had a quad room with an extra bed which was a tight fit, I would reccomend a family of 5 to get two rooms.

reviews.title: Checked in and checked straight back out
reviews.text: We had booked this hotel for a romantic weekend in Rome. Hotel was possibly the worst I have ever seen. Very strange entrance via courtyard with a sign pointing to the Lift for the Hotel entrance. You have to go up to the 3rd floor to access the hotel. Rude receptionist who mumbled out the time of breakfast. Corradore to the room had ripped wallpaper and grotty thread bare carpet. The room was grotesque and smelt like someone had died in it. Can't believe somewhere like this can exist. Just don't go

reviews.title: Excellent location
reviews.text: Family of four, children aged 12 + 8, we stayed at this hotel in July for 4 nights. Location was excellent. 10 mins walk to the vatican. 10 mins walk the other direction took us to the Trevi / spanish steps etc. Room was basic but clean - we tended to go out from 9am to about 10pm for the sights and then some dinner. Air conditioning system was working. Although a bit bulky and noisy, we all enjoyed a good night's sleep. Breakfast buffet was very good - but I repeat - the location was superb.

reviews.title: romantic hotel
reviews.text: I ve decided with my BF to spend few days in Rome, my favourite city! I ve been in Rome many times, when I ve a moment I always try to come here. This time I booked this hotel in internet and I was so happy with iy. Centrally located, beautiful large room and great staff. Moreover we found a very convenient price for the room. We spent 4 nights in this lovely city, dining out, walking around the narrow streets of the center, and shopping...for sure! The hotel is next to Via del Corso and Via Condotti, where to find the best shops of Rome and the best italian labels. Surely it was good to choose this hotel.

reviews.title: Elevator back in order!
reviews.text: I read the other reviews and called the hotel to check if the elevator was in order. It was, and I decided to book. On the phone they said all rooms were booked, but when I said I had found rooms available on the net, the story changed. It seems the hotel reserves rooms for internet booking. Through hotel I got a fair price, but the price I got by booking directly on the hotels web-site was better! So: Use this hotel! The location is great and the hotel good enough;) There are some rooms with access to a beatiful terrace, so ask for these! Book the room on the hotel's web site

reviews.title: Not the best
reviews.text: First off, this place is fine if you care a little about the comfort of your surroundings, but not too much. The whole hotel smelled of smoke...everywhere....it was just everywhere. Then we get to the room and there was no A/C....so we go to the desk and demand a room with A/C because it was promised in our reservation. We were told we could get another room the next day, but when pressed the concierge finally gave us another room. Also, we had a quad and they don't tell you that the other two beds are roll out sofas that feel absolutely terrible. Breakfast was horrific as well. The drain in the shower clogged and water went everywhere, no surprise since the shower looked so old. Only good thing was the location.

reviews.title: Satisfactorily
reviews.text: I found this hotel to be a tolerable place to stay. We got a double room which was not as big as pictures show but adequate and silent with a small bathroom. Breakfast room was crowded about 8 am but not as crowded if you come a little earlier. Breakfast was not bad but standart: croissants, bread, cheese, salame, boiled eggs, some fruits (oranges and apples), yogurt, cornflakes etc. Pluses: easy to reach by bus, not far from subway station; short walking distance to Piazza del Popolo and Vatican City; enough places to eat and shops around. Minuses: not strong pressure of hot water, no safe in the room.

reviews.title: A nice small hotel.
reviews.text: Hotel Ara Pacis is a small, nice and clean hotel. It is situated on the third floor in a building from 1907. It is some hundred meters to the center of Rome and on walking distance to the Vatican aswell as to Piazza di Spagna.And: By any means, don´t forget the Cat Sanctuary at the Torres Argentina. It can be hard to finds but look for the stairs close to the ruins and you will find this paradise for cat lovers!There are plenty of small and nice restaurants around the hotel.As the hotel only have 37 rooms, you get some kind of family feeling (the manager himself comes in to breakfast room every morning with a merry "bun giorno"). The service is perfect (free candy at the reception disk) and the breakfast is good with excellent coffee of your own choice. The bed was good, even for a bad back as mine.

reviews.title: Rude service, cramped room
reviews.text: Three friends and I booked this hotel about a month before our trip. We needed a place to stay for one night before our study abroad program began. I arrived at the hotel after the three girls had. I was very confused about it's location. There is a sign outside of the building above a random driveway. Aside from the sign, there is no direction about how to proceed. At the end of the driveway, there is a small elevator. It only fits one person with luggage. In the elevator, I believe there was a sign that said what floor the hotel was on. Once I found the hotel, I had to ring a bell for service at the front desk. The man told me what room my friends were in, but upon wandering around the confusing hallways, I couldn't find it. Eventually, I had him personally walk me there. The room had four beds in it, which were more like cots. This room was not meant for four people and their luggage. It was not comfortable. The stand-up shower and bathroom in general were clean, surprisingly. We had trouble locking our door with the old key, but it worked once we figured it out. The wifi password system is confusing and doesn't work. We paid too much for so little. $200 Euro for the night altogether for 4 people.

reviews.title: Do Not Stay At This Hotel!
reviews.text: The ONLY good thing about this hotel was that it had an elevator. Other than that, the carpet throughout the hotel is dark, old and dirty. Walking into the actual hotel (which is on the 3rd floor only) was eery because it was dark, rundown and had a weird old stench to it. With regards to the room - I was scared to walk on the carpet with bare feet. It wasn't one large strip of carpet, but a whole bunch of squares stuck together. The wall paper was coming off the wall and there was a cobweb on the ceiling. The Air Conditioning was like a massive glorified fan which worked worse than a fan. It kept our room at about 30 degrees celsius the entire night - we could barely sleep. They also only work with one taxi service so we went across the street to a nicer hotel and asked them to order us a taxi to the airport for the next morning - they were more than happy to oblige (it was cheaper than the service that Ara Pacis offered). Overall, I would never stay here again. I was actually scared to sleep in that room.

reviews.title: Sweating
reviews.text: July2-7, 2004 The hotel had no air conditioner. They called it one but it was so bad Red Cross would deem it inhumane living conditions. When we got there the front desk said do you want a room with a terrace. This sounded good but when we got in the room the bell boy was showing us how to use the airconditioner. We had to leave the terrace door open for it to work. I told him that where I come from that is not an air conditioner. It was about 95 degrees and the front desk said to leave the terrace door open. There was 2 problems with that. We had to share the terrace with the adjoining room and it was so hot I would of sweated to death. I told the front desk this was unacceptable and does he have a room with a real airconditioner. He said tommorrow we could change rooms. That night I only could sleep an hour and was very tired. The next day we changed rooms but this did not help. This room was very small. In the bathroom you could actually go to the bathroom, shave, and take a shower all at the same time. I never thought I be able to say that. Again the "so-called" air conditioner did not help as we were forced to sleep with the window open, oh and can you say "no screens". The choice was either sleep hot or with the window open and get bitten by mosquitos. Even with the window open it was still hot. I found out why all those old people died because of the heat in France. Good things about the hotel: The hotel is in a great location and you could walk to every site. The hotel did offer good tours. My advice would be that if you go there in the Spring, it's bearable.

reviews.title: Good location - Shame about the rooms
reviews.text: We chose to book the Ara Pacis for three nights to celebrate both our wedding anniversary and my husbands birthday at a cost of £50 per night as they offered "Great rooms, Great rates". The hotel is in a good location, situated in a beautiful building and the hotel foyer impressive. The size of the room we were allocated (room 35), left us both deflated and momentarily speechless!. The room was so small that there was no room to walk up the sides of the bed. Access could only have been by crawling up from the bottom of the bed. A very large wardrobe blocked more than 50% of the access to the toilet and shower room, making it almost impossible to get into (and we are not large people). There was also a very strong smell of paint or some other substance that even if the room had been big enough, would have made it impossible to sleep in. We asked for a different room and were told that we had not paid much money, and this was what we had paid for (remember the advert "Great rooms, Great rates". We were told we could have a larger room (that had been allocated to someone else!) at an additional cost of 30 euros per night. Having no alternative, we paid the money and were given room 10. This was, in my opinion the size of room we had paid for (a standard double). This was apparently their 'double superior' and large enough for 3 people. We would like to be there when they try to put a third bed in. My husband is an engineer and couldn't work it out! This room was dark and noisy, overlooking a very busy road. We were woken up by the bin lorries, sirens, and at 6am, the person in the adjoining room taking a shower. It sounded as though they were in the same room!. The soundproofing between the adjoining rooms and the kitchen across the corridor was appalling. Although clean, the showeroom had mould spores on the tiles, walls and shower cubicle and beware the hole in the floor by the wardrobe!. We did see some very nice spacious rooms in the hotel (when they were being cleaned) but I'm not sure what the criteria for being allocated one of these was (but obviously we didn't meet it). On the plus side, the bed was clean and comfortable (once we had bought some earplugs) and the breakfast was basic but plentiful. Most of the staff were courteous and helpful. Question: Would I return to the Ara Pacis? Answer: Definitely not. There are many hotels in the same area to chose from for the price we paid. Question: Should you stay at the Ara Pacis? Answer: After reading all the reviews, the decision is yours!.

reviews.title: loved this hotel
reviews.text: Only by case we discovered this hotel. We arrived in Rome by car and we passed by the hotel and we decided to ask for a family room. They were very helpful and the location and the price given was very convenient. Excellent staff, they helped us to park the car and more during our stay. The room was big as well as the bathroom.We were impressed of the beautiful ceiling dated 18Th Century. We walked from the Hotel to the Vatican, the Spanish Steps, Navona Square and so on..all was very close to us. We liked our stay, we were lucky to find this hotel!

reviews.title: Stay clear of this place!!
reviews.text: I truly felt from the first moment I walked to that front desk that I was simply inconveniencing the staff. I did not find one staff member at this hotel that would even attempt crack a smile, or be even half pleasant. They were down right rude. The building shown on the picture is not really the whole truth. The so called 'hotel' is burried up on the top floor of this residential building, with very bad and frustrating signage. It took a while just to find where it actually is. The hallway in the hotel start nice and wide, then turn into a narrow white, hospital like corridor you can barely get your suitcase through. There was absolutely no decor in the room... it felt more like a dorm room... meaning white wash dirty walls without even one picture on he wall. For $175 Euros, I was expecting way more. The bathroom was dirty, with the last guests hair all over the floor... disgusting! Vanity shelf was broken off and there was black mold all around the corners of the shower. The WIFI internet does not work in the room... only in the lobby and it only worked the first day. Following days it was down and I was told by the staff that it's not their problem, to call tech support my self. The breakfast was not bad but not one piece of fruit to be found anywhere... even a banana would have been great. The keys on the room door are from the turn of the century and can easily be opened with probably a bread knife, so I did not feel the my belongings were secure at all. Location was decent and I would give that the only upside. Otherwise I would stay clear of this place. Truly a very disappointing experience.

reviews.title: The Most Hideous Hotel I've Ever Stayed In... And I'm No Snob!
reviews.text: I'll start with the positives: Great location, with in walking distance of just about anything you would want to see in this beautiful city! The rest is terrible. Bad service, horrible dark, dingy rooms. Tired, disgusting decor. I asked to move rooms straight away and did so with-out question as to why i wanted to move. As if they needed to ask, they knew they were taking the micky... €145 per night for that tiny dump! i would have expected more from a youth hostel. I wouldn't have fed the breakfast to my dog! I usually can only afford 3* but thus was 1* at a push. On top of all this there was constant work on the floor above the hotel with drilling and banging from 7am which we were not informed of when booking and which the hotel staff thought was not a problem and couldn't even muster a tiny hint of sympathy let alone an apology! AVOID AVOID AVOID

reviews.title: Not Impressed
reviews.text: Did some research and the AraPacis was the only one available in the area we wanted. Unfortunately the price was 180 EU/night. A little steep in our opinion. There is definitely an ambiance and the elevator was very efficient (Sep. 04). However, the A/C was non-existent even though they seemed to think it worked and there was not enough lighting in the room - hard to read. Our room was at the front and it was extremely noisy during night from the motor vehicles on the street. The TV did not get many channels and we could not watch the soccer game. The staff was aloof, breakfast was fine and the location suited us perfectly. We walked to every sight, even the train station. Definitely an average hotel. We will not be returning to this hotel.

reviews.title: Horrible
reviews.text: We got to the hotel early (by an hour) and was rudely turned away, until check-in. Our bed had bed bugs, the shower over-flowed and there was just one employee at the desk who was willing to help us, or answer any questions we had. The charges posted for the hotel shuttle are not correct, (when we inquired, the price was significantly higher then what was posted) and the room was so small there was no where to even keep one suitcase open. They advertise internet, but you only get it if you ask for it and only in the lobby area. Overall, we couldn't wait to leave.

reviews.title: great hotel
reviews.text: I ve been in Hotel Ara Pacis for 3 nights with my girlfriend and we really liked the Hotel and the location. Great clean room (the ceiling is the from the 18th century!marvellous!!), all comforts, great air conditioning. We enjoyed the buffet breakfast in the morning, rich and plentiful. The location is superb, all is within walking distance. We loved Rome, we loved this Hotel.

reviews.title: delicious
reviews.text: A friend of ours living in Rome reserved us this hotel for a leisure trip I did with my family.. We had 3 rooms on the back side of the building and we really liked our stay. Excellent staff, lovely clean rooms, nice breakfast in the morning. We spent 4 days in Rome walking a lot around, seeing all the magnificence of this wonderful city. We loved the little restaurants in the centre, the friendly roman people..we felt in love for this city. I hope we' ll have the chance to come agin and for sure we will come back in this hotel.

reviews.title: Find another hotel.....do yourself a favor.
reviews.text: This hotel is one of the worst I have ever stayed in. It is old, dirty and worn. The wallpaper is literally falling off the walls in the threadbare rooms. The bed was awful , lumpy with worn out springs and hurt my back. The bathroom was clean but the toilet seat was cracked and the shower drain was stopped up. The night manager was more than rude and pompous, he was a jerk! The breakfast was inculded and adequate. The best thing about this hotel is its location, but there are many others with just as good a location. We were given a quote for an airport taxi for our departure one day and it magically increased the next day. When we finally fought with the jerk of a manager, he finally relented. STAY AWAY!!!!!!

reviews.title: These reviews are far too generous
reviews.text: I stayed at this hotel because the majority of the reviews here recommend it. I was so disappointed that I feel compelled to write this just to warn potential guests that you may be in for a surprise. I was given a miniscule single room to begin with -- one of those rooms where they built the bathroom into an already small square room, so the end result is an L-shaped room with a big square bathroom in one corner. From the room, I could step out onto a terrace, and this was nice. However, I discovered the next morning that there was no warm water. I asked for this to be remedied, was assured it would be, and woke up the next morning to -- you guessed it -- another ice-cold shower. I was told to change rooms, and was put in an even smaller double-room facing the back. Same bathroom construction, which meant that between the beds and the bathroom, there was enough space to take about 2 steps in the whole room. The television didn't work in this room and it smelled of smoke. The hotel has one of those charming policies of getting the maids to begin running their roaring vacuum cleaners in the corridors at just before 8 am. The walls are extremely thin, so if you want to sleep in, forget it. The breakfast 'buffet' is served in a claustrophobic space and consists of slices of bread, ham, industrial croissants wrapped up in plastic, processed white 'cheese' in plastic sheets, and, if you get there early, some quite OK pastries (these go quickly though, and are not replenished). Coffee and tea is provided by a single overworked waiter, so if there are more than about 6 people having breakfast at the same time, you may have finished eating by the time your cup of coffee arrives. I would not stay here again and recommend that other people shop around before choosing this hotel.

reviews.title: visit off-season
reviews.text: We decided to go to Rome with a friend, since we found an incredible last-minute offer for airline tickets.(ATH-FCO-ATH 57 Euro :-) ) Since this trip was not planned, we had only a little money to spend. We were indroduced to this hotel by a tourist kiosk at the airport which provides shuttle bus service. We told the agent that we wanted something cheap but in an area that is not dangerous for two girls to walk. It is located in a really strange building. You walk by a corridor to take the elevator and go to the third floor. We found this building very interesting yet wierd; we couldn't find out if there was any other person staying in it. Our room was small but not in a way that we couln't agree with that. It was charmingly decorated and clean. I didn't like very much the bathroom, we had to shower in a really small place. (I don't know the english word for it). The curtain was flooding in my feet as I was showering myself. The room got a little bit hot at night. The breakfast hasn't got any variety at all, but we didn't want to take breakfast anyway. The worst thing in this hotel is the staff. They seem to be bored and that they don't want to help you in any way. We wanted them to tell us us things to do in the area and they just showed us a map telling us to find it all by ourselves. They all seemed a little bit rude, and they speak very litlle english. (in Greece, were I come from, there is no way a receptionist doesn't speak fluent english). The best thing was the location. You could go to the Vatican Museum and the city center on foot, in a very little distance. It was a very good area, and we weren't frightened at all to walk at night alone. We stayed there 2 nights, and I stayed alone for one more night after my friend left. When she left, I paid the same price even though I was only one person. It was very cheap, we paid 50 euro per room each day. (it was off season). I think that this price were extremely good for this hotel, I stayed in other hotels that were not as good as this and paid more. If you visit Rome off-season and you seek for an acceptable place to stay, I think it is a good idea to stay there.

reviews.title: Never again
reviews.text: We stayed at Ara Pacis Hotel for two nights and it was a terrible experience. The bathroom was about two squared meters: impossible to have a regular shower. Moreover the whole bathroom was soon soaked, and water ran out into the bedroom. Ants walking along a moldy wall. Very poor breakfast. Need more? Never again.

reviews.title: Disappointed in the stifling Ara Pacis
reviews.text: We just spent 6 nights at the Ara Pacis. This should be listed as a 2 star, rather than 3 star, hotel -- and, even then, it is of dubious quality. The 2 star Casci in Florence -- a wonderful place -- is vastly superior. The worst thing about the Ara Pacis is the dissimulation about air conditioning. The "air conditioner" in our room was only a dehumidifier, and did nothing to cool the stifling room (other guests we spoke to at breakfast also had been told that their dehumifiers were air conditiners). If we opened the windows, the noise was deafening. The room (a quad) was barely big enough to walk around in. The bathroom was fine. Breakfasts were good. Some staff were friendly, some were aloof. Location was ideal. The elevator was still working. We would not stay here again in the summer, because of the nonexistent air conditioning.

reviews.title: beautiful room, excellent location
reviews.text: Me and my family stayed at the ara pacis in february of 2005 for 4 nights. When we arrived at the hotel we were a day late for our reservation and dead tired from traveling from germany that morning. The wonderful desk clerk Claudio promptly offered us a wonderful breakfast and then let us settle into an upgraded room. It was so beautiful. The hotel itself is moderately classy located on the 3rd floor of a building. They have a functioning elevator which is very helpful. The free breakfast is wonderful in the morning, all of the staff are very welcoming and friendly. The location is awesome. It is only about a 20 minute walk to the colloseum and several other popular destinations are along the way. Walking is a little scary because of the wild drivers in rome but the shopping is wonderful. I would advise you to walk though because you really get to see everything and it is not that far at all. I truly loved our stay at the ara pacis and would definetly stay there again. Hope this review was helpful.

reviews.title: Stuffed us around big time
reviews.text: We booked 3 nights at this hotel only to arrive and be told we'd have to stay at another hotel in their chain for one night, then be moved back to this hotel for the remaining 2 nights. The other hotel we agreed to stay in was terrible - apparently classified as a 4 star - what a JOKE !!! The room was really small, no shower curtain, no bath mat, no room to put your suitcase. I don't recommend this hotel or any in the chain at all !

reviews.title: Great location, good value 4 $, however....
reviews.text: Hotel refurbished in '92... and still ongoing today! They don't tell you that reception is on 5th floor & there is an "antique" elevator only available on demand, so if you have elderly people with you... Otherwise the location compensates a lot - almost all places of major interest are in walking distance and bus stop right in front of hotel.Taxi stand only 5 minute walk away. Romans are definitely "not Italians" as it is hard to find friendly waiters, taxidrivers in general and honest provider of other services in particular... visited there early February and had a busy 3 days to see most of the famous tourist attractions!

reviews.title: great location...adequate acommodations
reviews.text: The grand foyer of the hotel is quite impressive with an elegant marble staircase and and very tall wooden double doors. The elevator was a bit hidden, but thank god we found them as the actually hotel is located on the third floor. Staff was welcoming upon arrival and fairly helpful. The room we had was ok and just enough room for the four of us. The high ceilings in the room were vaulted and very impressive looking. Unfortunately, the entire hotel is in need of some upgrading as the lock and knob on our door was falling off, which made us a little weary about the security of our belongings when we left the room. Fortunately nothing happened and the hotel seemed to be very safe and secure. Breakfast was mediocre consisting of white bread slices (wonderbread), individually wrapped cheese slices (kraft singles), hard boiled eggs, and store bought pastries. It did the trick though. Location was hard to beat as it was 15 min walk from the Vatican, 10 min walk from Spanish steps and Trevi Fountain, 30 min walk from Coloseum, and just a few steps away to some impressive shopping (ie. Fendi, Gucci, Prada, D&G, the list goes on!) Overall, you get what you pay with this hotel. I was generally pleased with my experience.

reviews.title: Excellent value for money.
reviews.text: Wonderful value for money hotel in a great spot. Ideal for the Vatican & St Peters and just a short bus ride to the Colloseum.Staff were friendly and corteous at all times.Room was a decent size and the breakfasts were ok.Only problem was that the lift was out of order and seven flights of stairs is a lot when you have been walking around Rome all day.Overall I would recommend this hotel to anyone who does not want to spend big money.

reviews.title: Not Impressed
reviews.text: We stayed at the Ara Pacis for one week in February 2005. We prefer staying at smaller friendly hotels in Europe, so we were looking forward to the Ara Pacis. We were disappointed. I agree with the traveler who said "You get what you pay for". This is a 2 star (not a 3 star) hotel. The breakfasts were very nice, but nothing special. The location is suberb, and for the most part, the hotel is clean. However . . . the accomodations were dated and not very comfortable. The hotel needs upgrading and renovation. For example, the windows did nothing to drown out the noise of trucks and busses throughout the night, the blowdryer in the bathroom was falling apart, housekeeping forgot to give us fresh towels twice, the radiator worked sporadically, the lighting in the room was horrible, and the doors were paper thin and could not insulate us from the loud drunken tourists who were on either side of our room and routinely came in at 1:30 am! Yet, the most disappointing aspect of the hotel was the personnel. Although the breakfast waitresses and the concierge on the late night shift was quite nice, but the day-time concierge was lazy, apathetic and generally inhospitable. He would not even make eye-contact and when I asked him if he could help us make reservations at the Uffizi for our day-trip to Florence, he told me to look up the number myself and call from my room phone. He was no help when we asked him where to purchase bus tickets either. Useless and unfriendly. If not for the location and price, I would not recommend this hotel under any circumstances.

reviews.title: Absolutely Pathetic
reviews.text: It was hot in Rome and the hotel was not at all prepared with the airconditioning. They have this standalone AC in the room with a huge duct going out of the window (because of which you cannot close the window). ACs were totally ineffective and it was unbearably hot. To add to this toilet flush was not working. We saw atleast 4 rooms before settling on a room with a "new" AC (which wasn't any good either). So I guess we can say that it was not "problem with a particular room" but decadence in general.
