I wanted a smoking room, was told that the whole hotel is non smoking but "if you smoke, we don't know" !!!! Stay clear of this place. Not at all worth the money you will pay.

reviews.title: miserable staff
reviews.text: I found the staff on the desk at this hotel very unhelpful, they always seemed very un friendly and miserable. Sometimes not even acknowledging you when you said good morning. I found the lady who brought out the breakfasts also to be very miserable when you asked for a pot of tea, it seemed as if it was too much trouble to her. A cleaner from the hotel kept coming into the dining room from the kitchen and taking food from the table where the guest had to pick their breakfast, the cleaner didnt look very clean and I felt that this practice should not happen. On the whole the hotel was ok, but the staff need replacing for people who have visited to come back or recommend the hotel. I wouldnt recommend or re visit.

reviews.title: Beware about giving credit card details
reviews.text: I am writing this review to warn others to be cautious about giving out credit card details when booking hotels in Rome. I have booked many hotels in Spain etc without being asked for credit card details, however when I recently contacted several hotels in Rome, they all requested that I e-mail my credit card details in order to confirm the booking. I refused to e-mail my card details as it's not secure, but eventually agreed to give them to the Hotel Ara Pacis (one of the Ludoviki chain) through their secure web-site. A few hours before we were due to fly, all flights to and from Rome were cancelled due to a general workers strike in Rome. Out of courtesy we e-mailed the hotel and taxi firm to explain (although they would already have been aware about the strike). A couple of days later I received an e-mail stating that the hotel was going to charge my credit card for 1 night (if I hadn't e-mailed when I did it would have been 2 nights). I attempted to stop the payment, however I was informed by the bank that by me giving my card details to the hotel I was authorising the payment and there was no way I could prevent them from taking the money! I have since e-mailed the Hotel Ara Pacis, Ludoviki Group and Rome Hotel Services (who I booked the hotel through) stating that it is appalling and nothing short of robbery that they have taken this payment, but they have all declined to respond. It is legal for them to take the payment as it is in line with their cancellation policy; however under these circumstances it is certainly unethical. PLEASE BEWARE WHEN YOU OFFER YOUR CREDIT CARD DETAILS YOU ARE AUTHORISING THE HOTEL TO TAKE PAYMENT, AND THE ARA PACIS AND LUDOVIKI GROUP WILL TAKE PAYMENT NO MATTER WHAT THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CANCELLATION ARE (EVEN A GENERAL WORKERS STRIKE WHEN IT IS COMPLETELY OUT OF YOUR CONTROL!!)- SHOULD YOU BE AS UNLUCKY AS WE WERE!

reviews.title: Well located and friendly
reviews.text: I have just spent a pleasant weekend at the Ara Pacisand would like to add to previous opinions on this hotel. The hotel is situated on the third floor of a very well located building , and contrary to previous reports the lift is now brand new and in perfect working order. When checking in I asked whether we had been allocated a room with a balcony , although one was not available that night we were transferred for our second night . If there is any way that you can get a room with a balcony , do it ! . Not only is the patio and view an added bonus but the balconied rooms are situated in a quieter side street ( not so much traffic noise ) The only gripes I have are that neither room had air conditioning and the bathrooms are rather small , but overall a good hotel at a fair ( for Rome ) price

reviews.title: perfect location
reviews.text: We found this hotel very well located and really comfortable for all our needings during our recent visit to Rome. Ideal location, few minutes walking from the Vatican and the Spanish Steps. Around the hotel is full of restaurants and pubs where we spent our roman nights.Look for the area of Campo dei Fiori, it is the place where to find people and fun.

reviews.title: We'll be back
reviews.text: Despite some bad reviews, we liked this hotel. It is located in the centre of the city and we had two large rooms with all comforts. Good breakfast to start the day and helpful staff. It was really convenient for us, we will syrely come back again.

reviews.title: Hidden gem
reviews.text: Transferred to this hotel when our booked accommodations fell through - and very happy to do so. Located on the 3rd floor of an older building, this hotel has retained as many of it's charming features as possible (wood beam ceilings, marble stairs, old windows with shutters, skeleton key door locks, etc.) Rooms are clean and comfortable with minifridge, airconditioning and cable tv. Staff is very courteous (makes such a difference when staying there) and very helpful. Breakfast buffet offers continental choices. Very conveniently located for visitors, 5 minutes walk from Vatican, in a neighborhood that offers restaurants, coffee shop, tobacco shop and pharmacy, with buses travelling to major tourist attractions stopping just across the street. Neighborhood relatively free from graffiti & crowds.

reviews.title: excellent
reviews.text: For business reasons I had to spend 4 nights in Rome, and that was my first time. My company booked me this hotel and I ve found it convenient and well located. The room was large and clean. Good breakfast in the morning. The hotel is within walking distance from the Spanish Steps and the main shopping area. Definitly a good choose.

reviews.title: Falsely advertised- aweful hotel experience
reviews.text: My wife and I prepaid for 3 nites- which, from thie website looks like an ideal hotel. Instead, we were given a room with cigarete burn holes in the covers and peeling,torn wallpaper , a plastic sheet as a ceiling and a 20 watt bulb on the wall sconce. The hallway had disgusting old rug squares with holes in the main corridor floor. We switched to another room, one with a plastic wire leading into the wall which served as a toilet flush. We finally switched rooms again to one with a loose toilet seat . When showering the entire bathroom floor received the water. This hotel, in my opinion, and we have stayed in many is what I would call a fleabag. It does not look as if any repairs are/have been made to the place for years. I would highly recommend finding another hotel.

reviews.title: not very impressed
reviews.text: The hotel is well-placed for sight-seeing, especially for the Vatican. However, I think the hotel is cashing in on its location and is over-priced for the facilities offered. The hotel corridors are dingy and the whole place needs decorating. The entrance to the hotel does not feel safe, particularly at night-time. The staff are surly and do not offer help willingly. The room was much smaller than shown on the website, and the bathroom was little more than a cupboard. Breakfast was mediocre. The hotel should not be graded as a 3 star.

reviews.title: This made our week!
reviews.text: What a great hotel - November, unusally warm and beautiful. Room smaller than USA hotels but very adequate. Excellent location - we didn't need a car. Everything is in walking distance. 15 minutes to the Vatican, Colliseum,Trevi, Spanish Stairs, shopping, tons of restaurants,staff was excellent, breakfast very good. Always greeted with a smile- anything we asked help on they delivered. Arranged limo from FCO airport both ways and got us a discount. Fluent in English - really made us feel like family. We will stay with them again. For dinner visit Vito's Irish Pub around the corner.

reviews.title: Good Location for Vatican City
reviews.text: Well located, fifteen minutes walk to Vatican City. Lots of local restaurants, cafes and shops five minutes from the hotel. Access to buses right outside the door. About twenty to thirty minutes walk to the tourist areas; Spanish Steps, Trevi Fountain, Colliseum a little further. Twenty minutes walk to the Spagna stop on the subway. Five minutes to Ponta Cavour and the Tiber River. Single small room with double bed, decent bathroom with shower,clean and well taken care of. Little bit on the rundown side, here and there. Clean linen and towels everyday. Hairdryer, soap, shampoo, notepaper and map of Rome in the room. Rooms were tiny but efficient with desk, chair, wardrobe that locked with key. Small bar refrigerator. Eighty euros per night single occupancy. Continental breakfast buffet every morning at eight A.M., hard crusty rolls, toast, sliced meats, cheese, juice, hard-cooked eggs, coffee etc.. Bread often day old but manageable. Hotel staff helpful and knowledgable, day desk clerk spoke english, french, italian, and some german. Polite and kind if you were not pushy or aggressive with them. Maids and Cook spoke Italian. Few little problems; Doors to rooms made alot of noise, difficult to lock and unlock with ancient keys. Little privacy, walls seemed paper thin. In the two rooms that I stayed in, both small locks on the wardrobes had been forced at one time or another. They locked, but were easy to force open. Carried any money and passport with me, so there was little to steal of any value in my room.

reviews.title: Clean & courteous lodging
reviews.text: I stayed at the Aris Pacis in July of 2003, after being bounced from my booked hotel, and was glad I ended up there! The staff was exceedingly courteous, doing everything within their means to make my stay as pleasant as possible. The building is centuries old, so the lift (mentioned in several of the other reviews on this site) is small and tempermental, but the hotel is located on the 3rd floor of the building - so it is not overly difficult to reach if walking up and down. My daughter and I made a game of seeing who would reach the top/bottom first if one was in the lift and one ran up/down the stairs. The rooms are small - as with most European hotels, but clean. Our room had a mini-fridge, a color tv, air conditioning, and windows which we could open if we chose. The hotel offers an extended continental breakfast every day, included in the price of the hotel. This consists of various beverages (milk/juice/coffees/tea), cereals, rolls, fruit, yogurt. Enough to satisfy travellers that want to get out and explore their surroundings. The neighborhood is one of the safer and cleaner areas of Rome from what I could see (much more pleasant than the district around Termini Station). The location is very convenient, within walking distance of the Vatican, and the city center, with several buses stopping literally just outside the door of the hotel. There are restaurants and coffee shops nearby, as well as a pharmacy, and a store just around the corner to purchase bus tickets. All in all, my daughter and I were very happy to stay here. The staff made what would have been a bad experience pleasant and enjoyable, and we loved the experience of staying in a building as old as this. We were quite surprised at how easy it was to get to everything from the hotel. All of this for a price that was - if not downright cheap, certainly not exhorbitant!

reviews.title: 3 Star in a great location....
reviews.text: First impression was note great, but got better - I arrived late on Saturday night and they had limited rooms left. So, they changed me (from Room #3 to #11) on Sunday and it was a lot brighter and larger, with a much better & cleaner bathroom.I stayed a week, and it was fine for the price - on hindsight I might have searched for other location, but it would have been pricier. It was a 3-star; the hotel staff were helpful and friendly enough, and breakfast was ok. There were marvelous large marble steps to the Hotel, which was on 3rd floor of the building. There was an elevator and it was old, but worked fine. Location was super, as it was easy to walk everywhere. I walked about 10 minutes down the Tiber River towards St. Peter's & Vatican daily - beautiful view. This is Rome...there are neat places, and it had character. It was clean. WiFi was free and worked in the lobby area - staff said it didn't in most rooms - other friends stayed in hotels which charged 11 - 14 euros/day for internet.

reviews.title: Great place!
reviews.text: Great place to stay, I would recommend it to anyone. The location of the hotel is spectacular! It's right in the heart of Rome. We stayed at this hotel for a fun, relaxing, enjoyable weekend, this hotel made it possible. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The hotel was gorgeous inside and out, day or night. Our room was quiet and comfortable, probably one of the best beds I have ever slept in. The hotel was still very peaceful with all of the many people staying in there. Alexander, Moscow (Russian Federation).

reviews.title: nice and clean
reviews.text: During our recent stay in Italy we have been travelling to Rome and we spent 3 days in this lovely hotel. It has a great location and we had a big family room.The hotel is really comfortable and we loved our stay. The breakfast is rich and perfect to start a long day in town. Helpful staff.Thanks Claudio at the front desk for all.

reviews.title: You get what you pay for
reviews.text: This hotel was very inexpensive, I think we paid $93 US dollars a night, what can you really expect? Our room was very small, wasn't exactly a looker, but it did the trick. It had a small bathroom with new fixtures, but sticking with Italian tradition, it had the random,"shower-head in the middle of the room" motif happening. Once you get over how ridiculous that is, it is really fine. The room did not have central air, but they did wheel in a teletubbie-looking portable air conditioner that worked just fine. If you are able to get over the "petite-ness" of the space and the bizarre quirks, you will realize you are getting a pretty good deal in a good location for a very expensive city.

reviews.title: Location is the only positive
reviews.text: This hotel is shabby, run down and managed by unhelpful staff. I has initially booked a single room for 2 nights, but I was told I had to change rooms each night, which was a nuisance. The 'air conditioning' in the second room was merely a fan on a desk. I then was booked into a triple room with friends - the room was clean, but poorly maintained. There was no hot water on their arrival and when we complained and came back, there was still no hot water and the plumber had turned off the air con and on the heat in 36 degrees! Any complaints were poorly dealt with - on one occasion the desk clerk walked away when I was in mid conversation. The location of this hotel is the only thing it has going for it, and on the experience of the rudeness alone, I would not recommend this hotel for anyone.

reviews.title: Nice location, but noisy...
reviews.text: Great location near all the attractions in Rome, we could walk to almost everything within about 20 minutes. Room was very small for four adults and was extremely noisy. Air conditioning would only work about half the night and then you had to have the windows open which meant no sleeping because of the noise! Staff was friendly and breakfast was good

reviews.title: Ara Pacis - Great location
reviews.text: Stayed at the Ara Pacis with family of four July 25th to the 29th. Room was small but clean, Requested balcony room on the web site when booking and was pleased to find it was a total walk out terrace. Total area was 3-4 times the size of the room. Bathroom was update and hot water and presure perfect. Staff were friendly (it helps if you speak Italian, like my wife, but ok if you don't, like me) and request for second in room fan was acted on right away (no AC in our room but double doors opened to terrace so no problem). Elevator is brand new. Location is very good, possible to walk to all sites. Area is very safe, mostly banking and Government offices. There are two little food shops around the back were you can get anything you need at a good price and they speak a little bit of english. Breakfast was ok, Capp. for the parents hot choc for the kids. Nice all round place if you are not looking for to many extras. Left Rome on the 29th by train to the very South (Capo Vaticano) one of the most beautiful places in all of Italy.

reviews.title: Excellent Location - but only for the fit
reviews.text: We were delighted with this hotel and got it at a great rate via www.*********. It is perfectly located to see all the major sites, and is very close to the Vatican. It is in a very good area with good shops, banks, coffee houses, etc. The only negative thing was that while we were there (Jan 2004) the lift was out of order and the climb up to the top floor certainly kept us fit. I would check if it is working before you book if you are not keen on the climb. The room was great, the shower superb and the facilities more than adequate. Room had a fridge and a minibar. The breakfast was very nice - coffee of your choosing, pastries, breads, meats, cheeses, cereals, yoghurts, etc. If we were to return to Rome we would not hesitate to use this hotel again. Enjoy your stay!

reviews.title: It was okay........
reviews.text: It was a convenient hotel wrt the sights of Rome. Only major grievance I have is the fact that I could not book the hotel online for 3 days and on the second day whilst there, they doubled the room rate. Also, I was disgusted with the bed linen........quite filthy even after they changed it at my request.

reviews.title: DO NOT STAY AT ANY COST!
reviews.text: I stayed there with my husband and my little 18month old boy in February 09. We booked the accommodatoin on wotif and it was the worst choice ever. Not knowing how horrible the experience would be, it was the longest 5 nights of my life. First there was not even a microwave to heat up my son's milk, and they weren't willing to help out. So i needed to go to the front dest and ask for boiled water to heat up his milk everytime i needed it. The bathroom was small and stank bad. This made the whole room stink like a male toilet cubical. The room was old and so in need of rennovation. The sheets were yuk and the man at the reception was not friendly. Everything in that room was old and horrible. To top things up with my stay I had to be sick with vomiting and the runs! It was the last place you want to be in when you're sick. Breakfast was very limited and internet didn't always work. I don't recommend this place to anyone. I regret staying for that long, this made my experience in Rome not so good. We got desperate and wanted to leave, but knew we have already paid for it and we wouldn't get the rest of our money back. Each night I would dreaded going back to the smelly hotel room! I think I have said enough!

reviews.title: Good Location
reviews.text: I think the location of the hotel is great, it is in the centre of most things and within walking distance to most of the main sites. The room was very dark and dingy, with very little lighting and in need of decoration. The rooms were clean and linen was changed daily, but the staff were not very helpful and the breakfast could have been better. There were no views of rome from the hotel, like shown in pictures on the hotels own website. Ideal place to stay if you are not after the little luxuries in life, like a cooked breakfast or decent cup of coffee/tea!!

reviews.title: Lying and Impolite Staff
reviews.text: It was terrible staying. When we booked the room, they told us there would be air conditioner. However, there was nothing and then we talked to a guy there. He took us to another room with a fan and kept saying that was an air conditioner!!!! It was late at night, so we had to accept. The day after, we tried to talk to another guy and we finally changed to a room with air conditioner but the room was really small. Most of staff were very impolite, answering without smile (sometimes with anger)! We would never return!

reviews.title: Very Good for Price
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here a few months ago. I booked through Hotels.com and found the room for approximatly $100. I read the reviews on here for the hotel,after booking it and was very nervous. The hotel staff are great and the room was as to be expected for being a european room. It was small but I was there to see Rome not to hang out in a hotel. There is no AC, but the hotel provides a floor fan. That and having the window open will give you a nice breeze. Rooms open onto courtyard so noise is minimal. I go to Rome alot right now because we are stationed in Italy and I will definetly stay here everytime. It is a 5 minute walk to Piazza de Spagna and about 25 to Collosium. I would recommend this to any.

reviews.title: Pretty average and small rooms
reviews.text: We stayed here in November 2004. The room was small with only a foot or so space around the bed and had tiny windows. The bathroom was very narrow and basic. The breakfast room (again small) was a joke, only the first few got the croissant and sometimes you had to wait for a table. The staff were often over worked and neglated waiting guests. Possibly the hardest part is finding the entrance from the street as you have to take a hidden lift to reception. All in all below average and we will not be staying there again.

reviews.title: Excellent and great staff!!
reviews.text: We enjoyed staying here. The staff made us feel welcome. Minutes to everywhere. This hotel had a great location to the Vatican area and we felt safe walking around. We will definitely stay here again when we come back.. Thanks, P. Nguyen

reviews.title: Do NOT stay here - Dirty beyond belief
reviews.text: We arrived from Barcelona 3/14 and made our way to the Ara Pacis by hired car. The Hotel entrance was difficult to find - dark entrance leading to an elevator with the lobby of the hotel being on the 2nd floor. We checked in and were taken to our room fairly quickly - up and around a few sets of stairs - The room was dismal to say the least. Wallpaper was peeling off the walls and what paint you could see was absolutely filthy, the bed was sunken in the middle and after pulling back the sheets we saw that they were a dirty gray colour. The doors leading to the balcony did not have any locks (this was an open balcony serving several rooms on our floor) This did not match the lovely pictures we saw on their website by any means. So we asked for another room and explained why we did not care for the present one. We were shown room number 2 - which was actually worse than the first one, now off to room number 3 which was off the sitting/lounge area from the lobby. This was a tad cleaner (but not by much) so we brought the suitcases down and I checked out the bed - upon looking up there was a separation between the door and the door frame with a perfect view of the lounge area. We had enough, left the hotel found another and returned for our baggage and to check out. At this point they tried to show us yet another room (which would have been #4) we declined and said they were falsely advertising on their website and we would be addressing it when we returned home. So here it is. The hotel is a solid one star or below if that's possible.

reviews.title: The lift/elevator not fixed yet...
reviews.text: We'll agree with everything positive in the other reviews (e.g. location, clean rooms) BUT the elevator has not been fixed yet and asking guests to hike up four floors is unacceptable. Based on the other reviews, this elevator has been under repair since last October, yet they greeted us with "we hope to have the elevator fixed between Monday and Wednesday" (we checked in Sunday). Since we had read the other reviews while we were staying at the hotel, we inquired every day as to whether it would be fixed. We were told "tomorrow we think". While the location can't be beat, there are other hotels in the area and the price range that do not require a workout on arrival.

reviews.title: Fine for the price
reviews.text: Small, dark bedroom with a comfortable bed. Thin walls and floors so very noisy at night. Some staff very friendly and welcoming while others were not. Breakfast was just ok. Located right opposite San Pedro market and a supermarket but not close to nice restaurants.

reviews.title: My worst hotel experience ever for this kind of price
reviews.text: We choose this hotel since Trop Advisor gave it a good review. As soon as we entered we had a bad feeling. No welcome drink, no smiles as everywhere else in Peru. Everything looks old fashioned. We paid for a double room which was exactly the same as our daughter's single room. The bathroom doesn't make you feel like using it. Moreover, it's noisy and cold. Breakfast was a disaster, but unfortunately I ate anyway. 2 hours later I was really sick and I was really ashamed since I did not even make it to the bathroom. It must have been because of the breakfast. We came back from the Incatrail the night before and were too tired to eat. In the beginning we had the intention to comme back after our next trip but we changed hotel. We did not want to come back. Checking out this evening, we were quite shocked to see the hotel asked us to pay for the cleaning of towels and blanket! Which hotel does ????? And in this case, we are certain I was sick because of the hotel's breakfast!!!! Can anyone explain how this hotel can possibly be noted 4,5???????

reviews.title: Perfect location in Cusco
reviews.text: I loved this hotel! It was clean and actually had HOT water, both very important when traveling. We went to Machu Picchu by way of Cusco, but weren't actually staying the night at this hotel until after we returned from Machu Picchu. I called in advance to ask their opion on the train schedule and how I should plan for that leg of the trip. They were very helpful over the phone and answered all of my questions. They allowed us to drop our luggage off before catching the train and held onto it for us until we checked in 2 days later. It was the best place we stayed while we were in Peru. It was also close to everything we needed and wanted to do. It was in the city center, which is very noisy, but once you got to your room you couldn't even tell you were in the city. It was so quiet and comfortable.

reviews.title: UNACCEPTABLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!
reviews.text: We travel a lot, so we know that things may not always go smoothly, but we have never experienced such an UNACCEPTABLE CUSTOMER SERVICE before. Never. So, if you book this hotel, fingers crossed that everything is fine, otherwise you may well be in trouble... This is what happened to us. On the first night (paid in advance) we found out that there was no hot water. After a few attempts the staff gave up and we were offered another room of lower grade. At this point it was 10.30 pm and we had to weak up at 5.00am on the following day to start a hike. Not an ideal situation but, honestly, these things happen. And generally they end up with the hotel offering you not to pay for the night or giving you at least a 50% discount (plus of course the price difference between the two rooms, as we were moved to a lower grade one). It doesn't give you back your sleep but at least you don't pay for poor service. This is not quite what happened to us. The room was already paid for, so we couldn't get a refund on the first night. However, as we were coming back after 4 days for a second night, we were expecting some favourable treatment on the second one. But none of this happened: they just presented us with the full bill for the second night (despite the staff having ensured us that they would speak with the manager about our situation before we left for the trek). We managed to speak with the manager only after we requested it. The manager tried to argue that we weren't even entitled for a refund of the difference in price between the two rooms, because we had used the first room for most of the time (until 10.30pm), which we found offensive. When we made clear that it is by sleeping in a room that you can say you used it, she offered to refund the difference in price between the two rooms plus (after further negotiations) a further discount of circa USD 14 (!!) on a USD 92 per night room for the hassle, take it or leave it. We don't think that this is in any way acceptable (without even mentioning her rudeness in repeatedly turning to her colleague while we were explaining our issues to her). Problems with electricity, water or any other element of the service may just happen. To anyone. The problem with such a poor customer service is that, when they happen it is the customer who pays for it, instead of the hotel. And this is unacceptable.

reviews.title: Freezing
reviews.text: A hotel can't have problems with hot water, having a freezing shower at this cold city is being at hell, and this is not a cheap hotel. Also the room was badly aislated, cold air could pass down the door and had to use the extra stove to warm a little bit... Terrible experiencie in a "Deluxe room"...

reviews.title: Hotel Monastario
reviews.text: Excellent hotel right next to San Pedro Market and the old Monestary. We were only here one night, but given the chance, we would have spent multiple nights here. Great buffet breakfast, right across the street from San Pedro Market!

reviews.title: Great Price, Interesting Experience
reviews.text: I stayed here over 2 nights and it was a comfortable and affordable experience. Our room did not have heating other than a small space heater between the two beds. Other than that, the beds were very comfortable and the water pressure, and hot/cold response of the shower was excellent.

reviews.title: Picturesque Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is in the San Pedro Plaza. It is very old and attached to the church and a convent which includes an girls orphanage. The staff were good and also friendly and helpful. The rooms had a comfortable bed and included a small radiator for cool mornings. The breakfast provided was good.

reviews.title: Perfect location
reviews.text: My family and I stayed here 2 nights, New Year's Eve and day. It was a perfect location close to all the celebrations. In walking distance to everything. Tons of restaurants, marketplaces, squares, historical sites, etc. It was insanely fun with all the fireworks and festivities. The rooms were clean, large, comfortable. (Could have a little more hot water for the shower but that seemed typical of everywhere we have stayed in Peru.) I loved the fact that it was an old monastery and that proceeds were being used to help the local orphanage. It made a perfect end to our trip to the area.

reviews.title: Excellent hotel, deserving 5 stars in Cusco - all is perfect
reviews.text: Hotel is located in front of San Pedro market, very close to city center. Located inside monastery complex, with very nice gardens and interesting environment. Quite and fantastic place for the rest. Good location to know city which is not just for tourists. Every day have some local events and ceremonies in front of the church and hotel. Spent 3 days and nights in this wonderful quite and very clean hotel. Staff is very kind and helpful. Always can take coca tea or coffee in the lobby. Returned few hours after check out because of cancelled flight. On the reception had been given same room with same price (online booked with discount). Hotel restaurant is serving breakfast only, included in room price. Rooms are large, with big and comfortable bed. Equipped with heather and safe for your values. Bathroom is very clean, with hydro massage bath, was surprised with. And enjoyed of course. More than enough hot water for warm up your body in cold evenings.

reviews.title: Horrible service and old and cold hotel
reviews.text: We were in this hotel for two days with my parents. I disliked many things: -service and welcoming is poor -additional fees -breakfast is not fresh and makes you sick -quality and services in the room are not worth the price First thing we noticed : no smile at the reception and pretty cold welcoming. The place is a bit less nice than the photo. It has a nice history but that its only advantage. The room is old (from the 50s especially the bathroom) and old fashioned. It is clean though. The room is very cold and there is only a little heating that heats a very small portion of the room (Cuzco gets really cold at night). My room was very noisy. I heard both the sounds of the corridors late at night and early in the morning. I also heard the sounds of the city (loud music and cars horning). There are very limited services in the room and especially no drinkable water in the room which is very annoying if you arrive late and had no chance to refill your bottles. The breakfast is offered but you get to know why... it has no taste. Even the fruits and scrambled eggs were difficult to eat. It is not fresh. We did not ate for the past 20 hours and my mom got strong food poisoning after eating the butter. The hotel charged us for cleaning the sheets etc even if she made her best to avoid the worst cleaning for the staff ! This is a shame ! Would you charge someone if they put blood on the sheets ???? That's the same !!!! The have a very poor service. The laundry service is also pretty expensive and the results are not really incredible (the clothes are clean but that's all). I think you can have a better service somewhere else. Definitely not worth the price.

reviews.title: Train Whistle Wake-up call at 6
reviews.text: For the price, you get a clean room. What seems like it should be a quiet environment, is filled with noise starting at 6 AM thanks to the train. The first day I thought I'd see the bright side and walk to the market that sits immediately across the street, however it doesn't open until 9. Bottom line - if you're on a tight budget and have done your homework, go for it.

reviews.title: Lots Of Character, Nice Staff.
reviews.text: The hotel was older but clean and the rooms were spacious with comfortable beds. Plenty of hot water in the showers. Check-in went smoothly and staff was friendly and helpful, Susan at the front desk even arranged a last minute Sacred Valley tour for us. Would definitely go back.

reviews.title: A Very Authentic Experience
reviews.text: The hotel was located just across the road from the San Pedro Market. The location was our saving grace due to a very affordable supermarket located about a 3 minute walk away. The greeting was warm and the staff all spoke English. The property appeared to have been a converted monastery. Just walking to the room gave us a blast to the past with a very nostalgic feeling. As such, much of it was pretty much the original, ie only stairs, no lifts. We were on the 3rd floor at the restaurant section and it was a little problematic to get our bags up but were assisted by the friendly staff. Room had that old rustic feeling which was nicely furnished and was split into 2 sections. the first with 2 single beds and the second with 1 King bed. Only noticable drawback was that the first section had a roof light with no covering and those sleeping there would wake at morning's first light. Bathroom was at the King Bed section and shared. Conditions very clean and came with clean towels, shampoo, bath gel and conditioner. Shower was a highly sophisticated water jet and the flow of hot water was excellent after a long day. Only draw back was that the bathroom had no floor mat and the tiled floor was freezing. Breakfast had a good spread and the best were the banana pancakes which were amazing!! There were also a good variety of fruits with a free flow of drinks. Overall, an incredible experience and would love to stay here again.

reviews.title: Quaint, clean, outstanding value
reviews.text: We stayed here for 2 weeks and would absolutely recommend to anyone looking for a place that is quiet and clean, conveniently located but not too close to the Plaza de Armas. The staff is incredibly friendly and accommodating. The breakfast is varied, healthy and delicious, including breads, jams, cheese, ham, fruit, granola, eggs cooked to order, coffee, mate de coca and one hot dish every morning. The rooms surround several courtyard gardens for a lovely view. While the rooms are small, they are comfortable and the showers had plenty of hot water and good water pressure. The hotel is also home to an orphanage for young orphan girls - run by the Mercedales nuns, so your stay helps support this effort. The hotel is adjoining to one of the many cathedrals in Cusco and a short walk from the main plaza and located on a busy street directly across the street from El Mercado San Pero - an open air market with some of the best prices you'll find on clothes and handicrafts, not to mention all variety of food - including fruits, vegetables, cheeses, nuts, meats, grains, fruit smoothies, frog soup, san pedro cactus, etc. It's worth a walk through just to see the sights and take a few pictures. Be prepared to deal if you're looking to buy. If you come in early June as we did, you'll be treated to a full on street fair all over town, including the open plaza across the street from the hotel, where you'll find cuy (guinea pig), pomegranates, hard boiled quail eggs, boiled potatoes, corn, all variety of drinks - fermented and unfermented (often served "to go" in a plastic bag with a straw), games and all kinds of merchandise - from hats, to CDs to nail clippers. We had a blast and ate something from this fair everyday. The hotel is also located between a larger grocery and a small convenience store, so you can grab snacks, drinks, "dinner" of sorts if you're too tired to go out. It's also right by the train station, so arranging transport to Machu Picchu is fairly easy - just do it early as tourist tickets sell out quickly. The folks at the front desk will also gladly help with tours and such. We were glad to have found this place, we enjoyed our rather long stay and would highly recommend to all.

reviews.title: Good hotel helping kids!
reviews.text: The hotel has everything you need to have a good stay. Good bed, warm water for cold weather, normal breakfast (could be better), good location (closed to "Plaza de Armas"). It could be better for the price we paid but we liked the mission they have with the hotel. It is at the same time a monastery which helps orphan kids giving them a place to live, food and love by a religious woman who also live there. We never saw them but we would to spend time with the girls who live there. Good action!

reviews.title: Very varying
reviews.text: We stayed three nights; different bookings. First room was good and the bed excellent! We slept loke rozes. Ok you can hear the neighbours, but room was just redecorated. The second stay we got a room upstairs; much smaller and with an old bed; same third time. The side, good centre location and clean!

reviews.title: Great Cuzco Hotel
reviews.text: This little hotel was a former monastery and the architecture shows this everywhere. The location could not be better, directly across from the San Pedro Market and only minutes walking distance to all major squares and restaurants etc. Cuzco is a very walkable city. Large hot/cold buffet breakfast was excellent. Coca tea available in the lobby 24/7. Tip: We asked locals where to buy the Peruvian alcohol “Pisco”. They said the smaller stores downtown would charge double so go to Supermarket Orion. We found one and stocked up on pisco as well as juice/water/snacks for the next days trip to Machu Picchu. We lugged these things around until we got back to our hotel when we noticed that there was a big Orion right beside the hotel. Oh well, now YOU know. Lol.

reviews.title: A piece of heaven in cusco
reviews.text: Very nice hotel situated in cusco center. The rooms are very nice and clean, the shower is very correct. What is amazing here is the silence you can enjoy where cusco is a bit noisy sometimes. The gardens are lovely and the food is very tasty

reviews.title: great start at Monasterio
reviews.text: I have only spent one night so far at the Monasterio but the hotel is lovely and the service superb. The breakfast buffet is amazing and I have been lucky enough to have a great wait staff, Wilbert Soncco, attend to my every need. We are off to a great start.

reviews.title: The good, the bad, and the ugly
reviews.text: I write books for a living and it would be easy to write a novel about the problems with this hotel - but it's easier to first deal with the few things they got right. The Good 1. We paid $10.00 for a taxi from the airport - it never showed up and when we called the hotel they just told us to take a taxi. We did and they did pay us back our $10.00 BTW it's a ten minute drive from the airport and only cost us s./ 6 to take a taxi to the airport. 2. The shower was great when we had hot water. 3. Breakfasts were okay but nothing spectacular. The Bad 1. The bed in our room was STRANGE! It had a big black plastic part as the headboard, the left side of the bed had some sort of weird platform half the height of the bed that made it hell to get out of at night to go to the bathroom. 2. Mentioning the bathroom, the street noise, especially at night was terrible and bothered our sleep. 3. Sleep - HA like that cold happen between the noise of the street and the streetlight outside the window shining in at night... 4. Oh yeah, I almost forgot about the fricken nasty blue light on the bottom of the flat screen TV that stayed on all night. 5. There was a refrigerator in our room, but there was no place to plug it in? The Ugly 1. Housekeeping needs to empty the bathroom trash, they didn't two days and it gets smelly from the used TP (IN Peru you don't throw the TP in the toilet). 2. Housekeeping needs to clean under the bed, many dust bunnies and some trash was under it the whole time. 3. Hotel staff doesn't communicate. Night shift doesn't know what happened on day shift. We had a call from a travel agency about a trip, the night shift didn't know what time it was. 4. The hotel has a pizza restaurant on the second floor which is ground level to a side street. There's a access door to a stairway that leads to the other floors which doesn't appear to be guarded. This is a serious breech of security. Finally a complaint in general about Cusco, in specific the Catholic churches! I have never been to a cit in Peru that all the churches charge an entrance fee. FOr a city that makes 80% of it's money of tourists, the churches should be free.

reviews.title: Centrally located Hotel with comfortable rooms and friendly staff
reviews.text: This is a lovely hotel with friendly and obliging staff. This former monastery has been sympathetically converted, retaining many of the original features including quiet garden courtyards. Understandably there is no lift so if this could pose a problem request a room on the ground floor. I used this hotel has my base in Peru and, during December, 2016 and January 2017, I made several visits to the hotel staying from anything from 2 nights to over a week. On each of these visits I always found there was a friendly welcome, a substantial breakfast and constant hot water. Cusco does experience cold weather during December and January, usually cold mornings and evenings, but the heater in the room provided sufficient heat. The rooms/bathrooms were always clean and well presented. The free WiFi is fast and constant throughout the hotel. The hotel is in walking distance of the central market and many shopping areas, restaurants and coffee shops. Cusco is full of historical sites easily visited from this hotel. The 10% service charge included on the bill does, I am assured, go to staff and a connection is maintained between the hotel, the church and a local orphanage which receives funds from the hotel. I have stayed in other 3 star hotels in Peru and this is far and away the best. I have no hesitation in recommending this hotel.

reviews.title: A Recommendable Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is located at downtown of Cusco, just across the road from the San Pedro Market where you could sense local ordinary people's daily life. I stayed at this hotel for 3 days and liked my room. It's clean and very quiet. Front desk staff were very friendly and helpful. The breakfast was good with many choices. It is a convenient location to the major parts of the city. Plus, the room price was reasonable. Recommend.

reviews.title: Great location near the heart of Cusco.
reviews.text: We spent a total of 4 nights at the hotel, 3 before our trip to Aguas Calientes, and one night after. They graciously held our larger luggage for us while we were away. Delightful place to stay - it is unique as it seems to have been converted from an old monastery to a modern hotel, thus each room is a bit different. It is close to the San Pedro Market, just up the street from the main shopping and restaurant areas, and close to the main plaza. The staff also helped us to arrange a private driver and guide for a side trip. All in all a good choice.

reviews.title: Excellent hotel, a real Monasterio and also a hotel combined at perfection!
reviews.text: Beautiful, peaceful hotel, full of flowers and ancient / renovated construction, a place in the history, a perfect place to stay in Cusco, Peru. The service was excellent, a fare price and they accept all kind of cards. Also has a restaurant and a bar with room service with very good food.

reviews.title: Very good hotel delicious breakfast
reviews.text: We stayed here for one night in a double room with a friend. Hotel location is good in the center of Cusco. Room was nice, spacious and clean. They have a delicious breakfast with lot of options. One thing to take into consideration, they have no mini bar in the room, so make sure you bring water with you.

reviews.title: Changed name!
reviews.text: This hotel now has another name: Monasterio San Pedro and it has new owners, I really liked this hotel, it's close to San Pedro Church and they help an abandoned children home. Nice gardens, our room had a window on the roof so you could see the sky

reviews.title: Beautiful world class hotel
reviews.text: Just completed a 2 night stay at this wonderful hotel. From the gracious personalized check in to our simple check out everything was fantastic. A bright star in The Belmond collection I highly recommend you make this hotel your choice when in Cusco.

reviews.title: Great Staff
reviews.text: Great Staff, nice size rooms however if you need to sleep or have hot water after 7am do not expect either.. the other guests are loud and the wood floors and high ceilings make sound travel.. unfortunately most of the tours in peru start very early so getting sleep when people are checking in or parting in their rooms doesnt work the grounds are wonderful and the breakfast is good.

reviews.title: Considerable problems for a hotel.
reviews.text: The Ashiana is a interesting place, but have some serious problems, especially if you consider that a basic hotel have to provide you at least a good sleep and bath, with hygiene. The location is good, in the center of Cusco, but you have a train station around the hotel, and you can hear the noise of the trains around 5 o'clock in the morning. If you can ignore the noises, then consider the other problems. Cusco is a cold city. We had extremely cold nights (2~10º Celsius), but the heater of the room was poor and the corridors are in open sky, without heaters, and you have big stairs to get to the rooms (in the altitude of Cusco that is a problem). And that wasn't the biggest problem. The water of the bath was freaking COLD! It was impossible to have a good bath. We complained with the hosts, but they said that nothing was wrong. The water ran out in one of the days of our staing. Only in the last day we had hot water. Same thing with the wifi, that didn´t work in the rooms the most of the time, or even in the corridors, next to the routers. Despite all those things, the hygiene is poor. Towels and rooms aren't well cleaned and a friend that was travelling with me found a huge rat inside the room. Is a beautiful place, good location, but have a lot of thing to improve. I don´t recommend the experience!

reviews.title: Beautiful monastery with great service
reviews.text: Rooms are clean and well equiped and the staff is super friendly and helpful. The neighbourhood is vibrant with San Pedro market in front of this huge and beautiful monastery with 3 gardens to relax. They support several good causes like a childrens project in the back of the building so your money is very well spent.

reviews.title: Rest for the body and soul
reviews.text: I wanted to stay here because most of the profit supports the orphanage run onsite. It is right next to a beautiful church and an amazing mercado. The rooms are pretty spartan in appearance which is perfect given the location and purpose but everything else gave the guest all the comfort needed. The beds were great and there was PLENTY of hot water and soft towels. There were portable heaters that kept the temperature perfect all night. The staff was super helpful. When I told them we would be leaving before breakfast, they told me they would wake up and give us some food for the journey which they did. I really loved staying here and would absolutely stay here again.

reviews.title: Friendly hotel with a mission to help orphans
reviews.text: An old monastery with a courtyard, transformed into a modern hotel. A really big compliment to all the staff here, who really go the extra mile to make your stay a superb one. In 3 weeks travelling through Peru, we didn't have such a great experience with the staff! Extremely friendly and helpful all of them! Furthermore, the rooms (especially the newer ones at the back) are modern and clean. Breakfasts were also some of the best we had during our stay in Peru, especially try the fresh avocados!

reviews.title: Gorgeous courtyard and great food
reviews.text: The hotel is expensive but is absolutely beautiful. The courtyard is a nice place to hang out and eat lunch, or have a glass of wine. The food was great (we enjoyed opera night in the dining room). Great location near Plaza de Armas.

reviews.title: Quiet spot near all the action
reviews.text: I was happy to find this quiet oasis that was near all the sites. Although next to the busy San Pedro Market it was very quiet and serene. The rooms are small but modern and adequate. I was feeling unwell from the altitude and they brought me oxygen to my room. The small gardens are a nice touch. The breakfast was adequate but not exciting. The only problem I had was with the tourists smoking in the interior gardens. It's horrible to have to walk by them especially when suffering from altitude sickness. This should be a non-smoking hotel.

reviews.title: Very good Indian food
reviews.text: We were in a large group and ate a few meals here although we did not stay here and the Indian food was as good as u ll get in a good restaurant in India itself. The host are very kind and some of us were vegetarian and they made sure food was cooked as per our needs and of very good taste

reviews.title: Hotel deserves better staff
reviews.text: - Staff is always smiling but useless. They could not provide the room we paid for and could not sort the problem idem. After an hour complaining, manager involved and 24 hours waiting, they finally gave us the room we paid for and without a single sorry. Internet is horrible, you can use at all. + Location. Nice renovated old building.

reviews.title: Sofia
reviews.text: The hotel is located near the historical center of Cusco, next to the Cathedral with the same name. There is a taxi stand near the hotel - very comfortable for us. The owner is very kind and helpful woman that gave us very useful advices and help. The rooms are suitable and correspond the prices. The cleaning could be improved as well as the breakfasts, which are quite modest. The thing that most impressed me was the kindness, fairness and responsiveness of the owners. I can recommend the hotel especially to the visitors from less rich regions of the world.

reviews.title: Comfortable, good location, great staff.
reviews.text: This hotel has beautiful grounds and comfortable beds/rooms. We unexpectedly had to book a few extra days here, and the staff was lovely. They helped us with booking taxis, changing rooms, etc. and everyone was very personable. It is easy to feel at home here. In general, this is a great value, and we were very happy and comfortable during our stay. I wish breakfast was available a little later, though. The only drawback is the noise. There was a lot of street noise, especially since the Mercado San Pedro and plaza are right outside. In another room I stayed in, there was a fair amount of noise from the religious school next door, as well as from the hallway and adjacent rooms (old building - you can pretty much hear everything). I did hear, however, from other guests that their rooms were quiet. If a little more noise doesn't bother you at all, this is the perfect place to stay. Otherwise, just bear this in mind. Still worth it, in my opinion, for the value you get.

reviews.title: Basically good.
reviews.text: Great location. Nice short walk to Plaza de Armas full of local flavor and color. The gardens are beautiful and well maintained. The staff cannot be more courteous, friendly and polite. Excellent guys. The included breakfast is good and the restaurant area where it is served is very comfortable, looking at the gardens with awesome natural light. The rooms are small which is ok, the problems with the rooms are: wifi signal does not reach inside the rooms, it is a common problem all over since other guess complained about it too. Beds are awfully hard! Almost wood feeling. Electrical outlets are too few (2 in be area and 1 in bathroom). There is NO where to put toiletries in the bathroom but a very small skinny glass shelf. Closets are good enough and pretty clean all over. Advice: stay away from restaurant other than eating the included breakfast. Food is lame for Peruvian standards, bad service specially at night. My food order was served cold after being microwaved (portions on the plate were cold while others warm and kind of dried out) Budget wise is a ok hotel because its location and friendly staff.

reviews.title: Great Customer Service for a 3 Star Hotel
reviews.text: I booked this hotel as a way to acclimate to the altitude in Cuzco before doing a 4 day trek on the Inca Trail to Macchu Picchu. When we arrived it looked like they couldn't find our reservation but was still able to find us a room and honor the price that we booked it at. The rooms were what you would expect from a 3 star hotel. The Internet sometimes worked in our room, but it mostly worked in the lobby. The hotel and rooms are not spectacular by any means, but as this was a family-owned hotel, most of the great things about it was from the service. The room itself was clean and roomy and provided all of our basic needs like hot water and clean sheets. And there was a water jug and tea and books on the side of the building if you needed any of those things. The towels they provided us were on the tough, not-so-soft side but still usable. The owner was very sweet and personable. The location was good. It was about a 10 minute walk to the main plaza so not very far from all the action, and it was right across the street from the flea market and next door to a church. When it was time to leave, they let us store our bags in their storage room for 4 days, which was a nice touch considering we had not planned to stay there when we got back. After our trek, we came to find out that the apartment we booked with a private owner was not even for the whole apartment and only for a private room, so we ended up cancelling it and begged Hotel San Pedro to take us in. Luckily on this New Year's Eve, there was room for us, and they were able to accommodate us on the busiest nights of the year! A party of 5 had cancelled at the last minute, so we ended up being upgraded to a nicer room. The owner was incredibly understanding and made our night. They truly care about their customers and aim to please. And for that, I recommend staying here if all you need are the bare essentials of a great hotel.

reviews.title: Good but too pricey
reviews.text: Great social responsibility: Some of the money goes to an orphanage. Nice rooms but not great value for your money. Low quality breakfast. Good, reliable internet connection. Nice garden and location next to the San Pedro market. We asked for another night but they said they were full although we realised booking.com said they had an available room, so make sure to confirm your booking.

reviews.title: Excelent Hotel and stuff, highly recommend!
reviews.text: We stayed for 3 nights before and after our trip to Machu Picchu and it's in a great location, close to the main square in Cusco. The service was excellent, stuff very polite, friendly and helpful, they store our luggage for us while we were away in Aguas Caliente. They have plenty of coca tea in the reception lobby and oxygen tank in case you get sick from the altitude. I recommend to take Azetosolamida twice a day and plenty of coca tea. The hotel room was really nice, had an electric heather and we used it all 3 nights. Great breakfast with plenty of food choice. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Beautiful hotel with friendly staff
reviews.text: Our room was pretty quiet but we were in the middle of the complex on the second level. Facilities were basic, heater and bankets, a desk, Tv which we didn't watch, wifi was usable, water pressure was good and the water was hot almost instantly. There is an orion supermarket on the corner next to the hotel and it is walking distance to most things you need in Cusco. The hotel has free tea-(three different types) at the desk but no kettle in the room and also there is an oxygen cylinder which may be of use as it takes some time to get used to the altitude, at about 3400m it is 1000 meters higher than Machu Picchu. The front desk staff and all staff were very friendly and helpful. Breakfast was good with good coffee and juices, as was dinner, I recommend the grilled fish, I think it was trout, we had half board with breakfast and dinner included. We went to Machu Picchu for a day trip and they packed dinner and lunch, a sandwich some fruit and water for the trip. We took our own taxi from the airport for 15 soles, the hotel arranged a taxi for the trip to the airport which was 20 soles paid to the driver, we thought this was reasonable as the taxi was booked in advance and we made our flight with some time to spare. Domestic flights take a lot longer to get through security so luckily the hotel recommended we leave earlier as we would not have made the flight (if it was on time), our flight ended up being delayed anyway but it was better that we got there at the time they recommended.

reviews.title: Delightful converted monestary experience
reviews.text: We chose this hotel because of proximity to the railway station (which was closed for the wet season) and were impressed with very helpful staff and the location of rooms which were set well back from the street, thus escaping traffic noise. The converted monastic rooms although small were very clean and suited our short-term stay. The only drawback was the timber flooring of the corridors which generated foot-traffic noise which interfered with sleep. Carpeting would solve the problem. The location provided easy walking to the central part of the city for the cafes and shopping. The hotel would be our choice if we returned to this charming city.

reviews.title: Fantastic Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is a few blocks from the main plaza, but an easy 10 minute walk. It is adjacent to the San Pedro Market which is fantastic. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Grounds are well kept and rooms are very clean. Great value for the money. Breakfast is fantastic. Very safe area. Hotel access monitored.

reviews.title: A memorable long weekend
reviews.text: For years my wife and I had planned to visit Machu Picchu. Now we had a perfect trip! One night in Lima at the Westin hotel (great city, we missed a great dinner as we went to Astrid & Gaston ..... terrible), however the next day we flew to Cusco, and staid at the Belmont monasterio hotel (amazing location, service..... just excellent). We took the Belmont Brigham Hiram train to Machu Picchu (wow, this is the train to take) service, views, food...... and then arrived to Machu Picchu.......... not much more to say. That place is special and spectacular!! If you have the chance to make this trip.. it’s a bucket list trip

reviews.title: Pity of the small room with no window! Otherwise very recomandable
reviews.text: We stayed one night in a room that was small but had a lovely view on the garden and overlooking the breakfast room. We traveled in a group and after that one night we came back for 2 nights after our trip to the Sacred Valley. For the last 2 nighs we had another room that was smaller than the first one and this time we even didn't have a window! Just a small one in the ceiling! There was a large shower but everything else in the bathroom was very small. It was ok for 2 nights but surely not recomandable if you book a longer stay. That is my only complaint as otherwise the staff is very helpful and friendly, very good breakfast, special environment. If you wanted to enter or leave the hotel there was someone of the staff at the door to open it.

reviews.title: Cusco Hotel Monestario
reviews.text: The Hotel Montesario truly provides an exceptional experience. From arrival to departure, every person we came in contact with was welcoming and helpful. The setting is beautiful and relaxing, the food excellent, and the furnishings iconic. The rooms are unique with very comfortable beds. The location is very accessible to the square and historic sites of Cusco.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: This is a lovely hotel, peaceful with very helpful and friendly staff. The courtyards are very nice and I loved the fact that it is still a functioning monaster and that the money I paid went to help the monaster itself. It's also in a great location, close to everything. I stayed there before and after my visit to Macchu Picchu and they were more than happy to keep my bag for 5 days. Definitely recommend this place.

reviews.title: Good Overnight stay. Comfortable and Well Located.
reviews.text: Enjoyed our one night stay. Even though our plane was late, there was someone waiting for us at the airport with our name on a sign. Our room was comfortable with a modern bathroom and a portable heater. We were nicely greeted and informed about the monesterio grounds. Beautiful gardens, nice breakfast buffet. Good walking location to restaurants. Would definitely stay again.

reviews.title: Very quiet and comfortable, next to the main market of downtown Cusco
reviews.text: I arrived on business and only stayed for a few hours. I chose the hotel because of its proximity to the downtown Cusco and San Pedro Market, where you can find typical products of the Region. The staff were friendly and the rooms are spacious, comfortable and warm, with free but some slow Wi-Fi. The style of the hotel is traditional because it shares the location with the convent of the Mercedarian Sisters, which means that it has several beautiful courtyards with magnificent views of the convent, the hotel and the San Pedro catholic church. In summary I liked the hotel, but I think it should improve the variety and flavour of the breakfast and put the final rate on the web, because in the web offer, services and taxes are not included.

reviews.title: beautiful but noisy
reviews.text: This hotel is old but clean and beautiful, however it is very noisy because it is located next to rail road and right opposite to Mercado Central de San Pedro. You heard train and construction noise in the very early morning before dawn. they offer good breakfast with great varieties and all the necessary toiletry including conditioner which I appreciate . It cost 10-12 soles to take taxi to the town square and 30-40 soles for 4 people to get to Poroy or airport.

reviews.title: A pleasant surprise
reviews.text: This is a great boutique hotel just a few blocks from the central square of Cusco. Front desk staff are always friendly, smiling and helpful. Rooms are basic but spread out across a huge connected group of small buildings. The bed was very comfortable with great blankets to keep you warm at night when the temperature drops. My room didn't have a heater, but they brought a space heater when I inquired and it worked fine. It's next to San Pedro Market where, during the day, you can buy fresh fruits, vegetables, etc. It's about a 5-10 minute walk to Plaza de Armas. Breakfast in the morning was a buffet but the scrambled eggs they pre-prepared were cold. When I asked for fresh fried eggs, I was told no. Only after I persisted did they make fresh eggs. That was my only gripe. Overall, it's a nice hotel, very well maintained and the staff are great. I'd stay here again if I return to Cusco.

reviews.title: SRT - 'Socially Responsible Travel'
reviews.text: The profits from this converted monastery fund an orphanage housed at the back. It's location was off the beaten tourist track, but right across from the oldest and biggest market in town. The building is far from glamorous, but is quite clean and the courtyard provided excellent refuge. The rooms were of adequate size, the bed was quite good and the shower pressure was excellent. The buffet breakfast was really good. The front desk spoke broken English and was very friendly and helpful (We had delayed luggage that our travel agent had to deal with. She indicated that the staff were quite rude, which surprised us). Our attraction to the hotel was that the nuns that owned it, we saw them once, and helped support local children that need it.

reviews.title: Wonderful hotel - would return!
reviews.text: My brother, sister, and I stated here for 2 nights while visiting Cusco and Machu Picchu. We loved it here and would return. The location was right across from the San Pedro Market and very close to various Plazas in historic Cusco. We walked every where in town, and had a very easy time getting a taxi/uber when we needed them to and from the airport and train station. Check in was quick and we were brought to our room by a very kind staff person who told us (in English) about the history of the hotel/monastary. Our room had 3 single beds - with layers of snuggly covers - and a clean, modern bathroom. There was a TV (which we didn't use) and free wifi. Plenty of outlets to charge our gadgets. The breakfast buffet was delicious and available from 6-9am. It had a lovely combination of breakfast standbys (eggs, toast, coffee, juice, fruit) and some unique treats (special juices, breads, sweet potatoes, etc.) The grounds were well kept and stunning. There was a bar, which we didn't see. Our room was on the 2nd floor and there was some noice from an accompanying establishment. We had a sound machine on our phone, so it didn't bother us! We would come back here again in a heartbeat! The staff was helpful and kind! Thanks for the wonderful stay!

reviews.title: Tried to ruin my Cusco experience. Horrible.
reviews.text: Firstly I would like to say how disappointed I am with this whole experience of Ashiana. A few days previous to our stay, we visited the Makhiana. This restaurant is owned by the same people, it was empty, the food was an average change but the lady said she gives the leftovers to the homeless so I rated it 5 stars in a bid of generosity. It was here that the owner showed us pictures of her hotel, set in the grounds of the church with wifi, breakfast and hot water ; all for 80 soles. Double the price of a hostel but I thought after returning from MP it would be worth it. Well wolf in sheep's clothing springs to mind. No hot water, no wifi and no coffee at breakfast. All after climbing Machu Picchu! When I asked her to help with the wifi- she said quote 'I'm having the worst day of my life'. Well I guess you have a pretty decent life ripping off tourists. When we went to pay, we were invoiced 220 sole! You'd have thought in a desperate bid to rectify the situation she would reduce the price, not increase it! I demanded to speak to the owner over the phone who blamed our 'machine' for the lack of wifi and said that the hot water came on at 10. Check out is at 10. She screamed and shouted at me on the phone and I've come to the conclusion that she is a raging liar- I don't think she gives leftovers to the homeless. Awful.

reviews.title: Tide too high and I do not want to hold it on
reviews.text: Service was good but it was not pleasant at all to be asked to pay 30% more because of a tax that was mentioned in tiny letters. The shower did not have a roof! Breakfast did not include typical breakfast food from the region.

reviews.title: Cozy Place to Stay in Cusco
reviews.text: This hotel is unique and interesting. It supports a cause - the profits provide financial support for the attached girls school. It is a historical building - a renovated monastery. It is a peaceful oasis with 3 inner courtyards of green lawns, birds, statuary and flowers. It is in the heart of the Cusco historical district, walking distance to the cathedral and across from the largest public market in the city. And it is an attentive hotel with good beds, sparkling clean spaces and an ample breakfast.

reviews.title: Amazing place
reviews.text: My first day in Cuzco and excelent experience, comfortable room bed hot water, clean and colonial style very nice garden around flowers.the service excelent the y help With the tours transportation to machupichu

reviews.title: Sleeping in former monastery
reviews.text: This hotel is converted from monastery which connects to the San Pedro church. What a unique experience staying at former monastery built in 1650. Room is comfortable, good size, with full amenities including mobile heater. Location is good. It locates opposite market, supermarket within walking distance of main square. Rate is quite reasonable too.

reviews.title: A lovely stay at Hotel Monasterio San Pedro
reviews.text: My family and I had a wonderful time at this hotel. The staff was helpful and courteous. The rooms were clean, beautiful and comfortable. The restaurant was delightful. The location is great. It's walking distance from everything. I highly recommend it. The staff and manager made it a lovely experience. Thank you very, very much!!!

reviews.title: Potential
reviews.text: My family and I checked into the hotel our first night in Cusco before heading off to Machu Picchu the next morning. The hotel has so much potential. It used to be a monastery that connected to a church. There is apparently still an active order of nuns that oversee an orphanage for girls on the property. None of the hotel employees could speak English or Spanish that we came into contact with. Only the lady in charge of the place could, and she was very nice. The property was very poorly cared for, but has loads of potential with a little bit of TLC. Maybe the beginning of rainy season had gotten them a little behind on their gardening. Also, internet was not available in the rooms on our side of the hotel.

reviews.title: An unusual experience
reviews.text: Remember that this was a monastery and so you can imagine a life of quietness, discipline and simplicity - the entire place and the rooms exude this feeling for me. I don't mind rooms without windows or small openings for lighting only but if you do than its not for you. So much calm and serenity with cathedral chanting (not spooky) and the staff were just like calming to the soul. Loved every moment.

reviews.title: Cozy, clean and accommodating monastery
reviews.text: I traveled to Peru with my 2 sisters. This was the first hotel we checked into a soon as we arrived to Cuzco. The people that work at the hotel are very accommodating and helpful. We had a room on the 3rd floor which was okay for us but if you are an older person or have problems climbing or breathing it may be a bit of a struggle. We purposely planned to stay a couple of days in Cuzco before travelling to Aguas Calientes for our Machu Pichu experience in order to acclimate. The gentlemen carried our suitcases for us up the stairs which was a great relief to us... I did not think that I would feel out of breath since I am accustomed to working out frequently but getting acclimated is part of the experience when you visit Cuzco. The hotel offers oxygen tanks if you feel the need for it and from the moment you enter the hotel you are offered Coca tea which I suggest you drink plenty of to help with acclimation. The hotel offered clean, tidy rooms with warm covers on the beds, a clean shower and the restaurant onsite is good. There were several evenings that we opted to order room service from the restaurant after spending a long day of walking on inclines and exploring. The breakfast is served in the restaurant and offers a variety of hams, cheese, breads and they will make your eggs to order. They also offer a meat, rice and vegetable dish. If there is something in particular that you would like I am sure you can ask one of the waiters and they will do their best to serve you what you like. Nearby you will find a supermarket and a open market similar to a farmers market but you will find all kinds of artisan products locally made. When exiting the hotel if you walk straight you will run into the plaza which is where everything happens. Around and near the plaza you will find clubs, bars, cafes, stores and restaurants. IF you make a right exiting the hotel you will run into a neighborhood similar to Chinatown In NY where you will find all kinds of shop that sell locally made items cheap.

reviews.title: A Unique Venue
reviews.text: This hotel, "converted" from the adjacent monastery, is in a central location in this large (pop. 450,000) city. It is directly across the street from the mercado central. The market offers any foodstuff or soft good any tourist could want. The hotel's staff is its principal asset. They are polite, genuinely friendly, and helpful. The hotel's physical condition is wanting. Rooms are plain, beds are well made-up, mattresses are firm, but the wooden floors are filthy. There is no palpable effort to clean beneath the beds. Dust tumbleweeds were prevalent. The bathroom is adequate, but the sink is minuscule. It is adequate for washing one hand at a time. There is adequate space for a larger one. The sun's rise (between 5:45 and 6:00AM) heralds the arrival of much horn honking from the intersection immediately behind the back of the building. This is adequate to frustrate any efforts at further sleep. The breakfast buffet is generous and of good quality; the room in which it is set is quite shopworn. We found this hotel adequate for two nights, but felt it would have been burdensome beyond that.

reviews.title: Great location in cusco
reviews.text: The hotel is managed byan indian couple and for us,Indians, it was a great experience because of the location. It is right next to San Pedro cathedral and opposite to San Pedro market. All sights in historical area of cusco are nearby. Taxi stand is just outside and the plaza de aramas is five minutes walk away. Cocoa tea is available all 24 hours. While we were lucky not to have altitude sickness, the hotel provides oxygen cans at ten usd, if used. The negative points are poor plumbing, Toiletteries and towels which are not white. Rooms are comfortable with room heaters and hot water is available at select times only. The interior of the hotel, which is inside the monastery, is amazing and the twisty corridors to reach the rooms takes us back by a century. However the corridors are not heated and in winters this can be pretty uncomfortable. On the whole not an European standards hotel but for us it was the best in cusco.

reviews.title: Fantastic Place
reviews.text: Stayed here one night for business, lovely owners and the breakfast was great. The room i stayed in was very comfy and had all the modern requirements. I will be visiting again for business in the coming weeks and months so i am more then happy to stay here on my return. Thanks for the hospitality and help. Simon

reviews.title: Paul and Sam
reviews.text: stayed for a wedding and was by far the best b&b ive stayed in, Dave and Hazel coundnt do more for us, room was fantastic and the breakfasts were amazing. we both cant wait to come back for another trip. hope to see you again soon

reviews.title: Mrs S Hartlett
reviews.text: We use the private swimming pool on a regular basis, both of our children have learnt to swim there. The facilities are superb. A very clean, friendly and relaxing environment. The B&B facilities are beautifully presented and the owners are very friendly and helpful. Would highly recommend.

reviews.title: EXCELLENT B&B
reviews.text: Made a last minute booking to the Olde Hall B&B and was pleasantly surprised by how great it was. Our room was clean and modern, breakfast was excellent and the owners made sure that you had exactly what you wanted. They were extremely obliging and helpful and I wouldn't hesitate recommending the Olde Hall to anyone. Really liked the special touches that made our stay even more enjoyable.

reviews.title: POSH HOSTEL
reviews.text: Stayed for a two night weekend and is certainly odd as others have pointed out I describe as a posh hostel for the following reasons: There seems to be a lot of rules and requirements. You must let them know before you arrive as to the exact time you will be arriving otherwise somebody may not be there to greet you. You must remove your shoes on entry. You shouldn’t have to do this, especially when most of the floors are exposed wood anyway. The “welcome” manual in the room has more things you must not do! You need to complete a form the day before as to what you want for breakfast the next day and breakfast is served at a presise time, not a time range. Worst of all the breakfast is served at a large communal table. This is horrible and not necessary, as there is plenty of room to have the tables set individually. We felt very uncomfortable sitting with strangers where you feel obliged to make conversation and small talk. I’m sure the other people there felt exactly the same. This is unacceptable. Although the breakfast was good we did not enjoy it on either day. The room we had was small but the bed and bedding was very comfortable. It was not ensuite which we knew about when booking, but the very small communal bathroom was on the other side of the landing and was a pain. Unfortunately the host Hazel is not a natural host. A welcoming smile when we arrived would have helped. She had a busy time as she was having to do the work and breakfasts on her own. She tried to make conversation and show an interest but it is obvious when something is insincere and forced. Finally, on the Saturday night she was entertaining in the back garden with a small fire which sent smoke directly into our bedroom at the back of the house. When we got back to the room it stunk of smoke and we then had to keep window shut all evening. Not very thoughtful. Even though Hazel may not believe this,we are not ones to complain lightly. If you do one thing, GET RID OF THE COMMUNUAL TABLE !!!
